chapters.title: Chapter 601: A Love Fated To End [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Before either Tariq or Safira could find their voices to reply, Menes’s right hand moved.
SWOOSH!
It wasn’t a strike like Tariq expected... instead it was a gentle, sweeping wave of warm golden sand that rose from the floorboards like a living blanket.
The sand swept around Tariq and Safira, lifting them both effortlessly off their feet.

Tariq’s lances dissolved into harmless dust, and before they could even let out a gasp of protest, the tide of sand carried them through the lounge archway, sliding them smoothly down the private corridor and directly into the primary royal suite.
CLANG-CLICK!
The heavy titanium suite door slammed shut behind them as the magnetic deadbolts engaged with a definitive motorized hiss.
Back in the empty lounge, Menes Al-Mansur stood alone.
He listened to the muffled confused voices of his son on the other side of the bulkhead with a bitter fragile smile resting on his lips.
"Enjoy it while you can, my son," Menes whispered into the quiet air, his voice barely louder than the hum of the jet engines. "Hold her tight and savor every breath."
He turned back to the glass table, reaching for the crystal bottle of aged sparkling vintage.
His bronze hand was trembling so violently that the neck of the bottle clinked against the rim of his glass with a rhythmic tink-tink-tink.
He filled the flute to the brim, raised it toward the endless desert outside, and swallowed the alcohol in a single burning gulp.
"Because we are all about to die."
THUD!
Tariq landed on the thick plush velvet carpet of the master suite with his boots skidding across the floor as the golden sand dissolved into fine harmless powder around his ankles.
Beside him, Safira stumbled, letting out a soft surprised gasp before Tariq caught her around the waist with his bandaged forearm, pulling her flush against his chest.
"Hey..." Tariq breathed, his pulse racing as he looked back at the locked titanium door. "Are you alright?"
Safira rested her palms against his chest, her dark eyes still wide with utter disbelieving shock.

"Tariq..." she whispered, her voice trembling slightly. "Did your father just... did he really say that? A grandfather? Since when does the Pharaoh-President care about grandchildren? He looked... he looked almost happy."
Tariq’s face flushed bright crimson with the heat spreading from his neck to the tips of his ears.

"I don’t know," Tariq muttered, rubbing the back of his neck with an awkward self-conscious chuckle. "He’s never spoken to me like that in my entire life. Usually, if I raise a sand lance in his presence, he breaks three of my ribs and leaves me in the training yard to reflect on filial piety..."
Safira looked at him with her lips curving into a slow breathtaking smile that chased away the lingering shadows of the arena.

"You threatened to burn the throne room down for me," she whispered, her fingers trailing up the lapel of his linen tunic. "You risked everything. Why? Any other prince in your position would have accepted the decree... A concubine’s bed is still warm, Tariq. You could have taken three noble wives from the southern clans and secured your borders..."
Tariq reached out, his bandaged fingers gently cupping the side of her face.
Despite the rough spirit-silk wrapping, his touch was impossibly tender.
He leaned down, pressing his lips softly against the center of her forehead, breathing in the familiar intoxicating scent of lotus blossoms and warm desert air that clung to her hair.

"I told you four years ago, Safira," Tariq murmured against her skin. "I’m going to change the cycle... The Al-Mansur dynasty has ruled this desert for centuries by treating women like currency and our children like disposable soldiers. My brothers... Malikar and Khensu... they lived and died as tools of the state."
A brief dark shadow flickered across his eyes, his voice dropping into a solemn tone.

"I grieve for them. Truly, I do... They were my flesh and blood. But if their deaths are what it took to shatter that cycle, if their absence is what finally forces the crown onto my head without a civil war, then I won’t waste this chance... I won’t rule from a cold loveless palace... We rule the Sun Court together... Side by side... As equals!"
Safira’s breath hitched with tears welling in her dark eyes.
She buried her face against his stomach, wrapping her arms tightly around his waist, clinging to him as if terrified he’d dissolve into the desert air.

"When Seraphina’s fire hit me..." Safira sobbed softly, her voice muffled against his clothes, "...when my flesh turned to glass and I felt the cracks spreading through my chest, do you know what my biggest regret was, Tariq?"
"What, my love?"

"I never got to be a mother," she whispered, looking up at him with her lower lip trembling with raw vulnerability. "I’ve held lances since I was seven years old. I’ve killed crawlers in the Sovereign Realm and I’ve bled for the state but I hate it... I hate the fighting... All I ever wanted, all I dreamed about when we were hiding in the southern gardens at midnight, was holding your child. A son who looks like you and a daughter with your eyes."
Tariq’s heart hammered against his ribs with fierce overwhelming tenderness.

He looked down at her beautiful tear-stained face with the memory of her near-death washing over him, replaced instantly by an urgent burning hunger to reaffirm that she was here, that she was warm, that she was alive.
"Then why are we waiting?" Tariq whispered, his voice thick with sudden husky heat.
Safira blinked, her cheeks blooming with a deep radiant blush that reached the roots of her hair.
"R-Really? Right now? We’re still thirty thousand feet in the air—"
Tariq didn’t let her finish the sentence as he leaned down, capturing her lips in a deep fierce desperate kiss that stole the air clean from her lungs.
"Mmh~"
SMACK!
Safira let out a soft muffled sound against his mouth with her arms instantly winding around his neck, pulling him down with an urgency that matched his own.
Her fingers tangled into his thick dark curls, her body pressing against his with a feverish heat that made the heavy fabric between them feel like an unbearable wall.
Tariq’s bandaged hands moved with hunger, sliding under the hem of her silk tunic, feeling the smooth flawless skin of her waist.
With a swift fluid motion, he pulled the garment over her head, letting it flutter to the floor, followed instantly by his own linen shirt.
Their bodies met immediately and they were hot.
’I always tell Saf this but she’s really hot...’
Tariq scooped her into his arms, carrying her the two steps to the enormous silk-draped bed at the center of the suite.

They tumbled onto the mattress together in a tangle of limbs as Tariq shifting his weight smoothly until he was hovering over her with his knees pinning her thighs as he looked down at her beneath the amber lamplight.
Safira was breathless with her chest heaving and her dark eyes molten with surrender.
"Come on~"
Tariq dipped his head, trailing his lips down the sharp elegant curve of her jawline, moving to the soft sensitive hollow beneath her ear.
"Mmh~" Safira moaned softly, her head tilting back into the pillows and her spine arching upward as a violent shiver rippled down her skin.

Tariq parted his lips, pressing a slow deliberate kiss into the crook of her neck with his teeth gently grazing the tender flesh before drawing it into a deep bruising suction, marking her skin with an unmistakable dark-crimson bloom of possession.
"Hgnh~!" Safira gasped with her nails digging into the muscles of his bare back as her breath began coming in ragged shallow pants. "Tariq... please..."

Tariq lifted his head slightly, his amber eyes dark with pure concentrated adoration, preparing to lower himself further and to taste every inch of the woman who had returned from the grave for him...
FLICKER!
Tariq’s gaze instinctively drifted toward the panoramic viewport set into the suite’s outer wall as he froze.
Thirty thousand feet in the air, against the brilliant blinding azure of the desert sky, there was a blot of pure lightless black.
It wasn’t a bird and it wasn’t an aircraft either.
’Weird...’
It was like a massive tear in the sky, barely a mile off the starboard wing of their escort formation.
It looked like a swirling vortex of pitch-black sand, twisting against the sunlight like an ink stain spreading across clean water.
Safira felt him hesitate as she reached up with both hands, cupping his face, her lips parting with a playful teasing pout.
"Tariq... don’t look away," she whispered, her voice dripping with sweet intoxicating longing as she drew his head back down toward her chest. "Look at me. Only at me..."
Tariq looked down into her beautiful dark eyes, smiling softly, letting the strange anomaly in the sky slip from his mind.
"Always."
He leaned down, their lips meeting in another deep passionate embrace.
...It only took one moment after that. That was all it took... A single microscopic fraction of a heartbeat.
SHRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRK!
There was no sound of an impact as one second, Tariq was hovering over his lover on the soft silk mattress of the royal suite and the next second, the entire world simply ceased to exist.
WHOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
The hurricane-force slipstream of the upper atmosphere hit Tariq’s bare skin with the violence of a freight train.
The ceiling, the bed, the titanium bulkheads, the luxury furnishings, the entire forward fuselage of the Aethel-Sun had been instantly vaporized into thin air.
’H–huh?’
Tariq tumbled through the freezing, violent thirty-thousand-foot void, completely naked with his eyes burning as the thin sub-zero air whipped through his hair.
"WHAT—"
A strangled horrified shriek ripped from his throat as he twisted his body, fighting against the terminal velocity drag...
All around him in the open sky, butchery was unfolding.
CRACK-CRUNCH-SHATTER!

Massive, colossal rivers of jet-black sand, thousands of tons of coarse lightless mineral screaming through the stratosphere like ancient ravenous serpents, were violently coiling around the eight escort cruisers.
The star-iron hulls of the warships didn’t dent or buckle under physical weight.
The moment the black sand touched the polished metal, an unnatural horrific chemical corruption spread across the plates...
The white titanium instantly turned into brittle lightless black glass!
BOOM! SHATTER!
A cruiser carrying sixty royal guards shattered into millions of microscopic black glass fragments in mid-air with the soldiers inside tumbling into the open sky!
Tariq watched in paralyzed, waking horror as a lieutenant, a seasoned Third Stage warrior, was swallowed by a swirling tendril of black sand.
The man didn’t bleed and he didn’t burn either.
As the black grains coated his armor and skin, his flesh, his eyes, his screaming mouth, and his core violently calcified, turning into a solid statue of jet-black glass.
SNAP!
The glass statue tumbled into the slipstream, caught by a stray shockwave, and instantly pulverized into fine drifting black powder.
"SAFIRA!" Tariq screamed, his voice tearing raw against the roaring wind as his terror reached a hysterical fever pitch! "SAFIRA! WHERE ARE YOU?!"
He whipped his head around, wildly pumping his core as he was desperate to manifest his sand-glider to arrest his fall...
And then he saw her.
Ten yards below him, falling through the azure sky, was Safira.
Her bare olive skin was completely exposed to the freezing winds with her hair whipping violently around her face.
SPLAT-SHRRRRK!

A thick undulating tendril of black sand, barbed like an ancient harpoon and dripping with an aura of total soul-erasure, had shot directly through the center of her chest, impaling her clean through her sternum.
"Gah—!"
Thick dark crimson blood erupted from Safira’s mouth, spraying into the freezing wind.
Her hands frantically clawed at the black sand spike piercing her ribs, but her fingers found no purchase since the grains were living churning needles that bit straight through her palms.
"T-Tariq..." she choked out, blood pouring over her lips, her voice a broken rasp that was barely audible over the roaring slipstream. "Tariq... help... it hurts..."
CRACKLE!
Before Tariq’s dilated horror-stricken pupils, the horrific calcification began...
From the wound in her chest, the corruption spread as her olive skin violently hardened, turning into an oily lightless black glass.
The smooth curves of her hips, her thighs, her neck, the very skin he had kissed bare seconds ago, were freezing into solid brittle crystal...
"NO! NO! NO!" Tariq shrieked, an animalistic wail tearing from the depths of his soul.
He threw both arms forward, ignoring the agonizing burn in his fractured hands, desperate to ignite his blood-quartz to bridge the gap.
"HOLD ON! SAFIRA! I’M COMING! I’M—"
THWIP-THWIP-THWIP-THWIP!
Four massive razor-sharp tendrils of black sand erupted from the void behind him.
SHRUNK-CRUNCH!

They tore through his physical body with merciless precision as one tendril punched straight through his right shoulder, severing the clavicle while a second impaled his left hip, shattering the pelvis and a third drilled through his lower abdomen, pinning his spine.
"AGHHH!" Tariq choked, his vision instantly exploding into stars of agony as blood flooded his trachea.
And the fourth tendril...
SQUEEZE!
It coiled tightly around his chest, driving inward between his ribs, wrapping its coarse freezing black grains directly around his primary mana core!
Tariq’s body went completely rigid.
’N-nooo...’
He looked down through the blood dripping into his eyes with his gaze locking onto Safira’s face one final time.
She was screaming.
Even with her chest turned to black glass, her head was still flesh and her dark eyes wide with pure terror as she watched the black tendrils tear through the man she loved.
"TARIQ! NO! PLEASE! GODS, NO—"
CRACK-CRUNCH!
The tendril inside Tariq’s chest tightened into an fist as his core... his spiritual organ that made him a Lord, shattered like a hollow eggshell.
The light in Tariq Al-Mansur’s amber eyes instantly died, snuffed out like a candle submerged in cold water.
"NOOOOOOOOOOOOO!" Safira shrieked, a sound so broken and so filled with soul-shattering agony that it seemed to tear through the sky itself!
CRUNCH!
The tendril in her chest didn’t give her another second to mourn... It constricted, crushing her fractured heart and her mana core simultaneously.
SHATTER!
In the blink of an eye, the black glass consumed both of them completely.

chapters.title: Chapter 602: Somebody Is In My Body...
paragraphs: Two statues of lightless oily glass tumbled through the thirty-thousand-foot void for a single second, before the atmospheric drag tore them apart, shattering Tariq and Safira into millions of drifting lifeless black particles that scattered across the sky with their souls erased from the wheel of reincarnation forever.
High above the falling debris, tumbling through the sky clad in his pristine white military suit, was Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur.
His gold pectoral collar had been ripped away by the wind with his beaten-gold headdress lost to the clouds.

His Fourth Stage mana was flaring violently, manifesting a massive shimmering disc of golden solar-sand beneath his boots to slow his descent, but his liquid-gold eyes were fixed entirely on the cloud of black dust below.
...He had watched it all.

...He had watched his last surviving son, the boy who had pointed a lance at him for love, the boy he had secretly blessed, be impaled, crushed, and erased from existence without even being granted the mercy of a corpse.

’If only...’ Menes thought, his composure cracking down the center with a deep bitter thought filling his head. ’If only our ancestor hadn’t been so greedy. If only she hadn’t reached for power she had no right to claim...’
SHRRRRK!
The sky darkened as a colossal wave of black sand, spanning three miles across, towering over the clouds like an apocalyptic tidal wave, descended upon the Pharaoh-President.
Menes looked up with his Fourth Stage solar shield holding for barely half a second before the black sand dissolved the gold mana like acid through paper.
PIERCE!

A massive jagged spear of black glass punched clean through Menes’s abdomen, lifting the ruler of Khemet into the air and the pain was immediate and accompanied by the freezing horrifying sensation of his own flesh calcifying into brittle black glass.
...The calm imperial facade that Menes Al-Mansur had maintained for three decades completely shattered.
"NO!" Menes screamed, his voice cracking into a high-pitched undignified shriek of pure terror. "I DON’T WANT TO DIE! I DON’T WANT TO DIE! THIS WASN’T MY SIN!"
He clawed frantically at the black spear with his fingernails snapping off against the glass as blood poured from his nose and ears.

"THIS IS ALL HER FAULT!" the Pharaoh-President wailed into the roaring wind, his mind breaking under the weight of the ancient curse. "OUR ANCESTOR! SHE DID THIS! IF ONLY SHE HADN’T BETRAYED NITOCRIS! IF ONLY SHE HADN’T THROWN THE WOMAN AWAY... WE WOULDN’T BE PAYING FOR IT! WE WOULDN’T—"
SNAP!
The black glass crawled over his throat, over his jaw, over his eyes.
CRACK-BOOM!
The body of Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur shattered into a cloud of black dust with his soul devoured whole, leaving only the empty wind.
RUMBLE-CRASH!
Thirty seconds later, the flaming wreckage of the Aethel-Sun and its eight escort cruisers slammed into the golden dunes below.

Massive concussive shockwaves rippled outward, throwing towering plumes of white-hot sand hundreds of feet into the air, the seismic thunder rolling across the desolate Khemet desert for sixty miles in every direction, signaling the total extinction of the main royal house of Al-Mansur.
In all of that...
’I’m scared...’
The thought was small and trembling like a plucked wire in the freezing dark.
’I’m so scared... Silas... please... somebody help me...’
Harper Whitmore stood, or rather she floated, in the center of an infinite lightless void that smelled of crushed dry lotus and ancient tomb-dust.
She had no weight and she had no breath.
When she looked down at her hands, she didn’t see the smooth pale skin of a noble trade heiress... she saw a translucent shimmering specter of pale violet light, rippling like an oil slick on water.
She was a ghost... A detached helpless soul trapped in the passenger seat of her own existence...
And barely five feet away from her spiritual eyes was her physical body.
Harper’s physical frame stood with its bare feet planted firmly upon the burning white-hot crest of a massive sand dune.
The desert wind whipped her tailored suit and the dark charcoal wool coated in fine silt while her long vibrant purple hair was loose, thrashing violently around her shoulders.
In her physical right hand, resting loosely at her side, was the First Khopesh of the Khemet Dominion.
The curved ancient sickle-sword gleamed with a sickening iridescent black sheen, its golden crossguard humming with a pulse that seemed to synchronize with the heartbeat of the desert itself.
In the distance, three miles away, black smoke billowed into the azure sky from the shattered burning crater where the royal fleet had fallen.
SLURP!
Harper watched in paralyzed nauseated horror as her physical tongue extended, licking her own lower lip with a slow relish that made Harper’s spirit want to vomit.
’What’s her issue...?’
SWOOSH!
Across the endless golden dunes vast rivers of black sand that had just slaughtered eighty royal guards and erased the ruling dynasty of Khemet came rushing back...

They flowed like living black water up the slope of the dune, swirling around Harper’s bare ankles, crawling up her calves, and seamlessly dissolving directly into the pores of her flesh, vanishing into her core with a soft warm hiss.
"Harper" chuckled.
The sound came from Harper’s own vocal cords, but the tone was off.
"Mmh..." the entity murmured with Harper’s physical fingers flexing tightly around the hilt of the khopesh. "What a truly magnificent vessel you are, little mortal."
The physical head turned slightly, the neck rolling with a slow fluid elegance that looked completely unnatural on Harper’s usually brisk professional frame.
Harper’s physical eyes locked directly onto Harper’s spiritual form.

The eyes were no longer the soft intelligent violet that Silas knew as they were burning with an intense emerald-green fire... a sickening radiance that seemed to pierce straight through Harper’s ethereal soul, pinning her like an insect on a display board.
Harper’s spirit gasped with an involuntary shudder of terror tearing through her incorporeal chest.
"Give it back..." Harper wept, her spiritual voice echoing in the dead space between them, cracking with rage. "Give me back my body, you monster! Get out of my head! GET OUT!"
The green-eyed entity didn’t scowl as she simply offered Harper a wide grin that stretched Harper’s lips until the corners practically tore.
’I’m sorry for acting like this Harper...’

"Now, now," Nitocris drawled, her tone carrying the smooth patronizing patience of an empress humoring a petulant servant. "Do not be so terribly ungrateful, little Harper... You should be down on your ethereal knees thanking me... I was not fully aware, when we first spoke in the quiet corridors of your mind, that you carried Khemet’s blood in your veins."
Nitocris raised Harper’s left hand, turning the pale wrist over, admiring the blue veins running beneath the translucent skin.

"It’s distant, of course," the entity continued, her voice rich with amused observation. "Diluted by generations of northern commoners and trade mongrels... A mere trickle from some wayward concubine who fled the southern wars three hundred years ago and yet, the genetic match is unmistakable... The sand magic, the authority I possess, harmonizes with your nervous system so effortlessly! You were practically born to be my scabbard."

"I am not your scabbard!" Harper screamed, lunging forward with her spiritual hands, desperate to claw at her own physical face and desperate to force her way back into her own meridians. "Why are you doing this...?"
VUM!
The moment Harper’s ethereal form crossed within two feet of her physical body, an invisible impenetrable barrier of dense pressure slammed into her soul.
"I’m sorry."
’Sorr—?’
CRACK!
Harper was violently repelled backward, tumbling through the empty air with her spiritual form flickering dangerously like a dying lightbulb.
Nitocris let out a soft sigh, resting the flat of the black khopesh against Harper’s shoulder.

"Do not embarrass yourself, child," Nitocris chided gently. "I told you... as a true Spirit of the old era, the mortal plane is forbidden to me. Those wretched Suppression Engines anchored in the lower crust by the World Council, they crush consciousness into inert stardust the moment we attempt to cross the waking threshold without a vessel..."
She looked up at the burning suns, her green eyes blazing with centuries of cold malice.

"I cannot walk upon this sand with my own flesh... Therefore, I must extend my deepest, most heartfelt gratitude to you, Harper Whitmore... By voluntarily opening your core, by surrendering your trust to the ’great warlord’ in the blade, you have generously donated your vessel to my holy vengeance."
Harper froze with her spiritual hands clutching her chest as a terrible nauseating realization washed over her.
’I opened my core...’ Harper remembered, the memory flashing through her mind like a jagged blade.
For a while now, the voice in the weapon had whispered sweet intoxicating promises.

It had offered her strength... It had shown her visions of grand battles, promising her the power to stand proudly beside Silas, promising that she would no longer be a weaker woman hiding behind his broad shoulders... And this morning, in the quiet privacy of her bedroom, the entity had told her that the final breakthrough required absolute surrender, that she had to drop her mental wards entirely to receive the ’gift.’
She had done it willingly and she had walked straight into the trap with a smile on her face.
"Who are you...?" Harper whispered, her spiritual voice shaking so violently it barely carried across the dune. "You aren’t Nitocris. You aren’t the First Per-aa... who the hell are you?!"
Nitocris paused.
Harper’s physical face tilted to the side, a slow dark mocking chuckle rumbling from her throat.

"Oh? Have you forgotten so quickly, little mortal?" Nitocris asked, her voice dropping into a deep tone that made the bedrock beneath the sand vibrate with sickening familiarity. "You have stood in my presence before and you walked through the sunken ruins of my sanctuary... You saw the broken pillars of my realm too."
Harper’s ethereal eyes widened in horror.
The memories of the ancient sunken tomb, the suffocating lightless domain that Silas had dragged her through weeks ago, surged back with suffocating clarity.
"I... Ititius...?" Harper choked out, her spirit trembling so hard she could barely maintain her human shape. "You... you are Ititius?!"
"We are one and the same," Nitocris replied, her tone conversational yet carrying the weight of an ancient abyss.
’Ititius was destroyed!’ Harper screamed internally with tears spilling from her spiritual eyes. ’Thor shattered that core and ripped that domain apart! How are you still here?!’
Nitocris didn’t bother to answer the unasked question.
She turned Harper’s physical body around with her green-lit gaze locking onto the shimmering heat haze on the northern horizon.
Fifty miles away, barely visible through the distortion of the desert sun, rose the colossal gleaming white walls of Iunu, the capital of the Sun-Crown.
VUUUUUUUM!
Nitocris bent Harper’s physical knees as the golden sand beneath her bare feet violently compressed into solid quartz.
BOOM!
In a detonation that threw a colossal crater of sand fifty feet into the air, Harper’s physical body rocketed forward.
She tore across the desert floor at three times the speed of sound with a trailing jet of black sand screaming behind her like the tail of a falling comet, heading directly toward the capital city.
’NO!’ Harper wailed, her spiritual form being dragged helplessly through the air in the physical body’s wake, tethered by an unbreakable glowing silver thread of soul-binding.
"Stop it! Please, stop!" Harper begged, rushing through the sky beside her own sprinting body. "There are millions of people in Iunu! My sister... Penelope is in the north! Silas is—"
"Quiet."
Nitocris didn’t stop running.
Her green eyes remained fixed on the horizon, but her voice carried an edge of cold sharp annoyance that made Harper’s spirit seize.

"I have an ancient tale to tell you, scabbard," Nitocris said, her tone level as she bounded over a three-hundred-foot sand dune with an effortless gravity-defying leap. "A tale of how this wretched nation was forged in betrayal, and why every soul carrying the name of Al-Mansur must be erased from this world... You will listen to me so I can return back to normal and be ni—"

"I don’t care about your story!" Harper screamed, her terror finally boiling over into desperate hysterical defiance. "I don’t want to hear it! Give me back my body! Give it back, you sick, rotting bitch! GIVE IT BACK—"
SWOOSH!
Harper’s physical body abruptly stopped as she landed on the peak of a high razor-thin dune overlooking the distant outer suburbs of the capital.
Nitocris slowly lowered the black khopesh, turning Harper’s head toward the floating spirit.
The green fire in her eyes was completely still, radiating an emotionless void that was far more terrifying than any rage.

"You seem confused, Harper Whitmore," Nitocris spoke softly. "You seem to believe that your compliance is a matter of negotiation... You seem to believe that because I require your body, you possess leverage over me..."
Before Harper could even comprehend the words—
SHING-CRUNCH!
Nitocris’s right arm blurred and with a swift casual thrust, Nitocris drove Harper’s own bare left hand straight through Harper’s own physical chest.
SPLAT-TEAR!
The fingers, coated in sharp black sand, tore through the charcoal suit, punched clean through the sternum, shattered four ribs, and closed tightly around Harper’s physical heart.
With a sharp wet rip, Nitocris crushed the heart into bloody pulp right inside the thoracic cavity as Harper’s spiritual form froze.
She didn’t feel physical pain since her spirit possessed no nervous system, no flesh to bleed and no lungs to choke on air.

Yet, watching her own hand buried inside her own shattered chest, seeing the bright blood fountain outward, drenching her white silk blouse and dripping onto the golden sand below, a wave of paralyzing existential horror seized Harper’s soul.
Her mind fractured and the reality of her own physical death stared her dead in the face.
"You see?" Nitocris murmured, her voice smooth and unbothered by the gaping bloody hole in her chest.

chapters.title: Chapter 603: A Tale Of Betrayal [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She turned her green eyes toward Harper’s trembling ghostly form with a cruel mocking smile playing on her lips.

"I can sever this connection in a single second," Nitocris said, her tone dropping into a terrifying intimate whisper. "I can step out of this vessel right now, return control of this shattered meat to your spirit, and watch you tumble back into this flesh just in time to feel your lungs fill with your own blood... I will watch you die in agony on this burning sand, and then I will simply claim another vessel from the millions walking the streets of Iunu..."
Nitocris leaned Harper’s bloody face closer to the weeping spirit.

"So I ask you, little mortal, do you wish to die right now? Or do you wish to remain quiet, keep your fragile little soul intact, and pray that your pathetic little prince arrives before I finish burning this continent to ash?"
Harper couldn’t speak.
She hovered in the air with her spiritual form shaking so violently that her outline blurred and tears of pure terror pouring silently from her eyes.
She slowly shook her head, clutching her hands against her mouth that was completely stripped of every scrap of defiance.
Nitocris let out a soft satisfied hum.
VUUUUUM!
A radiant wave of dense black sand surged through Harper’s thoracic cavity.
CRACK-CLICK-SNAP!
In the blink of an eye, the shattered ribs knitted together with rapid sickening clicks.

Fresh cardiac tissue braided itself back into existence like living thread... the severed arteries reconnected, the skin sealed over without a single scar and the blood coating the white blouse dried and flaked away into dust with a soft clean pop.
THUMP-THUMP. THUMP-THUMP!
Harper’s physical heart resumed its steady beat as Nitocris casually wiped her bloody fingers against her trousers, turning her gaze back toward the gleaming white walls of Iunu.

"Like I was saying..." Nitocris began smoothly with her voice echoing across the desert dunes like the tolling of a funeral bell as she began moving once again. "...I have an ancient tale to tell. Listen closely, Harper. It begins with the woman whose bones are buried beneath that city..."
The golden expanse of the Great Dunes blurred into streaks of blinding ochre and white heat beneath Harper’s physical boots.
FWOOOOOOSH!

The displacement of air flattened the crests of three-hundred-foot dunes into glassy trenches, sending plumes of pressurized silt screaming across the desert like artillery shells but Nitocris didn’t tire.
’She’s using my body better than me... Why...?’
Floating a pace behind her own shoulder, Harper’s translucent soul trailed along like a kite bound to an iron mast.
The glowing silver tether connecting her astral sternum to the base of her physical neck hummed with sickening resonance, dragging her through the blistering slipstream.
’I’m still a passenger in my own skin,’ Harper wept in the silent suffocating privacy of her mind.
Every time her physical feet touched the earth, she could feel the phantom vibration, not as pain, but as an obscene violation of ownership.
Nitocris tilted Harper’s chin upward, her green-lit pupils narrowing against the blinding horizon, and spoke.
Her words echoed directly within the marrow of the skull, vibrating through Harper’s ethereal ears with the heavy intimate gravity of stone grinding against stone.

"Once upon a time..." Nitocris began, her tone carrying a strange hollow melancholy that sounded jarringly human coming from lips that had just feasted on the slaughter of a fleet. "I was revered as a great hero."
She took a massive bounding stride, clearing a jagged outcropping of sun-baked shale by forty yards before hitting the sand with a soundless weightless glide.

"You modern children speak of the Sovereign Realm as though it were a grand colosseum," the entity mused with Harper’s physical fingers adjusting their grip on the black-hilted khopesh. "A place where nobles flaunt their bloodlines, where merchants barter for spirit cards, and where lords play at war under the amused gaze of the Nine Powers... You have forgotten the beginning... When the first rifts tore through reality during the Apocalypse, there were no cities of marble and there were no World Council decrees... The Earth wasn’t merely bordering the Sovereign Realm, it was being violently consumed by it."
Harper’s translucent form flickered in the wind.

She wanted to cover her ears and she wanted to scream at the monster to stop talking but the terror from earlier, the memory of watching her own hand punch through her ribs and rip her living heart to pieces, kept her tongue locked in paralyzed submission.

"The sky turned the color of bruised copper," Nitocris continued, leaping over a dried riverbed of cracked clay. "Monstrosities crawled out of the tears, things that didn’t possess flesh, things that fed upon the collective sanity of entire settlements... Most of the chosen ones, those who felt the initial stirrings of an Awakened core, panicked as they fled directly into the Sovereign Realm, throwing themselves into the foreign territories, desperate to hide behind the system’s defensive shields but I refused."
Harper’s physical lips curved into a bitter nostalgic sneer.

"I was the First Per-aa of the Khemet Dominion. The First Pharaoh-President... What kind of ruler abandons her people to be digested in the dark while she cowers in an unformed citadel? I didn’t descend into the realm. Instead, I anchored my soul directly to the bedrock of this desert and with nothing more than the unrefined fire of a freshly awakened core and this very blade, I slaughtered them."
SH-SH-SH-SH-SH!
A low tremor rippled through the dunes beneath their path, as if the desert itself remembered the carnage.

"One million," Nitocris whispered, Harper’s voice dropping into a tone that made Harper’s spirit tremble. "One million nightmares carved from the dunes without ever properly ascending as a lord... I fought until the sand turned into a knee-deep swamp of black bile... I fought so that mothers could sleep with their children in their arms, so that families could share bread without waiting for the sky to fall... And when the others, the cowards who had fled into the Sovereign Realm, finally returned with their granted system powers and their shiny territorial titles, they found an empire already waiting for them as together, we drove the last of the abyssal rot beyond our borders..."
Nitocris slowed her stride with her bare feet carving a smooth decelerating arc through the sand as they reached the crest of a colossal ridge.
She stood motionless as the hot desert breeze whipped her long vibrant purple hair around her face.
Harper looked through her physical eyes.
In the vast distance, rising out of the shimmering heat mirage, the colossal white perimeter of Iunu stretched from east to west.

It wasn’t simply a city at all... it was an artificial mountain range of polished limestone, white titanium, and solar-jade barriers, spanning so wide across the horizon that even from this elevated vantage point, the eye could find no boundary.
"It’s much larger than it used to be," Nitocris observed softly, her green pupils contracting as she studied the monolithic skyline. "And yet, nothing has truly changed..."
She let out a dry rattling sigh that sounded like sand pouring through a sieve.

"Do you know how I fell, scabbard?" Nitocris asked, not waiting for an answer. "It wasn’t a beast from the rift... It was an expedition into the corners of this desert to eliminate a Primordial Abomination, a creature whose very breath withered the water aquifers of the southern basin and my entire Squad was eradicated. Every loyal knight, every sworn commander, shredded to bone. In the end, only two souls stood over the beast’s severed skull. Myself... and my older sister."
The air around Harper’s physical body abruptly froze.
The temperature plummeted as frost crystals began spider-webbing across the sand grains beneath her heels.

"Her name was Nefertari Al-Mansur," Nitocris spoke, each syllable laced with ancient calcified hatred. "She had failed the divine trials of the First Rift... The core within her chest was flawed, weak, unable to process the pure power of the crown... She had watched from the shadows as the people chanted my name, as the armies knelt before my khopesh and there, in the quiet blood-soaked dark of that cavern, while I was broken, bleeding from fourteen shattered ribs and paralyzed from the beast’s venom, she carried me."
Nitocris raised Harper’s physical hand, looking at the calloused palm.

"She carried me on her back," Nitocris said, her voice dropping into a mocking poisonous imitation of gentle comfort. "She whispered that we were going home and she whispered that the nightmare was over as well. However, she stopped before an open unstable portal leading into the deepest unmapped abyss of the Sovereign Realm... She looked into my dying eyes, told me how utterly sick she was of living in my shadow, and pushed me through."
Harper’s translucent jaw dropped.
Despite the suffocating terror gripping her soul, the horror of the betrayal struck her like a physical blow.

"She took my khopesh from my paralyzed fingers," Nitocris continued coldly, tapping the dark blade against her thigh. "The very weapon you bought at that frivolous little auction as she returned to the surface alone, probably weeping false tears of grief, claimed I had perished saving her, and crowned herself the second ruler of Khemet but she was a fool... She didn’t understand the true nature of the steel she held... from what I can see."
Harper’s physical face turned slightly, her green eyes locking dead onto Harper’s hovering astral form.

"I knew what she was," Nitocris whispered. "I had seen the rot in her eyes for years so before we ever marched into that trench, I severed a sliver of my own soul and wove it into the core of this khopesh. My true body, the original vessel, was swallowed by the endless void of the Sovereign Realm but this fragment, I remained asleep within this blade, century after century, passing through the hands of ungrateful heirs, waiting for the day the seal would crack."
"You’re... a fragment?" Harper finally found her voice with the words coming out as a reedy trembling gasp from her spiritual lips.

"I am the wrath she left behind," Nitocris affirmed simply. "I have inherited some of the memories of what my true body suffered on the other side, enough to know that the woman who pushed me down must pay..."
Nitocris paused, taking a slow deep breath of the hot desert air.
The white towers of Iunu gleamed in the distance, bathed in the midday sun.

"My goal is remarkably simple, Harper Whitmore," Nitocris said, carrying only the certainty of an executioner reading an edict. "I am going to butcher every single soul that carries Nefertari’s blood... Whether it’s an old woman withering in a silk bed, or a suckling infant in a golden cradle. I will end the royal bloodline of Khemet down to the final drop."
Harper’s astral form shuddered.
"You... you can’t... an infant? That’s madness! That’s—"
Before Harper could finish, Harper’s physical body did something unexpected.
Nitocris lowered her arms as she bent her waist, Harper’s head dipping forward in a deep respectful bow toward Harper’s floating soul.

"I apologize, Harper," Nitocris said softly, her green eyes softening by an almost imperceptible fraction. "Truly... During the time we spent speaking in the quiet of your room, I came to appreciate your spirit... You possess ambition, yet you carry an earnest heart so under different stars, we might have been genuine friends and I know that what I am about to do using your flesh is an unspeakable, monstrous thing. But I give you my sacred unbreakable word as the First Per-aa... the moment the last Al-Mansur stops breathing, I will return your body to you intact."
Harper blinked, completely stunned by the sudden eerie shift in demeanor.
"You... you’ll give it back?"

"I have no desire to live in this modern cage," Nitocris replied, straightening her spine. "Once Nefertari’s blood is extinguished, my purpose is fulfilled. I will shatter this fragment of my soul. I will kill myself, and you will walk away as the sole master of your body once more... I have no interest in whatever madness my true self is cultivating in the dark."
Harper swallowed hard with her ethereal form drifting closer, driven by a desperate instinctual need for clarity.
"Your true self..." Harper asked, her voice shaking. "Back in the dunes, you said Ititius. Who is Ititius, really?"
Nitocris slowed her pace, walking leisurely toward the lower highway leading into the capital.

"Ititius was a god," Nitocris explained, her tone dripping with disdain. "Or rather, the name of a god our ancestors foolishly worshiped before the First Rift shattered the heavens. When the gates opened, we learned the truth... all manner of ancient terrifying entities exist across the cosmic strata, but ’Ititius’ was merely a myth, a bedtime story invented by desert nomads to explain the shifting sands so why my other half, the broken remnant of my true body in the Sovereign Realm, chose to drape herself in the shroud of a fictional deity, I cannot fathom but whatever she’s orchestrating, it cannot be good. It’s better that she and I remain severed..."
She paused at the edge of the asphalt highway, looking down at Harper’s clothes.
"Now," Nitocris murmured, Harper’s physical fingers weaving a subtle complex mudra. "We cannot enter the city looking like an unwashed nomad."
SH-SH-SH!
A delicate paper-thin layer of golden sand flowed out from Harper’s pores, coating her skin, her hair, and her clothes in an optical refraction spell.

Within seconds, the vibrant purple hair shifted to a common dusty chestnut brown; her sharp noble features softened into the plain, forgettable face of a mid-tier merchant’s clerk; and her blood-stained suit transformed into a modest traveling cloak of beige desert cotton.
"There," Nitocris smiled, Harper’s physical lips curling with genuine satisfaction. "This should ensure you aren’t implicated in the coming unpleasantness."

CRACK-CLICK-SNAP!

Harper’s physical heart resumed its steady beat as Nitocris casually wiped her bloody fingers against her trousers, turning her gaze back toward the gleaming white walls of Iunu.

The golden expanse of the Great Dunes blurred into streaks of blinding ochre and white heat beneath Harper’s physical boots.
FWOOOOOOSH!

"I was revered as a great hero."

"A place where nobles flaunt their bloodlines, where merchants barter for spirit cards, and where lords play at war under the amused gaze of the Nine Powers...
You have forgotten the beginning...
When the first rifts tore through reality during the Apocalypse, there were no cities of marble and there were no World Council decrees...
The Earth wasn’t merely bordering the Sovereign Realm, it was being violently consumed by it."
Harper’s translucent form flickered in the wind.

She wanted to cover her ears and she wanted to scream at the monster to stop talking but the terror from earlier, the memory of watching her own hand punch through her ribs and rip her living heart to pieces, kept her tongue locked in paralyzed submission.
"The sky turned the color of bruised copper," Nitocris continued, leaping over a dried riverbed of cracked clay.
"Monstrosities crawled out of the tears, things that didn’t possess flesh, things that fed upon the collective sanity of entire settlements...

Most of the chosen ones, those who felt the initial stirrings of an Awakened core, panicked as they fled directly into the Sovereign Realm, throwing themselves into the foreign territories, desperate to hide behind the system’s defensive shields but I refused."
Harper’s physical lips curved into a bitter nostalgic sneer.
"I was the First Per-aa of the Khemet Dominion.
The First Pharaoh-President...
What kind of ruler abandons her people to be digested in the dark while she cowers in an unformed citadel?
I didn’t descend into the realm.
Instead, I anchored my soul directly to the bedrock of this desert and with nothing more than the unrefined fire of a freshly awakened core and this very blade, I slaughtered them."
SH-SH-SH-SH-SH!
A low tremor rippled through the dunes beneath their path, as if the desert itself remembered the carnage.
"One million," Nitocris whispered, Harper’s voice dropping into a tone that made Harper’s spirit tremble.
"One million nightmares carved from the dunes without ever properly ascending as a lord...
I fought until the sand turned into a knee-deep swamp of black bile...
I fought so that mothers could sleep with their children in their arms, so that families could share bread without waiting for the sky to fall...

chapters.title: Chapter 604: Nitocris In The City [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Harper watched the illusion settle with her mind spinning.
’She’s actually protecting my identity? Why?’
Ten minutes later, they reached the grand southern checkpoint of Iunu.
The gates were titanic, two three-hundred-foot slabs of white alloy flanked by automated mana-cannons and manned by dozens of royal guards clad in gleaming gold plate.
A long line of hover-trucks, merchant caravans, and tourists snaked toward the scanners.
When it was their turn, a burly guard with a scarred chin leaned out of the terminal booth, tapping his scanner wand against the counter.
"Identification," the guard grunted, not even looking up. "Name, sector of origin, and purpose of entry."
Harper’s physical body abruptly stiffened.
Nitocris had faced armies of primordial horrors without flinching, but standing in front of a modern turnstile, she looked completely lost.
’Wait, where did the girl keep the little rectangular glass tile...?’ Nitocris’s thoughts echoed into Harper’s mind like a grandmother trying to operate a high-velocity particle accelerator.

Harper’s physical hands began patting frantically across her cloak, diving into her pockets, pulling out a lip balm, a half-empty packet of mints, a hair clip, and a receipt for dry cleaning as her face began flushing bright red with uncoordinated embarrassment.

’I am so sorry, Harper!’ Nitocris apologized frantically in their shared consciousness, her dignity entirely evaporating into panicked fluster. ’Which pocket?! Why does mortal clothing possess six different hidden pouches?! Is it the left one?! Oh gods, he is looking at me!’
The guard slowly raised his head with his brow furrowing as he watched this plain-looking girl clumsily juggle three coins, a receipt, and an empty wrapper.
Floating beside them, Harper slapped her ethereal hands over her face, groaning in pure secondhand embarrassment.
’Stop, please, just stop...’ Harper whimpered mentally. ’Inner left breast pocket... Inside the leather card-sleeve and tap it flat against the blue glass, don’t shove it into his face.’
Why was she helping the woman that ripped out her heart... Harper really didn’t know. Was she this forgiving, what the hell was wrong with her?
’Ah! Bless you, scabbard!’
Nitocris deftly reached into the inner lining, pulled out the sleek silver ID card, and carefully tapped it against the reader.
BEEP!
[Entry Approved: Whitmore Commercial Logistics — Priority Class B.]
The guard sighed, handing the card back.
"Move along, miss. Don’t block the lane."
"M-May the sun shine favorably upon your household, honorable gatekeeper!" Nitocris blurted out with an awkward formal curtsy that belonged in a court from eight hundred years ago.
The guard stared at her as if she had grown a second head. "Yeah, yeah. Welcome to Iunu. Keep walking, weirdo..."
Nitocris scurried past the turnstile with Harper’s physical boots practically kicking up dust as she rushed into the bustling lower plaza of the capital.
Once they cleared the security perimeter, Nitocris leaned Harper’s back against a stone pillar, letting out an enormous shuddering sigh of pure relief.
’That was horrifying,’ Nitocris confided to Harper, wiping cold sweat from her brow. ’Modern bureaucracy is infinitely more terrifying than the rift-beasts of the first era...’
Harper’s astral spirit simply stared at her, completely numb.
’Is this the same woman as before...?’
It made her very confused. How did that terrifying woman turn into a frightened schoolgirl at a toll booth...?
However, the moment Nitocris turned around to face the main thoroughfare, her eyes widened into massive sparkling emerald saucers.
The lower market of Iunu was an explosion of her senses.

Towering holographic banners floated between white limestone arches, automated vendor carts rolled along magnetic tracks and the air was also thick with the mouth-watering aromas of roasting spiced lamb, caramelized figs, fried honey pastries, and sweet iced pomegranate nectar.
Hundreds of tourists and citizens in colorful silk tunics laughed, bargained, and strolled through the open-air pavilions.

"By the three suns..." Nitocris breathed, Harper’s physical throat audibly swallowing as her eyes darted from one stall to the next. "What is that marvelous contraption? And that smell, is that roasted fowl glazed in date syrup? Harper, look at that frozen white cream in those tiny paper bowls!"
Nitocris turned Harper’s head toward the floating spirit with her expression filled with a child-like, pleading eagerness that looked absurd on a conqueror.

"Harper..." Nitocris whispered softly. "I am going to die very soon. Within hours, my existence will fade into nothingness so before I shatter this soul, may I please try some of these wonderful things? Could I, could I use some of your money?"
Harper’s translucent form remained dead quiet.
She stared at the woman wearing her body.
’Why are you asking me like that? You’re holding a sword that can cleave a fortress... You could just force my hands to swipe the card so why ask for my permission?’
Seeing Harper’s heavy conflicted silence, Nitocris quickly lowered her eyes with an embarrassed flush dusting her cheeks.

"I... I understand," Nitocris murmured apologetically. "It was presumptuous of me... You don’t need to share your wealth so tell you what, once I breach the palace and slaughter Nefertari’s heirs, I will open the royal treasury for you. I will dump mountain-loads of pure, refined gold and ancient spirit gems into your Lord Inventory! You’ll be the wealthiest merchant in the entire world so, just two sweet pastries for now? Please?"
Harper let out an exhausted defeated breath that lacked physical air.
’Go to the bakery stall on the corner,’ Harper transmitted dryly. ’Buy the almond honey cakes and get the pistachio ice cream from the brass cart beside it. The card’s pin is four-eight-two-one.’
"You are an angel of mercy, Harper Whitmore!"

Within five minutes, Nitocris was strolling down the sidewalk with Harper’s physical cheeks stuffed full of sticky honey pastry, holding a double-scoop cone of bright green pistachio ice cream in her left hand.
LICK!

"Mmmph!" Nitocris’s eyes practically rolled back in sheer, unadulterated ecstasy. "Cold! It’s sweet, creamy, and freezing cold... How do they capture winter in a bowl during the height of the summer heat?! This era is truly miraculous!"
After devouring the treats with astonishing speed, Nitocris walked to the curb, looking at the stream of sleek hovering yellow vehicles gliding past.
’Now, how does one summon these mechanical chariots?’ Nitocris wondered, tilting her head.

She stepped right into the road, planted her boots wide, and aggressively raised both arms over her head, waving her hands in frantic circular motions as if she were signaling a naval fleet in the middle of a typhoon.
SCREEEEEECH!
A yellow hover-cab swerved violently with its repulsor coils hissing as it slammed to a halt barely three inches from Harper’s knees.
The driver, a middle-aged Khemet man with a thick black mustache and a floral print shirt, rolled down his window, sticking his head out with a furious scowl.
"Are you trying to commit suicide, lady?!" the driver yelled. "What kind of lunatic jumps into active traffic waving her arms like a windmill?!"
Nitocris didn’t flinch.
She simply offered him a bright and completely shameless smile, opening the rear door and sliding onto the faux-leather seat.
"Greetings, master of the chariot!" Nitocris announced regally. "Take me to the Grand Temple-Keep of Hathor-Sekhmet, situated at the apex of the High Dune!"
The driver stared at her through the rearview mirror, his mustache twitching in confusion.
"The... the what now?" the driver blinked. "The Grand Temple-Keep? Lady, what history book did you crawl out of? You mean the Royal Citadel of the Pharaoh-President?"
Nitocris blinked Harper’s eyes. "Is that what they call it now?"
The driver let out a booming laugh, shaking his head as he shifted the hover-drive into gear with the cab smoothly gliding into the flow of traffic.

"Man, you historical reenactment nerds are getting wilder every year," the driver chuckled. "First it was the kids dressing up in linen sheets for the Sun Festival, now you’re talking like an ancient inscription but yeah, I can take you to the inner gate tourist drop-off... Ain’t nobody getting past the second perimeter unless you’ve got an Al-Mansur seal tattooed on your forehead."
As the cab glided through the sprawling urban corridors, Nitocris looked out the tinted window with her green eyes drinking in the sights.
"Tell me, chariot master," Nitocris asked casually. "How fares the realm in this modern age? Is Khemet truly unified under the sun?"
The driver scoffed, tapping his fingers against the steering yoke.

"Unified? On paper, sure but that’s just propaganda for the World Council cameras... Ever since the First Era, way back after the death of the legendary First Per-aa, Nitocris, this entire nation’s been a mess. You know your history, right? Her older sister, Queen Nefertari, took the throne, and her reign was a disaster."
Nitocris’s posture subtly stiffened, her fingers digging slightly into the leather seat cushion.
"A disaster? How so?"

"The woman was a paranoid tyrant," the driver explained casually, navigating a busy skyway interchange. "She spent her entire rule purging Nitocris’s loyal generals, terrified they’d find out whatever shady shit she pulled in the rifts... When she died, the succession broke down immediately as the country fractured into four warring sectors... North Khemet, South Khemet, East, and West. Even today, centuries after the Al-Mansur dynasty patched it back together, the discrimination is disgusting."
He gestured out the window toward a sprawling crowded district of drab concrete housing blocks far below the skyway.

"Look down there. That’s the Southern Sector migrants... The High Court in Iunu hoards all the solar-quartz and water rights for the Northern aristocrats. If you’re from the South or the West, you’re treated like third-class dirt. You pay double taxes, you get no military protection from the rift-creepers, and you’re barred from holding high administrative office... They call us ’one nation under the Sun-Crown,’ but it’s just one ruling family sitting on the necks of millions."
CRUNCH!
A cracking sound echoed from the rear seat as Nitocris was staring down at her own lap.
Harper’s physical right fist was clenched so hard that the knuckles were bloodless, tiny fissures of black glassy energy leaking through the pores of her skin.
Beneath the beige cotton cloak, the ancient warrior’s heart was screaming with agonizing fury.

’I bled a million monsters into the dirt so that all the people of Khemet could walk as equals,’ Nitocris wept silently, her soul burning with unmitigated wrath. ’I built this empire for the humble, for the farmers, for the mothers! And that wretched jealous snake turned my paradise into a slaughterhouse!’
"Hey, we’re approaching the inner threshold," the driver announced, unaware of the apocalyptic demon sitting behind him.
The cab pulled up to a massive shimmering gold energy barrier that divided the commercial sprawl from the core.
Armed sentries in ceremonial eagle-visored helms stood beside automated toll terminals.
BEEP!

"That’ll be ten thousand Spirit Credits just to cross the gate, miss," the driver said, grimacing slightly. "The inner district is exclusive to high-tier nobility and verified luxury tourists... Even breathing the filtered air near the Pharaoh’s palace has a price tag."
Nitocris reached into Harper’s pocket, seamlessly tapping the credit card against the cab’s terminal.
"Paid," Nitocris said softly, her voice remarkably calm as the golden barrier parted, and the cab glided into the inner sanctuary.
Here, the air was entirely different.
It was cool, perfumed with imported jasmine and lotus oils, filtered by massive atmospheric terra-scrubbers.

Pristine gardens of luminescent blue flora lined wide, paved avenues of white quartz and in the center of the district, towering majestically against the burning sun, rose the White Citadel of Iunu, a colossal stepped pyramid of polished white titanium and gold, radiating the sovereign might of House Al-Mansur.
The cab pulled over at a designated tourist observation turnout three hundred yards from the citadel’s outer moat.
"Here you go, miss," the driver smiled, unlocking the doors. "Take lots of pictures, but don’t wander off the paved path. The palace guards don’t have a sense of humor about trespassers..."
Nitocris stepped out of the cab with her clothes fluttering in the gentle breeze as she paused, looking back through the open window with her expression genuinely warm.
"Thank you, chariot master," Nitocris said softly. "Drive far away from this district today. Go home to your family, take your children into your arms, and do not look back at the palace."
The driver blinked, confused by the strange farewell. "Uh, sure thing, lady. Take care of yourself..."
WHOOSH!
The yellow hover-cab turned around, its thrusters humming as it sped back toward the outer gates.
Nitocris stood alone on the manicured grass of the turnout, looking up at the towering white pyramid.
Her jaw was set and her green eyes blazed with cold resolution.

"Khemet was once a sanctuary for all living souls," Nitocris whispered, her voice trembling with righteous fury. "The land belongs to the people, not to the parasites who wear my sister’s face... As much as I wish I could stay and rebuild what was broken, I have made a sacred promise... I will end the bloodline, and then I will leave this world in peace..."
STEP! CLANK!
"Halt! Identify yourself!"
A palace sentinel, clad in full-body solar-quartz plate armor, holding an eight-foot kinetic halberd, stepped out from a decorative marble pavilion twenty paces away.
His visor lowered with his weapon locking onto Harper’s chest.
"This is restricted grounds! Civilian presence is forbidden beyond the marker! Hands where I can see them—"
SWOOSH!
Nitocris didn’t reach for a blade as her physical body simply collapsed inward instead.
Before the guard’s stunned dilated eyes, the plain-looking girl violently dissolved into a swirling, vortex-like stream of dense, lightless pitch-black sand.
WHOOOOOOSH!
The black sand didn’t strike the guard.
It flowed along the manicured lawn like an oily serpent, diving straight through the brass intake grates of a massive ventilation turbine set into the garden bedrock.
The guard stumbled back, his boots nearly slipping on the grass, his breath catching in his throat as cold sweat drenched his padded gambeson.
"Black... sand...?" the man stammered, his hands shaking violently against the shaft of his halberd. "What was that?! Was that the ancient omen...?"

sentences.text: Harper watched the illusion settle with her mind spinning.
’She’s actually protecting my identity?
Why?’

The gates were titanic, two three-hundred-foot slabs of white alloy flanked by automated mana-cannons and manned by dozens of royal guards clad in gleaming gold plate.
A long line of hover-trucks, merchant caravans, and tourists snaked toward the scanners.
When it was their turn, a burly guard with a scarred chin leaned out of the terminal booth, tapping his scanner wand against the counter.
"Identification," the guard grunted, not even looking up.
"Name, sector of origin, and purpose of entry."
Harper’s physical body abruptly stiffened.

’Wait, where did the girl keep the little rectangular glass tile...?’ Nitocris’s thoughts echoed into Harper’s mind like a grandmother trying to operate a high-velocity particle accelerator.

Harper’s physical hands began patting frantically across her cloak, diving into her pockets, pulling out a lip balm, a half-empty packet of mints, a hair clip, and a receipt for dry cleaning as her face began flushing bright red with uncoordinated embarrassment.
’I am so sorry, Harper!’ Nitocris apologized frantically in their shared consciousness, her dignity entirely evaporating into panicked fluster. ’Which pocket?!
Why does mortal clothing possess six different hidden pouches?!
Is it the left one?!
Oh gods, he is looking at me!’
The guard slowly raised his head with his brow furrowing as he watched this plain-looking girl clumsily juggle three coins, a receipt, and an empty wrapper.
Floating beside them, Harper slapped her ethereal hands over her face, groaning in pure secondhand embarrassment.
’Stop, please, just stop...’ Harper whimpered mentally. ’Inner left breast pocket...
Inside the leather card-sleeve and tap it flat against the blue glass, don’t shove it into his face.’
Why was she helping the woman that ripped out her heart...
Harper really didn’t know.
Was she this forgiving, what the hell was wrong with her?
’Ah!
Bless you, scabbard!’
Nitocris deftly reached into the inner lining, pulled out the sleek silver ID card, and carefully tapped it against the reader.
BEEP!
[Entry Approved: Whitmore Commercial Logistics — Priority Class B.]
The guard sighed, handing the card back.
"Move along, miss.
Don’t block the lane."
"M-May the sun shine favorably upon your household, honorable gatekeeper!" Nitocris blurted out with an awkward formal curtsy that belonged in a court from eight hundred years ago.
The guard stared at her as if she had grown a second head.
"Yeah, yeah.
Welcome to Iunu.
Keep walking, weirdo..."
Nitocris scurried past the turnstile with Harper’s physical boots practically kicking up dust as she rushed into the bustling lower plaza of the capital.
Once they cleared the security perimeter, Nitocris leaned Harper’s back against a stone pillar, letting out an enormous shuddering sigh of pure relief.
’That was horrifying,’ Nitocris confided to Harper, wiping cold sweat from her brow. ’Modern bureaucracy is infinitely more terrifying than the rift-beasts of the first era...’

Nitocris turned Harper’s head toward the floating spirit with her expression filled with a child-like, pleading eagerness that looked absurd on a conqueror.

Could I, could I use some of your money?"
Harper’s translucent form remained dead quiet.
She stared at the woman wearing her body.

You’re holding a sword that can cleave a fortress...
You could just force my hands to swipe the card so why ask for my permission?’
Seeing Harper’s heavy conflicted silence, Nitocris quickly lowered her eyes with an embarrassed flush dusting her cheeks.
I understand," Nitocris murmured apologetically.

You’ll be the wealthiest merchant in the entire world so, just two sweet pastries for now?
Please?"
Harper let out an exhausted defeated breath that lacked physical air.
’Go to the bakery stall on the corner,’ Harper transmitted dryly. ’Buy the almond honey cakes and get the pistachio ice cream from the brass cart beside it.
The card’s pin is four-eight-two-one.’
"You are an angel of mercy, Harper Whitmore!"

Within five minutes, Nitocris was strolling down the sidewalk with Harper’s physical cheeks stuffed full of sticky honey pastry, holding a double-scoop cone of bright green pistachio ice cream in her left hand.
LICK!
"Mmmph!" Nitocris’s eyes practically rolled back in sheer, unadulterated ecstasy.
"Cold!
It’s sweet, creamy, and freezing cold...
How do they capture winter in a bowl during the height of the summer heat?!
This era is truly miraculous!"
After devouring the treats with astonishing speed, Nitocris walked to the curb, looking at the stream of sleek hovering yellow vehicles gliding past.
’Now, how does one summon these mechanical chariots?’ Nitocris wondered, tilting her head.

She stepped right into the road, planted her boots wide, and aggressively raised both arms over her head, waving her hands in frantic circular motions as if she were signaling a naval fleet in the middle of a typhoon.
SCREEEEEECH!
A yellow hover-cab swerved violently with its repulsor coils hissing as it slammed to a halt barely three inches from Harper’s knees.
The driver, a middle-aged Khemet man with a thick black mustache and a floral print shirt, rolled down his window, sticking his head out with a furious scowl.
"Are you trying to commit suicide, lady?!" the driver yelled.
"What kind of lunatic jumps into active traffic waving her arms like a windmill?!"
Nitocris didn’t flinch.
She simply offered him a bright and completely shameless smile, opening the rear door and sliding onto the faux-leather seat.
"Greetings, master of the chariot!" Nitocris announced regally.
"Take me to the Grand Temple-Keep of Hathor-Sekhmet, situated at the apex of the High Dune!"
The driver stared at her through the rearview mirror, his mustache twitching in confusion.
"The... the what now?" the driver blinked.
"The Grand Temple-Keep?
Lady, what history book did you crawl out of?
You mean the Royal Citadel of the Pharaoh-President?"
Nitocris blinked Harper’s eyes.
"Is that what they call it now?"
The driver let out a booming laugh, shaking his head as he shifted the hover-drive into gear with the cab smoothly gliding into the flow of traffic.
"Man, you historical reenactment nerds are getting wilder every year," the driver chuckled.

Ain’t nobody getting past the second perimeter unless you’ve got an Al-Mansur seal tattooed on your forehead."
As the cab glided through the sprawling urban corridors, Nitocris looked out the tinted window with her green eyes drinking in the sights.

Is Khemet truly unified under the sun?"
The driver scoffed, tapping his fingers against the steering yoke.

On paper, sure but that’s just propaganda for the World Council cameras...
Ever since the First Era, way back after the death of the legendary First Per-aa, Nitocris, this entire nation’s been a mess.
You know your history, right?
Her older sister, Queen Nefertari, took the throne, and her reign was a disaster."
Nitocris’s posture subtly stiffened, her fingers digging slightly into the leather seat cushion.

How so?"
"The woman was a paranoid tyrant," the driver explained casually, navigating a busy skyway interchange.

When she died, the succession broke down immediately as the country fractured into four warring sectors...
North Khemet, South Khemet, East, and West.
Even today, centuries after the Al-Mansur dynasty patched it back together, the discrimination is disgusting."
