chapters.title: Chapter 605: Morally Grey...
paragraphs: He stood frozen in the sunlight, terrified to even sound the alarm as his mind was paralyzed by the ancient superstitions that every soldier in Khemet was taught from childhood.
Deep within the infrastructure of the White Citadel, the world was a labyrinth of humming machinery, pressurized coolant pipes, and reinforced steel conduits.
SH-SH-SH-SH-SH!
The stream of black sand moved through the primary ventilation duct at high speeds.
Inside the swirling mass, Harper’s astral spirit drifted along, completely unharmed by the friction.
Her mind was a chaotic bleeding battlefield of contradictory emotions.
’If she keeps acting like this, how am I supposed to hate her with all my heart?’ Harper thought, her translucent hands curling against her chest.
She did hate her...

She had spent the last two hours terrified out of her mind as Nitocris had played her like an instrument, manipulating Harper’s desire to grow stronger, whispering sweet mentorship into her ear for all that time... all to steal her body and turn her into an executioner’s scabbard.

And yet, hearing the woman’s tragic history, watching her clumsy child-like wonder over a bowl of ice cream, seeing her bow with genuine sincere remorse, and witnessing her raw grief over the suffering of the common people, Harper couldn’t muster the pure blind hatred she wanted to feel.
Nitocris wasn’t an evil soulless demon who wanted to slaughter the world for fun.
She was a betrayed founder whose entire legacy had been defiled by her own sister, returning from the grave to balance the board... If it could be put that way.

’Why couldn’t she just be an evil villain?’ Harper lamented in the dark. ’If she were just a monster, I could hate her with every fiber of my being but she understands pain and she understands loyalty. Why couldn’t she just talk to me?! Why did she have to steal my body like a thief in the night?!’
As if hearing the desperate turmoil in Harper’s thoughts, Nitocris’s voice echoed gently through the flowing black grains.

"I promised to make you vastly stronger, Harper," Nitocris spoke, her tone steady as the sand surged through a narrow junction. "And a Per-aa never breaks her word... When I sever this soul fragment and die, I will not be able to guide your training directly. Therefore, as we move through this citadel, I am engraving the complete combat formulas of the First Dominion directly into the spiritual architecture of your soul."
Harper blinked, feeling a sudden warm harmonic pulse thrumming along the silver tether connecting them.

"The sand magic I wield now, it doesn’t belong solely to me anymore," Nitocris explained. "Your body has adapted to it and the black sand is yours to command... Watch closely, scabbard... Watch how I breathe... Watch how I fold the earth as this is the true power of Khemet."
Harper hovered in the dark with her heart hitching as a strange chilling question crossed her mind.

’Wait,’ Harper thought. ’Earlier, back on the ridge, she said I had Khemet blood in my veins that was distant, but real... If she wants to slaughter every single descendant of Nefertari, why doesn’t she want to kill me too?’
Was it because Harper was an innocent bystander? Or was it because, deep down beneath the ancient wrath, Nitocris carried a crushing weight of guilt?
WHOOSH!

The stream of black sand suddenly executed a sharp ninety-degree banking turn, narrowly avoiding a massive high-pressure industrial water exhaust pipe that was flushing boiling coolant toward the cooling towers.
Nitocris navigated the sprawling multi-tiered duct system with astonishing spatial awareness.

Even though she had never seen the modern architectural schematics of this modernized citadel, her sensory perception swept through the concrete walls, mapping every elevator shaft, every security checkpoint, and every structural load-bearing pillar with flawless precision.
HUMMMMM!
Suddenly, an obstacle appeared ahead.

Blocking the primary ventilation junction was a mana-barrier, a dense vibrating mesh of woven solar runes and spatial distortion fields designed to incinerate any rogue elemental or gaseous intrusion attempting to breach the palace interior but Nitocris didn’t slow down.
’Watch, Harper,’ Nitocris commanded.
Instead of trying to smash through the barrier with brute force, Nitocris subtly adjusted the internal mana frequency flowing through Harper’s cellular structure.
She twisted the flow into an inverted counter-clockwise spiral, perfectly mirroring the harmonic frequency of the solar barrier...
’Huh?!’
SHUUUU!
The black sand didn’t collide with the glowing runes.

It slipped effortlessly between the microscopic spatial gaps of the energy like water passing through a loose fishing net, completely bypassing the automated alarms without triggering a single warning light.
’Incredible...’ Harper marveled internally, despite herself.
The effortless mastery required to perform such a delicate calculation in a fraction of a second was beyond anything she had ever seen.
The ventilation duct began to slope steeply upward.
VUUUUUM!

The black sand surged up a vertical exhaust shaft, bursting through a decorative brass vent on the highest terrace of the White Citadel; however the black sand didn’t merely spill onto the ground after all that...
It shot sixty feet into the air, gracefully curving over a three-hundred-foot marble balustrade, and landed lightly upon the secluded elevated sun-terrace of the palace’s private domestic wing.
SWOOSH!
The black sand swirled together, condensing instantly into the physical form of Harper Whitmore.
Her beige cotton cloak dissolved, revealing the sleek charcoal suit beneath.
Her long vibrant purple hair thrashed in the gentle breeze with her hands resting easily at her sides and her green eyes blazing with a cold look.
’And suddenly she doesn’t want to hide my identity anymore...?’
Floating right behind her, Harper’s astral spirit gasped, taking in their surroundings.
The terrace was private, paved with polished rose-colored quartz, surrounded by hanging gardens of blooming night-lotus and gentle bubbling fountains of clear spring water.
In the center of the terrace, standing near a gilded drying rack of freshly laundered silk tunics, was a woman.
She was young, barely twenty years old, with soft delicate features, wearing a flowing loose-fitting gown of pure white linen.
Her belly was prominently swollen as she was heavily pregnant, carrying a child barely two months from birth.

Sitting on a low velvet cushion beside her, playing with a set of carved wooden toy chariots, was a little girl of five with her hair tied in golden ribbons, giggling softly as she rolled the wheels across the quartz tiles.
Before Harper’s sudden arrival broke the moment, the little girl looked up from her toys, tilting her small head at her mother with the guileless curiosity only a five-year-old could manage.

"Mama," the little girl piped up, still rolling one wooden wheel idly against her palm, "is it really alright that you go visit Grandpa’s chambers so late at night? You already have a whole new baby brother growing in your tummy... Does Grandpa know you’re going to have another one?"
Zahra’s cheeks flushed a deep mortified crimson.
She reached down quickly, smoothing a hand over her daughter’s hair with a soft, flustered laugh.
"Hush now, sweetling. That’s grown-up business. Go on, play with your chariots."
The little girl only shrugged and went right back to rolling her wheels across the tiles, humming a small, tuneless song to herself.
Standing five paces away, holding a ceremonial short-sword, was a personal royal guard wearing the white-and-gold livery of the domestic watch.
The pregnant woman paused, turning her head toward the sudden rustle of air with her gentle dark eyes widening as she saw Harper materialize on the terrace.
"Who... who are you?" the pregnant woman asked softly, her hand instinctively rising to shield her swollen belly. "How did you get up here? This is the private pavilion of—"
Nitocris didn’t ask for a name.

Her senses flared for a single microscopic second, locking onto the unmistakable inherited genetic frequency running through the woman’s veins, through the little girl’s heart, and through the unborn child in the womb...
’Nefertari.’
Behind that cold flare of certainty, something else flickered through the shared consciousness Nitocris and Harper now occupied.
’So the rumors that were whispered through the Inner zone hadn’t been idle gossip after all...’

Sound traveled much better underground and even on the streets, it was being talked about so she could hear... The old Pharaoh was sharing his dead son’s bed with his dead son’s wife, right beneath the same roof where his granddaughter slept.
Nitocris’s stomach turned at the thought with a fresh private layer of contempt for the rot her own bloodline had curdled into, separate from the sentence she had already come here to carry out.
SHING-CRACK!
There was no hesitation as Nitocris’s right arm blurred with terrifying, speed.
A massive razor-sharp spike of jet-black sand erupted from the terrace flagstones directly beneath the pregnant woman’s feet.
SPLAT-SHRRRRK!
The spike punched straight through her pelvis, tearing upward through her abdomen, impaling her clean through her chest and the little girl didn’t even have time to scream.
A secondary tendril of black sand whipped across the tiles, wrapping tightly around her tiny neck and torso.
CRACKLE!
Before the guard could even draw his short-sword from its scabbard, the horrific lightless calcification claimed them both.
The pregnant woman’s skin instantly turned to brittle oily black glass with her swollen belly freezing into solid dark crystal.
The little girl, her mouth open in a silent wail of terror, petrified into a tiny statue of black glass.
"No! No! No!" The royal guard let out a choked horrified gasp, lunging forward with his blade...
SNAP!
A third tendril whipped through the guard’s throat, turning his armor, flesh, and weapon into black glass within half a heartbeat.
SHATTER!
Nitocris flicked her wrist and a concussive shockwave of compressed wind slammed into the three statues.
CRASH-CRUNCH!

The pregnant woman, the unborn child, the five-year-old girl, and the royal guard violently shattered into millions of microscopic black glass shards that clattered uselessly across the rose-quartz terrace with their souls entirely devoured by the void-sand.
Harper’s astral form watched the butchery in horror.
"NOOOOO!" Harper’s spirit wailed, tears streaming down her ghostly face. "WHY?! SHE WAS PREGNANT! THAT WAS A BABY! YOU MONSTER! YOU SICK, TWISTED—"
Harper’s spiritual voice choked on its own grief.
Because in that exact second, Harper looked at her own physical face.
...Nitocris was standing perfectly still.
The green fire in Harper’s physical eyes remained bright, but across the left cheek, a microscopic involuntary muscle twitched violently.
The corner of Harper’s physical lips trembled, dipping downward in a silent agonized spasm of pure suffocating grief.
Nitocris didn’t look proud and she didn’t look triumphant as well...
She looked like a woman who had just swallowed a cup of molten lead...
WEEEEWOOOOOO!
An ear-splitting siren shattered the silence of the White Citadel as pillars of blinding red light shot from the palace spires into the afternoon sky, casting blood-red text across the terrace.
[CODE RED BREACH DETECTED! HIGH CITADEL DOMESTIC PAVILION! DEADLY FORCE AUTHORIZED!]
FWOOOOOOM!

The rose-quartz tiles beneath the terrace violently churned as from the solid stone, dozens, then hundreds, of high-ranking royal palace sentinels began to manifest, utilizing high-tier earth and solar-meld techniques.

Within five seconds, over three hundred elite guards surrounded the terrace, clad in heavy star-iron armor adorned with golden cobra crests with their hands wielding halberds, curved khopeshes, and heavy repeating mana-arbalests.
WHISTLE!
A sharp piercing sound cut through the air and with a subtle casual tilt of Harper’s neck, she swayed three inches to the left.
THWIP!
A six-foot-long armor-piercing bolt grazed the tips of her purple hair, slamming into the marble balustrade behind her with enough concussive force to blow a ten-foot crater into the stone.
SHING!
In Harper’s physical right hand, the First Khopesh of the Khemet Dominion materialized in a burst of black static lightning.
Nitocris stood in the center of the terrace, facing the three hundred elite guards... her green eyes sweeping across their ranks with cold dead authority.
"Clear the way," Nitocris spoke, Harper’s voice echoing through the courtyard with the crushing weight of a collapsing mountain.
From the front rank of the sentinels, three men stepped forward.

They were massive, over six and a half feet tall, their breastplates adorned with four golden sun-seals, the Imperial Guard Captains, seasoned Third Stage commanders who had held the borders of Khemet for decades.
The lead captain, a scarred man with a brutal square jaw and eyes burning with white-hot solar mana, pointed his broad curved executioner’s blade straight at Harper’s throat.

"Treasonous whore!" the Captain bellowed, his voice laced with incandescent rage. "You dare step into the sacred house of Al-Mansur?! You dare lay your filthy hands upon Lady Zahra, the favored consort of the late Crown Prince?!"
Off to the side, one of the younger sentinels, barely out of his teens, muttered something under his breath to the man beside him, too rattled by what he’d just witnessed to fully guard his tongue.
"Consort of the Crown Prince, my ass. Everyone below the third floor knew whose bed she’d really been warming since the funeral—"

"Silence in the ranks!" the Captain roared without even turning his head, his blade never wavering from Harper’s throat. "You slaughtered her, her daughter, and the seed in her womb... There is no grave deep enough to hold your severed limbs! Surrender your core, or we will flay the flesh from your bones and feed your intestines to the drakes!"
Nitocris looked at the three captains.

Then, she looked past them, looking into the eyes of the young soldiers holding the line, men with trembling grips, men with wives waiting in the lower districts... These were the same as the men whose families she had sworn to protect two thousand years ago.

"Part," Nitocris warned softly, her tone carrying a sorrowful gravity. "There is no victory for you here. I seek only the blood of Nefertari... If you step aside, you will live. Do you not have families? Do you not have children waiting to feel your embrace when your shift ends? Why throw your lives away for a family of parasites?"
"DIE, WITCH!"

sentences.text: He stood frozen in the sunlight, terrified to even sound the alarm as his mind was paralyzed by the ancient superstitions that every soldier in Khemet was taught from childhood.
Deep within the infrastructure of the White Citadel, the world was a labyrinth of humming machinery, pressurized coolant pipes, and reinforced steel conduits.
SH-SH-SH-SH-SH!
The stream of black sand moved through the primary ventilation duct at high speeds.
Inside the swirling mass, Harper’s astral spirit drifted along, completely unharmed by the friction.
Her mind was a chaotic bleeding battlefield of contradictory emotions.
’If she keeps acting like this, how am I supposed to hate her with all my heart?’ Harper thought, her translucent hands curling against her chest.
She did hate her...

She had spent the last two hours terrified out of her mind as Nitocris had played her like an instrument, manipulating Harper’s desire to grow stronger, whispering sweet mentorship into her ear for all that time... all to steal her body and turn her into an executioner’s scabbard.

And yet, hearing the woman’s tragic history, watching her clumsy child-like wonder over a bowl of ice cream, seeing her bow with genuine sincere remorse, and witnessing her raw grief over the suffering of the common people, Harper couldn’t muster the pure blind hatred she wanted to feel.
Nitocris wasn’t an evil soulless demon who wanted to slaughter the world for fun.
She was a betrayed founder whose entire legacy had been defiled by her own sister, returning from the grave to balance the board...
If it could be put that way.

’Why couldn’t she just be an evil villain?’ Harper lamented in the dark. ’If she were just a monster, I could hate her with every fiber of my being but she understands pain and she understands loyalty.
Why couldn’t she just talk to me?!
Why did she have to steal my body like a thief in the night?!’
As if hearing the desperate turmoil in Harper’s thoughts, Nitocris’s voice echoed gently through the flowing black grains.
"I promised to make you vastly stronger, Harper," Nitocris spoke, her tone steady as the sand surged through a narrow junction.
"And a Per-aa never breaks her word...
When I sever this soul fragment and die, I will not be able to guide your training directly.
Therefore, as we move through this citadel, I am engraving the complete combat formulas of the First Dominion directly into the spiritual architecture of your soul."
Harper blinked, feeling a sudden warm harmonic pulse thrumming along the silver tether connecting them.
"The sand magic I wield now, it doesn’t belong solely to me anymore," Nitocris explained.
"Your body has adapted to it and the black sand is yours to command...
Watch closely, scabbard...
Watch how I breathe...
Watch how I fold the earth as this is the true power of Khemet."
Harper hovered in the dark with her heart hitching as a strange chilling question crossed her mind.
’Wait,’ Harper thought. ’Earlier, back on the ridge, she said I had Khemet blood in my veins that was distant, but real...
If she wants to slaughter every single descendant of Nefertari, why doesn’t she want to kill me too?’
Was it because Harper was an innocent bystander?
Or was it because, deep down beneath the ancient wrath, Nitocris carried a crushing weight of guilt?
WHOOSH!

The stream of black sand suddenly executed a sharp ninety-degree banking turn, narrowly avoiding a massive high-pressure industrial water exhaust pipe that was flushing boiling coolant toward the cooling towers.
Nitocris navigated the sprawling multi-tiered duct system with astonishing spatial awareness.

Even though she had never seen the modern architectural schematics of this modernized citadel, her sensory perception swept through the concrete walls, mapping every elevator shaft, every security checkpoint, and every structural load-bearing pillar with flawless precision.
HUMMMMM!
Suddenly, an obstacle appeared ahead.

Blocking the primary ventilation junction was a mana-barrier, a dense vibrating mesh of woven solar runes and spatial distortion fields designed to incinerate any rogue elemental or gaseous intrusion attempting to breach the palace interior but Nitocris didn’t slow down.
’Watch, Harper,’ Nitocris commanded.
Instead of trying to smash through the barrier with brute force, Nitocris subtly adjusted the internal mana frequency flowing through Harper’s cellular structure.
She twisted the flow into an inverted counter-clockwise spiral, perfectly mirroring the harmonic frequency of the solar barrier...
’Huh?!’
SHUUUU!
The black sand didn’t collide with the glowing runes.

It slipped effortlessly between the microscopic spatial gaps of the energy like water passing through a loose fishing net, completely bypassing the automated alarms without triggering a single warning light.
’Incredible...’ Harper marveled internally, despite herself.
The effortless mastery required to perform such a delicate calculation in a fraction of a second was beyond anything she had ever seen.
The ventilation duct began to slope steeply upward.
VUUUUUM!

The black sand surged up a vertical exhaust shaft, bursting through a decorative brass vent on the highest terrace of the White Citadel; however the black sand didn’t merely spill onto the ground after all that...
It shot sixty feet into the air, gracefully curving over a three-hundred-foot marble balustrade, and landed lightly upon the secluded elevated sun-terrace of the palace’s private domestic wing.
SWOOSH!
The black sand swirled together, condensing instantly into the physical form of Harper Whitmore.
Her beige cotton cloak dissolved, revealing the sleek charcoal suit beneath.
Her long vibrant purple hair thrashed in the gentle breeze with her hands resting easily at her sides and her green eyes blazing with a cold look.
’And suddenly she doesn’t want to hide my identity anymore...?’
Floating right behind her, Harper’s astral spirit gasped, taking in their surroundings.
The terrace was private, paved with polished rose-colored quartz, surrounded by hanging gardens of blooming night-lotus and gentle bubbling fountains of clear spring water.
In the center of the terrace, standing near a gilded drying rack of freshly laundered silk tunics, was a woman.
She was young, barely twenty years old, with soft delicate features, wearing a flowing loose-fitting gown of pure white linen.
Her belly was prominently swollen as she was heavily pregnant, carrying a child barely two months from birth.

Sitting on a low velvet cushion beside her, playing with a set of carved wooden toy chariots, was a little girl of five with her hair tied in golden ribbons, giggling softly as she rolled the wheels across the quartz tiles.
Before Harper’s sudden arrival broke the moment, the little girl looked up from her toys, tilting her small head at her mother with the guileless curiosity only a five-year-old could manage.
"Mama," the little girl piped up, still rolling one wooden wheel idly against her palm, "is it really alright that you go visit Grandpa’s chambers so late at night?
You already have a whole new baby brother growing in your tummy...
Does Grandpa know you’re going to have another one?"
Zahra’s cheeks flushed a deep mortified crimson.
She reached down quickly, smoothing a hand over her daughter’s hair with a soft, flustered laugh.
"Hush now, sweetling.
That’s grown-up business.
Go on, play with your chariots."
The little girl only shrugged and went right back to rolling her wheels across the tiles, humming a small, tuneless song to herself.
Standing five paces away, holding a ceremonial short-sword, was a personal royal guard wearing the white-and-gold livery of the domestic watch.
The pregnant woman paused, turning her head toward the sudden rustle of air with her gentle dark eyes widening as she saw Harper materialize on the terrace.
"Who... who are you?" the pregnant woman asked softly, her hand instinctively rising to shield her swollen belly.
"How did you get up here?
This is the private pavilion of—"
Nitocris didn’t ask for a name.

Her senses flared for a single microscopic second, locking onto the unmistakable inherited genetic frequency running through the woman’s veins, through the little girl’s heart, and through the unborn child in the womb...
’Nefertari.’
Behind that cold flare of certainty, something else flickered through the shared consciousness Nitocris and Harper now occupied.
’So the rumors that were whispered through the Inner zone hadn’t been idle gossip after all...’
Sound traveled much better underground and even on the streets, it was being talked about so she could hear...
The old Pharaoh was sharing his dead son’s bed with his dead son’s wife, right beneath the same roof where his granddaughter slept.
Nitocris’s stomach turned at the thought with a fresh private layer of contempt for the rot her own bloodline had curdled into, separate from the sentence she had already come here to carry out.
SHING-CRACK!
There was no hesitation as Nitocris’s right arm blurred with terrifying, speed.
A massive razor-sharp spike of jet-black sand erupted from the terrace flagstones directly beneath the pregnant woman’s feet.
SPLAT-SHRRRRK!
The spike punched straight through her pelvis, tearing upward through her abdomen, impaling her clean through her chest and the little girl didn’t even have time to scream.
A secondary tendril of black sand whipped across the tiles, wrapping tightly around her tiny neck and torso.
CRACKLE!
Before the guard could even draw his short-sword from its scabbard, the horrific lightless calcification claimed them both.
The pregnant woman’s skin instantly turned to brittle oily black glass with her swollen belly freezing into solid dark crystal.
The little girl, her mouth open in a silent wail of terror, petrified into a tiny statue of black glass.
"No!
No!
No!" The royal guard let out a choked horrified gasp, lunging forward with his blade...
SNAP!
A third tendril whipped through the guard’s throat, turning his armor, flesh, and weapon into black glass within half a heartbeat.
SHATTER!
Nitocris flicked her wrist and a concussive shockwave of compressed wind slammed into the three statues.
CRASH-CRUNCH!

The pregnant woman, the unborn child, the five-year-old girl, and the royal guard violently shattered into millions of microscopic black glass shards that clattered uselessly across the rose-quartz terrace with their souls entirely devoured by the void-sand.
Harper’s astral form watched the butchery in horror.
"NOOOOO!" Harper’s spirit wailed, tears streaming down her ghostly face.
"WHY?!
SHE WAS PREGNANT!
THAT WAS A BABY!
YOU MONSTER!
YOU SICK, TWISTED—"
Harper’s spiritual voice choked on its own grief.
Because in that exact second, Harper looked at her own physical face.
...Nitocris was standing perfectly still.
The green fire in Harper’s physical eyes remained bright, but across the left cheek, a microscopic involuntary muscle twitched violently.
The corner of Harper’s physical lips trembled, dipping downward in a silent agonized spasm of pure suffocating grief.
Nitocris didn’t look proud and she didn’t look triumphant as well...
She looked like a woman who had just swallowed a cup of molten lead...
WEEEEWOOOOOO!
An ear-splitting siren shattered the silence of the White Citadel as pillars of blinding red light shot from the palace spires into the afternoon sky, casting blood-red text across the terrace.
[CODE RED BREACH DETECTED!
HIGH CITADEL DOMESTIC PAVILION!
DEADLY FORCE AUTHORIZED!]
FWOOOOOOM!

The rose-quartz tiles beneath the terrace violently churned as from the solid stone, dozens, then hundreds, of high-ranking royal palace sentinels began to manifest, utilizing high-tier earth and solar-meld techniques.

Within five seconds, over three hundred elite guards surrounded the terrace, clad in heavy star-iron armor adorned with golden cobra crests with their hands wielding halberds, curved khopeshes, and heavy repeating mana-arbalests.
WHISTLE!
A sharp piercing sound cut through the air and with a subtle casual tilt of Harper’s neck, she swayed three inches to the left.
THWIP!
A six-foot-long armor-piercing bolt grazed the tips of her purple hair, slamming into the marble balustrade behind her with enough concussive force to blow a ten-foot crater into the stone.
SHING!
In Harper’s physical right hand, the First Khopesh of the Khemet Dominion materialized in a burst of black static lightning.
Nitocris stood in the center of the terrace, facing the three hundred elite guards... her green eyes sweeping across their ranks with cold dead authority.
"Clear the way," Nitocris spoke, Harper’s voice echoing through the courtyard with the crushing weight of a collapsing mountain.
From the front rank of the sentinels, three men stepped forward.

They were massive, over six and a half feet tall, their breastplates adorned with four golden sun-seals, the Imperial Guard Captains, seasoned Third Stage commanders who had held the borders of Khemet for decades.
The lead captain, a scarred man with a brutal square jaw and eyes burning with white-hot solar mana, pointed his broad curved executioner’s blade straight at Harper’s throat.
"Treasonous whore!" the Captain bellowed, his voice laced with incandescent rage.
"You dare step into the sacred house of Al-Mansur?!
You dare lay your filthy hands upon Lady Zahra, the favored consort of the late Crown Prince?!"
Off to the side, one of the younger sentinels, barely out of his teens, muttered something under his breath to the man beside him, too rattled by what he’d just witnessed to fully guard his tongue.
"Consort of the Crown Prince, my ass.
Everyone below the third floor knew whose bed she’d really been warming since the funeral—"
"Silence in the ranks!" the Captain roared without even turning his head, his blade never wavering from Harper’s throat.
"You slaughtered her, her daughter, and the seed in her womb...
There is no grave deep enough to hold your severed limbs!
Surrender your core, or we will flay the flesh from your bones and feed your intestines to the drakes!"
Nitocris looked at the three captains.
Then, she looked past them, looking into the eyes of the young soldiers holding the line, men with trembling grips, men with wives waiting in the lower districts...
These were the same as the men whose families she had sworn to protect two thousand years ago.
"Part," Nitocris warned softly, her tone carrying a sorrowful gravity.
"There is no victory for you here.
I seek only the blood of Nefertari...
If you step aside, you will live.
Do you not have families?
Do you not have children waiting to feel your embrace when your shift ends?
Why throw your lives away for a family of parasites?"
"DIE, WITCH!"

chapters.title: Chapter 606: New Application Of Lightning [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The lead Captain didn’t listen.
BOOM!
The stone beneath the Captain’s boots exploded into fine powder as he launched himself forward with terrifying acceleration...
’Huh?’

Harper’s astral spirit couldn’t even track the movement as the man moved faster than sound, his executioner’s blade igniting with three thousand degrees of blinding solar plasma, cleaving through the air in a downward diagonal executioner’s arc aimed directly at Harper’s neck.
’DODGE!’ Harper screamed internally but Nitocris didn’t dodge at all... The woman never planned to do so,
CLANG-SHRRRRRK!
With a terrifyingly casual flick of Harper’s right wrist, the First Khopesh rose.
The black sickle-blade caught the Captain’s three-thousand-degree plasma sword right at the sweet spot which was two inches below the crossguard.
"Hm."

She didn’t try to block the force of the attack as instead she rotated the curve of the khopesh by half a degree, sliding the Captain’s massive momentum effortlessly across her shoulder, completely unbalancing his center of gravity.
The Captain’s eyes widened in shock as his entire body pitched forward into the empty air.
"Your footwork is sloppy," Nitocris murmured softly, Harper’s physical lips parting with detachment. "You rely too heavily on the heat of your steel, rather than the memory of the stone."
Before the Captain could recover his stance—
SPLAT!

Nitocris’s bare left palm slammed directly into the center of his solar-quartz breastplate as a single concentrated pulse of black sand shot directly from her skin, bypassing the armor, penetrating the sternum, and violently erupting inside his chest cavity.
CRACKLE-SHATTER!

In the span of a single horrific second, the Guard Captain didn’t merely die... his entire body, from his steel boots to the crown of his helmet, petrified into oily black glass and instantly shattered into fine drifting powder before he even touched the ground.
The remaining two hundred and ninety-nine guards froze with their breaths catching in their throats, their eyes dilating in paralyzing horror as well.
...A seasoned Third Stage Captain, erased in half a second?
FSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSH!
The terrace fell into dead suffocating silence, broken only by the sound of shifting mineral as Nitocris slowly lowered the black khopesh.

From the pores of Harper’s skin, from the hems of her tailored trousers, from the sleeves of her charcoal coat, massive billowing rivers of coarse, lightless black sand began to aggressively leak out.

The black sand churned around Harper’s feet, rising into towering undulating serpents that blotted out the midday sun, casting the rose-quartz courtyard into the lightless gloom of an ancient eclipse.
Nitocris tilted Harper’s chin up with her radioactive green eyes burning through the darkness, locking onto the three hundred trembling soldiers.
"My warning has concluded," Nitocris proclaimed, her voice tolling like the bell of a funeral as she raised the First Khopesh, pointing the dark tip toward the palace gates.
"Now, you will all die."
Two hundred and ninety-nine imperial guards stood frozen across the terrace with their boots rooted to the tiles and their breath whistling through the slit visors of their star-iron helms.
The fine white and black dust of the dead commander still hung in the air, swirling lazily in the wake of the desert breeze.
FSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSH!

The coarse lightless black sand that bled from the cuffs of Harper’s tailored charcoal jacket coiled as though it was whispering against the stone with the sound of thousands of tiny starving mouths chewing through paper.
Floating three feet above her own physical right shoulder, Harper’s astral spirit was trembling so violently that the edges of her violet form frayed into static.
Her ghostly chest heaved with phantom panic.
’Look at them,’ Harper thought, her non-physical hands clutching at her own head. ’They’re not moving. Why aren’t they running?! Can’t they see what she is?!’
In the center of the terrace, Nitocris shifted Harper’s physical weight.
She lowered her center of gravity by a bare inch, settling her heels onto the flagstones.
Her green eyes, which were radioactive and burning with several calculations, swept over the interlocking lines of shields, halberds, and repeating arbalests.
"Now..." Nitocris whispered through Harper’s throat with her voice dry and carrying none of the grandeur mortals expected of monsters. "Watch closely, scabbard."
The words weren’t spoken to the courtyard.
They reverberated straight into Harper’s ethereal mind, vibrating along the silver soul-cord that anchored her consciousness to the meat of her skull.

"You possess lightning," Nitocris lectured, like a seasoned tutor tapping a chalkboard. "A common northern mutation which is impressive to peasants because it makes a great deal of noise and burns through cheap armor but raw lightning is crude... It disperses and it seeks the path of least resistance, which means half your output bleeds into the atmosphere as useless heat before your edge ever bites bone."
Across the courtyard, the two surviving Guard Captains snapped out of their stupor.𝗳𝗿𝐞𝕖𝘄𝗲𝕓𝗻𝚘𝚟𝕖𝐥.𝚌𝕠𝕞
"FIRE!" the left captain roared, his voice cracking with the frantic hysterical edge of a man staring down an executioner. "DO NOT ENGAGE HER IN REACH! DROWN HER IN SUN-FIRE! RELEASE!"
TWANG-TWANG-TWANG-CLACK-TWANG!
A deafening volley of ninety heavy imperial mana-arbalests erupted simultaneously.
The six-foot bolts were forged from solid star-iron, their tips capped with pressurized solar-quartz crystals engineered to violently detonate upon resistance.

They tore through the air in a screaming horizontal sheet of golden fury, traveling at high speeds as the concussive pressure of the volley ripped the rose-bushes from their stone planters, shattering the decorative fountains into clouds of vapor.
’NITOCRIS!’ Harper’s spirit shrieked in blind reflex. ’MOVE! I DON’T WANT MY BODY TO DIE!’
Nitocris didn’t flinch at all.
CRACKLE!

Deep within Harper’s sternum, the secondary electrical pathways, the native purple lightning affinity Harper had cultivated since she awakened, violently ignited... however Nitocris didn’t project it outward like a storm.
With terrifying compression, she forced the purple current down Harper’s right arm, funneling the entire voltage directly into the sickle-curved steel of the First Khopesh.
BZZZZZZZZZZT-SHRRK!

The lightning was compressed so densely against the cutting edge that the violet arcs collapsed into ultra-thin microscopic filament threads, vibrating at millions of hertz, humming with a high-pitched mosquito-like whine that drowned out the roar of the incoming artillery.

"Do not project the arc," Nitocris commanded inside Harper’s head. "Compress the frequency until the metal itself acts as a conductor of void-suction... The sand provides the mass and the lightning provides the shearing frequency. Like this..."
STEP!
Harper’s physical right boot pushed off the quartz.
BOOM!
The flagstone beneath her heel vaporized into dust as she vanished... To the mortal eyes of the palace sentinels, the purple-haired woman simply ceased to occupy the space where the bolts landed!
KABOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

Ninety solar-quartz warheads detonated against the marble balustrade where she had stood a fraction of a microsecond prior, blowing a fifty-foot crater through the palace wall and throwing tons of smoking, pulverized stone into the gardens below.
"WHERE IS SHE?!" the right captain screamed, swinging his twin khopeshes in blind paranoia. "CEILING! CHECK THE SPIRES—"
THWIP!
A whisper of displaced air brushed against the back of his neck.
"Too slow," a woman’s voice murmured directly behind his ear.
The Captain’s blood turned to ice.

His Third Stage reflexes fired on pure survival instinct as he dropped his hips, twisting his torso with maximum force and bringing his left blade around in a horizontal decapitation arc while his solar mana flared into a barrier around his ribs.
It was a textbook counter-strike, executed with the brutal efficiency of a man who had survived a hundred sieges however Nitocris didn’t duck.
She simply leaned Harper’s upper body back by two inches, letting the burning edge of the Captain’s blade whistle through the empty air mere millimeters above her eyelashes.
The searing heat scorched a few stray strands of purple hair, but her balance remained undisturbed.
SHING!
In the exact microsecond the Captain’s momentum overcommitted, Harper’s right arm blurred.
The First Khopesh, wrapped in the buzzing filament of purple lightning, flicked upward in a reverse one-handed diagonal draw.
SHRIT!
There was no sound of armor resisting as the compressed purple frequency bypassed the star-iron plating of the Captain’s breastplate as if it were warm lard.
The sickle-blade entered his right hip, carved effortlessly through his pelvic bone, cleaved his spine in two, and exited through his left collarbone.
"Gah..." the Captain choked out.
He didn’t fall apart immediately... Because in the wake of the lightning cut, the coarse black sand followed...
SWOOSH!
The black grains poured out of the incision, instantly coating the severed edges of bone and flesh.
CRACKLE!
Before a single drop of blood could hit the ground, the Captain’s entire bifurcated body vitrified into oily black glass.
TAP!
Nitocris tapped the pommel of her khopesh against the glass statue’s chest.
SHATTER!
The seasoned commander exploded into millions of harmless drifting black motes that scattered across the ranks of his own men.
"Captain Thorn!" a young soldier in the second row screamed, his voice breaking in horror as the black dust coated his visor. "She just cut through his solar-plate like paper! What is that weapon?!"

"SHIELD WALL!" the surviving captain bellowed, retreating into the center of his formation, his eyes wide and bloodshot. "LOCK CORES! EARTH AND SUN POWER! SPREAD THE LOAD! DO NOT LET HER ISOLATE YOU!"
CLANG-CLANG-CLANG-CLANG!
Forty heavy infantrymen stepped forward, their massive rectangular tower shields slamming together edge-to-edge with the thunder of closing fortress gates.

They drove the spiked iron bases of the shields deep into the quartz tiles, their mana channels linking in a shared multi-layered defensive spell as a golden semi-translucent wall of interlocking runes flared to life, glowing with the combined weight of forty Awakened cores.
"HOLD THE LINE!" the sergeants roared. "HOLD FOR THE REINFORCEMENTS! THE HIGH MARSHAL IS ON HIS WAY!"
Nitocris stood ten paces away, watching the glowing barrier with Harper’s physical eyes.
A pitying sigh escaped her lips.

"A cooperative barrier," Nitocris murmured internally to Harper. "A sound doctrine against brute beasts... If a brute strikes this wall, the impact is distributed across forty nervous systems, diluting the shockwave so no single man is crushed but they make a fatal assumption, scabbard."
’What assumption...?’ Harper asked, her spiritual voice small yet helplessly drawn into the strength unfolding before her.
"They assume the ground beneath their feet belongs to them," Nitocris answered.
Harper’s physical left hand reached down with her bare fingertips lightly brushing the polished quartz floor.

"Every stone in this citadel was quarried from the Great Dunes," Nitocris whispered. "Every brick was baked in the southern sun. To an outsider, it is stone but to a Per-aa and her descendants, it’s merely asleep."
CRRRK!
Harper’s core shuddered... It was akin to a harmonic ripple, like a drop of water falling into an infinitely deep well.
CRRRRRR-SNAP!
The rose-quartz tiles beneath the forty shield-bearers dissolved.
In a fraction of a second, the solid stone flagstones reverted to their primordial state, thousands of tons of hyper-fine fluid sand as the foundation vanished beneath the infantrymen’s boots.
"WHAT?!"
"MY FEET, I’M SINKING!"
The forty soldiers pitched forward with their heavy plate armor dragging them down into the sudden churning quagmire of loose silt!
The perfect alignment of their shields fractured; gaps opened in the golden barrier as men flailed, fighting to keep their balance.
"Now," Nitocris instructed. "You do not strike the shield."
WHOOSH!
From Harper’s sleeves, two massive undulating tendrils of black sand shot forward but they didn’t crash against the failing golden shields... that would be too easy.
They flowed through the cracks in the formation like liquid mercury, wrapping around the ankles, thighs, and waists of the struggling men.
CRACKLE-CRACKLE-CRACKLE!
"NO! GET IT OFF—"
"MY LEGS! I CAN’T FEEL MY LEGS—"
"CAPTAIN! HELP US—"
The screams were cut short with terrifying synchronicity as the black sand climbed their bodies in a crawling oily wave, turning steel, flesh, and bone into solid black glass.
Within three seconds, forty elite infantrymen stood completely frozen in dynamic panicked poses with forty statues of jet-black obsidian sinking slowly into the sand.
Nitocris didn’t even look at them as she simply flicked Harper’s wrist.
BOOM!
A low-frequency wave washed through the formation.
CRASH-SHATTER!
All forty glass statues disintegrated simultaneously, collapsing into an enormous dark dune of pulverized black powder.
"Monster..." a young marksman whispered with his bow slipping from his numb sweat-soaked leather gauntlets.
He fell to his knees among the rose-bushes, his pupils dilated to pinpricks, staring at the empty courtyard where forty of his comrades had stood bare heartbeats ago.
"She isn’t human. This is the ancient rot... The curse has returned..."
"KILL HER! WHY ARE YOU STANDING THERE?! ATTACK!" the last captain shrieked, entirely losing his mind. He grabbed a soldier by the collar and hurled him forward. "DIE FOR THE PHARAOH, YOU COWARDS!"
Nitocris stepped into the center of the terrace.
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

The First Khopesh was thrust violently into the earth and from the point of impact, an apocalyptic wave of black sand, standing thirty feet high, crowned with screaming arcs of purple lightning, exploded outward in a complete three-hundred-and-sixty-degree circle.
The tsunami of lightless minerals tore through the courtyard like the scythe of an uncaring god...
SPLAT-SHRUNK-CRUNCH!

It didn’t matter if they raised their shields... It didn’t matter if they channeled their solar flames... The black sand ignored the heat, devoured the light, and drilled straight through their armor.
Tendrils of black glass impaled throats, sheared through torsos, and wrapped around skulls.
Men were lifted into the air, screaming, weeping, calling out for their mothers, their wives, their children, before their voices abruptly choked on crystalline bile.
CRACKLE-SHATTER! CRASH! CRACK! SNAP!
A continuous deafening cacophony of shattering glass echoed off the palace spires.

The Captain’s eyes widened in shock as his entire body pitched forward into the empty air.
"Your footwork is sloppy," Nitocris murmured softly, Harper’s physical lips parting with detachment.
"You rely too heavily on the heat of your steel, rather than the memory of the stone."
Before the Captain could recover his stance—
SPLAT!

Nitocris’s bare left palm slammed directly into the center of his solar-quartz breastplate as a single concentrated pulse of black sand shot directly from her skin, bypassing the armor, penetrating the sternum, and violently erupting inside his chest cavity.
CRACKLE-SHATTER!

In the span of a single horrific second, the Guard Captain didn’t merely die... his entire body, from his steel boots to the crown of his helmet, petrified into oily black glass and instantly shattered into fine drifting powder before he even touched the ground.
The remaining two hundred and ninety-nine guards froze with their breaths catching in their throats, their eyes dilating in paralyzing horror as well.
...A seasoned Third Stage Captain, erased in half a second?
FSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSH!
The terrace fell into dead suffocating silence, broken only by the sound of shifting mineral as Nitocris slowly lowered the black khopesh.

From the pores of Harper’s skin, from the hems of her tailored trousers, from the sleeves of her charcoal coat, massive billowing rivers of coarse, lightless black sand began to aggressively leak out.

The black sand churned around Harper’s feet, rising into towering undulating serpents that blotted out the midday sun, casting the rose-quartz courtyard into the lightless gloom of an ancient eclipse.
Nitocris tilted Harper’s chin up with her radioactive green eyes burning through the darkness, locking onto the three hundred trembling soldiers.
"My warning has concluded," Nitocris proclaimed, her voice tolling like the bell of a funeral as she raised the First Khopesh, pointing the dark tip toward the palace gates.
"Now, you will all die."
Two hundred and ninety-nine imperial guards stood frozen across the terrace with their boots rooted to the tiles and their breath whistling through the slit visors of their star-iron helms.
The fine white and black dust of the dead commander still hung in the air, swirling lazily in the wake of the desert breeze.
FSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSH!

The coarse lightless black sand that bled from the cuffs of Harper’s tailored charcoal jacket coiled as though it was whispering against the stone with the sound of thousands of tiny starving mouths chewing through paper.
Floating three feet above her own physical right shoulder, Harper’s astral spirit was trembling so violently that the edges of her violet form frayed into static.
Her ghostly chest heaved with phantom panic.
’Look at them,’ Harper thought, her non-physical hands clutching at her own head. ’They’re not moving.
Why aren’t they running?!
Can’t they see what she is?!’
In the center of the terrace, Nitocris shifted Harper’s physical weight.
She lowered her center of gravity by a bare inch, settling her heels onto the flagstones.
Her green eyes, which were radioactive and burning with several calculations, swept over the interlocking lines of shields, halberds, and repeating arbalests.
"Now..." Nitocris whispered through Harper’s throat with her voice dry and carrying none of the grandeur mortals expected of monsters.
"Watch closely, scabbard."
The words weren’t spoken to the courtyard.
They reverberated straight into Harper’s ethereal mind, vibrating along the silver soul-cord that anchored her consciousness to the meat of her skull.
"You possess lightning," Nitocris lectured, like a seasoned tutor tapping a chalkboard.
"A common northern mutation which is impressive to peasants because it makes a great deal of noise and burns through cheap armor but raw lightning is crude...
It disperses and it seeks the path of least resistance, which means half your output bleeds into the atmosphere as useless heat before your edge ever bites bone."
Across the courtyard, the two surviving Guard Captains snapped out of their stupor.𝗳𝗿𝐞𝕖𝘄𝗲𝕓𝗻𝚘𝚟𝕖𝐥.𝚌𝕠𝕞
"FIRE!" the left captain roared, his voice cracking with the frantic hysterical edge of a man staring down an executioner.
"DO NOT ENGAGE HER IN REACH!
DROWN HER IN SUN-FIRE!
RELEASE!"
TWANG-TWANG-TWANG-CLACK-TWANG!
A deafening volley of ninety heavy imperial mana-arbalests erupted simultaneously.
The six-foot bolts were forged from solid star-iron, their tips capped with pressurized solar-quartz crystals engineered to violently detonate upon resistance.

They tore through the air in a screaming horizontal sheet of golden fury, traveling at high speeds as the concussive pressure of the volley ripped the rose-bushes from their stone planters, shattering the decorative fountains into clouds of vapor.
’NITOCRIS!’ Harper’s spirit shrieked in blind reflex. ’MOVE!
I DON’T WANT MY BODY TO DIE!’
Nitocris didn’t flinch at all.
CRACKLE!

Deep within Harper’s sternum, the secondary electrical pathways, the native purple lightning affinity Harper had cultivated since she awakened, violently ignited... however Nitocris didn’t project it outward like a storm.
With terrifying compression, she forced the purple current down Harper’s right arm, funneling the entire voltage directly into the sickle-curved steel of the First Khopesh.
BZZZZZZZZZZT-SHRRK!

The lightning was compressed so densely against the cutting edge that the violet arcs collapsed into ultra-thin microscopic filament threads, vibrating at millions of hertz, humming with a high-pitched mosquito-like whine that drowned out the roar of the incoming artillery.
"Do not project the arc," Nitocris commanded inside Harper’s head.
"Compress the frequency until the metal itself acts as a conductor of void-suction...
The sand provides the mass and the lightning provides the shearing frequency.
Like this..."
STEP!
Harper’s physical right boot pushed off the quartz.
BOOM!
The flagstone beneath her heel vaporized into dust as she vanished...
To the mortal eyes of the palace sentinels, the purple-haired woman simply ceased to occupy the space where the bolts landed!
KABOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

Ninety solar-quartz warheads detonated against the marble balustrade where she had stood a fraction of a microsecond prior, blowing a fifty-foot crater through the palace wall and throwing tons of smoking, pulverized stone into the gardens below.
"WHERE IS SHE?!" the right captain screamed, swinging his twin khopeshes in blind paranoia.
"CEILING!
CHECK THE SPIRES—"
THWIP!
A whisper of displaced air brushed against the back of his neck.
"Too slow," a woman’s voice murmured directly behind his ear.
The Captain’s blood turned to ice.

His Third Stage reflexes fired on pure survival instinct as he dropped his hips, twisting his torso with maximum force and bringing his left blade around in a horizontal decapitation arc while his solar mana flared into a barrier around his ribs.
It was a textbook counter-strike, executed with the brutal efficiency of a man who had survived a hundred sieges however Nitocris didn’t duck.
She simply leaned Harper’s upper body back by two inches, letting the burning edge of the Captain’s blade whistle through the empty air mere millimeters above her eyelashes.
The searing heat scorched a few stray strands of purple hair, but her balance remained undisturbed.
SHING!
In the exact microsecond the Captain’s momentum overcommitted, Harper’s right arm blurred.
The First Khopesh, wrapped in the buzzing filament of purple lightning, flicked upward in a reverse one-handed diagonal draw.
SHRIT!
There was no sound of armor resisting as the compressed purple frequency bypassed the star-iron plating of the Captain’s breastplate as if it were warm lard.
The sickle-blade entered his right hip, carved effortlessly through his pelvic bone, cleaved his spine in two, and exited through his left collarbone.
"Gah..." the Captain choked out.
He didn’t fall apart immediately...
Because in the wake of the lightning cut, the coarse black sand followed...
SWOOSH!
The black grains poured out of the incision, instantly coating the severed edges of bone and flesh.
CRACKLE!
Before a single drop of blood could hit the ground, the Captain’s entire bifurcated body vitrified into oily black glass.
TAP!
Nitocris tapped the pommel of her khopesh against the glass statue’s chest.
SHATTER!
The seasoned commander exploded into millions of harmless drifting black motes that scattered across the ranks of his own men.
"Captain Thorn!" a young soldier in the second row screamed, his voice breaking in horror as the black dust coated his visor.
"She just cut through his solar-plate like paper!
What is that weapon?!"
"SHIELD WALL!" the surviving captain bellowed, retreating into the center of his formation, his eyes wide and bloodshot.
"LOCK CORES!
EARTH AND SUN POWER!
SPREAD THE LOAD!
DO NOT LET HER ISOLATE YOU!"
CLANG-CLANG-CLANG-CLANG!
Forty heavy infantrymen stepped forward, their massive rectangular tower shields slamming together edge-to-edge with the thunder of closing fortress gates.

They drove the spiked iron bases of the shields deep into the quartz tiles, their mana channels linking in a shared multi-layered defensive spell as a golden semi-translucent wall of interlocking runes flared to life, glowing with the combined weight of forty Awakened cores.
"HOLD THE LINE!" the sergeants roared.
"HOLD FOR THE REINFORCEMENTS!
THE HIGH MARSHAL IS ON HIS WAY!"
Nitocris stood ten paces away, watching the glowing barrier with Harper’s physical eyes.
A pitying sigh escaped her lips.
"A cooperative barrier," Nitocris murmured internally to Harper.
"A sound doctrine against brute beasts...
If a brute strikes this wall, the impact is distributed across forty nervous systems, diluting the shockwave so no single man is crushed but they make a fatal assumption, scabbard."
’What assumption...?’ Harper asked, her spiritual voice small yet helplessly drawn into the strength unfolding before her.
"They assume the ground beneath their feet belongs to them," Nitocris answered.
Harper’s physical left hand reached down with her bare fingertips lightly brushing the polished quartz floor.
"Every stone in this citadel was quarried from the Great Dunes," Nitocris whispered.
"Every brick was baked in the southern sun.
To an outsider, it is stone but to a Per-aa and her descendants, it’s merely asleep."
CRRRK!
Harper’s core shuddered...
It was akin to a harmonic ripple, like a drop of water falling into an infinitely deep well.
CRRRRRR-SNAP!
The rose-quartz tiles beneath the forty shield-bearers dissolved.
In a fraction of a second, the solid stone flagstones reverted to their primordial state, thousands of tons of hyper-fine fluid sand as the foundation vanished beneath the infantrymen’s boots.
"WHAT?!"
"MY FEET, I’M SINKING!"
The forty soldiers pitched forward with their heavy plate armor dragging them down into the sudden churning quagmire of loose silt!
The perfect alignment of their shields fractured; gaps opened in the golden barrier as men flailed, fighting to keep their balance.
"Now," Nitocris instructed.
"You do not strike the shield."
WHOOSH!
From Harper’s sleeves, two massive undulating tendrils of black sand shot forward but they didn’t crash against the failing golden shields... that would be too easy.
They flowed through the cracks in the formation like liquid mercury, wrapping around the ankles, thighs, and waists of the struggling men.
CRACKLE-CRACKLE-CRACKLE!
"NO!
GET IT OFF—"
"MY LEGS!
I CAN’T FEEL MY LEGS—"
"CAPTAIN!
HELP US—"
The screams were cut short with terrifying synchronicity as the black sand climbed their bodies in a crawling oily wave, turning steel, flesh, and bone into solid black glass.
Within three seconds, forty elite infantrymen stood completely frozen in dynamic panicked poses with forty statues of jet-black obsidian sinking slowly into the sand.
Nitocris didn’t even look at them as she simply flicked Harper’s wrist.
BOOM!
A low-frequency wave washed through the formation.
CRASH-SHATTER!
All forty glass statues disintegrated simultaneously, collapsing into an enormous dark dune of pulverized black powder.
"Monster..." a young marksman whispered with his bow slipping from his numb sweat-soaked leather gauntlets.
He fell to his knees among the rose-bushes, his pupils dilated to pinpricks, staring at the empty courtyard where forty of his comrades had stood bare heartbeats ago.
"She isn’t human.
This is the ancient rot...
The curse has returned..."
"KILL HER!
WHY ARE YOU STANDING THERE?!
ATTACK!" the last captain shrieked, entirely losing his mind.
He grabbed a soldier by the collar and hurled him forward.
"DIE FOR THE PHARAOH, YOU COWARDS!"
Nitocris stepped into the center of the terrace.
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

The First Khopesh was thrust violently into the earth and from the point of impact, an apocalyptic wave of black sand, standing thirty feet high, crowned with screaming arcs of purple lightning, exploded outward in a complete three-hundred-and-sixty-degree circle.
The tsunami of lightless minerals tore through the courtyard like the scythe of an uncaring god...
SPLAT-SHRUNK-CRUNCH!
It didn’t matter if they raised their shields...
It didn’t matter if they channeled their solar flames...
The black sand ignored the heat, devoured the light, and drilled straight through their armor.
Tendrils of black glass impaled throats, sheared through torsos, and wrapped around skulls.
Men were lifted into the air, screaming, weeping, calling out for their mothers, their wives, their children, before their voices abruptly choked on crystalline bile.
CRACKLE-SHATTER!
CRASH!
CRACK!
SNAP!
A continuous deafening cacophony of shattering glass echoed off the palace spires.

paragraphs: Over two hundred elite sentinels were petrified and pulverized in a single rolling breath of violence...

The terrace became a slaughterhouse of sound without a single drop of blood touching the stones, only an ocean of coarse lightless black sand that hissed as it consumed their cores, leaving nothing behind for the soil and nothing behind for the grave either.
Harper’s astral spirit couldn’t take it anymore.

’STOP IT!’ Harper screamed, curling her ghostly form into a fetal ball, clamping her translucent hands tightly over her eyes, weeping uncontrollably. ’PLEASE! STOP IT! I CAN’T WATCH THIS! I CAN’T LOOK AT IT ANYMORE!’
She closed her spiritual eyes, burying her face against her knees, trying desperately to block out the horrific wet snaps of breaking bone and the dry ringing of shattering glass.
Yet, even with her eyes shut tight, she could feel the feedback.
Every soul devoured by the black sand sent a faint icy tremor along the silver cord connecting her to the physical body...
Nitocris pulled the khopesh from the ground with a soft metallic scrape as the courtyard was dead.
Not a single soldier remained standing.

The two hundred and ninety-nine men, their captains, their armor, their weapons, all of it had been reduced to a thick knee-deep layer of black powder that blanketed the rose-quartz courtyard from wall to wall.
The grand arched doors leading into the domestic palace stood wide open and unprotected, leading into the opulent corridors of the imperial family.
Nitocris stepped over the threshold with Harper’s physical boots sinking soundlessly into the black sand.
"It is time, scabbard," Nitocris spoke softly into Harper’s mind. "Keep your eyes closed if you must but the debt must be balanced."
The next thirty minutes were a waking nightmare that burned itself permanently into the architecture of Harper’s soul...
Even with her astral eyes pressed shut, Harper could hear everything.
She could sense every room they entered, mapped out through the physical body’s heightened perception.
It was at this point that she wished that she could be unawakened...
CREAK!
They walked through gilded chambers of white marble and gold filigree.

They walked through private solariums scented with frankincense, through nursery pavilions decorated with spun-silk tapestries, through secluded bathhouses where clear spring water rippled over turquoise tiles.
And everywhere they walked, the screams followed.
SPLAT-CRACKLE!
"Who are you?! Guards! GUARDS—"
SHATTER!
It was Lady Samira, the second wife of the Vice President, caught in the middle of writing a letter at her ebony desk.
Her pen clattered to the floor as a spike of black sand erupted through her throat, turning her into black glass before she could finish drawing breath.
TAP-TAP-TAP!
The footsteps continued down the hallway as doors were kicked open.

Inside a grand bedchamber, three young women, royal concubines belonging to the late Crown Prince, draped in diaphanous yellow silk, huddled together in the corner of a massive feather bed, weeping hysterically, clutching each other as they stared at Harper’s approaching figure.

"Please..." one of them sobbed, her face pale, her hands clasped in frantic prayer. "We never held weapons! We never fought! We were only brought here from the eastern clans three months ago! Please have mercy!"
Nitocris stood in the doorway as Harper’s physical eyes were cold and dead.
"Your womb was bought to carry Nefertari’s blood," Nitocris stated simply. "That is your only crime and that is your execution sentence."
SHING-CRACK!𝒇𝙧𝙚𝓮𝙬𝙚𝓫𝒏𝓸𝓿𝓮𝒍.𝓬𝙤𝓶
A wave of black sand rolled across the bed.
SHATTER!
Three piles of black dust collapsed into the silk sheets.
Harper’s spirit was thrashing inside the dark, sobbing until she thought her ethereal form would tear apart.
’Why?! They had nothing to do with what happened two thousand years ago! They didn’t even know her name! Why must you kill the innocent?!’
Harper was no supporter of random people but still... Wasn’t there a point where the murder was too much? The only sin everybody had here was the sin of being born.
Nitocris didn’t pause.
STEP! STEP! STEP!
She descended into the private nursery wing.

Two wet-nurses were huddled beneath a heavy mahogany wardrobe, their bodies trembling violently, shielding two infants wrapped in linen blankets with the youngest grandchildren of the Pharaoh-President, born barely six weeks prior.
The nurses looked up, their eyes wide with the terror of prey animals backed into a corner.

"Take us," one of the nurses begged, blood dripping from her lip where she had bitten it in fear. "Take our lives, lady but the children, they don’t even have teeth yet. They don’t know who their father was. Leave them..."
Nitocris stood over them as Harper’s physical right hand rose slowly into the air.

Inside the physical chest, Harper felt the microscopic agonizing hesitation... the barest fraction of a heartbeat where Nitocris’s internal mana stuttered, where the ancient warrior’s soul screamed in protest against the monstrous duty she had bound herself to perform.
’H-huh... my eyes...’

Harper saw it through their shared connection... It was a memory of Nitocris two thousand years ago, kneeling in the ruins of a burning village during the First Rift, pulling a crying orphan from the rubble and cradling it against her armor, whispering that she would protect them all.
And now, here she stood.
TWITCH!
Harper’s physical cheek spasmed violently as a single hot tear rolled down Harper’s right cheek, dripping off her jawline and hitting the polished floor with a soft pat.
"Forgive me," Nitocris whispered through Harper’s lips, her voice breaking into a ragged broken gasp. "May the wheel of rebirth grant you a kinder mother in the next life..."
SHRUNK!
Black sand enveloped the wardrobe... unfortunately, there would be no next life.
SHATTER!
The room fell into suffocating silence.
By the time the thirty minutes had concluded, the entire interior of the White Citadel’s domestic wing was devoid of living breath.

Over seventy members of the extended bloodline, consorts, concubines, royal cousins, scions of the cadet branches, and every infant carrying the genetic markers of Nefertari Al-Mansur, had been mercilessly erased.

Along with them lay the remnants of over five hundred personal retainers, eunuchs, and elite palace guards who had thrown themselves into the corridors in futile attempts to halt the purple-haired demon.
Nitocris walked out into the grand central rotunda beneath the main dome of the citadel.
Her charcoal suit was pristine, not because she had avoided violence, but because the black sand consumed everything cleanly, leaving no blood to stain her fabric.
Nitocris stopped before the colossal seventy-foot double doors of the Treasury as she leaned her forehead against the cool carved star-iron panel, taking a long deep shuddering breath.
Her physical shoulders slumped with the terrifying posture of the ancient conqueror melting away, leaving behind the exhausted broken silhouette of a woman whose soul had been ground to dust.
"It is done..." Nitocris breathed softly, her voice trembling in the empty hall.
Harper’s astral form slowly unfolded, hovering beside the physical body with her ghostly eyes hollow and red with unshed tears.
"Is it?" Harper asked, her voice cracking with raw bitter exhaustion. "Did you get your revenge? Are you happy now?"
Nitocris let out a dry hollow laugh that carried zero mirth.

"Happy?" Nitocris murmured, turning Harper’s head toward the empty corridor. "There is no happiness in butchering children, scabbard... There is only balance. Truly, there may be distant drops of Nefertari’s blood scattered across the continents, perhaps a bastard child born to a merchant in the northern reaches, a displaced descendant living in the eastern isles but the throne is broken. The direct line that sat upon my people’s necks, it’s extinguished..."
She pushed the massive treasury doors open with a casual shove of Harper’s single right hand.
CREEEEEAK!
The gates swung wide, revealing a cavern of breathtaking obscene wealth.

Mountains of refined celestial gold bullion rose fifty feet into the air; chests of uncut diamond-quartz and star-sapphires spilled across the floor; racks of ancient enchanted weaponry, scrolls of classified cultivation methods, and crates of high-density spirit cards lined the walls as far as the eye could see.
It was the accumulated imperial hoard of eight centuries of dynastic rule as well as hundreds of billions of credits in raw unrefined capital.
Nitocris pointed Harper’s hand toward the glittering hoard.

"Take it," Nitocris said softly. "Open your Lord Inventory, Harper... Take as much as your spatial rings can hold. Take the gold, take the gems, take the weapons... You will need them in the world to come."
Harper’s astral spirit blinked, staring at the vast sea of gold with completely numb detachment.
"I don’t want their blood money."
She loved money as much as the next person but this... She was not emotionless.

"Do not be foolish," Nitocris chided gently as Harper’s physical lips curled into a sad tired smile. "Gold has no memory... It doesn’t care whose hands minted it so take it, scabbard. It is my final gift to you as your ancestor."
Nitocris walked to the center of the rotunda, beneath the massive glass skylight that looked up toward the burning desert sun.
’What a day... I am ready to die now...’
She slowly knelt down, Harper’s knees resting upon the cold lapis lazuli tiles as she extended her right palm, pressing it flat against the foundational stone of the citadel.
VVVVVVRRRRR!
A massive intricate magic circle, spanning over three hundred paces in diameter, began to slowly bleed outward from beneath Harper’s palm...
It was carved in the ancient runes of the First Dominion.
The runes glowed with an ominous pulsing crimson-black light, sinking deep into the structural load-bearing pillars of the palace, intertwining with the bedrock itself.
"What are you doing...?" Harper asked with a sudden prickle of anxiety piercing through her exhaustion.
"I am preparing the pyre," Nitocris explained softly,

Harper’s physical eyes half-closed as she poured her lingering soul-force into the array. "This citadel was built upon a lie... It was raised upon the bones of my loyal people, defiled by my sister’s greed. It doesn’t deserve to stand under the sun so once I depart, this spell will violently destabilize the underground mana aquifers beneath the foundations... The entire mountain, the palace, the spires, the walls, all of it will collapse into the void, buried under four thousand feet of black sand."
She looked up at Harper’s floating soul, her green eyes filled with a soft quiet warmth that looked impossibly tender.

"I am engraving every spell, every sand-weaving technique, and every combat formula I possess directly into the spiritual meridians of your soul like I said," Nitocris told her. "It is nearly complete. The moment my consciousness dissolves, the knowledge will lock permanently into your mind and you will have roughly five minutes to flee this place before the collapse triggers."
"Five minutes...?" Harper’s breath hitched.

"You have the sand-meld," Nitocris assured her. "With the formulas I have gifted you, you can slip through the outer walls as fluid dust... You will easily escape before the stone falls. I have caused you enough terror today, Harper Whitmore so I will not allow you to die in my grave."
Nitocris closed Harper’s physical eyes, resting her forehead against her own knuckles with a deep peaceful stillness settling over her features.

"You know..." Nitocris whispered into the quiet rotunda, her voice carrying a fragile nostalgic warmth. "In all my centuries of war, during the First Rift, and throughout the long dark years I spent sleeping within the cold steel of that khopesh, I never truly had anyone I could call a proper friend..."
Harper’s astral form floated motionless in the air, listening in silence.

"A Per-aa must always be an icon," the ancient woman murmured. "A statue of bronze and gold... You cannot show fear to your soldiers... You cannot show doubt to your ministers... But these past few days, sitting on your bedside table, listening to you complain about everything, listening to you laugh about silly mortal garments, hearing you speak about the world beyond the dunes..."
A soft genuine smile curved Harper’s physical lips.
"...and hearing you talk about that boy. Silas Graves, was it?"
Harper’s ghostly form stiffened with a sudden fierce blush spreading across her translucent cheeks despite the horror of the day.

"He truly is an exceptionally lucky young man," Nitocris chuckled softly with her voice light and fond. "To have a woman who looks upon him with such fierce uncompromising devotion... I would have loved to meet him, you know. To sit across a table, share a cup of spiced wine, and test whether his steel was truly worthy of holding your heart but my time here was long overdue. The dead have no place among the living."
She raised Harper’s physical head, looking directly into Harper’s ghostly violet eyes with her expression pure and unburdened.

"Thank you, Harper," Nitocris whispered, her voice trembling with profound sincerity. "For the sweets... For the stories... For allowing me to balance my debts under the sun. In the end, I truly thought of you as my frien—"
CLACK!
The sound was microscopic but it made Nitocris abruptly freeze.

Harper’s physical body remained knelt on the tiles with her right hand pressed to the floor, but the black mana radiating from the magic circle instantly calcified in mid-air, hanging suspended like frozen red lightning.
Floating beside her, Harper’s astral spirit tried to drift forward, and found herself utterly paralyzed as the air in the rotunda didn’t move.
The dust motes floating through the sunbeams stopped dead in their tracks.
The distant flags atop the palace spires ceased their fluttering.
Even the distant roar of the city outside vanished, replaced by an unnatural void of complete deprivation of senses.
’What is this?!’ Harper screamed in the silent prison of her mind. ’Why can’t I move?!’
Nitocris’s green pupils contracted to needle-points.
Inside Harper’s physical chest, the heart stopped beating though this was not from damage, but because time itself had been forcibly arrested.
STEP!
The sound of a single deliberate footstep echoed through the frozen rotunda.
STEP! STEP!
From the empty air five paces in front of the kneeling body, a thick billowing shroud of golden iridescent mist began to bleed into reality.
The mist didn’t disperse at all... it swirled violently, coalescing into the towering translucent figure of a man hovering three feet above the lapis floor.
He was large, draped in magnificent ancient ceremonial robes of beaten gold and deep azure silk that seemed to constantly shift and ripple like liquid sunlight.
His skin was flawless, radiating a blinding divine bronze sheen, his long golden hair crowned with an ornate imperial diadem depicting an undulating winged serpent.
His face was impossibly handsome, yet etched with an expression of utterly nauseating vanity.
A wide condescending amused grin stretched across his golden lips.
"Hoho~" the entity chuckled, his voice echoing through the frozen space like the ringing of a thousand silver bells.
He tapped his chin with a manicured glowing finger, his golden eyes sweeping over the slaughtered domestic wing with exaggerated delight.

"Well, well, well!" the figure proclaimed, his voice dripping with grandiose self-mythologizing arrogance. "Look at what my adorable, impatient little splinter has managed to accomplish in my absence! Truly, what a magnificent little bloodbath! You always were such an efficient little butcher, weren’t you, my dear?"
