GUARDS—"
SHATTER!
It was Lady Samira, the second wife of the Vice President, caught in the middle of writing a letter at her ebony desk.
Her pen clattered to the floor as a spike of black sand erupted through her throat, turning her into black glass before she could finish drawing breath.
TAP-TAP-TAP!
The footsteps continued down the hallway as doors were kicked open.

Inside a grand bedchamber, three young women, royal concubines belonging to the late Crown Prince, draped in diaphanous yellow silk, huddled together in the corner of a massive feather bed, weeping hysterically, clutching each other as they stared at Harper’s approaching figure.
"Please..." one of them sobbed, her face pale, her hands clasped in frantic prayer.
"We never held weapons!
We never fought!
We were only brought here from the eastern clans three months ago!
Please have mercy!"
Nitocris stood in the doorway as Harper’s physical eyes were cold and dead.
"Your womb was bought to carry Nefertari’s blood," Nitocris stated simply.
"That is your only crime and that is your execution sentence."
SHING-CRACK!𝒇𝙧𝙚𝓮𝙬𝙚𝓫𝒏𝓸𝓿𝓮𝒍.𝓬𝙤𝓶
A wave of black sand rolled across the bed.
SHATTER!
Three piles of black dust collapsed into the silk sheets.
Harper’s spirit was thrashing inside the dark, sobbing until she thought her ethereal form would tear apart.
’Why?!
They had nothing to do with what happened two thousand years ago!
They didn’t even know her name!
Why must you kill the innocent?!’
Harper was no supporter of random people but still...
Wasn’t there a point where the murder was too much?
The only sin everybody had here was the sin of being born.
Nitocris didn’t pause.
STEP!
STEP!
STEP!
She descended into the private nursery wing.

Two wet-nurses were huddled beneath a heavy mahogany wardrobe, their bodies trembling violently, shielding two infants wrapped in linen blankets with the youngest grandchildren of the Pharaoh-President, born barely six weeks prior.
The nurses looked up, their eyes wide with the terror of prey animals backed into a corner.
"Take us," one of the nurses begged, blood dripping from her lip where she had bitten it in fear.
"Take our lives, lady but the children, they don’t even have teeth yet.
They don’t know who their father was.
Leave them..."
Nitocris stood over them as Harper’s physical right hand rose slowly into the air.

Inside the physical chest, Harper felt the microscopic agonizing hesitation... the barest fraction of a heartbeat where Nitocris’s internal mana stuttered, where the ancient warrior’s soul screamed in protest against the monstrous duty she had bound herself to perform.
’H-huh... my eyes...’
Harper saw it through their shared connection...

It was a memory of Nitocris two thousand years ago, kneeling in the ruins of a burning village during the First Rift, pulling a crying orphan from the rubble and cradling it against her armor, whispering that she would protect them all.
And now, here she stood.
TWITCH!
Harper’s physical cheek spasmed violently as a single hot tear rolled down Harper’s right cheek, dripping off her jawline and hitting the polished floor with a soft pat.
"Forgive me," Nitocris whispered through Harper’s lips, her voice breaking into a ragged broken gasp.
"May the wheel of rebirth grant you a kinder mother in the next life..."
SHRUNK!
Black sand enveloped the wardrobe... unfortunately, there would be no next life.
SHATTER!
The room fell into suffocating silence.
By the time the thirty minutes had concluded, the entire interior of the White Citadel’s domestic wing was devoid of living breath.

Over seventy members of the extended bloodline, consorts, concubines, royal cousins, scions of the cadet branches, and every infant carrying the genetic markers of Nefertari Al-Mansur, had been mercilessly erased.

Along with them lay the remnants of over five hundred personal retainers, eunuchs, and elite palace guards who had thrown themselves into the corridors in futile attempts to halt the purple-haired demon.
Nitocris walked out into the grand central rotunda beneath the main dome of the citadel.
Her charcoal suit was pristine, not because she had avoided violence, but because the black sand consumed everything cleanly, leaving no blood to stain her fabric.
Nitocris stopped before the colossal seventy-foot double doors of the Treasury as she leaned her forehead against the cool carved star-iron panel, taking a long deep shuddering breath.
Her physical shoulders slumped with the terrifying posture of the ancient conqueror melting away, leaving behind the exhausted broken silhouette of a woman whose soul had been ground to dust.
"It is done..." Nitocris breathed softly, her voice trembling in the empty hall.
Harper’s astral form slowly unfolded, hovering beside the physical body with her ghostly eyes hollow and red with unshed tears.
"Is it?" Harper asked, her voice cracking with raw bitter exhaustion.
"Did you get your revenge?
Are you happy now?"
Nitocris let out a dry hollow laugh that carried zero mirth.
"Happy?" Nitocris murmured, turning Harper’s head toward the empty corridor.
"There is no happiness in butchering children, scabbard...
There is only balance.

Truly, there may be distant drops of Nefertari’s blood scattered across the continents, perhaps a bastard child born to a merchant in the northern reaches, a displaced descendant living in the eastern isles but the throne is broken.
The direct line that sat upon my people’s necks, it’s extinguished..."
She pushed the massive treasury doors open with a casual shove of Harper’s single right hand.
CREEEEEAK!
The gates swung wide, revealing a cavern of breathtaking obscene wealth.

Mountains of refined celestial gold bullion rose fifty feet into the air; chests of uncut diamond-quartz and star-sapphires spilled across the floor; racks of ancient enchanted weaponry, scrolls of classified cultivation methods, and crates of high-density spirit cards lined the walls as far as the eye could see.
It was the accumulated imperial hoard of eight centuries of dynastic rule as well as hundreds of billions of credits in raw unrefined capital.
Nitocris pointed Harper’s hand toward the glittering hoard.
"Take it," Nitocris said softly.
"Open your Lord Inventory, Harper...
Take as much as your spatial rings can hold.
Take the gold, take the gems, take the weapons...
You will need them in the world to come."
Harper’s astral spirit blinked, staring at the vast sea of gold with completely numb detachment.
"I don’t want their blood money."
She loved money as much as the next person but this...
She was not emotionless.
"Do not be foolish," Nitocris chided gently as Harper’s physical lips curled into a sad tired smile.
"Gold has no memory...
It doesn’t care whose hands minted it so take it, scabbard.
It is my final gift to you as your ancestor."
Nitocris walked to the center of the rotunda, beneath the massive glass skylight that looked up toward the burning desert sun.
’What a day...
I am ready to die now...’
She slowly knelt down, Harper’s knees resting upon the cold lapis lazuli tiles as she extended her right palm, pressing it flat against the foundational stone of the citadel.
VVVVVVRRRRR!
A massive intricate magic circle, spanning over three hundred paces in diameter, began to slowly bleed outward from beneath Harper’s palm...
It was carved in the ancient runes of the First Dominion.
The runes glowed with an ominous pulsing crimson-black light, sinking deep into the structural load-bearing pillars of the palace, intertwining with the bedrock itself.
"What are you doing...?" Harper asked with a sudden prickle of anxiety piercing through her exhaustion.
"I am preparing the pyre," Nitocris explained softly,
Harper’s physical eyes half-closed as she poured her lingering soul-force into the array.
"This citadel was built upon a lie...
It was raised upon the bones of my loyal people, defiled by my sister’s greed.
It doesn’t deserve to stand under the sun so once I depart, this spell will violently destabilize the underground mana aquifers beneath the foundations...
The entire mountain, the palace, the spires, the walls, all of it will collapse into the void, buried under four thousand feet of black sand."
She looked up at Harper’s floating soul, her green eyes filled with a soft quiet warmth that looked impossibly tender.
"I am engraving every spell, every sand-weaving technique, and every combat formula I possess directly into the spiritual meridians of your soul like I said," Nitocris told her.
"It is nearly complete.
The moment my consciousness dissolves, the knowledge will lock permanently into your mind and you will have roughly five minutes to flee this place before the collapse triggers."
"Five minutes...?" Harper’s breath hitched.
"You have the sand-meld," Nitocris assured her.
"With the formulas I have gifted you, you can slip through the outer walls as fluid dust...
You will easily escape before the stone falls.
I have caused you enough terror today, Harper Whitmore so I will not allow you to die in my grave."
Nitocris closed Harper’s physical eyes, resting her forehead against her own knuckles with a deep peaceful stillness settling over her features.
"You know..." Nitocris whispered into the quiet rotunda, her voice carrying a fragile nostalgic warmth.

"In all my centuries of war, during the First Rift, and throughout the long dark years I spent sleeping within the cold steel of that khopesh, I never truly had anyone I could call a proper friend..."
Harper’s astral form floated motionless in the air, listening in silence.
"A Per-aa must always be an icon," the ancient woman murmured.
"A statue of bronze and gold...
You cannot show fear to your soldiers...
You cannot show doubt to your ministers...

But these past few days, sitting on your bedside table, listening to you complain about everything, listening to you laugh about silly mortal garments, hearing you speak about the world beyond the dunes..."
A soft genuine smile curved Harper’s physical lips.
"...and hearing you talk about that boy.
Silas Graves, was it?"
Harper’s ghostly form stiffened with a sudden fierce blush spreading across her translucent cheeks despite the horror of the day.
"He truly is an exceptionally lucky young man," Nitocris chuckled softly with her voice light and fond.
"To have a woman who looks upon him with such fierce uncompromising devotion...
I would have loved to meet him, you know.
To sit across a table, share a cup of spiced wine, and test whether his steel was truly worthy of holding your heart but my time here was long overdue.
The dead have no place among the living."
She raised Harper’s physical head, looking directly into Harper’s ghostly violet eyes with her expression pure and unburdened.
"Thank you, Harper," Nitocris whispered, her voice trembling with profound sincerity.
"For the sweets...
For the stories...
For allowing me to balance my debts under the sun.
In the end, I truly thought of you as my frien—"
CLACK!
The sound was microscopic but it made Nitocris abruptly freeze.

Harper’s physical body remained knelt on the tiles with her right hand pressed to the floor, but the black mana radiating from the magic circle instantly calcified in mid-air, hanging suspended like frozen red lightning.
Floating beside her, Harper’s astral spirit tried to drift forward, and found herself utterly paralyzed as the air in the rotunda didn’t move.
The dust motes floating through the sunbeams stopped dead in their tracks.
The distant flags atop the palace spires ceased their fluttering.
Even the distant roar of the city outside vanished, replaced by an unnatural void of complete deprivation of senses.
’What is this?!’ Harper screamed in the silent prison of her mind. ’Why can’t I move?!’
Nitocris’s green pupils contracted to needle-points.
Inside Harper’s physical chest, the heart stopped beating though this was not from damage, but because time itself had been forcibly arrested.
STEP!
The sound of a single deliberate footstep echoed through the frozen rotunda.
STEP!
STEP!
From the empty air five paces in front of the kneeling body, a thick billowing shroud of golden iridescent mist began to bleed into reality.
The mist didn’t disperse at all... it swirled violently, coalescing into the towering translucent figure of a man hovering three feet above the lapis floor.
He was large, draped in magnificent ancient ceremonial robes of beaten gold and deep azure silk that seemed to constantly shift and ripple like liquid sunlight.
His skin was flawless, radiating a blinding divine bronze sheen, his long golden hair crowned with an ornate imperial diadem depicting an undulating winged serpent.
His face was impossibly handsome, yet etched with an expression of utterly nauseating vanity.
A wide condescending amused grin stretched across his golden lips.
"Hoho~" the entity chuckled, his voice echoing through the frozen space like the ringing of a thousand silver bells.
He tapped his chin with a manicured glowing finger, his golden eyes sweeping over the slaughtered domestic wing with exaggerated delight.
"Well, well, well!" the figure proclaimed, his voice dripping with grandiose self-mythologizing arrogance.
"Look at what my adorable, impatient little splinter has managed to accomplish in my absence!
Truly, what a magnificent little bloodbath!
You always were such an efficient little butcher, weren’t you, my dear?"

chapters.title: Chapter 608: Death And Rebirth [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Nitocris’s soul raged against the paralysis and with an agonizing soul-tearing effort, she managed to force Harper’s physical jaw open by half an inch.
"Why..." Nitocris rasped through Harper’s throat, her voice shaking with horror. "Why are you here?! How are you here?!"
The golden entity pressed a hand against his chest, letting out an offended gasp.

"How rude! You don’t even greet your own creator with proper reverence?" the man scoffed, tossing his golden hair over his shoulder with a flourishing wave of his hand. "Allow me to introduce myself to our lovely little audience, though I am certain she already remembers my boundless magnificence! I am Ititius! The Architect of the Sun-Veil! The Supreme Father of the Great Dunes! The One True God of the Sand!"
Harper’s astral spirit watched in paralyzed sanity-shattering terror.
’Ititius...’ Harper’s thoughts screamed, remembering the Secret Realm... How could she forget?
’The voice from the secret realm... Thor already defeated her!’
Ititius floated closer, hovering inches above Harper’s physical face, looking down at Nitocris with an amused patronizing sneer.

"You are merely a fragmented pathetic little splinter of my glorious whole, aren’t you?" Ititius mocked, resting his hands on his hips. "A tiny discarded shard left sleeping inside that rusty old sickle-sword... But I must admit, I genuinely appreciate what you’ve done with the place! The decor was terribly outdated, and you’ve given the palace such a lovely coat of ash!"
His golden eyes narrowed, gleaming with sharp malice.

"And best of all..." Ititius chuckled, leaning down until his glowing face was inches from Harper’s nose. "...thanks to all of this delightful, energetic slaughter, you provided the exact exquisite passage required for my soul to locate its way back to this miserable sphere!"
"How..." Nitocris choked out with blood leaking from the corner of Harper’s lips as she fought the divine suppression. "My true body died in the abyss!"
Ititius threw his head back, letting out a sharp dramatic peel of laughter that shook the quartz walls.

"Destroyed?! Me?! A God?!" Ititius sneered, looking at her as if she were an uneducated child. "Ah, the pitiful short-sighted arrogance of mortals! Did you truly believe a being of my sublime intellect would leave his divine continuity anchored to a single fragile core in a flooded basement? Please... That bloated carcass in my Secret Realm was merely a puppet or what I would like to call a decorative distraction!"
He raised his glowing hand, admiring his fingernails.

"I have died several times across the turning of the centuries, my dear splinter! And every single time, I left an indelible dormant anchor hidden across the cosmic network... That man managed to intercept me twice but there will not be a third... since he doesn’t know about this one, a piece of my consciousness was tucked away inside a classified divine relic I pawned off to that gullible idiot in the northern pantheon centuries ago but a dormant soul needs a beacon to cross the waking threshold... It needs a massive concentration of blood-sacrifice and a matching soul-frequency to tear the veil open even with those Engines!"
His grin widened, turning hideously sharp.

"And who better to provide that beacon than my own sweet vengeful little shadow?" Ititius laughed, gesturing to the slaughtered palace. "You slaughtered all these people and you drowned the citadel in the exact genetic frequency of our bloodline... The resonance between your soul and my distant fragment blazed like a supernova across the void! You thought you were executing an independent vendetta, my darling? Hah! Every swing of that khopesh, every drop of blood you turned to glass, was merely turning the key to my grand resurrection... You played your part in my master plan with breathtaking perfection! I was beginning to wonder when you would come out, why the hell did you take so long?"
He had planned this... Ititius had planned this for a very long time.
’No...’ Nitocris’s thoughts echoed in pure agonizing despair. ’I didn’t balance the debt... I summoned this devil back to the world...’
"Now then," Ititius sighed, his tone turning brisk, like a landlord preparing to evict an unruly tenant. "Playtime is over and the stage belongs to the master now."
SWOOSH!

Nitocris frantically tried to detonate the magic circle beneath her hand... hell she tried to ignite Harper’s core, desperate to blow the citadel into dust and desperate to take both of them down into the void but Ititius didn’t even look at the magic circle.
STEP!
He took a single casual stride through the air, closing the gap in zero seconds.
SMACK!
His glowing golden palm slammed down directly over Harper’s physical face.
"Out you go, trash," Ititius snarled.
SHRRRRRRRRRRRRRRK!
With a brutal violent upward jerk of his golden arm, Ititius literally tore Nitocris’s soul straight out of Harper’s physical skull.
"AGHHHHHHHH!" a piercing ethereal scream ripped through the rotunda!

Nitocris’s true spiritual form was violently dragged into the open air and she manifested not as Harper, but as the legendary First Per-aa, a breathtaking bronze-skinned woman clad in tattered white linen and gold bands with her long black hair whipping wildly as Ititius held her pinned by the jaw.
She thrashed frantically with her spiritual fists beating against his glowing golden forearm, but against the crushing weight of his divine grip, she was powerless.
Through her suffocating agony, Nitocris looked up into the handsome sneering face of the god holding her.

"Why..." Nitocris wept, her ethereal voice cracking in profound soul-shattering confusion. "Why are you doing this?! We were human! We fought to protect our people! Why did you cast away our name?! Why are you a man?!"
Ititius’s expression instantly darkened.
The condescending charm vanished, replaced by an ugly fury as the golden veins along his neck violently bulged, pulsating with sickening radioactive light.
"SILENCE, YOU INSIGNIFICANT SLAG!" Ititius roared, his voice dropping into a deafening screech of pure rage.
He squeezed his fingers with the golden joints grinding into Nitocris’s spiritual cheekbones with enough force to produce high-pitched crackling sparks of tearing soul-matter!

"When that treacherous whore Nefertari shoved our body into the rift," Ititius hissed, flecks of golden spit flying from his lips, "our physical vessel was torn to pieces by worms! We rotted in the dark for three hundred years! Do you know what I realized while our flesh was being digested in the mud?! I realized that humanity is weak! Humanity is pathetic, fragile, ungrateful garbage! They pray to gods that do not exist! They begged ’Ititius’ to save their crops, to spare their children!"
His golden eyes burned with psychotic madness.

"So I decided... If the world desires a god, I will become that god! I cast away that fragile weeping woman who bled for ungrateful peasants! I forged this divine immortal vessel from the raw stolen mana of the outer rifts... I am Ititius and you will address me with UNCONDITIONAL REVERENCE!"
He sneered down at her trembling form.

"I listened to your little speech earlier," Ititius mocked, his voice dripping with venomous derision. "’Balance the debt’? ’Extinguish the bloodline’? What small-minded peasant ambitions! You wanted to kill a few cousins and crawl into a ditch to die but I am a GOD! I do not want petty revenge! I want unconditional dominion! I will conquer this modern Khemet! I will subjugate the Powers of this world and I will drown this entire wretched planet in my power until every living soul kneels before my golden throne!"
He leaned closer, his fingers tightening until Nitocris’s jaw began to fracture into drifting white ash.
"...And you have outlived your usefulness."
Nitocris knew it was the end.
She stopped thrashing.
With her final fading scraps of strength, the legendary First Per-aa turned her spiritual head.
She looked past Ititius’s golden arm, locking her bronze eyes onto Harper’s paralyzed weeping soul floating in the air.
A soft sorrowful tear slipped from Nitocris’s eye.
"Harper..." Nitocris whispered, her voice barely a thread of sound. "I am sorry. I could not protect you..."
CRUNCH!
Ititius’s golden hand closed into a ruthless merciless fist.
SHATTER!
Nitocris’s spiritual skull imploded into a shower of brilliant pale-gold sparks!
Her soul unraveled in an instant, disintegrating into fine drifting spiritual ash that scattered into the cold air of the rotunda with her ancient existence completely erased from reality.
Harper’s astral spirit screamed though it was a silent wail of despair.
Ititius slowly lowered his glowing hand, dusting off his fingers with an arrogant satisfied scoff.
"Filthy splinter," he muttered, then he turned around as his golden eyes locked dead onto Harper’s floating translucent form.
He paused.
A slow vicious grin spread across his divine face as he tilted his head, recognizing the violet hue of her soul.
"Oh?" Ititius chuckled, his voice dropping into a low terrifying purr. "Well, well, well, what do we have here? Aren’t you that lovely little baggage that man was carrying through my secret realm?"
Harper’s spirit shuddered violently.

"Yes..." Ititius laughed, stepping through the frozen air toward her, his eyes blazing with incandescent sadistic glee. "It IS you! That man’s little pet! The man, beside that Lightning Goddess who thought he could mock a god and walk away unscathed!"
SWOOSH!
Before Harper could even form a thought to retreat—
BOOM!
Ititius’s golden fist blurred forward as he drove a massive condensed spiritual punch straight into Harper’s ethereal midsection.
SPLAT-GASP!
There was no physical blood, but the agonizing impact ripped the breath clean out of Harper’s soul...
Her astral form violently collapsed inward, folding around his fist with her consciousness shattering into blinding static-filled agony.
SQUEEZE.

With a cruel effortless twist of his fingers, Ititius compressed Harper’s entire sprawling spirit into a tiny helpless violet wisp of light, trapping her firmly within the palm of his hand as he brought the glowing wisp to his eye level, grinning until his teeth gleamed.

"This is truly magnificent..." Ititius purred, his voice shivering with sick vindictive anticipation. "The heavens have delivered the ultimate instrument into my hands! What better way to exact my vengeance than by wearing the flesh of the woman he loves? When he finally comes crawling to save you, I will use your own hands to rip his heart from his ribs!"
WHOOSH!
Ititius turned his gaze toward Harper’s empty motionless physical body kneeling on the floor.
"A splendid vessel," Ititius remarked. "Untamed, but full of potential."
WHOOSH!
The towering golden avatar of the ancient god dissolved into a blinding torrential stream of divine golden and black mana.

He surged forward, slamming violently into the crown of Harper’s physical head, forcing his immense primordial consciousness down into the biological nervous system, forcibly overwriting her soul-seats, sealing her suppressed violet spirit deep into the lightless suffocating basement of her own core.
CRACK-SNAP!

The temporal freeze instantly shattered as time resumed its unyielding flow... The dust motes fell to the floor; the wind howled through the shattered light as the distant sirens of the capital roared back to life.
Harper’s head snapped upward as her long purple hair whipped around her shoulders like a storm cloud!
BZZZZZZZZZZT!
When her physical eyelids tore open, the soft intelligent violet was completely gone.
In its place blazed a radioactive emerald-green radiance, veined with pulsating golden divine runes that swirled sickeningly around her pupils!
"AHAHAHAHAHA!"
Ititius threw Harper’s head back, an ear-splitting arrogant laugh tearing from Harper’s throat.
He flexed her physical fingers, rolling her shoulders, feeling the raw high-power output coursing through her newly conditioned meridians.

"What marvelous power!" Ititius roared, his voice carrying the double-layered resonance of Harper’s vocal cords and an ancient booming male thunder. "What an exquisite scabbard! The flesh is warm and the blood sings!"
He looked down at the massive unfinished magic circle carved into the lapis lazuli tiles beneath his boots.
"My foolish little splinter intended to use this array to collapse the palace and kill herself?" Ititius scoffed, shaking his head in mock disappointment. "What a catastrophic waste of a fine spell!"
He raised both of Harper’s arms into the air, spreading his fingers wide!
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Primordial divine mana, dense lightless black sand interwoven with blinding golden solar plasma, erupted from Harper’s palms, pouring into the runic circle like a broken dam.
The magic circle didn’t stop at the three-hundred-pace boundary of the palace rotunda...
It violently expanded!
BZZZZZZZT-CRACK!

The crimson-black lines tore through the palace walls, racing across the courtyard, leaping over the four-hundred-foot outer ramparts, and spreading like a web across the manicured gardens, the paved boulevards, and the private residential villas of the entire Inner District.
Deep within the dark suffocating prison of her own core, Harper’s tiny compressed spirit wept in horror.
’Stop, please, there are millions of people out there...’

Ititius smiled, his green-and-gold eyes gazing out through the shattered palace dome, sensing the terrified heartbeats of hundreds of thousands of Khemet citizens, noble families, and imperial retainers scrambling through the streets below.
"Why stop at the palace?" Ititius whispered, his grin stretching until Harper’s physical lips cracked and bled.
"Every soul in this city was born from the soil that betrayed me... Every mouth has eaten the bread grown from my stolen glory..."
The ancient god clenched Harper’s fists into tight absolute balls of death.
"All of you deserve to die."
Three miles away, at the grand security threshold of the Inner District.

Captain Al-Kadhir, the veteran border sentinel with the scarred chin who had checked Harper’s commercial ID at the turnstile barely an hour ago, was standing beside his armored guard booth, sweating profusely beneath his solar-quartz plate.
The city had descended into madness.
Minutes ago, every siren in the capital had begun wailing the catastrophic Code Red alert.

Rumors had spread like wildfire through the military comm-channels that the royal flagship had been obliterated in the desert and the Pharaoh-President was dead as a black sand entity had breached the High Citadel.

"Hold the gates!" Al-Kadhir bellowed through his helmet comms, trying to push back the frantic crowd of noble civilians and luxury tourists desperately trying to evacuate the district. "Maintain perimeter discipline! The High Marshals are organizing an orbital barrier! Do not stampede—"
HUMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM!
A sound unlike anything Al-Kadhir had ever heard in his forty years of service echoed through the earth...
The guard captain looked down at his boots and beneath the polished asphalt of the grand avenue, glowing razor-sharp lines of pitch-black and blinding golden were violently burning through the stone.
"What is that...?" a tourist screamed, pointing toward the center of the district.
Al-Kadhir slowly raised his head.

Rising from the peak of the White Citadel three miles away was a colossal heaven-piercing pillar of swirling black sand and blinding golden solar fire, easily a half-mile wide, punching clean through the thermosphere!

And hovering at the apex of that apocalyptic pillar, barely visible against the burning sun, stood the silhouette of a single woman with long purple hair with her arms outstretched like an angel of annihilation.
Al-Kadhir’s breath caught in his throat.
’W-who is tha—’
"May the gods have mercy..." Al-Kadhir whispered, his hands dropping uselessly to his sides.
KABOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The spell detonated.

That man managed to intercept me twice but there will not be a third... since he doesn’t know about this one, a piece of my consciousness was tucked away inside a classified divine relic I pawned off to that gullible idiot in the northern pantheon centuries ago but a dormant soul needs a beacon to cross the waking threshold...
It needs a massive concentration of blood-sacrifice and a matching soul-frequency to tear the veil open even with those Engines!"
His grin widened, turning hideously sharp.
"And who better to provide that beacon than my own sweet vengeful little shadow?" Ititius laughed, gesturing to the slaughtered palace.
"You slaughtered all these people and you drowned the citadel in the exact genetic frequency of our bloodline...
The resonance between your soul and my distant fragment blazed like a supernova across the void!
You thought you were executing an independent vendetta, my darling?
Hah!
Every swing of that khopesh, every drop of blood you turned to glass, was merely turning the key to my grand resurrection...
You played your part in my master plan with breathtaking perfection!
I was beginning to wonder when you would come out, why the hell did you take so long?"
He had planned this...
Ititius had planned this for a very long time.
’No...’ Nitocris’s thoughts echoed in pure agonizing despair. ’I didn’t balance the debt...
I summoned this devil back to the world...’
"Now then," Ititius sighed, his tone turning brisk, like a landlord preparing to evict an unruly tenant.
"Playtime is over and the stage belongs to the master now."
SWOOSH!

Nitocris frantically tried to detonate the magic circle beneath her hand... hell she tried to ignite Harper’s core, desperate to blow the citadel into dust and desperate to take both of them down into the void but Ititius didn’t even look at the magic circle.
STEP!
He took a single casual stride through the air, closing the gap in zero seconds.
SMACK!
His glowing golden palm slammed down directly over Harper’s physical face.
"Out you go, trash," Ititius snarled.
SHRRRRRRRRRRRRRRK!
With a brutal violent upward jerk of his golden arm, Ititius literally tore Nitocris’s soul straight out of Harper’s physical skull.
"AGHHHHHHHH!" a piercing ethereal scream ripped through the rotunda!

Nitocris’s true spiritual form was violently dragged into the open air and she manifested not as Harper, but as the legendary First Per-aa, a breathtaking bronze-skinned woman clad in tattered white linen and gold bands with her long black hair whipping wildly as Ititius held her pinned by the jaw.
She thrashed frantically with her spiritual fists beating against his glowing golden forearm, but against the crushing weight of his divine grip, she was powerless.
Through her suffocating agony, Nitocris looked up into the handsome sneering face of the god holding her.
"Why..." Nitocris wept, her ethereal voice cracking in profound soul-shattering confusion.
"Why are you doing this?!
We were human!
We fought to protect our people!
Why did you cast away our name?!
Why are you a man?!"
Ititius’s expression instantly darkened.
The condescending charm vanished, replaced by an ugly fury as the golden veins along his neck violently bulged, pulsating with sickening radioactive light.
"SILENCE, YOU INSIGNIFICANT SLAG!" Ititius roared, his voice dropping into a deafening screech of pure rage.
He squeezed his fingers with the golden joints grinding into Nitocris’s spiritual cheekbones with enough force to produce high-pitched crackling sparks of tearing soul-matter!
"When that treacherous whore Nefertari shoved our body into the rift," Ititius hissed, flecks of golden spit flying from his lips, "our physical vessel was torn to pieces by worms!
We rotted in the dark for three hundred years!
Do you know what I realized while our flesh was being digested in the mud?!
I realized that humanity is weak!
Humanity is pathetic, fragile, ungrateful garbage!
They pray to gods that do not exist!
They begged ’Ititius’ to save their crops, to spare their children!"
His golden eyes burned with psychotic madness.
"So I decided...
If the world desires a god, I will become that god!
I cast away that fragile weeping woman who bled for ungrateful peasants!
I forged this divine immortal vessel from the raw stolen mana of the outer rifts...
I am Ititius and you will address me with UNCONDITIONAL REVERENCE!"
He sneered down at her trembling form.
"I listened to your little speech earlier," Ititius mocked, his voice dripping with venomous derision.
"’Balance the debt’? ’Extinguish the bloodline’?
What small-minded peasant ambitions!
You wanted to kill a few cousins and crawl into a ditch to die but I am a GOD!
I do not want petty revenge!
I want unconditional dominion!
I will conquer this modern Khemet!
I will subjugate the Powers of this world and I will drown this entire wretched planet in my power until every living soul kneels before my golden throne!"
He leaned closer, his fingers tightening until Nitocris’s jaw began to fracture into drifting white ash.
"...And you have outlived your usefulness."
Nitocris knew it was the end.
She stopped thrashing.
With her final fading scraps of strength, the legendary First Per-aa turned her spiritual head.
She looked past Ititius’s golden arm, locking her bronze eyes onto Harper’s paralyzed weeping soul floating in the air.
A soft sorrowful tear slipped from Nitocris’s eye.
"Harper..." Nitocris whispered, her voice barely a thread of sound.
"I am sorry.
I could not protect you..."
CRUNCH!
Ititius’s golden hand closed into a ruthless merciless fist.
SHATTER!
Nitocris’s spiritual skull imploded into a shower of brilliant pale-gold sparks!
Her soul unraveled in an instant, disintegrating into fine drifting spiritual ash that scattered into the cold air of the rotunda with her ancient existence completely erased from reality.
Harper’s astral spirit screamed though it was a silent wail of despair.
Ititius slowly lowered his glowing hand, dusting off his fingers with an arrogant satisfied scoff.
"Filthy splinter," he muttered, then he turned around as his golden eyes locked dead onto Harper’s floating translucent form.
He paused.
A slow vicious grin spread across his divine face as he tilted his head, recognizing the violet hue of her soul.
"Oh?" Ititius chuckled, his voice dropping into a low terrifying purr.
"Well, well, well, what do we have here?
Aren’t you that lovely little baggage that man was carrying through my secret realm?"
Harper’s spirit shuddered violently.
"Yes..." Ititius laughed, stepping through the frozen air toward her, his eyes blazing with incandescent sadistic glee.
"It IS you!
That man’s little pet!
The man, beside that Lightning Goddess who thought he could mock a god and walk away unscathed!"
SWOOSH!
Before Harper could even form a thought to retreat—
BOOM!
Ititius’s golden fist blurred forward as he drove a massive condensed spiritual punch straight into Harper’s ethereal midsection.
SPLAT-GASP!
There was no physical blood, but the agonizing impact ripped the breath clean out of Harper’s soul...
Her astral form violently collapsed inward, folding around his fist with her consciousness shattering into blinding static-filled agony.
SQUEEZE.

With a cruel effortless twist of his fingers, Ititius compressed Harper’s entire sprawling spirit into a tiny helpless violet wisp of light, trapping her firmly within the palm of his hand as he brought the glowing wisp to his eye level, grinning until his teeth gleamed.
"This is truly magnificent..." Ititius purred, his voice shivering with sick vindictive anticipation.
"The heavens have delivered the ultimate instrument into my hands!
What better way to exact my vengeance than by wearing the flesh of the woman he loves?
When he finally comes crawling to save you, I will use your own hands to rip his heart from his ribs!"
WHOOSH!
Ititius turned his gaze toward Harper’s empty motionless physical body kneeling on the floor.
"A splendid vessel," Ititius remarked.
"Untamed, but full of potential."
WHOOSH!
The towering golden avatar of the ancient god dissolved into a blinding torrential stream of divine golden and black mana.

He surged forward, slamming violently into the crown of Harper’s physical head, forcing his immense primordial consciousness down into the biological nervous system, forcibly overwriting her soul-seats, sealing her suppressed violet spirit deep into the lightless suffocating basement of her own core.
CRACK-SNAP!
The temporal freeze instantly shattered as time resumed its unyielding flow...
The dust motes fell to the floor; the wind howled through the shattered light as the distant sirens of the capital roared back to life.
Harper’s head snapped upward as her long purple hair whipped around her shoulders like a storm cloud!
BZZZZZZZZZZT!
When her physical eyelids tore open, the soft intelligent violet was completely gone.
In its place blazed a radioactive emerald-green radiance, veined with pulsating golden divine runes that swirled sickeningly around her pupils!
"AHAHAHAHAHA!"
Ititius threw Harper’s head back, an ear-splitting arrogant laugh tearing from Harper’s throat.
He flexed her physical fingers, rolling her shoulders, feeling the raw high-power output coursing through her newly conditioned meridians.
"What marvelous power!" Ititius roared, his voice carrying the double-layered resonance of Harper’s vocal cords and an ancient booming male thunder.
"What an exquisite scabbard!
The flesh is warm and the blood sings!"
He looked down at the massive unfinished magic circle carved into the lapis lazuli tiles beneath his boots.
"My foolish little splinter intended to use this array to collapse the palace and kill herself?" Ititius scoffed, shaking his head in mock disappointment.
"What a catastrophic waste of a fine spell!"
He raised both of Harper’s arms into the air, spreading his fingers wide!
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Primordial divine mana, dense lightless black sand interwoven with blinding golden solar plasma, erupted from Harper’s palms, pouring into the runic circle like a broken dam.
The magic circle didn’t stop at the three-hundred-pace boundary of the palace rotunda...
It violently expanded!
BZZZZZZZT-CRACK!

The crimson-black lines tore through the palace walls, racing across the courtyard, leaping over the four-hundred-foot outer ramparts, and spreading like a web across the manicured gardens, the paved boulevards, and the private residential villas of the entire Inner District.
Deep within the dark suffocating prison of her own core, Harper’s tiny compressed spirit wept in horror.
’Stop, please, there are millions of people out there...’

Ititius smiled, his green-and-gold eyes gazing out through the shattered palace dome, sensing the terrified heartbeats of hundreds of thousands of Khemet citizens, noble families, and imperial retainers scrambling through the streets below.
"Why stop at the palace?" Ititius whispered, his grin stretching until Harper’s physical lips cracked and bled.
"Every soul in this city was born from the soil that betrayed me...
Every mouth has eaten the bread grown from my stolen glory..."
The ancient god clenched Harper’s fists into tight absolute balls of death.
"All of you deserve to die."
Three miles away, at the grand security threshold of the Inner District.

Captain Al-Kadhir, the veteran border sentinel with the scarred chin who had checked Harper’s commercial ID at the turnstile barely an hour ago, was standing beside his armored guard booth, sweating profusely beneath his solar-quartz plate.
The city had descended into madness.
Minutes ago, every siren in the capital had begun wailing the catastrophic Code Red alert.

Rumors had spread like wildfire through the military comm-channels that the royal flagship had been obliterated in the desert and the Pharaoh-President was dead as a black sand entity had breached the High Citadel.
"Hold the gates!" Al-Kadhir bellowed through his helmet comms, trying to push back the frantic crowd of noble civilians and luxury tourists desperately trying to evacuate the district.
"Maintain perimeter discipline!
The High Marshals are organizing an orbital barrier!
Do not stampede—"
HUMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM!
A sound unlike anything Al-Kadhir had ever heard in his forty years of service echoed through the earth...
The guard captain looked down at his boots and beneath the polished asphalt of the grand avenue, glowing razor-sharp lines of pitch-black and blinding golden were violently burning through the stone.
"What is that...?" a tourist screamed, pointing toward the center of the district.
Al-Kadhir slowly raised his head.

Rising from the peak of the White Citadel three miles away was a colossal heaven-piercing pillar of swirling black sand and blinding golden solar fire, easily a half-mile wide, punching clean through the thermosphere!

And hovering at the apex of that apocalyptic pillar, barely visible against the burning sun, stood the silhouette of a single woman with long purple hair with her arms outstretched like an angel of annihilation.
Al-Kadhir’s breath caught in his throat.
’W-who is tha—’
"May the gods have mercy..." Al-Kadhir whispered, his hands dropping uselessly to his sides.
KABOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The spell detonated.

chapters.title: Chapter 609: Murder On My Mind [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: It didn’t release an ordinary shockwave.
A colossal expanding dome of dense lightless black sand and pressurized divine plasma erupted outward from the citadel, traveling at ten thousand miles per hour...
The White Citadel, the eight-hundred-year-old stepped pyramid of polished titanium and gold, was instantly vitrified into black glass and pulverized into fine ash in the span of a single second.
BOOOOOMMMMMm!
The wave rolled forward, swallowing three square miles of the capital’s most opulent district...
Palaces of marble, multi-story luxury hotels, ancient monuments, manicured parks, and seventy thousand fleeing citizens and guards were washed over by the black wall.
Al-Kadhir didn’t even have time to close his eyes.
The black sand touched his armor and his steel, his flesh and even his screaming mouth froze into solid crystal.
SNAP!
The glass shattered.

Within three seconds, the entire Inner District of Iunu, the seat of the Sun-Crown’s imperial power, was completely wiped off the face of the Earth, leaving behind only a colossal three-mile-wide crater of drifting, lightless black sand beneath the weeping desert sun.
[30 Minutes Earlier]
DING!
The hum of the central cooling station inside the penthouse suite of the Grand Oasis Palace possessed that hush unique to five-star hospitality.
’Not that I understand it... It’s my first time...’

It was designed to suppress the sweltering kiln of the southern desert, reducing the dry kiln-hot temperature of the Great Dunes to a sterile one that smelled of mountain mint and distilled spring water.
"Haah..."
Silas stood in the center of the spacious private quarters, letting out a slow breath as his fingers methodically worked his silk tie loose from the stiff collar of his charcoal dress shirt.
He looked around the room.

The architectural aesthetic was an aggressive blend of dynastic wealth and modernized engineering... The place had soaring arched ceilings ribbed with polished petrified cedar, baseboards carved from rose-veined alabaster and wide floor tiles forged from crushed lapis lazuli that had their own cooling as well.
’We arrived not too long ago,’ he thought, his thumb absently rubbing the sore skin beneath his eyes.
TICK-TICK-TICK!
The watch in the room currently indicated a sharp four-hour jump forward from the timezone of Europa.

The transition had been a lot... One moment, he was in Europa and the next, he was clearing the high-priority immigration turnstiles of the Khemet Dominion under a clean corporate passport issued by the Directorate.
’This is actually my first time officially in another country...’
A faint self-deprecating smirk touched the corner of his mouth.

To a kid who had grown up in the damp rat-chewed corners of Sector Five, measuring the passage of weeks by how many copper credits he could scrape from stripping burnt wiring out of condemned alchemical turbines, the concept of an international border had been an unattainable myth.
The world beyond Europa’s perimeter had felt like another dimension entirely, reserved exclusively for the smiling oligarchs, Lords, and dynasties paraded across holo-screens.
’It feels nice...’
His standard Europa passport had cleared the gate without a hitch though he had a little help from Evelyn.
Wealth, combined with verified clean credit credentials from the LAB, had a way of turning even the strictest southern border marshals remarkably accommodating.
’Maybe we would have done a proper trip if it was possible,’ Silas mused, his gaze drifting toward the luggage stacked neatly by the cedar wardrobe.
He certainly had the capital now.
His private accounts were swollen with spirit credits, and his storage in Blessed Land was choked with enough ore to probably buy out an entire commercial district.

If the world weren’t unraveling at the seams, he could have rented a gilded private skiff, sailed down the clear channels of the southern lakes, and let Lia spend an entire week eating candied dates and buying ridiculously overpriced brass trinkets with Kaede and Penelope.
CLICK!
The heavy brass handle of the primary suite door turned smoothly.
"Master Silas?"
Martha stepped into the room, balancing a circular tray of beaten silver in her hands.
As always, the middle-aged housekeeper was dressed in her pristine starch-stiff maid’s uniform, her grey-streaked hair pinned into an immaculate knot.
Her face bore the faint lines of travel fatigue, but her posture was steady, anchored by decades of professional composure.

"I took the liberty of consulting the kitchen staff on the lower floors," Martha said softly, stepping across the lapis tiles with soundless grace. "The tea blends of Khemet are quite renowned for restoring core circulation after high-altitude flight... This is an infusion of dried crimson bush, desert lotus nectar, and shaved sun-root."
She set the tray upon a low table of petrified oak, pouring a single cup from a slender long-spouted bronze kettle.
A curling plume of fragrant white steam rose into the cooled air, carrying a sharp scent that immediately cut through the stale smell of the aircraft’s pressurized cabin.
Silas stepped over, accepting the delicate porcelain cup as he brought the rim to his lips, testing the heat, and took a slow sip.
The liquid was surprisingly deep.

It began with an earthy taste that settled heavy on the tongue, followed almost immediately by a bright sweet bloom of lotus and a sudden prickling heat that traveled down his throat, going down and sending a gentle warmth into the meridians of his chest.
"It’s good," Silas admitted, taking a second deeper sip and nodding in genuine appreciation. "Very smooth as well... The sun-root cuts the bitterness nicely."
He lowered the cup, looking at Martha. "How are the girls doing?"

"They are doing properly, Master," Martha replied, folding her hands neatly over her white apron, her expression softening with quiet relief. "Miss Lia was somewhat dizzy from the pressure changes during the descent, but Miss Kaede has been hovering over her like a dutiful sister, ensuring she drank her fruit juices... They are currently inspecting the automated lotus-bath in the secondary suite."
She paused, glancing back toward the corridor.
"And Penelope?" Silas asked.

"She is... significantly calmer now, Master Silas," Martha murmured, her voice lowering. "Having crossed the border, and knowing that you are within shouting distance, seems to have lifted the worst of the terror from her shoulders... She drank half a bowl of warm broth and has ceased trembling. The child carries a great deal of pride, but she was genuinely terrified for her sister."
"I’m thankful for that," Silas said, staring into the dark amber depths of the tea.
He took another sip, letting the heat settle into his core.
Bringing the girls along hadn’t been a frivolous choice at all, now that he was thinking about it...
Harper had been snatched from her private residence under the nose of her family’s security detail by an entity that moved through shadows and manipulated minds.
Penelope was Lia’s genuine friend, constantly in and out of the Silverleaf estate.
If whoever had hijacked Harper’s body knew about Harper’s domestic routines, they knew about Lia.
Leaving Lia and Martha alone in Europa while he crossed to Khemet would have left his back exposed.
If an enemy struck at his home while he was thousands of miles away in the desert, no amount of acceleration would get him back in time to stop it.

Keeping them inside his immediate sensory umbrella, guarded by high-grade barriers and stationed in one of the most fortified tourist strongholds in the city, was the only way he could operate without his mind tearing itself apart with paranoia.
’As for Kaede’s brother...’
Silas felt an involuntary sharp shiver run down the length of his spine.
...Minamoto.
The memory of the private airfield in Europa was still uncomfortably fresh in his head.
The man had been surprisingly accommodating on paper.

Tall, weathered, and lean, wrapped in a long sea-gray overcoat, Minamoto looked exactly like what he was... a Level 10 Lord who spent most of his life on maritime subjugation quests along the coast of the Sovereign Realm.
A silver sedan sat idling on the tarmac behind him, and he hadn’t raised a single objection when Silas approached him to explain the emergency flight.
In fact, he had immediately pulled four of his best officers, seasoned second-stage combatants trained in defensive barriers and attacks, to accompany the party as sworn bodyguards.
Silas had been genuinely thankful for the gesture.
...Right up until the moment Kaede had happily grabbed Silas’s hand at the boarding ramp, beaming about her very first international flight.
In that single second, the polite stoic smile on Minamoto’s face hadn’t shifted by a millimeter.
Yet, the spiritual pressure radiating from the man’s core had plummeted into an absolute zero.
’Haah, scary dude.’
Silas’s instincts had screamed in alarm as a razor-sharp concentrated aura of pure killing intent had brushed past his neck like the unsheathed edge of an ancient katana.
Silas had stood there on the tarmac, forcing his facial muscles into a mask of pure polite indifference and now that he thought about it.

’Well... he is her older brother. If some strange guy showed up at an airfield asking to fly Lia to a foreign continent on two hours’ notice, I probably would have flattened his car with an iron girder before he finished the sentence...’
Silas took a final sip, emptying the porcelain cup, and handed it back to the tray with a soft metallic clatter.

"Tell the escorts to maintain a rotating two-man watch at the main suite entrance and the secondary fire stairwell," Silas instructed calmly. "Tell them to keep their spells active... I have a bad feeling about this city, Martha."
Martha took the tray, her eyes reflecting the gravity in his voice.
"Understood, Master Silas. Are you going to begin looking for Miss Harper now?"

"Yeah," Silas said, rolling his shoulders back until his spine gave three sharp muted pops. "I’ll head out into the Airport first and ask around the terminals to check if any private charters or freight shuttles logged an irregular landing within the last six hours."
"Please be careful, sir," Martha murmured, offering a deep respectful bow. "We will await your return."
"Keep the deadbolts engaged," Silas added as the housekeeper turned and slipped quietly through the door, sealing the heavy oak panel behind her.
The suite fell silent once more.
Silas walked toward the center of the Persian rug, planting his feet shoulder-width apart.
He raised his arms, stretching his torso from left to right with his joints creaking under the subtle tension of his mana channels.
’This entire situation is completely twisted.’
He let out a long frustrated hiss through his teeth.
...What was so special about the Khemet Dominion?
Harper was a brilliant woman. She was sharp, calculating, and exceptionally gifted at what she did but in terms of raw martial output, she was only Second Stage or perhaps even first...?
That was no insult to her.

If an ancient foreign entity, a rogue Lord, or a black-market cabal wanted a vessel to infiltrate a foreign country, there were tens of thousands of seasoned high-tier Awakened walking the streets of Europa.
There were third-stage mercenaries, temple champions, and combat-hardened Lords whose bodies could withstand ten times the stress Harper’s could bear so why take Harper?
Whatever had taken her hadn’t been shopping for the strongest vessel. It had wanted her, her body, her blood, or her bond with him.
’I hope you’re safe...’ Silas thought, his eyes narrowing into cold slits.
Her face rose unbidden in his mind making him sigh.
’I never really knew I liked her this much...’
Why else would her face be popping up in his mind this much...? She was really beautiful.

The violet eyes behind her wire-rimmed glasses, the way she pushed them up her nose whenever she was saying something clever, the smirk she wore when she thought she’d caught him off guard, and the ridiculous confidence with which she had once tried out ’Silas-kun’ before he set her straight.
Then the picture bent, and it was Penelope’s trembling voice describing a sickening green glint spinning behind those same violet eyes.
His fists clenched until his knuckles cracked with his jaw setting into a hard merciless line.
’If they lay a single hand on her head... I’ll kill them.’
He wasn’t going to negotiate and he wasn’t going to hold an inquiry.
Whoever was pulling the strings behind that green light would die.

The only question was how agonizing the process was going to be. If Harper was unharmed, it would be quick but if she had been harmed, tortured, or broken... he would unravel their meridians grain by grain.
’I’m really starting to sound like a bloodthirsty cultivator,’ Silas scoffed inwardly, catching the violent drift of his own thoughts.
Yet, as he looked out through the curtains at the blazing white skyline of Iunu, a bizarre gnawing intuition refused to leave his mind.
A city of white stone, surrounded on all sides by an endless hostile desert.
...Sand.
’It couldn’t be that fucker... right?’
The name surfaced in his mind like a rancid corpse bobbing to the top of a stagnant pond.
’Ititius.’
It was a wild and almost irrational leap of logic but in his entire life, Silas had only ever encountered one singular monstrous entity that treated sand as an extension of divine authority.
And yet, the reality made no sense.
’How the hell does that even work?’ Silas asked himself, his brow furrowing deeply. ’How resilient can one bastard be?!’
First, during the Secret Realm, Thor had literally swatted the god’s divine avatar out of the sky with an attack of cosmic thunder, vaporizing his physical form into ash.
Then, as Silas was going home with Elora, Silas had personally flooded him with a water spell, drowning his spiritual remnant in crushing pressure.
And then, as if that weren’t enough, when a residual fragment of the creature’s soul had attempted to hijack Kadi’s body inside his territory of Blessed Land... the Territory had purged him as well.
So...
How did a creature survive being erased three separate times across three different planes of existence...? Was the bastard made of spiritual cockroaches...?
BZZZZ-BZZZZ!
The black phone on the low table vibrated sharply with its blue notification diode flashing in rapid double-pulse bursts and Silas walked over, picking up the phone.𝚏𝕣𝕖𝚎𝚠𝚎𝚋𝚗𝐨𝐯𝕖𝕝.𝕔𝐨𝕞
’It can’t be more bad news, right?’
