A curling plume of fragrant white steam rose into the cooled air, carrying a sharp scent that immediately cut through the stale smell of the aircraft’s pressurized cabin.
Silas stepped over, accepting the delicate porcelain cup as he brought the rim to his lips, testing the heat, and took a slow sip.
The liquid was surprisingly deep.

It began with an earthy taste that settled heavy on the tongue, followed almost immediately by a bright sweet bloom of lotus and a sudden prickling heat that traveled down his throat, going down and sending a gentle warmth into the meridians of his chest.
"It’s good," Silas admitted, taking a second deeper sip and nodding in genuine appreciation.
"Very smooth as well...
The sun-root cuts the bitterness nicely."
He lowered the cup, looking at Martha.
"How are the girls doing?"
"They are doing properly, Master," Martha replied, folding her hands neatly over her white apron, her expression softening with quiet relief.
"Miss Lia was somewhat dizzy from the pressure changes during the descent, but Miss Kaede has been hovering over her like a dutiful sister, ensuring she drank her fruit juices...
They are currently inspecting the automated lotus-bath in the secondary suite."
She paused, glancing back toward the corridor.
"And Penelope?" Silas asked.
"She is... significantly calmer now, Master Silas," Martha murmured, her voice lowering.
"Having crossed the border, and knowing that you are within shouting distance, seems to have lifted the worst of the terror from her shoulders...
She drank half a bowl of warm broth and has ceased trembling.
The child carries a great deal of pride, but she was genuinely terrified for her sister."
"I’m thankful for that," Silas said, staring into the dark amber depths of the tea.
He took another sip, letting the heat settle into his core.
Bringing the girls along hadn’t been a frivolous choice at all, now that he was thinking about it...
Harper had been snatched from her private residence under the nose of her family’s security detail by an entity that moved through shadows and manipulated minds.
Penelope was Lia’s genuine friend, constantly in and out of the Silverleaf estate.
If whoever had hijacked Harper’s body knew about Harper’s domestic routines, they knew about Lia.
Leaving Lia and Martha alone in Europa while he crossed to Khemet would have left his back exposed.
If an enemy struck at his home while he was thousands of miles away in the desert, no amount of acceleration would get him back in time to stop it.

Keeping them inside his immediate sensory umbrella, guarded by high-grade barriers and stationed in one of the most fortified tourist strongholds in the city, was the only way he could operate without his mind tearing itself apart with paranoia.
’As for Kaede’s brother...’
Silas felt an involuntary sharp shiver run down the length of his spine.
...Minamoto.
The memory of the private airfield in Europa was still uncomfortably fresh in his head.
The man had been surprisingly accommodating on paper.

Tall, weathered, and lean, wrapped in a long sea-gray overcoat, Minamoto looked exactly like what he was... a Level 10 Lord who spent most of his life on maritime subjugation quests along the coast of the Sovereign Realm.
A silver sedan sat idling on the tarmac behind him, and he hadn’t raised a single objection when Silas approached him to explain the emergency flight.
In fact, he had immediately pulled four of his best officers, seasoned second-stage combatants trained in defensive barriers and attacks, to accompany the party as sworn bodyguards.
Silas had been genuinely thankful for the gesture.
...Right up until the moment Kaede had happily grabbed Silas’s hand at the boarding ramp, beaming about her very first international flight.
In that single second, the polite stoic smile on Minamoto’s face hadn’t shifted by a millimeter.
Yet, the spiritual pressure radiating from the man’s core had plummeted into an absolute zero.
’Haah, scary dude.’
Silas’s instincts had screamed in alarm as a razor-sharp concentrated aura of pure killing intent had brushed past his neck like the unsheathed edge of an ancient katana.
Silas had stood there on the tarmac, forcing his facial muscles into a mask of pure polite indifference and now that he thought about it.
’Well... he is her older brother.

If some strange guy showed up at an airfield asking to fly Lia to a foreign continent on two hours’ notice, I probably would have flattened his car with an iron girder before he finished the sentence...’
Silas took a final sip, emptying the porcelain cup, and handed it back to the tray with a soft metallic clatter.
"Tell the escorts to maintain a rotating two-man watch at the main suite entrance and the secondary fire stairwell," Silas instructed calmly.
"Tell them to keep their spells active...
I have a bad feeling about this city, Martha."
Martha took the tray, her eyes reflecting the gravity in his voice.
"Understood, Master Silas.
Are you going to begin looking for Miss Harper now?"
"Yeah," Silas said, rolling his shoulders back until his spine gave three sharp muted pops.
"I’ll head out into the Airport first and ask around the terminals to check if any private charters or freight shuttles logged an irregular landing within the last six hours."
"Please be careful, sir," Martha murmured, offering a deep respectful bow.
"We will await your return."
"Keep the deadbolts engaged," Silas added as the housekeeper turned and slipped quietly through the door, sealing the heavy oak panel behind her.
The suite fell silent once more.
Silas walked toward the center of the Persian rug, planting his feet shoulder-width apart.
He raised his arms, stretching his torso from left to right with his joints creaking under the subtle tension of his mana channels.
’This entire situation is completely twisted.’
He let out a long frustrated hiss through his teeth.
...What was so special about the Khemet Dominion?
Harper was a brilliant woman.
She was sharp, calculating, and exceptionally gifted at what she did but in terms of raw martial output, she was only Second Stage or perhaps even first...?
That was no insult to her.

If an ancient foreign entity, a rogue Lord, or a black-market cabal wanted a vessel to infiltrate a foreign country, there were tens of thousands of seasoned high-tier Awakened walking the streets of Europa.
There were third-stage mercenaries, temple champions, and combat-hardened Lords whose bodies could withstand ten times the stress Harper’s could bear so why take Harper?
Whatever had taken her hadn’t been shopping for the strongest vessel.
It had wanted her, her body, her blood, or her bond with him.
’I hope you’re safe...’ Silas thought, his eyes narrowing into cold slits.
Her face rose unbidden in his mind making him sigh.
’I never really knew I liked her this much...’
Why else would her face be popping up in his mind this much...?
She was really beautiful.

The violet eyes behind her wire-rimmed glasses, the way she pushed them up her nose whenever she was saying something clever, the smirk she wore when she thought she’d caught him off guard, and the ridiculous confidence with which she had once tried out ’Silas-kun’ before he set her straight.
Then the picture bent, and it was Penelope’s trembling voice describing a sickening green glint spinning behind those same violet eyes.
His fists clenched until his knuckles cracked with his jaw setting into a hard merciless line.
’If they lay a single hand on her head...
I’ll kill them.’
He wasn’t going to negotiate and he wasn’t going to hold an inquiry.
Whoever was pulling the strings behind that green light would die.
The only question was how agonizing the process was going to be.
If Harper was unharmed, it would be quick but if she had been harmed, tortured, or broken... he would unravel their meridians grain by grain.
’I’m really starting to sound like a bloodthirsty cultivator,’ Silas scoffed inwardly, catching the violent drift of his own thoughts.
Yet, as he looked out through the curtains at the blazing white skyline of Iunu, a bizarre gnawing intuition refused to leave his mind.
A city of white stone, surrounded on all sides by an endless hostile desert.
...Sand.
’It couldn’t be that fucker... right?’
The name surfaced in his mind like a rancid corpse bobbing to the top of a stagnant pond.
’Ititius.’
It was a wild and almost irrational leap of logic but in his entire life, Silas had only ever encountered one singular monstrous entity that treated sand as an extension of divine authority.
And yet, the reality made no sense.
’How the hell does that even work?’ Silas asked himself, his brow furrowing deeply. ’How resilient can one bastard be?!’
First, during the Secret Realm, Thor had literally swatted the god’s divine avatar out of the sky with an attack of cosmic thunder, vaporizing his physical form into ash.
Then, as Silas was going home with Elora, Silas had personally flooded him with a water spell, drowning his spiritual remnant in crushing pressure.
And then, as if that weren’t enough, when a residual fragment of the creature’s soul had attempted to hijack Kadi’s body inside his territory of Blessed Land... the Territory had purged him as well.
So...
How did a creature survive being erased three separate times across three different planes of existence...?
Was the bastard made of spiritual cockroaches...?
BZZZZ-BZZZZ!
The black phone on the low table vibrated sharply with its blue notification diode flashing in rapid double-pulse bursts and Silas walked over, picking up the phone.𝚏𝕣𝕖𝚎𝚠𝚎𝚋𝚗𝐨𝐯𝕖𝕝.𝕔𝐨𝕞
’It can’t be more bad news, right?’

chapters.title: Chapter 610: Private Jet [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: He swiped his thumb across the screen.
’Fucking hell...’
Upon crossing the boundary into Khemet’s airspace, the location on Harper’s phone had completely vanished...
The red tracking dot was gone.
All he knew with certainty was that she had landed somewhere within the perimeter of Iunu, and then her digital footprint had been severed.
Silas grimaced with his thumb scrolling to the secondary global news wire as a massive crimson-bordered breaking alert dominated the feed.
[BREAKING: CATASTROPHIC ARCANE EXPLOSION AT REPUBLIC OF COLUMBIA RESEARCH FACILITY NO. 95!]
Silas paused.

[A high-powered mana chain reaction has completely destroyed the underground testing chambers of the Department of Arcane Metallurgy... Forty-two senior research alchemists and technical staff confirmed vaporized!]
[Grand Master Varun, the Earth’s foremost authority of runes, assigned to the project by the World King himself, is confirmed deceased in the blast.]

[The experimental gloves at the center of the research were not recovered as investigators found only a thin layer of scorched cowhide and, in the words of one exhausted technician, ’a distinctly smug atmosphere.’!]
Silas stood completely motionless in the center of the suite for five long seconds then, his chest hitched as a sudden sharp sputtering laugh broke from his lips.

"Pfft-hah! Hahaha!" Silas threw his head back, laughing aloud in the quiet room, shaking his head in amusement. "I warned him! I literally looked that arrogant bastard in the face across the negotiation table and made him sign a waiver against this exact outcome... Rowenna must have woven three different layers of spite into those sub-threads!"
His thumb flicked downward to read the casualty manifest.

[Update: President Julian Vanderbilt Senior miraculously survived the detonation... He is currently hospitalized with third-degree burns, a fractured pelvis, and, per hospital staff, ’a severely wounded ego.’]
[Legal analysts note that the President personally signed a binding liability waiver before the entire World Council as Columbia’s own lawyers have reportedly advised him not to read it aloud.]
The laugh died instantly with Silas’s mouth flattened into a sour disgusted scowl.
"Fuck," he muttered under his breath, tossing the comm-pad onto the cushions. "Of course the old leech survived. Cockroaches really do flock together..."
CREAK!
The inner bedroom door opened quietly as Penelope stepped into the room.
She had changed out of her crumpled clothes, now wearing an oversized grey knit sweater that belonged to Lia, its long sleeves completely swallowing her small hands.

Her vibrant purple hair, identical in hue to Harper’s, was tied back into a loose messy ponytail and her face was pale, but the hysterical weeping terror from the morning had settled into a grim fragile composure.
Silas turned his head, immediately grounding his expression into a smile.
"Hey, Penelope," he said gently. "How are you holding up?"
"I’m fine," Penelope answered as she stepped forward, her eyes darting toward the open balcony. "Silas... when are you going to find my sister?"
Silas walked over to the floor-to-ceiling glass doors, reaching out with both hands and sliding the heavy panels apart.
WHOOSH!
The dry scorching breath of the Khemet desert flooded the room, carrying different kind of scents.
From the thirty-story elevation of the Grand Oasis Palace, the city of Iunu lay spread out beneath them like a colossal sprawling place of pale limestone and gleaming titanium.

The city was starkly divided into two worlds... the sprawling Outer Commercial District, choked with bustling bazaars, mid-tier residential towers, and luxury tourist hotels and then there was the elevated white expanse of the Inner District, separated by a four-hundred-foot defensive rampart and a massive shimmering gold mana barrier that domed over the palaces of House Al-Mansur.

Silas had deliberately rented the entire penthouse floor of this specific hotel since it was the tallest structure in the Outer District, possessed an independent defensive barrier, and was garrisoned by private security forces licensed by the King of Khemet.
’Better to be safe than sorry...’
He turned his head, looking back over his shoulder at the eleven-year-old girl.
The afternoon sun caught the sharp line of his jaw, casting a warm amber glow across his features.
His blue eyes, ringed with gold, were completely calm, radiating the unshakable stability of an immovable mountain as he offered her a soft confident smile.
"I’m going now," Silas said. "And I’m not going to rest until I bring Harper back."
Penelope stared at him.
The casual certainty in his voice, the complete absence of doubt, fear, or hesitation, hit her like a physical shockwave.
For the first time all day, the crushing weight sitting on her chest shifted.
Her breath hitched with her small fists loosened from the oversized cuffs of Lia’s sweater, and she looked up at him the way she might have looked at a tower that refused to fall.
"Y-yes," Penelope said, straightening her spine like a soldier receiving orders. "Okay."
"Don’t worry," Silas smiled, giving her a reassuring nod. "Stay inside. Keep close to Martha and Lia as well as Kaede."
STEP!
Silas simply leaned forward, stepping off the edge of the thirty-story balcony into the empty air.
"SILAS!" Penelope shrieked, her composure shattering as she bolted across the room, throwing her hands onto the burning brass railing of the balcony and leaning over the drop.
She looked down.
There was no body falling and there was no concussive impact on the pavement three hundred and fifty feet below.
The air between the penthouse and the bustling avenue was completely empty as he had vanished into thin air, leaving not so much as a ripple in the desert heat haze.
Penelope blinked, clutching her chest, before slowly raising her eyes toward the southern sky.
High above the gleaming white spires of the Inner District, the clear blue heavens were beginning to churn.
Thick unnatural clouds were rolling across the sun, casting long dark shadows over the white stone of the city.
’It’s getting dark...’ Penelope thought, a sudden cold prickle of dread brushing against the back of her neck. ’Is it... going to rain in the desert?’
Three miles across the skyline, a dark silhouette moved across the rooftops with terrifying soundless grace.
FWOOSH!
A figure landed upon the weathered copper dome of a high-tier alchemical trading tower with the impact making no more sound than a dry leaf settling on water.
The figure was broad-shouldered, and draped in a long high-collared traveler’s mantle of deep midnight-blue wool.

The left sleeve of the coat was pinned neatly across the chest, entirely empty, fluttering lazily in the gathering wind and beneath the deep shadow of the cowl, the sharp striking features of a woman with high cheekbones, half-lidded violet eyes, and a wild mane of jet-black hair observed the city below.
It was Kara White.
Down in the crowded street below, pedestrian traffic ground to a sudden stuttering halt as heads snapped upward and hands pointed toward the copper dome.
"Look! Up there!"
"Is that... by the sun, is that her?!"
"Lord White! Sovereign of Blessed Land!"
"The Hero of Humanity! The Gold Core!"

In a city as strictly militarized as Iunu, traversing the rooftops without a registered reason was a severe offense that usually resulted in automated harpoons being fired from the street-level pylons.
Yet, looking up at the single-armed woman standing silhouetted against the dark sky, the local enforcers holding shock-halberds simply lowered their weapons with their mouths hanging open in awe.

A chorus of spontaneous echoing cheers began to rise from the merchant stalls... street vendors clapped their hands, and young Awakened slammed their fists over their breastplates in the traditional southern salute of reverence.
Kara looked down through the fringe of her dark hair, offering the crowd a brief lazy wave of her single right hand.
’Hah,’ Silas thought dryly from behind the disguise. ’I’m really famous, aren’t I... now I can’t even skip across a chimney without people cheering like I’m a parade.’
VUM!

She channeled a subtle concentrated burst of wind mana through her boot-soles, launching her body eighty feet into the air and crossing the wide boulevard with a weightless arc-like glide that carried her directly to the stone ledge of the central clock tower.
Kara landed beneath the massive brass clock face, looking out across the vast expanse of the capital.
’Iunu really is a beautiful place...’
Even under the looming gloom of the unnatural clouds, the grand architecture of the Sun-Crown commanded respect.
Vast avenues of white limestone cut through the desert like blades, lined with turquoise canals and solar-reflecting pylons that channeled heat into clean energy.
Yet, as Kara pushed her Gold Core sensory perception outward, spreading an invisible microscopic web of mana through the atmosphere... her brow furrowed.
’Nothing.’
There wasn’t a single flicker of Harper’s distinct violet lightning signature anywhere in the outer sector.𝒇𝓻𝓮𝓮𝙬𝙚𝒃𝒏𝓸𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Worse... a foul oily pressure was beginning to seep into the edges of her consciousness.
It wasn’t a physical smell at all, but a rotten feeling... it was a heavy suffocating dread that felt like coarse black dust grinding against the lining of her throat.
BZZZZ-BZZZZ!
The private comm-link embedded in Kara’s ear-cuff chimed with a tune.
’I’m glad that I bought this heh...’
She tapped the receiver with a manicured finger.
"Talk to me."
"Kara?"
Evelyn’s voice came through the speaker, accompanied by the distinctive high-pitched whine of jet turbines.
"Ev," Kara said. "Did the logistics clear? Did you get the extraction platform ready?"

"Yes," Evelyn replied, though her voice sounded thoroughly bewildered. "Though I honestly have no idea why you insisted on it on two hours’ notice! Do you have any idea what it takes to buy a private transport outright and clear an unscheduled departure through the City Air Corridor... I had to personally bribe three flight marshals and threaten a fourth with an audit but yes... I bought the jet. And I’m flying to Iunu right now."
She was so sweet that Silas almost let out a laugh at the absurdity of it all.
’A private supersonic jet on two hours’ notice...’
It was ridiculous but it was necessary.

"Don’t worry about it, I’ll pay you back," Kara said smoothly. "If this situation goes south, Evelyn, you’re my contingency... I need you to land on the Outer side, coordinate with Martha at the Grand Oasis Palace, and extract the girls, Martha, and Kaede’s security detail immediately. How much time do you need to touch down?"
Through the frequency, Kara heard the rustle of flight maps and the calm clipped voice of Claire, Evelyn’s head maid, reciting approach vectors.

"Claire says we’re roughly two to three hours out," Evelyn reported, her tone growing serious. "The desert winds are heavy over this side, but we’re pushing the plane as hard as the hull allows... We’re coming as fast as we can."
’I’d prefer twenty minutes,’ Kara thought grimly, her violet eyes tracking the churning storm-dark clouds gathering over the center of the city. ’But two hours is the limit.’

"Make it as fast as you can," Kara instructed. "And Ev, one more thing before you go quiet on me... The thing you fought in Valoria City, the one wearing Harper’s face, could you... walk me through it again?"
The turbines whined for a beat.

"Why now?" Evelyn asked. "Fine. Exactly what I told the police... It was a sand clone. It had her face, it even borrowed her voice for a few minutes, but it was sand all the way down. The city cleared her name for a reason, Kara as the footage doesn’t lie... It was never her."
"Then somebody built that clone," Kara said quietly, "and whoever built it is the reason she’s missing."
The line went silent except for the roar of the engines.
"...A decoy," Evelyn said slowly. "Or a rehearsal. Kara, if that thing was only a test run..."
"Then the real one is worse," Kara finished. "Keep flying."
"Kara..." Evelyn’s voice hesitated with a sharp note of genuine concern bleeding through the line. "Will you be alright? What is going on down there?"
"I’ll be fine," Kara replied, her single hand resting against the cold stone of the clock tower. "I just have a very bad feeling about all of thi—"
WUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUU!
An ear-splitting howl tore through the air, violently cutting her off as across every sector of Iunu, hundreds of high-priority sirens began shrieking in unison.
The sound was deafening like a relentless wail that shook the glass in the windows below.
Through the comm-link, Evelyn let out a sharp panicked gasp.
"What was that?! Is that a red siren?!"
"Yes," Kara said, her body instantly dropping into a combat-ready crouch.
"That’s impossible!" Evelyn shouted over the turbine roar. "Iunu hasn’t triggered a red signal in several decades... Not since the Second Incursion! What could possibly be the cause—"
Before Kara could speak, the automated public address arrays mounted atop every pylon and tower clicked on with a trembling military voice booming across the capital in three different languages.
[ATTENTION ALL CITIZENS. EMERGENCY MANDATE FROM THE HIGH DEFENSE MINISTRY.]
[SATELLITE RECONNAISSANCE CONFIRMS... THE ROYAL TRANSPORT FLEET OF PHARAOH-PRESIDENT MENES AL-MANSUR HAS BEEN COMPLETELY DESTROYED IN THE HIGH DESERT.]

[NO SURVIVORS DETECTED... THE IMPERIAL CARRIER AND EIGHT ESCORT VESSELS WERE REDUCED TO RUBBLE AS THEY RETURNED FROM THE WORLD COUNCIL SUMMIT, OBLITERATED BY A MASSIVE ANOMALY OF BLACK MINERAL COMPOSITION.]
[SIMULTANEOUSLY, A DISTRESS SIGNAL HAS BEEN BROADCAST FROM THE WHITE CITADEL... THE CITADEL GATES ARE CLOSED... REPEAT: THE IMPERIAL FLEET HAS FALLEN—]
CLICK!
Kara severed the connection as she didn’t need to hear another word.
’The royal family was turned to dust... by black sand?’
The blood in Silas’s veins ran freezing cold.
Menes Al-Mansur had been sitting at the World Council table barely a day ago and Tariq had survived the tournament... How did their entire dynasty get wiped out ?!
...Then Harper’s location had gone dark right at the border.
’The person who took control of Harper is behind all of this,’ the realization struck him with the force of an iron hammer.
BOOM!
Kara didn’t bother preserving the rooftop.

With a deafening explosion of wind mana that shattered the clock tower’s slate shingles into powder, she launched herself forward as she became a streak of dark blue lightning, cutting straight toward the four-hundred-foot wall that separated the outer city from the Inner District.
"Get here as fast as you can, Ev," she muttered into the dead comms.

A chorus of spontaneous echoing cheers began to rise from the merchant stalls... street vendors clapped their hands, and young Awakened slammed their fists over their breastplates in the traditional southern salute of reverence.
Kara looked down through the fringe of her dark hair, offering the crowd a brief lazy wave of her single right hand.
’Hah,’ Silas thought dryly from behind the disguise. ’I’m really famous, aren’t I... now I can’t even skip across a chimney without people cheering like I’m a parade.’
VUM!

She channeled a subtle concentrated burst of wind mana through her boot-soles, launching her body eighty feet into the air and crossing the wide boulevard with a weightless arc-like glide that carried her directly to the stone ledge of the central clock tower.
Kara landed beneath the massive brass clock face, looking out across the vast expanse of the capital.
’Iunu really is a beautiful place...’
Even under the looming gloom of the unnatural clouds, the grand architecture of the Sun-Crown commanded respect.
Vast avenues of white limestone cut through the desert like blades, lined with turquoise canals and solar-reflecting pylons that channeled heat into clean energy.
Yet, as Kara pushed her Gold Core sensory perception outward, spreading an invisible microscopic web of mana through the atmosphere... her brow furrowed.
’Nothing.’
There wasn’t a single flicker of Harper’s distinct violet lightning signature anywhere in the outer sector.𝒇𝓻𝓮𝓮𝙬𝙚𝒃𝒏𝓸𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Worse... a foul oily pressure was beginning to seep into the edges of her consciousness.
It wasn’t a physical smell at all, but a rotten feeling... it was a heavy suffocating dread that felt like coarse black dust grinding against the lining of her throat.
BZZZZ-BZZZZ!
The private comm-link embedded in Kara’s ear-cuff chimed with a tune.
’I’m glad that I bought this heh...’
She tapped the receiver with a manicured finger.
"Talk to me."
"Kara?"
Evelyn’s voice came through the speaker, accompanied by the distinctive high-pitched whine of jet turbines.
"Ev," Kara said.
"Did the logistics clear?
Did you get the extraction platform ready?"
"Yes," Evelyn replied, though her voice sounded thoroughly bewildered.
"Though I honestly have no idea why you insisted on it on two hours’ notice!
Do you have any idea what it takes to buy a private transport outright and clear an unscheduled departure through the City Air Corridor...
I had to personally bribe three flight marshals and threaten a fourth with an audit but yes...
I bought the jet.
And I’m flying to Iunu right now."
She was so sweet that Silas almost let out a laugh at the absurdity of it all.
’A private supersonic jet on two hours’ notice...’
It was ridiculous but it was necessary.
"Don’t worry about it, I’ll pay you back," Kara said smoothly.
"If this situation goes south, Evelyn, you’re my contingency...
I need you to land on the Outer side, coordinate with Martha at the Grand Oasis Palace, and extract the girls, Martha, and Kaede’s security detail immediately.
How much time do you need to touch down?"
Through the frequency, Kara heard the rustle of flight maps and the calm clipped voice of Claire, Evelyn’s head maid, reciting approach vectors.
"Claire says we’re roughly two to three hours out," Evelyn reported, her tone growing serious.
"The desert winds are heavy over this side, but we’re pushing the plane as hard as the hull allows...
We’re coming as fast as we can."
’I’d prefer twenty minutes,’ Kara thought grimly, her violet eyes tracking the churning storm-dark clouds gathering over the center of the city. ’But two hours is the limit.’
"Make it as fast as you can," Kara instructed.
"And Ev, one more thing before you go quiet on me...
The thing you fought in Valoria City, the one wearing Harper’s face, could you... walk me through it again?"
The turbines whined for a beat.
"Why now?" Evelyn asked.
"Fine.
Exactly what I told the police...
It was a sand clone.
It had her face, it even borrowed her voice for a few minutes, but it was sand all the way down.
The city cleared her name for a reason, Kara as the footage doesn’t lie...
It was never her."
"Then somebody built that clone," Kara said quietly, "and whoever built it is the reason she’s missing."
The line went silent except for the roar of the engines.
"...A decoy," Evelyn said slowly.
"Or a rehearsal.
Kara, if that thing was only a test run..."
"Then the real one is worse," Kara finished.
"Keep flying."
"Kara..." Evelyn’s voice hesitated with a sharp note of genuine concern bleeding through the line.
"Will you be alright?
What is going on down there?"
"I’ll be fine," Kara replied, her single hand resting against the cold stone of the clock tower.
"I just have a very bad feeling about all of thi—"
WUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUU!
An ear-splitting howl tore through the air, violently cutting her off as across every sector of Iunu, hundreds of high-priority sirens began shrieking in unison.
The sound was deafening like a relentless wail that shook the glass in the windows below.
Through the comm-link, Evelyn let out a sharp panicked gasp.
"What was that?!
Is that a red siren?!"
"Yes," Kara said, her body instantly dropping into a combat-ready crouch.
"That’s impossible!" Evelyn shouted over the turbine roar.
"Iunu hasn’t triggered a red signal in several decades...
Not since the Second Incursion!
What could possibly be the cause—"
Before Kara could speak, the automated public address arrays mounted atop every pylon and tower clicked on with a trembling military voice booming across the capital in three different languages.
[ATTENTION ALL CITIZENS.
EMERGENCY MANDATE FROM THE HIGH DEFENSE MINISTRY.]
[SATELLITE RECONNAISSANCE CONFIRMS...
THE ROYAL TRANSPORT FLEET OF PHARAOH-PRESIDENT MENES AL-MANSUR HAS BEEN COMPLETELY DESTROYED IN THE HIGH DESERT.]
[NO SURVIVORS DETECTED...
THE IMPERIAL CARRIER AND EIGHT ESCORT VESSELS WERE REDUCED TO RUBBLE AS THEY RETURNED FROM THE WORLD COUNCIL SUMMIT, OBLITERATED BY A MASSIVE ANOMALY OF BLACK MINERAL COMPOSITION.]
[SIMULTANEOUSLY, A DISTRESS SIGNAL HAS BEEN BROADCAST FROM THE WHITE CITADEL...
THE CITADEL GATES ARE CLOSED...
REPEAT: THE IMPERIAL FLEET HAS FALLEN—]
CLICK!
Kara severed the connection as she didn’t need to hear another word.
’The royal family was turned to dust... by black sand?’
The blood in Silas’s veins ran freezing cold.
Menes Al-Mansur had been sitting at the World Council table barely a day ago and Tariq had survived the tournament...
How did their entire dynasty get wiped out ?!
...Then Harper’s location had gone dark right at the border.
’The person who took control of Harper is behind all of this,’ the realization struck him with the force of an iron hammer.
BOOM!
Kara didn’t bother preserving the rooftop.

With a deafening explosion of wind mana that shattered the clock tower’s slate shingles into powder, she launched herself forward as she became a streak of dark blue lightning, cutting straight toward the four-hundred-foot wall that separated the outer city from the Inner District.
"Get here as fast as you can, Ev," she muttered into the dead comms.

chapters.title: Chapter 611: Black Sand [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She soared over the grand transition boulevard and in the distance, towering majestically against the bruised purple sky, the White Citadel gleamed... It was a colossal stepped pyramid of polished white titanium and gold with its dome piercing the heavens like the crown of an ancient empire.
’I need to get there—’
Suddenly... the world stopped.

To Silas’s heightened Gold Core perception, the flow of time seemed to violently seize, dragging physical reality into an agonizing crawl and high above the White Citadel, the dome... simply ceased to exist.
FLASH!
A microscopic point of blinding absolute lightless black materialized at the very tip of the golden spire and then... the heavens tore open.
KABOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The detonation was so monstrous that the sound didn’t register as an explosion... instead it registered as a violent concussive blow directly against the inner ear.

A heaven-piercing pillar of swirling radioactive black sand and blinding divine golden plasma erupted through the ceiling of the White Citadel, blowing the three-hundred-foot marble dome into subatomic dust before tearing ten miles straight into the stratosphere.
WHOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
The concussive shockwave hit Kara while she was still a mile away in mid-air.
The atmospheric pressure spiked to forty atmospheres in a second as Kara’s single right arm snapped across her chest... Her Gold Core flaring with a barrier of compressed wind mana instantly.
CRUNCH!
The blast wave slammed into her barrier like an iron mountain!
Kara was violently hurled backward through the sky.
"Fuckin—!"

She tumbled three hundred yards across the rooftops with her boots skidding across the reinforced copper tiles of an administrative tower, tearing a fifty-foot furrow through the metal before she slammed her right heel into a concrete parapet, forcibly arresting her momentum.
She coughed with the sudden vacuum created by the detonation dragging the air from her lungs as her cloak whipped frantically in the violent back-draft.
Kara managed to stabilize her footing, wiping a speck of dust from her lips, and slowly raised her head.
The blood in Silas’s heart dropped straight into his stomach.
"No..." Kara whispered, her voice trembling in genuine horror.
The Inner District was gone.

Where the White Citadel, the grand ministerial palaces, the lush hanging gardens, the luxury hotels, and the private residential villas of seventy thousand souls had stood bare moments ago... there was only a terrifying void.
A colossal smoking crater, three miles in diameter and four hundred feet deep, yawned in the center of the capital like an open grave carved into the crust of the earth!
There were still a few untouched residential fringes along the outer perimeter walls, but that did nothing to change the horrific reality of the three-mile-wide abyss.
The walls of the crater were smooth vitrified sheets of solid lightless black glass that hissed and bubbled with residual divine heat.
’So many people...’ Silas thought, his hand trembling beneath the folds of his cloak. ’They’re all dead...’
Seventy thousand lives had been deleted in half a second yet, as Kara pushed her vision through the swirling heat mirage, her eyes widened.
There were no bodies.
Not a single mangled corpse lay among the vitrified stone... No severed limbs, no pools of crimson blood either.
There was only a thick undulating sea of coarse pitch-black sand that churned lazily across the floor of the crater, whispering against the glass.
SH-SH-SH!
Fifty yards below her, resting upon the surface of the black sand sea, a single thumb-sized tendril of black mineral shifted.
It possessed no eyes, yet the moment Kara’s boots touched the rim of the crater, the tendril froze as it turned with its tip vibrating in the air, locking directly onto her Gold Core mana signature.
SCREEECH!
A high-pitched metallic shriek ripped from the sand and in an instant, the entire three-mile basin of black sand violently awakened.

Tens of thousands of undulating razor-sharp tendrils erupted from the floor of the crater, twisting together into colossal serpentine leviathans that rose two hundred feet into the air with their faceless needle-sharp maws turning simultaneously toward the single-armed woman on the ledge.
"Fucking hell," Kara snarled through her teeth.
WHOOSH!
The three closest tendrils blurred forward, aiming straight for her throat, her chest, and her legs but Kara didn’t dodge.
SNAP!
Her right hand thrust forward with her fingers splaying wide as she took a deep breath.
"Incineration Ray!" she barked.
BOOM!
A colossal white-hot beam of concentrated fire erupted from her palm!

The flames unraveled the atomic structure of the incoming tendrils, incinerating the black mineral and all the tendrils near them into drifting white ash before they could touch her coat as the concussive back-blast cleared a hundred-yard circle of empty air around her.
Kara lowered her hand with smoke curling from her palm, and looked out over the sea of black sand.
...Nothing had changed.
The ash of the incinerated tendrils drifted down like dirty snow, and beneath it the sand simply closed over the gap as if she had dropped a pebble into a pond.

Fifty yards below, a fresh forest of tendrils was already braiding itself upward, thousands of them this time, every one turned toward her Gold Core signature with the blind hunger of something that had never once been full.
’It really does get everywhere,’ Silas thought, a grim humorless smirk tugging at Kara’s lips.
She flexed her single hand, raised it again, and let the heat gather in her palm as the sand rose to meet her.
Four thousand feet beneath the surface of the earth.
The air parted with a violent concussive screech as a figure shot downward through a sixty-foot shaft bored straight through the bedrock!
FWOOOOOOSH!
It was Harper’s body.

Her tailored charcoal trousers and silk blouse were torn at the cuffs, coated in fine silt with her long vibrant purple hair whipping wildly around her face as she plummeted toward the core of the earth but her eyes... her eyes were burning with an emerald fire.
Harper’s physical hands were thrust downward, parting the solid bedrock with massive churning waves of coarse black sand that dissolved stone into fluid dust with a terrifying hiss.
A voice broke from Harper’s throat, a deep one layered over the soft timbre of the young woman’s vocal cords.
"It is truly... marvelous!"
Ititius threw Harper’s head back, letting out a delighted purring chuckle that echoed off the descending stone walls.
He raised Harper’s hands, turning the pale delicate fingers over in the dark, watching the coarse black sand flow between the knuckles like living liquid mercury.

"When I was cast into the abyss by that treacherous whore Nefertari," Ititius mused. "when my glorious original flesh was devoured by those wretched worms upon entering the Sovereign Realm all that time ago... I believed this sublime power had been stripped from me forever! Ten thousand years I spent wandering the fragmented tiers of the Sovereign Realm, for time races there while this sluggish mortal sphere crawls, and two thousand years dragged past up here while I endured ten thousand down there... I ascended to true godhood... I bound domains... I forged divine artifacts and yet... throughout all those millennia, despite becoming a deity, I somehow couldn’t wield this black sand!"
His green-and-gold pupils flared with psychotic triumph.

"And now? After leaving the other half of my soul asleep in this world... after wiping that sweet little splinter out as though she had never existed, and drinking every last one of her memories into my essence... I can wield this power as though it were second nature!"
He gritted Harper’s teeth with a cold shudder running down his spine.
’I... am a Deity.’
Deities were meant to emulate their natures well.
Many people complained about sand... Mortals whined that it was coarse, rough, irritating, and that it got everywhere...
But they were fools! Blind, uneducated insects!
That was the very definition of supreme authority... To get everywhere... To infiltrate every crack, every vessel, every breath!
Ititius prided himself on being like a cockroach.

Regardless of whatever was thrown at him, regardless of whether his avatar was swatted out of the sky, drowned in a tomb, or purged from a vessel’s core, he would survive as sand stuck and sand endured.
In his own case, he had contingency plans woven into the very fabric of the cosmos.
’I am only living up to the legend, after all...’ Ititius thought, thoroughly pleased with his own genius.
Perhaps, eons ago, before the First Rift tore the sky, he had once been a woman named Nitocris... but why in the heavens would he ever remain as Nitocris?
It wasn’t that he possessed a petty hatred for men or women.
It was far simpler... the god that humanity had worshiped, the Ititius that he had prayed to as a naive child before the Apocalypse, didn’t exist as the heavens had been empty.
So, he had simply decided to embody that Ititius!
He wasn’t some tragic misunderstood anti-hero... He wasn’t like those melodramatic people he had met all those millennia ago who whined about ’justified vengeance’ and ’the tragedy of the rifts.’
Ititius was a remarkably simple creature... he only wanted to rule.
His foolish little soul-fragment had possessed the tiny pathetic ambition of a peasant as she had merely wanted to slaughter Nefertari’s children and crawl into a hole to die.
’What a waste of fine plan!’ Ititius laughed internally.
He didn’t just want House Al-Mansur dead... He wanted it all to extend outward! He wanted to force this entire world to submit to him!

And once he conquered humanity, once he forced all eight billion mortals to bow their heads in the dirt and worship his holy name, all that vast divine power he had lost from splitting his soul so many times and being killed across the eras would be gloriously regained.

With that restored power, he would use humanity as his divine engine to contest with Odin, to challenge Ra, and to war against all the other higher gods of the cosmos and then... the entire Sovereign Realm would belong to him!
...That was his goal.
That was his goal from the very beginning.
Why else would a god bother ruling humanity? He wanted to make them submit and harness their collective spiritual power to increase his own!
"And I must extend my deepest, most sincere gratitude to you, my dear descendant," Ititius purred aloud, Harper’s vocal cords vibrating with mock tenderness. "Truly, all the odds went in my favor!"
Deep within the lightless suffocating prison of her own core, Harper’s tiny compressed violet spirit blinked in sheer terror.
’Wh-what is he talking about...?’ Harper wept, her ghostly form curled tight against the crushing weight of the divine intruder.
Ititius chuckled, it was a cold slimy sound that echoed through their shared soul-space.

"Not only did I use my old soul-fragment as a gateway to step back into this mortal sphere, bypassing even the barriers humanity erected to prevent beings of the Sovereign Realm from spilling into their world, but I also required a proper vessel in order to anchor my presence!"
He turned Harper’s wrists in the dark, admiring the delicate bone structure.
"And what were the chances of picking a vessel that was directly related to me?"
Harper’s spiritual mind froze.
’Related to him...?!’

"When I was still a human," Ititius explained casually, like an elder recounting old family lineage, "before Nefertari threw me into the rift... I had children as well. Two died in the chaos, but it seems one of them managed to survive the collapse! They fled north with their bloodlines intermingled across the centuries, and that is where you came along from! Oh, my splinter knew, of course... The sentimental fool spun you some pretty tale about a wayward concubine, all to avoid admitting she couldn’t bring herself to spill her own blood!"
He let out a delighted mocking laugh.

"It really doesn’t matter whether your bloodline is mixed with common northern water now! As long as there is a sliver of my blood living within your marrow, you are the perfect vessel for my soul and with this vessel... I will do something that will make my conquering of humanity so much easier!"
FWOOOOOOSH!
Ititius parted the earth one last time with an explosive sweep of Harper’s arm and the tight sixty-foot stone shaft suddenly opened into a colossal void.
At this point, it was a pure unimpeded freefall downward through the darkness...
Far below in the deep abyss, cutting through the pitch-black shadows, a radiant blue glow began to bleed upward, illuminating Harper’s falling silhouette in brilliant azure light.
Harper’s physical lips curved into a wide smirk as Ititius gazed down at the colossal azure machinery suspended in the chasm below.
"These Suppression Engines..." Ititius whispered, his voice echoing through the falling wind.
"How about we destroy the one below Khemet?"

The sentimental fool spun you some pretty tale about a wayward concubine, all to avoid admitting she couldn’t bring herself to spill her own blood!"
He let out a delighted mocking laugh.
"It really doesn’t matter whether your bloodline is mixed with common northern water now!
As long as there is a sliver of my blood living within your marrow, you are the perfect vessel for my soul and with this vessel...
I will do something that will make my conquering of humanity so much easier!"
FWOOOOOOSH!
Ititius parted the earth one last time with an explosive sweep of Harper’s arm and the tight sixty-foot stone shaft suddenly opened into a colossal void.
At this point, it was a pure unimpeded freefall downward through the darkness...
Far below in the deep abyss, cutting through the pitch-black shadows, a radiant blue glow began to bleed upward, illuminating Harper’s falling silhouette in brilliant azure light.
Harper’s physical lips curved into a wide smirk as Ititius gazed down at the colossal azure machinery suspended in the chasm below.
"These Suppression Engines..." Ititius whispered, his voice echoing through the falling wind.
"How about we destroy the one below Khemet?"

chapters.title: Chapter 612: Sub-Suppression Engine [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The sub-level chamber four thousand feet beneath the scorched bedrock of Iunu didn’t smell like the desert.
The chamber was immense, a hollowed-out dome of dark basalt spanning half a mile across, reinforced by tiered ribbing of dense star-iron that anchored directly into the continental crust.

Far above, the circular exhaust shaft plunged straight up into the lightless throat of the earth which an engineering marvel designed to expel millions of cubic meters of superheated atmospheric mana whenever the tectonic grids flared.
And in the center of the floor, casting long rhythmic bars of cold azure light across the stone flags, rose the machine.
It was colossal... the size of a four-story fortress.
Massive rings of polished white alloy and dark celestial quartz rotated in counter-balanced orbits, whispering against their magnetic housings with a sound like a distant turbine idling underwater.

Intricate circuits, etched in the Second King’s silver script, pulsed with calm steady respiration along the outer perimeter, projecting an iridescent honeycombed dome of pure mana that sealed the core from the regular world.
[Sub Mana-Suppression Engine: Northern Sector Anchor No. 4.]

Not many people knew, well unless you worked around here... One wouldn’t be able to know that this wasn’t the Main Suppression Engine, that one was much further down in the center of Khemet and very close to the Earth’s crust, however these Sub-Mana Suppression Engines mattered a lot too.
Outside the glowing perimeter of the barrier, twelve men were gathered around an overturned packing crate that had been converted into an impromptu card table.

Three of them sat on folding stools directly facing the blue glow with their unbuttoned service jackets revealing sweat-stained undershirts and their service khopeshes as well as sidearms leaning carelessly against the crates.
A battered brass radio sat on a toolbox, quietly playing a tinny rhythmic string melody from a local Iunu frequency.
"Pass the dried figs, Hamid," one of the men muttered, flicking a plastic playing card onto the scarred wood. "You’ve been hoarding the bag since the fourth watch..."

"Eat your own rations, Farid," the man named Hamid grunted, his bronze skin shining with a sheen of grease under the work lamps. "My wife packed these with honey... If I give them to you, you’ll just choke on the seeds and blame the air scrubbers."
Laughter rippled through the group.

"Speaking of wives," a younger sentinel leaned back, his hands folded behind his head as he grinned toward the empty bunk area near the perimeter wall. "Has anyone heard from Nabil? He took the three-day pass up to the surface yesterday morning... That boy was shaking so hard when he clocked out, I thought his mana core was misfiring."

"First baby," an older, scarred veteran chuckled, pouring dark amber spirit from a ceramic flask into a tin cup. "The first one turns every proud desert warrior into a whimpering puppy, just give him forty-eight hours of changing soiled linen and hearing the infant screech at sunrise, and he’ll be begging the captain to send him back down here to scrub turbine intake vents..."
"He’s a good man," Farid smiled, leaning forward to claim the card trick. "I left two bottles of aged palm wine in his locker before he took the lift... He’s going to need the sleep."
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The bedrock violently shuddered.
The entire half-mile dome groaned as if a colossal fist had struck the stone miles above, raining a fine powdery blizzard of pulverized rock and ancient dust down upon the metal ribbing.

The lights strung along the catwalks flickered violently, cutting out for two seconds before the secondary batteries hissed and clicked back on with a sickly amber dimness as the tin cup spilled across the wooden crate, dark liquor soaking into the face-down cards.

The twelve men were on their feet in a fraction of a second, but their movements lacked the sharp manic terror of soldiers on a battlefield... it was the slow confused irritation of men whose quiet shift had been interrupted.

"What in the hell was that?" Farid frowned, squinting up into the gloom of the exhaust shaft where dust still drifted through the work-lamp beams. "Did the high-altitude line drop a freight container over the Citadel again?"
Standing near the perimeter console, a young man who had arrived only three days prior on an exchange detail stood completely rigid.

His uniform was different from the loose, embroidered linens of the Khemet guard... his tunic was stiff, slate-gray wool, carrying the double-eagle crest of the Europa Directorate’s Continental Watch.
His hand was clamped over the butt of his standard-issue carbine, his pale face turned up toward the dark ceiling with dilated pupils.

"What are you doing?!" the Europa substitute shouted, his voice cracking slightly with high-pitched nervous alarm. "Why are you looking at the cards?! That was a high-order detonation! Where is the rest of the battalion?! Where are the reserve squads?!"
Hamid looked at the boy, let out a short sigh, and casually picked up his spilled cup, shaking the excess droplets onto the flags.

"Take a breath, kid," Hamid said, his voice flat and condescending. "You came down on the transfer from Sector Three three days ago, right? You northern boys are always wound tighter than a cheap crossbow..."

"I asked where the rest of the station complement is!" the substitute pressed, stepping toward the table with his knuckles whitening on his sling. "The roster logged thirty-four men on active roster for this quadrant! There are twelve of us here! Where is the Station Director?!"

"Gone to the city," Farid answered, leaning against his chair and rolling his eyes. "Along with twenty other men... In case nobody briefed you before you boarded the transport, the Grand Sun Festival of Iunu kicks off in forty-eight hours, the entire city is flooded with millions of tourists, trade delegates, and street markets... The Director’s brother owns three silk pavilions in the outer plaza so he took early leave to manage the inventory."
The Europa substitute stared at them, his jaw literally slacking.
"He... he left? The Manager of a Sub-Suppression Engine abandoned his post for a market stall?!"

"Don’t look at us like we committed treason, boy," the scarred veteran scoffed, wiping dust from his collar. "This engine has sat in this exact basalt ring since the era of the Second King... The Apocalypse came and went, the rifts were sealed, and this machine hasn’t blinked once. You think a beast is going to buy a tourist ticket, take the public elevator down through four thousand feet of reinforced rock, and ask us for directions?"

"It’s... it’s gross negligence!" the substitute gasped, his chest heaving as he looked between the indifferent laughing vanguards. "The Suppression Engines are the single most valuable technological installations in human civilization... Even the Sub-suppression Engines. They are the only reason higher-tier horrors and abominations can’t manifest directly into the waking world and you’re sitting here playing cards and drinking palm wine while the surface shakes?!"

"Come drink, kid," Hamid chuckled, shaking his head and holding out the flask. "Seriously. You’re giving yourself an ulcer over nothing... Look at where you are. To get to this chamber, you have to enter the High Citadel, clear the Guard checkpoints, take the primary lift that requires an Al-Mansur blood-seal, and descend through four miles of solid bedrock. Look at the monitors."
Hamid walked over to the auxiliary security console, tapping a scarred finger against the cracked glass slate.
HUM!
A flickering three-dimensional green hologram sputtered to life, displaying the main corridor that descended from the heart of the palace above.
The image was static, showing the massive seven-foot-thick vault doors of solid star-iron sealed tight with the locking bolts engaged.

"See?" Hamid smirked, tapping the boy’s breastplate with the back of his hand. "The entrance is completely closed off and the seal is green too. Nothing moves through the tube unless the Pharaoh-President himself authorizes the current... So unless your imaginary terrorist can turn into a ghost and slip through four thousand feet of solid basalt, nobody is getting down here."

"And what if they don’t use the primary tube?!" the substitute demanded, pointing an accusatory finger toward the dark unmapped cavern mouths that ringed the outer circumference of the dome. "What about the natural fissures? The drainage ducts?!"
Farid took a long noisy swig from his cup, letting out a satisfied smack of his lips.

"Those drainage tunnels?" Farid laughed. "Kid, half of those fissures drop into blind magma pockets that haven’t been mapped since the Second Era and the other half? They are wired with the old defensive runes the World Kings laid down during the cleansing... High-power Destruction mana. The moment any foreign entity sets foot in those ducts, their flesh doesn’t even have time to burn as their atomic bonds get eviscerated into cold grease before they can take two steps... So unless your intruder is some kind of ancient invincible god that can somehow resist destructio—"
CRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRACK!
The four-foot-thick basalt slab sixty feet directly above the card table violently imploded downward in a detonation of shattered granite, flying shale, and choking black dust.
THUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
The impact of the landing shook the entire chamber with such terrifying violence that the wooden crate exploded into kindling, sending playing cards, cups, and liquor bottles spinning into the dark!

The twelve men were thrown backward onto their shoulders, scrambling frantically across the flagstones, their eyes burning with the thick black grit that billowed through the air like a sudden smoke grenade.
"WEAPONS!" Hamid roared, rolling onto his knees with his service khopesh clearing its scabbard with a sharp ringing shing. "FORM ON ME! RAISE THE SOLAR—"
The words froze in his throat as the dust began to settle beneath the flickering work-lamps.
Standing in the center of a five-foot-deep impact crater was the silhouette of a woman.
Her tailored charcoal trousers and silk blouse were torn at the sleeves, coated in fine lightless black soot.

Long vibrant purple hair fell around her shoulders, thrashing gently as if an invisible storm were circulating beneath her skin as she slowly rolled her shoulders back, her neck tilting to the left with three sharp wet clicks of bone adjusting to gravity.
She shook her wrists, letting the fine black silt flow from her fingertips like liquid ink.
"Intruder!" Farid screamed, leveling his sidearm with shaking hands. "Halt! Keep your hands where we can see them! Who are you?! How did you bypass the upper shaft?!"
The woman slowly turned her head and the guards drew sharp collective breaths.
Her face was that of a young noble woman, perhaps an heiress or a high-ranking merchant’s daughter from the northern sectors but her eyes...
There was no human pupil.

Her eyes were burning with a radioactive emerald-green fire, veined with spinning complex golden runes that rotated in opposite directions around the optical center, radiating an aura of crushing arrogance that made the air in the chamber feel heavy, like wet cement filling their lungs.
A voice broke from the woman’s throat.
"A ’who’?" the entity murmured, Harper’s physical lips curling into a wide smirk. "How wonderfully quaint and first of all... I am a He."
Ititius flexed Harper’s fingers, stepping lightly out of the crater with his boots clicking rhythmically against the stone.

"I must say," Ititius purred, looking at his palms with admiration, "the descent was remarkably stimulating but after spending so long locked inside that dark narrow little scabbard... my newly reclaimed limbs feel slightly stiff. I believe a brief... physical calibration is in order."
He dropped his center of gravity, assuming an ancient low-slung northern dueling stance that looked scary on Harper’s slender frame.
"Now then, ambitious little guardsmen," Ititius smiled, his green eyes flaring with sadistic light. "Do try to die entertainingly."
"OPEN FIRE!" Hamid bellowed.
BANG-BANG-BANG-BANG-CLANG!
The Europa substitute and four Khemet vanguards opened fire simultaneously!
High-velocity slugs and pressurized solar-plasma bolts tore through the sixty-foot gap, converging on Harper’s chest in a crisscrossing web of energy but Ititius didn’t blink.
SWOOSH!
Harper’s physical body seemed to bend at an unnatural, ninety-degree angle at the hips, swaying through the incoming line of fire with the sickening fluid grace of a cobra dancing through rain.
A kinetic slug grazed the fabric of her coat, a plasma bolt scorched the air half an inch above her ear and in the exact second the barrage ended...
BOOM!
The flagstone beneath Harper’s left boot shattered as she closed the thirty-foot gap in zero seconds, appearing directly inside Hamid’s guard.

Hamid’s Third Stage instincts fired in blind reflex as he dropped his shoulder, bringing his heavy bronze khopesh up in an explosive rising diagonal parry designed to sever the girl’s outstretched forearm.
"Die, bitch—" Hamid snarled!
CLANG-SHRRRK!

Harper’s bare right palm snapped forward, the fingers coated in an ultra-thin film of pressurized black sand as she caught the side of the bronze blade with her fingertips, twisting her wrist inward with terrifying torque.
CRACK!
The reinforced bronze khopesh snapped clean in two like dried kindling and Hamid’s eyes widened in horror as the momentum pulled his chest forward.
"Your form is atrocious," Ititius whispered softly into his ear. "A common soldier relying on heavy metal... How thoroughly disappointing."
SPLAT!
Harper’s bare left palm slammed flat against Hamid’s solar plexus.
A concentrated pulse of black sand shot directly from her skin, boring through his leather gambeson, entering his chest cavity, and violently expanding.
CRACKLE!
Hamid didn’t even have time to scream.
The light in his eyes died instantly as his skin, his armor, his blood, and his screaming mouth turned into an oily lightless statue of pure black glass.
TAP!
Ititius flicked the statue with a single fingernail.
SHATTER!
Hamid exploded into a million drifting black shards that scattered across the flagstones!
"HAMID!" Farid screamed, his mind snapping under the sudden horror.
He threw his sidearm aside with his hands blurring through complex hand seals as his core flared with desperate bright crimson fire mana.
"SOLAR PIERCE!"
FWOOOOOOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 613: Trap [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Nine spiraling lances of white-hot three-thousand-degree solar flame erupted from the floor around Farid, converging on Harper from every angle to incinerate her down to her marrow.
Ititius chuckled.
"Hehe."
VUM!
He raised Harper’s right hand, casually snapping his fingers.
CRACKLE-SNAP!

The purple lightning native to Harper’s body manifested as a dense spinning disk of violet current that rotated around her forearm like a buzzsaw as Ititius swept Harper’s arm in a wide horizontal arc.
SHRIT-SHRIT-SHRIT!
The violet frequency cleaved through the nine solar lances as if they were threads of warm silk, scattering the high-tier fire into harmless sparks!
Before Farid could even begin to process the counter...
WHOOSH!

A massive barbed tendril of black sand erupted from the floor beneath Farid’s feet, shooting upward between his thighs, piercing through his groin, his spine, and exploding out through the top of his skull.
CRACKLE-SHATTER!
Farid turned to black glass and pulverized into ash before the sparks of his own spell hit the floor.
"MONSTER!"
"RUN! GET TO THE ELEVATOR—"
The remaining nine Khemet men broke completely.
They threw their halberds to the floor, turning on their heels, scrambling frantically toward the reinforced airlock at the edge of the cavern.

"Now, now," Ititius laughed, Harper’s voice echoing with cold amusement as he took three leisurely steps forward. "Did I give you permission to leave the stage? A proper audience remains seated until the final bow!"
FWOOOOOOOOOOOM!
From Harper’s sleeves, dozens of undulating razor-sharp ribbons of black sand surged forward and they began to hunt...
The attacks whipped through the air like ancient ravenous eels, wrapping around throats, drilling through kneecaps, and coiling around chests.
SPLAT! CRACKLE! SHATTER! CRASH! SNAP! CRUNCH!
A rapid-fire rhythmic sequence of glassy detonations echoed through the subterranean chamber.

One by one, the fleeing people were petrified in dynamic panicked strides with their arms outstretched toward the heavy vault doors, before shattering into drifting heaps of dark powder that settled over the lapis tiles like an obscene snowfall.
Within forty seconds, the floor was silent as eleven men were gone and erased completely with their souls devoured by the void-sand without leaving a drop of blood behind.
...Only one man remained.
The young Europa substitute sat huddled against the base of an iron pillar, his slate-gray uniform drenched in cold sweat with his carbine lying discarded five feet away.
His teeth were chattering so violently that the clicking sound was clearly audible in the quiet cavern.
His eyes were wide, bloodshot, staring at the purple-haired demon who was slowly walking toward him.

"P-Please..." the young man whimpered, tears cutting clean pale tracks through the soot on his cheeks. "Please... I don’t belong here... I just arrived from Europa... I have a mother in Sector Four... please don’t kill me... I beg you... I’ll open the vault for you... I’ll do anything..."
Ititius stopped three paces away.
He tilted Harper’s head, looking down at the weeping boy with an expression of mild curiosity.

"A mother?" Ititius murmured, his green-and-gold eyes gleaming with mocking amusement. "How surprising... Mortals always bring up their progenitors when the blade touches their throat. Do you honestly believe a god cares about the weeping of a northern peasant?"
The substitute threw himself forward with his forehead slamming against the cold flagstones, groveling at Harper’s boots.

"Please! I have no magic! I’m just a technician! I don’t care about Khemet! I don’t care about the Sun-Crown! Just let me take the service lift! I won’t speak a word! I swear by the World King, I will never speak of this—"
"You speak far too much," Ititius sighed, shaking Harper’s head in mild exasperation. "It is truly exhausting."
SHRUNK!
A single needle-thin spike of black sand shot directly from Harper’s toe.
It entered through the base of the boy’s skull, traveled down his cervical vertebrae, and flared outward into his heart.
The Europa substitute didn’t even have time to finish his prayer as his groveling form instantly hardened into black glass, the desperate weeping expression permanently frozen into the dark crystal.
SNAP!
The statue collapsed under its own weight, turning into a neat three-foot pile of black dust beneath Harper’s boots.
Ititius turned his back on the carnage, wiping a speck of gray soot from his collar with Harper’s fingers.
"Filthy commoners," he muttered, Harper’s voice carrying that distinctive arrogant snarl. "Always making such an unsightly mess before they expire..."
He walked leisurely toward the center of the cavern, his green-and-gold eyes locking onto the colossal humming fortress of the Terrestrial Mana-Suppression Engine.
The machine rotated with cold indifference as it was unmoved by the slaughter that had just unfolded outside its perimeter.
The honeycombed dome of the primary defensive barrier hummed with an impenetrable sound that vibrated directly against Ititius’s marrow.

"Ah..." Ititius hissed, Harper’s physical face twisting into an ugly venomous sneer. "You wretched, miserable little toy... Since the age of the Second King, your disgusting hum has pricked at the heavens, locking true divinity away in the cosmic dark while mortals play at civilization."
WHOOOOOSH!
Ititius raised Harper’s right arm, her palm igniting with a massive concentrated orb of black sand and compressed purple lightning.
"DIE, YOU ROTTING MACHINE!" Ititius roared!
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

The divine blast detonated directly against the honeycombed blue barrier and the concussive shockwave ripped through the half-mile chamber, tearing the steel catwalks from the walls and throwing clouds of pulverized basalt into the air.
Yet, when the smoke cleared...
The blue barrier wasn’t cracked, hell it didn’t even flicker.
The stabilization runes simply absorbed the impact, routing the divine energy through its heatsinks and releasing it into the exhaust vents with a soft dismissive hiss.
"WHAT?!" Ititius shrieked, Harper’s physical vocal cords cracking under the sudden furious screech.
The veins along her neck bulged with blinding golden light.
"IMPOSSIBLE! A mortal cage resisting my divine authority?!"
’Why... why is he so annoying...?’
Harper was scared of course and she was also pissed off but she felt a bit of shame too, after all, this was her ancestor which she descended from.
...Were they always so dumb? Also she was glad about the fact that Ititius only had access to Nitocris’s memories and not hers.
’This is a Sub-suppression engine.’ She thought to herself, if he did destroy this one, Khemet as a whole would still be okay but this North Khemet would be overrun by rifts to the Sovereign Realm.

Many people would die, but hopefully they could evacuate on time though Harper didn’t know how long it would take before he figured it out and went deeper for the other Suppression Engine, the main one.
’I know... I know I wanted to grow stronger but please Silas... please save me.’
Ititius threw two more explosive strikes against the barrier, but each impact was swallowed whole, dispersing across the barrier without leaving so much as a scratch.
"Damn it! Damn it all!" Ititius snarled, pacing frantically back and forth across the flagstones with Harper’s fingers digging into her own scalp in unhinged irritation.
...He knew.
He could feel it through the atmospheric vibrations of the exhaust shaft far above.
’Someone is coming,’ Ititius calculated, his eyes darting toward the dark ceiling. ’A signature... cutting through the crater at breakneck speed. This is very bad...’
He had to execute the next phase of his plan immediately.

If he was caught locked in an extended siege against an automated fortress while being pressured by someone strong, his newly reclaimed vessel would be ground to pieces before his divinity could fully stabilize.

"Calm yourself, Ititius," he whispered through Harper’s lips, forcing her chest to draw a deep trembling breath. "You are an ancient master of magic... There is no lock forged by mortal hands that cannot be picked."
He stopped before the shimmering blue ward, lowering his hands but he didn’t strike it again.
Instead, Harper’s physical palms pressed flat against the outer surface of the blue barrier.
’If the wall refuses to break... I will simply drink the stone.’
BZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZT!
Ititius began weaving a forbidden primordial absorption array.

He inverted Harper’s internal mana circuits, forcing her secondary pathways to operate as a high-velocity spiritual vacuum as the raw stabilization mana of the Suppression Engine was violently, forcibly siphoned directly out of the barrier runes, pouring through Harper’s palms like boiling oil.
"Ngh...!" Harper’s physical body groaned with her knees trembling under the agonizing pressure of the intake. "This is good..."
Harper’s mortal meridians weren’t built to process such monumental quantities of mana output.
The blue energy coursed through her arms like liquid glass, tearing microscopic fissures through her vascular walls, turning her veins bright azure beneath her pale skin.
Yet, Ititius didn’t stop... He was a god and he didn’t care if the scabbard frayed at the edges.
’I will survive.’
He harnessed the stolen stabilization mana, utilizing its specific harmonic frequency to temporarily dissolve the molecular cohesion of the inner barrier.
SHUUUUUU!
The honeycombed blue dome parted, opening a narrow six-foot fissure directly in front of him as Ititius stepped through the threshold, reaching the physical hull of the Suppression Engine itself.

The machine’s outer casing was forged from an ultra-rare high-density alloy known only to the highest research ministries of the World Council, a substance practically impervious to conventional elemental decay.
Ititius reached out, pressing Harper’s bare right palm directly against the spinning housing.
KRZZZZZZZZ-CRACK!
The machine’s automated anti-tampering wards fired in pure reflex as a blinding arc of concentrated disintegration flashed across the metal!
SPLAT-TEAR!
Harper’s physical right hand, her wrist, and her forearm up to the elbow were instantly disintegrated into fine dust!
"AGHHH!" Ititius roared, Harper’s head snapping back in raw agony. "Insolent scrap iron!"
CRACKLE!
Before the blood could even spray from the severed stump, a violent wave of black sand surged from the elbow.
The bone, the muscle, the flesh, and the skin knitted back together with rapid sickening clicks, regenerating the entire limb in the span of two heartbeats.
Ititius didn’t hesitate.

He gritted Harper’s teeth, channeled every scrap of Harper’s newly enhanced physical output, and drove Harper’s regenerated sand-hardened fist straight into the central maintenance intake seam of the machine.
BOOM-CRUNCH!
The plates groaned.
"Hurry... Hurry..."

With an agonizing metallic screech that set the teeth on edge, Harper’s hand punched three feet deep into the internal machinery, shattering the delicate silver-script conduits, crushing the central mana-regulator, and ripping free a bundle of glowing sparking copper-quartz coils.
BZZZZZT-SPARK-POP!
The smooth hum of the Suppression Engine instantly hitched as the rings shuddered violently, wobbling in their magnetic tracks.
Sparks of blinding blue and red plasma erupted from the breached casing with the cooling fluids hissing as they boiled against the exposed heatsinks...
The machine began to violently short-circuit with its stabilization frequency dropping by forty percent in a single breath.
THUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
A concussive impact rattled the floor behind him as Ititius slowly withdrew Harper’s bloody arm from the smoking breach, shaking the boiling oil from her knuckles.
"Stop."
The voice wasn’t loud but it carried a suffocating power that seemed to physically pin the air in the chamber to the stone flags.
Ititius slowly turned around, clapping Harper’s hands together in slow applause as he stepped lightly backward, vaulting over a fractured steel pipe to create twenty yards of distance.
"Hoho~" Ititius purred, a massive grin spreading across Harper’s face. "The hero arrives at the eleventh hour! How exquisitely predictable!"
Standing thirty paces away, silhouetted against the dark mouth of the exhaust shaft, was Kara White.
Her long midnight-blue cloak was torn at the hem, coated in gray ash and scorched soot.

Her long wild black hair thrashed in the dust, and her half-lidded violet eyes were fixed on Harper’s face with a pair of cold murderous pupils that burned with an intensity so terrifying that the temperature around her seemed to drop into an icy void.
A dense suffocating aura of pure murderous intent rolled off Kara’s single-armed frame, pressing against the cavern walls with the weight of an entire falling mountain.
Ititius laughed, tilting Harper’s head with an amused scoff.

"The machine is remarkably durable," Ititius chuckled, resting his hands on Harper’s hips. "I must give credit to your mortal artificers but... do you feel that, little hero? Can you feel the shift in the ether?"
He closed his eyes for a microsecond, Harper’s chest inhaling the ozone-thick air with genuine ecstatic relish.

"The seal is fractured," Ititius whispered. "The anchor is slipping and the sweet boundless energy of the Sovereign Realm is beginning to bleed back into this pathetic little sphere... My true divine power is answering the call! I need only finish dismantling this heap of iron, and the gates will tear wide open!"
He turned his green-and-gold eyes back toward Kara with his pupils narrowing as he studied the specific vibration of the mana rolling off her body.
He paused as the arrogant smile on Harper’s lips subtly twitched.
"Wait..." Ititius murmured, his voice dropping into a sharp suspicious rasp. "This mana... this dense suffocating stench of..."
His eyes widened, recognition flashing like a lightning strike through his divine mind.
"It’s YOU!" Ititius shrieked, pointing an accusatory manicured finger straight at Kara’s face! "You are that insolent peasant cur from the secret realm! You are Silas Graves!"
Silas, standing within the shell of Kara White, didn’t answer.
Ititius threw his head back, a sharp mocking bark of laughter tearing from Harper’s throat.

"AHAHAHAHA! Look at you! Look at the mighty!" Ititius mocked, waving Harper’s hands with exaggerated feminine flourishes. "What is this ridiculous little costume?! Did you cross the sea and cast away your manhood just to play at being a woman?! How utterly pathetic! How disgraceful!"
There was nothing... Kara didn’t say anything.

’I’m sure of it now... Ititius,’ Silas thought, the name landing in his skull like a dropped anvil. ’The cockroach who refused to stay dead... The thing that wore her face, butchered a palace, and turned a district into glass...’
’I’m going to kill you.’
SHUUUUUU!
The pinned left sleeve of Kara’s midnight-blue coat tore open.

With a soft fluid hiss of regenerating bone and muscle, a pale muscular left arm materialized from the shoulder, its fingers flexing with sharp cracks as Kara brought both hands up into a low aggressive brawling stance.
Yet beneath the cold fury, her jaw gritted until her teeth ached.
’The body...’
That was the trap, and it was a clean one.
Ititius wasn’t fighting through an avatar as he was wearing Harper’s nervous system.
Every punch Silas threw, every blade he summoned, every spell he channeled would tear through Harper’s flesh before it ever touched the god inside.
The Dawn Blade would cleave her in two and anything fire would burn her to ash.
He didn’t want to hurt Harper.
