paragraphs: Ititius noticed the microscopic hesitation, and his grin widened until the corners of Harper’s lips practically tore.

"Oho~?" Ititius purred, stepping forward with sickening confident ease. "What’s the matter, Graves? Why aren’t you drawing that shiny little sword? Why aren’t you summoning those noisy ocean waves you loved so much in the deep tomb?"
He raised Harper’s left hand and pressed the palm flat against her own sternum.
"Because you know, don’t you? I have her right here... The soul of the woman you love, sealed inside my fist."
SQUEEZE!
Deep within the soul-space, the tiny violet wisp convulsed in his golden grip, flickering like a candle caught in a gale.
’SILAS! IT HURTS! SILAS, PLEASE—’

"Lay a single finger on this body," Ititius smiled, leaning Harper’s face closer, his green eyes burning with pure evil, "and I crush her and if you’re clever enough to keep your hands to yourself, it makes no difference... In a few minutes, once I’ve finished dismantling that heap of iron, I’ll crush her anyway."
He waited, eager and hungry, for the familiar delicious sight of a mortal hero collapsing into weeping paralyzed despair.
He waited for Silas to fall to his knees, to beg, to offer his own life for the woman he loved but there was no despair.
There were no tears either.
Kara White stood completely still, and the silence that settled over her frame was so heavy that the shrieking short-circuit of the Suppression Engine seemed to fade into the background.
Her lips parted.
"Go to hell."
Ititius blinked with his grin freezing for a single second then his golden veins flared with fury.
"DIE, YOU INSIGNIFICANT CUR!" Ititius shrieked.
BZZZZZZZZZT-CRACK!
The machine sparked with a blinding deafening arc of blue lightning, and in that exact second both figures charged.
BOOM!
The stone floor between them violently ruptured as Kara closed the thirty-yard gap with terrifying acceleration with her right fist driving straight toward Harper’s jaw.
’I’ll kill you...’
At the last possible second, Silas hesitated, pulling his force back by thirty percent to avoid shattering Harper’s neck and Ititius saw it.
"WEAK!" Ititius screamed.
SWOOSH!
He dipped Harper’s head beneath the pulled punch and stepped inside Kara’s guard...
Harper’s right elbow, coated in diamond-hard black sand, snapped upward in a vicious rising strike aimed straight at Kara’s throat.
THWACK!
Kara caught the elbow in her fresh left palm and the shockwave tore through the back of her coat, but she didn’t yield an inch.
She pivoted her hips and drove her knee into Harper’s ribs, and once again Silas pulled the force, aiming only to pin the body.
’DAMN IT!’ Silas cursed. ’Every time I pull a strike, he uses the recovery frame!’
Inside the soul-space, Harper’s tiny violet wisp flared with desperate agonizing resolve.
’Silas...’ Harper’s thoughts screamed, thrashing against the crushing golden fingers of the god. ’Don’t hold back! HIT ME! HIT HIM!’

She poured every scrap of her soul-force into disrupting Ititius’s command over her motor nerves as Harper’s left arm spasmed with her fingers twitching uncontrollably, and Ititius’s follow-up strike veered three inches off target.
"Insolent little insect!" Ititius snarled within their shared consciousness, clamping down on her soul with a burst of blinding golden pressure.
CRUNCH!
Silas took the opening, swept Harper’s lead foot, and drove his shoulder forward to send the body crashing to the floor.
THUD-CRACK!
Harper hit the flagstones, but Ititius didn’t skip a beat as he didn’t need balance.
WHOOSH!
Six massive tendrils of black sand erupted from Harper’s back like the legs of a monstrous arachnid, launching her upward while lashing toward Kara’s chest.
SHRIT-SHRIT-SHRIT!
Kara twisted through the air with her boots kicking off the ceiling ribbing, dodging four of the tendrils, but the fifth grazed her cheek and carved a deep bloody gouge along her jawline.
CRACKLE!
The black sand on the wound tried to vitrify her flesh into glass.
"Disperse," She grunted.
FWOOSH!
A pulse of Gold Core mana flushed through Kara’s facial capillaries, incinerating the black mineral before the calcification could take hold and the wound sealed with a hiss of rapid regeneration.
Kara landed thirty paces away, panting slightly and across the chamber, Ititius rose laughing.
"Is that all you have, Graves?!" he mocked. "Even with your other arm in place?!"
CRRRRRR-SNAP!
He didn’t even bother targeting her.
With a sweep of Harper’s arms he drove three massive barbed lances into the short-circuiting hull of the Suppression Engine behind him.
KABOOM!

The plates tore open further as boiling coolant flooded the floor into thick choking clouds, and the machine’s rings began to grind against their tracks with gravity dipping by fractions of a percent as the barrier weakened.
"Every second you waste hesitating," Ititius sneered, "the machine dies and when it dies, my brothers from the Sovereign Realm will pour through the sky like locusts!"
’Physical attacks won’t work,’ Silas thought, his pulse hammering. ’Even if I beat this body unconscious, he’ll burn Harper’s life-force to keep the meat moving until her organs fail...’
He couldn’t hurt the body, and he couldn’t reach the god so Silas did the only thing he had left that he was good at.
He stopped fighting the body and then...
He read it.
The film of moisture across his eyes shivered as he pushed a thin pulse of water mana through it anchored in the tears themselves so the boiling coolant clouds couldn’t smear the image...
The chamber dissolved into glowing blue current lines as every tendon, every twitch of Harper’s frame, every shift of weight, traced in light a heartbeat before it happened.
It should have made this easy but it didn’t... The lines lagged as Harper’s left knee bent, and then its blue line lit...
’What the hell...?’
Her shoulder rolled, and then its line lit and Silas frowned.
He had it backwards, no the body wasn’t moving first.
Something was moving before the body, and the body was only answering.
...There.
Threaded through the blue, so thin he’d taken it for a reflection, ran a second current, gold.
It didn’t follow the muscle at all, instead it poured down from a single knotted point behind Harper’s sternum and out along every limb a hair before the limb obeyed.
When Ititius decided to strike, the gold flowed, and the flesh followed like a puppet on a string.
’He isn’t hitting me with her arms,’ Silas realized, and a cold clean clarity settled over his mind. ’He’s hitting me with that... The body is just where the string ends.’
Mana was the ink and the body was the paper so all this time he’d been punching the paper.
"Stop staring at me!" Ititius shrieked, and lunged.
WHOOM!
Harper’s arm came in cocked for a killing elbow with the gold current flaring down it like a lit fuse, and Silas didn’t dodge.
He watched the gold and the room went quiet.
It was like sinking underwater, every sound dulled and stretched, the roar of the dying Engine draining into a distant hum.
The golden river in Harper’s chest slowed until Silas could see each strand braiding into the knot behind her sternum and his heartbeat fell into step with it.
Thump! Thump!
’The goal is to save Harper and to ensure that he suffers...’
He didn’t push his mana against the current the way he’d pushed against everything his whole life but he let it flow with the current like the way a tide answers the moon.
’There.’
His right fist moved, and it wasn’t aimed at the body at all but it was aimed at the knot beneath it.
WHOOSH!
There was no sound as a hairline tear of black light bloomed at his knuckles, ringed with gold sparks, and then sound returned.
BANG!
"GAAAAAAAHHH!"

Ititius’s scream tore out of Harper’s throat in his own raw tone as Harper’s body didn’t move an inch... She had broken no bones, no thread of her blouse was torn either, but the golden shape inside her chest convulsed and a mouthful of glittering spiritual bile sprayed from her lips.
Ititius’s grip on the violet wisp slipped a full inch and the quiet snapped as the roar of the Engine crashed back in.
Silas staggered a step, staring at his own knuckles and they tingled a bit, as though he’d struck a bell.
’What... was that?’
He had no name for it, what he did just now didn’t feel real at all but he was sure that he did it.
"WHAT DID YOU DO?!" Ititius shrieked with golden veins flaring along Harper’s neck.
Fear turned to blind rage in a heartbeat, and he slammed both hands into the floor.
"DIE!"
Black sand exploded outward in a lashing storm, and Silas threw himself back into the feeling and reached for it.
...Nothing.
He forced it, and it wasn’t there as he swung at a chest that was only a chest, and a sand-hardened elbow crushed into his ribs.
CRUNCH-THUD!
Kara hurtled backward and hit an iron pillar hard enough to dent it and blood filled her mouth.
’Not force,’ Silas thought while pushing himself up. ’It came when I stopped trying to force it... When I listened in a way.’
Ititius was already laughing, gathering himself for a killing blow however Silas closed his eyes for a single breath.
He needed the blue lines and the gold currents as well as the slow patient pulse beneath both...
He opened them, and the world dipped underwater again.
Ititius came at him, and the gold flared down Harper’s right arm a heartbeat before the arm moved; however Silas was already gone from its path.
WHOOSH!
He slid inside the elbow, turned his hip, and his left fist met the current at its source.
The black tear bloomed again.
BANG!
"GAH!"
Ititius spun away, gagging with one hand clawing at a chest that wasn’t hurt, and hurled everything he had.
"DAMN YOU..."

He shot out six lashing legs of sand, a spinning buzzsaw of violet lightning and a lance of black glass punching up through the floor as well... Everything was to ensure that this man in front of him died.
’It won’t be that easy...’
Every attack lit gold before it lit blue.
Silas read each one the way you read a word before it’s finished.
WHOOSH!
He slipped under the disk.
WHOOSH!
He stepped through the gap between two tendrils like a man crossing a busy street.
FWOOSH!
He hopped the glass lance and came down beside it, and the third strike drove into the knot from below like a rising tide.
"IMPOSSIBLE!" Ititius shrieked, and something in his voice cracked. "I AM A GOD! HOW ARE YOU—"
He tried to retreat however he never even started.
The gold flowed toward Harper’s legs, toward the coolant pool behind him, and Silas was already there before the legs finished the thought.
WHOOSH! BANG!
The fourth strike hammered into the knot, and a hairline fracture of silver light split through the golden shape inside Harper’s chest.
"AGHHHHHHHHHHH!"𝙛𝒓𝓮𝙚𝔀𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝓵.𝙘𝒐𝒎
Ititius roared and gave up on dignity.
"DIE, YOU FILTH!"
Harper’s right hand, sheathed in black sand and screaming purple lightning, tore across the air in a blind desperate swipe.
CRUNCH!
It caught Kara across the left side of the face as her cheek, brow, and eye, tore away down to the bone in a spray of vaporized blood...
"Hahaha! I TOOK YOUR EYE, YOU DOG!" Ititius howled but Silas didn’t blink his remaining eye.
He had already stepped in...
His strike had left a half-second before Ititius’s, and it was already traveling.
’I think I need two more strikes.’
The Gold Core roared in his chest with fresh muscle braiding across exposed bone as the fifth strike went home.
BOOM!
"AGGHHHHHHHHHH! STOPPPPPP! W-What kind of monster ARE you?!" Ititius choked with light bleeding through the widening cracks in his soul.
Deep in the soul-space, the crushing grip on Harper’s wisp had gone slack, and she didn’t waste it.
’GET OUT OF MY BODY, YOU SICK BITCH!’
With everything she had, Harper seized her own motor nerves as her knees locked which kept her feet rooted to the flagstones.
Ititius found the body he had stolen, refusing to move...
"NO! MOVE! MOVE, YOU INSIGNIFICANT SLAG!" Ititius shrieked with his soul clawing at a body that was no longer his.
Silas drew back his fist, and the underwater quiet closed over the world one last time.
The blue lines... Gold river... The single violet thread waiting in the middle, and all of it converging on the knot he had struck five times.
’Thank you, Harper.’
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The sixth strike went in like a spear through the center of the tide.
SHRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRK!
Harper’s body didn’t move an inch.
AND YET... An explosion of golden light erupted from Harper’s back.
TEAR!
Like an oil slick scraped from clean glass, Ititius’s towering translucent soul was knocked clean out of Harper’s flesh.
"AGHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH!"
An ear-splitting wail of soul-tearing agony ripped through the cavern as the god’s spiritual avatar tumbled backward through the air and crashed against the basalt wall forty paces away.
Harper’s body swayed on locked knees with her eyes flickering from green back toward violet.

Ititius on the other hand hovered there with his golden robes shredded, his divine diadem cracked in two and his handsome face twisted into disbelieving horror as he looked down at his own translucent hands.
’I... I was expelled...?’ Ititius thought, his mind struggling to comprehend the reality. ’A mortal expelled a god from a vessel?!’
CRACK!
A hairline sound came from his spiritual chest and Ititius looked down as a glowing silver fracture had torn straight through his primary soul-seat.
CRACK! CRACK-CRACK!
The fracture spread... It raced up his neck, across his cheekbones, down both arms!

’Think! I am Ititius! I am a deity!’ the god screamed in the frantic panic of his fading mind. ’I have contingencies! The anchor in the northern pantheon! The soul-shard hidden within the Sovereign Realm’s eighth tier! The dormant relic I pawned to the sea-lords! I will simply transfer my consciousness! I will sleep for three hundred years and return—’
SNAP!
Deep within the cosmic strata, across the infinite expanse of the Sovereign Realm, a series of muted distant pops echoed through reality.
The anchor in the northern pantheon shattered... The soul-shard in the eighth tier was vaporized and the dormant relic in the sea got pulverized in the same instant.

Silas’s strikes hadn’t merely hit the remnant... They had traced the power of the parasite’s unique spiritual frequency and sent a lethal traveling shockwave down every thread that tied him to existence!
Ititius’s golden eyes widened.
"No..." he whimpered, his voice shrinking into a small reedy squeak. "My anchors... all of them... every one..."
CRACK-CRACK-CRACK!
The cracks swallowed his jaw and crept toward his eyes, and his voice spilled out in a broken flood.

"You don’t understand! I was going to fix it! No more hungry children! No more stolen thrones! No more sisters with knives! A god doesn’t get carried to a portal! A god doesn’t get pushed! Nobody would ever... ever... carry me anywhere I didn’t choose to go again!"
The voice cracked and something in it slid, note by note, into a higher softer older tone, until the voice drifting from the crumbling golden figure wasn’t a god’s at all...
"It was so dark, after," the voice said. "I used to sing to them, the little ones, before they were gone... I didn’t know any other songs..."
Silas whose fists were still half-raised went very still.
The dying figure turned its head toward Harper’s swaying body, toward the violet slowly returning to her eyes, and for a moment there was no vanity in the golden face at all.
"Violet," it whispered. "She has my little girl’s eyes."
The cracks reached the lashes.
"I liked the ice cream," the voice said, almost shy. "Pistachio... It was so cold. I never told her..."
A breath like sand pouring through fingers. "Sister... you said we were going home."
A tear of light slid down the cracked golden cheek.
"I only wanted to go home."
SHATTER!
Ititius’s soul imploded into drifting lightless ash.
The ash hung in the cold air for half a second, then evaporated into nothing, leaving not so much as a whisper of him behind on either plane of reality.

"Sister... you said we were going home."
A tear of light slid down the cracked golden cheek.
"I only wanted to go home."
SHATTER!
Ititius’s soul imploded into drifting lightless ash.
The ash hung in the cold air for half a second, then evaporated into nothing, leaving not so much as a whisper of him behind on either plane of reality.

paragraphs: Silas watched it go.
"Good riddance..."
A flicker of something like pity moved through his chest, and he set it aside where it belonged... The man had done too much to just be pitied.
"He’s a waste of the word."
He was happy... the god was dead, for good this time. He would have thrown a celebration if not for the fact that this was not the time.
SWOOSH!
Across the room, Harper’s physical body went completely limp with her knees buckling as gravity claimed her frame.
Kara blurred forward with her arms sliding smoothly under Harper’s shoulders, catching the girl before her face could hit the flagstones.
"Harper!" Kara called out, her voice filled with concern. "Harper, can you hear me?!"
She swept mana through Harper’s core... the golden parasite was gone.
The violet soul was there, firmly seated within her chest and circulating her native lightning mana through her newly healed meridians.
’This is good...’
Harper was whole, for real, and she was fine too.
Kara let out a massive shuddering breath of pure dizzying relief.
"Thank the gods..."
Harper’s eyelids fluttered open.
Her eyes were no longer burning with green or gold fire, they were her own... that intelligent beautiful shade of deep violet.
She looked up.
She saw Kara White’s face hovering over her with the dark hair, the sharp jawline, the half-lidded violet eyes, and found something underneath it that she knew.
"You..." Harper’s voice cracked.
Her pale face was drained of color with her lips trembling violently.
"Vespera... That was... you were Silas?" A wet broken laugh shook out of her. "Ah, I didn’t think it was yo— Sniff!"
With a sudden frantic sob, Harper threw both arms around Kara’s neck.
She pulled herself upward, wrapping her long legs tightly around Kara’s waist, clinging to her as if she were a drowning sailor clutching the last spar of a shattered ship.
"So–sorry..."
Harper buried her face deep into the crook of Kara’s neck, her body shaking with violent uncontrollable sobs that soaked the collar of Kara’s coat with hot tears.

"Don’t let go..." Harper wept hysterically, her fingers digging so hard into the wool of Kara’s mantle that her knuckles turned white. "Please... Silas... Kara... whoever you are... never let go... please don’t leave me in the dark again..."
Kara’s arms wrapped securely around Harper with one at her lower back holding the weeping girl flush against her chest and the other hand gently patting her trembling hair.
"I’ve got you," Kara murmured softly. "You’re safe and the bastard is dead. I’m not letting you go..."
HUMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM!
A strange unnatural sound vibrated through the floorboards which made Kara froze.
She slowly turned her head, looking over Harper’s shoulder toward the center of the chamber.
The Mana-Suppression Engine was no longer glowing azure as the short-circuiting breach where Ititius had punched through the casing had ceased sparking with blue mana.
Instead... a deep crimson light was beginning to bleed from the internal core.
The rings weren’t merely wobbling... they were spinning in erratic screaming reverse.
DING! DING! DING!
The First King’s stabilization runes along the housing were turning cherry-red, hissing violently as the alloy began to warp and liquify under an unprecedented build-up of mana.
Kara’s eyes blinked once then twice.
"No..." Kara muttered, the blood draining from her face until she looked like a corpse. "No, no, no, no, no..."
Harper sniffled against his neck, sensing the sudden tension. "Wh-what is happening...?"
BOOM!
Kara didn’t answer.
She kicked off the floor with every ounce of physical power her legs could generate as she sprinted toward the circular exhaust shaft, carrying Harper tightly against her chest.
"IT’S GOING TO BLOW!" Kara roared.
She reached the base of the vertical shaft, channeled a colossal column of compressed wind mana beneath her boots, and rocketed upward through the four-thousand-foot chimney like an artillery shell.
KABOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Beneath them, the Mana-Suppression Engine reached critical mass and it did what anything in its position would do... It exploded.
VRM! VRM! VRM!
The explosion that followed wasn’t a regular one though... It was an apocalyptic rupture of space itself.

The crimson detonation vaporized the half-mile basalt dome into subatomic dust in the span of a single second as an expanding sphere of raw spatial distortion tore through four thousand feet of solid continental bedrock, shooting straight up the exhaust shaft like a volcanic piston of energy.
The shockwave tore through reality itself, sending seismic and dimensional waves rolling across the entire continent.
Above ground, in the ruins of the three-mile crater of Iunu...
BOOM-CRASH!

Kara broke through the surface of the earth, tumbling violently out of the yawning crater shaft... as the concussive back-blast of the detonation clipped her heels, throwing her sixty yards across the vitrified black glass of the basin.
"Fuck! Fuck! Fuck!"

She twisted her body in mid-air, curling her torso into a protective shield around Harper, taking the brutal impact across her own back and shoulders as they rolled across the glass, kicking up plumes of dark silt before coming to a sliding halt against the shattered rim of the crater.
Kara coughed, spitting a mouthful of blood and black sand onto the glass with her vision spinning from the impossible force of the blast.
There were many forces that she could withstand easily and this seemed to not be one of them...
Kara rolled onto her side, looking down at Harper.
The girl was completely unconscious with her breathing shallow, but she was alive as the shock of the dimensional rupture had knocked her out cold.
"Good... Ugh..."
Kara let out a trembling breath, slowly pushing herself up onto her knees.
"We made it..." she whispered, wiping the blood from her chin. "We survived the blast..."
She slowly raised her head, looking up toward the sky above Iunu and in that single microsecond... Kara completely froze.
The breath died in her throat as the sky was no longer blue... It wasn’t even the bruised purple of the earlier clouds...
High above the capital of Khemet, tearing straight through the upper thermosphere... a colossal tear in the fabric of space was violently ripping open.
...It wasn’t one... It wasn’t two...
CRACK-CRACK-CRACK-CRACK-CRACK!
Dozens, then hundreds, of massive swirling pitch-black gates to the Sovereign Realm were violently manifesting across the sky with their edges bleeding raw chaotic mana into the atmosphere.
And from the center of the largest portal directly over the city...
CREEEEEEAK!

A colossal rotting skeletal hand, easily the size of an entire city block, slowly reached out from the void with its bone fingers gripping the edge of the dimensional tear as an ear-splitting roar of thousands of monsters echoed through the heavens!
’Wh... what...’
Kara’s mind fractured in pure horror.
’What he took down was a Suppression Engine...’

Since the Suppression Engine was dead, the anchor was broken... The barrier that had kept the horrors of the Sovereign Realm locked away from the mortal world since the era of the Second King had just been shattered right above their heads.
Down in the outer sectors, sirens were screaming... buildings were collapsing as smaller portals began tearing open directly on the street level.
Citizens were running through the avenues, screaming in helpless terror as winged horrors and four-legged chittering abominations began raining from the sky.
’What am I supposed to do...?’ Kara thought with her hand trembling as he looked down at the unconscious woman in her lap.
Where was the World Council?! Where was everybody else?!
People were going to die... Tens of thousands of innocent civilians were going to be butchered in the streets... all because of that dead bastard Ititius.
’I killed him but now I don’t even feel happy...’
And his own family... Kara’s heart seized with suffocating dread.
’Lia... Martha... Penelope... Kaede...’
They were three miles away in the Grand Oasis Palace!

Evelyn’s private jet was still two hours out and if Silas abandoned this crater to sprint across the city to shield his hotel, his reputation as Lord Vespera, the Hero of Humanity, the beacon of hope the World Council had made her to be, would vanish the moment the cameras caught him fleeing the frontlines.
But if he stayed here to fight... how could one single Gold Core hold back an entire falling ocean of monster legions?!
Even with the local Awakened, Iunu’s elite forces had already been wiped out in the palace!
’What do I do...?!’ Silas screamed internally, staring at the descending skeletal hand with wide desperate eyes. ’How do I save them all?!’
Suddenly...
A sharp crisp chime echoed directly in his head.
DING!
A glowing translucent blue notification slate materialized in the air before Kara’s face.
[THE ENERGY OF THE SOVEREIGN REALM HAS BEEN DETECTED IN THE SURROUNDING AREA.]
[COMMAND: SELECT TEN (10) ENTITIES (HERO / TROOP / MOUNT) TO SUMMON FOR DEPLOYMENT FROM YOUR TERRITORY.]
Kara blinked.
The hopeless desperate terror that had clamped around Silas’s heart vanished in a fraction of a second.
A slow smile spread across Kara White’s blood-stained face.
’Summon...?’
She raised her right hand, her thumb hovering over the glowing interface.
’Thank you.’
Kara tapped the tab.
The sky above the northern expanse of the Khemet Dominion decayed.
For centuries, the mortal realm had lived beneath the invisible reassurance of the Suppression Engines.

To the average merchant in the lower bazaars of Iunu, to the dockworkers unloading salt-crates along the canals, and to the tourists sipping iced hibiscus nectar beneath white-linen awnings, the Sovereign Realm was a distant abstraction... a place cordoned off behind strict international treaties, governed by licensed territorial lords who entered through their System tabs under the watchful eye of the World Council.
Whenever a wild rift had occasionally torn through the desert in the decades prior, it was an isolated telegraphed anomaly.
Sirens would sound twelve hours in advance.

Atmospheric barometers would register mana spikes with clean precision and Imperial marshals would evacuate surrounding sectors, cordon the perimeter with portable runic pylons, and dispatch a vetted strike team to clear the incursion before the beasts could take their first breath of Earth air.
Civilization had grown accustomed to order... Civilization had forgotten that the world was built upon a thin crust of cooling stone floating over an infinite ravenous ocean of nightmares...
Now, that crust was gone.

Across thirty thousand square miles of the northern part of Khemet, stretching from the smoking glass-lined crater where the White Citadel had once stood all the way to the jagged shale ridges of the border escarpments, space was tearing itself to ribbons.
CRACK-CRACK-CRACK-CRACK-CRACK!
Hundreds upon hundreds of jagged lightless fissures fractured the sky in violent detonations of atmospheric pressure...

They looked like veins of black ink spreading through clear water, vomiting thick plumes of sulfurous crimson mist and howling winds that stripped the roofs from high-rise complexes and sent parked hover-transports tumbling down the avenues like crumpled paper cups.
And from the yawning bellies of those fissures, the horrors poured forth.
SCREEEEEECH!
GROOOOOOOWL!

Winged chittering monstrosities with segmented chitinous carapaces and lamprey maws... four-legged stalkers whose muscles were exposed cords of black lightning, undulating masses of necrotic sludge that melted the asphalt beneath their bellies and thousands of abominations, starved of flesh for centuries, converged upon the living city in a falling shrieking avalanche of violence.
Two thousand feet above the skyway of Iunu’s Major Sector, a twin-rotor civilian news helicopter bucked and rattled violently against the gale-force thermals.
THWAP-THWAP-THWAP-THWAP-THWAP!
Inside the vibrating cockpit, warning klaxons were blaring in an ear-splitting intermittent rhythm.

Red fault indicators flashed across the flight console as the pilot... a middle-aged man named Bakr whose flight suit was completely saturated with dark rings of cold sweat wrestled frantically with the collective stick with his knuckles white and his foot stomping the anti-torque pedal as turbulent gusts of spatial displacement threatened to flip the airframe inverted.

"WE HAVE TO TURN AROUND!" Bakr screamed over the roar of the engines and the deafening shriek of the sirens, his voice cracking into panic. "ARE YOU OUT OF YOUR GODDAMN MINDS?! LOOK AT THE SENSORS! THE ENTIRE UPPER STRATOSPHERE IS CHOKED WITH HIGH-TIER MANA-SHEARS... IF A SINGLE RIFT CREATURE CLIPS OUR ROTOR HEAD, WE’RE DEAD BEFORE WE HIT THE ASPHALT! I’M ABORTING THE FLIGHT! I AM PULLING PITCH FOR THE SOUTHERN MOUNTAINS RIGHT NOW!"
"DON’T YOU DARE TOUCH THAT YOKE, BAKR!"
Standing by the open side-cargo hatch, leaning precariously out into the sub-zero, roaring slipstream with only a nylon safety harness keeping her from plunging into the abyss, was Nadia Khoury.
Nadia was thirty-two, an investigative war correspondent for the Mediterranean Broadcast Syndicate who had covered border insurgencies and illegal rift-mining operations across three continents.

Her windbreaker was whipping violently against her ribs with her short dark hair plastered against her forehead by sweat and freezing mist, but her hand clamped onto the broadcast microphone with the grip of a vice.
Beside her, braced against the bulkhead with his knees bent and his back braced against an avionics rack, was Samir, her veteran cameraman.

He had a heavy shoulder-mounted arcane optical rig pressed against his right eye, his calloused thumbs constantly tweaking the focal rings as he tracked the descending nightmare below with his jaw clenched so hard his molars ground together audibly.

"Nadia!" Samir yelled over his shoulder, his eye still glued to the glowing ocular viewscreen. "The global satellite uplink just synchronized... The feed went live on thirty-six international feeds! Views just cleared forty million, now eighty! It’s spiking exponentially! Every network in the Europa Directorate and the North American Coalition is rebroadcasting our feed!"
Nadia didn’t care about the numbers and she didn’t care about the corporate ratings either.
She turned her face into the stinging gale, looking directly into the high-definition lens of the arcane rig with her voice projecting through the microphone.

"If you are watching this broadcast anywhere in the civilized world... Listen to me!" Nadia spoke, the camera panning slightly to frame the apocalyptic horizon behind her. "This is not an unverified rumor... This is not a controlled military exercise. At fourteen hundred hours, following an unprecedented detonation that completely erased the Inner District of Iunu, It seems the Suppression Engine has suffered a failure!"
She pointed her trembling hand outward toward the city below.

"Look at your screens! Rifts to the Sovereign Realm are tearing open by the hundreds! The northern skyline of Khemet has completely ceased to exist! There is no barrier! Monsters of high-tier classification... creatures not seen since the Incursion are descending directly into residential districts! If this breach is not contained immediately, the chain reaction will propagate across Khemet within twelve hours!"
She leaned forward, her eyes wide, pleading with the look of someone watching their world burn in real-time.

"To the High Marshals of the World Council! To the standing armies of the Nine Powers! To any Lord or guild within traveling distance... Iunu needs help! We are facing a total extinction event! Send reinforcements! SEND—"
SCREEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEECH!
A bone-scraping wail tore through the roar of the turbine.
"SAMIR! LOOK OUT!" the pilot shrieked.

Monsters of high-tier classification... creatures not seen since the Incursion are descending directly into residential districts!
If this breach is not contained immediately, the chain reaction will propagate across Khemet within twelve hours!"

"To the High Marshals of the World Council!
To the standing armies of the Nine Powers!
To any Lord or guild within traveling distance...
Iunu needs help!
We are facing a total extinction event!
Send reinforcements!
SEND—"
SCREEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEECH!
A bone-scraping wail tore through the roar of the turbine.
"SAMIR!
LOOK OUT!" the pilot shrieked.

paragraphs: From the base of a swirling crimson cloud three hundred yards above, a shadow dropped like a falling meteor.

It was a monstrosity forged from yellowed bone and calcified sinew... a creature spanning forty feet from wingtip to wingtip, possessing the curved ribcage of a feline and the colossal hooked skull of a raptor.
WHOOOOSH!
It had no feathers as its wings were ribbed sheets of translucent rotting skin through which pulsing black veins pumped bile.
Its hollow eye sockets burned with cold corpse-blue fire. This monster was known as a Bone-Gryphon though none of them would be able to know this...
"EVASIVE!" Bakr wailed, hauling the stick back with all his strength, however the motion was useless.
CRASH-CRUNCH!
The massive serrated bone talons of the beast slammed directly into the helicopter’s tail-boom.
The reinforced titanium-alloy structural tubing crumpled like an empty tin can with the high-speed tail rotor violently severing in a blinding shower of sparks and shearing metal.
BZZZZZZT-KABOOM!
The torque instantly threw the helicopter into a violent uncontrolled flat spin.
Inside the cabin, gravity inverted.

Nadia was ripped from her footing with her harness snapping taut with enough force to bruise her sternum while Samir’s heavy camera rig slammed against the bulkhead, his head bouncing off the metal with a sickening wet crack as blood sprayed across the lens.

"MAYDAY! MAYDAY! WE’RE SPINNING OUT! WE’RE GOING IN—" Bakr’s screams dissolved into hysterical breathless prayers as the ground... the burning streets, the shattered limestone avenues, and the charging hordes of monsters, they all rushed upward at one hundred and twenty miles per hour.
The centrifugal force tore the breath from Nadia’s lungs as the sky and the earth blurred into a dizzying kaleidoscope of smoke, fire, and roaring wind.
’I’m going to die,’ She thought. ’I’m dying live on international television.’
Nadia squeezed her eyes shut, waiting for the concussive fiery impact that would pulverize her bones into paste against the concrete.
...Except the impact never came.
WHOOOOOOSH!
The violent sickening rotation abruptly ceased...
The roaring scream of the runaway turbines was swallowed by an impossibly deep soundless vacuum of cool fragrant air which made Nadia blink while her eyelashes were caked with cold sweat.
The helicopter wasn’t shattered across the asphalt... It was sitting perfectly upright instead.
Its landing skids rested upon the cracked flagstones of a wide, sunken public plaza outside the depot of Sector Four.
The engine was smoking with the shattered tail-boom hanging limp, but the cabin was intact.

Beside her, Samir was groaning, holding his bleeding forehead, while the pilot, Bakr, was still white-knuckle gripping the controls with his chest heaving as he screamed incoherently at the instrument panel.
"Bakr... Bakr, stop screaming!" Nadia gasped, her hands shaking frantically as she fumbled with the buckle of her harness. "Stop shouting! We’re on the ground! We’re... we’re alive?!"
"H-Huh?!" Bakr blinked, his voice hitching as he looked out the cockpit canopy. "What... what did we hit?! Did the auto-rotations work?! Where are the flames?!"
"Nadia..." Samir whispered, his voice trembling so hard the words barely left his lips.
He didn’t look at the damaged helicopter, instead he was pointing his trembling blood-stained index finger straight up through the open cargo hatch toward the sky.
"Look... look up..."
Nadia turned her head, stepping out onto the skid, and froze.
Directly above them, doming over the entire four-square-block plaza like an impenetrable glowing mountain of solid crystal was a purple barrier.
It was mesmerizing.
It wasn’t the flat utilitarian gold of Khemet’s solar shields that she was used to... It was a radiant luminous purple, pulsing with a honeycombed design that hummed slowly.
THUD! CRACK! CRUNCH!

Outside the glowing purple dome, dozens of beasts... hulking six-legged trench-drakes, swarms of razor-winged carrion bats, and necrotic ghouls were hurling themselves against the crystalline hexagons with suicidal fury.
Yet, the moment their claws, their teeth, or their bile touched the purple surface, they didn’t even leave a scratch!
The barrier simply reflected the kinetic output straight back into their bodies, turning their bones to powder and sending their mangled carcasses tumbling backward into the dust.
...And hovering thirty feet in the air, right at the apex of the honeycombed dome, stood the architect of their salvation.
Nadia’s breath died in her throat.
It was an elf.
She was breathtakingly regal, suspended weightlessly against the smoky sky as if gravity were merely a polite suggestion she chose to ignore.
Her hair was a cascading river of spun pale gold, falling past her waist, shimmering with iridescent motes of starlight.
Her skin was porcelain and unblemished by the falling ash, and her eyes...
They were a deep gold-silver light that was actively bleeding out from the pupil, carrying a terrifying luminescence that seemed to hold the silent uncaring infinity of a thousand distant nebulae.
She was draped in pristine form-fitting armor, its pauldrons and vambraces etched with intricate runes that subtly shifted and rotated across the metal plates in real-time.
The elven woman looked down through the glowing purple dome with her gaze sweeping over the terrified news crew and the hundreds of battered bleeding civilians huddled in the sunken plaza below.
"Calm yourselves, everyone," the elf spoke.
Her voice wasn’t loud at all yet it resonated within the marrow of their bones, carrying an effortless authority that immediately cut through the hysterical weeping of the crowd.
This woman was strong...

"I have been made aware by the locals that the heavy access hatches situated at the center of this place lead into the civil protection bunkers," she said, her slender armored hand gesturing gracefully toward the massive blast-rated iron doors embedded in the plaza floor. "You will proceed down those stairs in an orderly fashion immediately... Do not stampede and do not leave your wounded behind."
Nadia scrambled down from the skid, her journalistic instincts firing through the fog of her adrenaline.
She looked around the plaza.
...It was true.

Dozens of people... families carrying crying children, wounded office workers, and bruised guards were actively materializing into the plaza in brief soft flashes of violet light, plucked from collapsing buildings across the sector and deposited safely onto the stone flags.

Guiding them toward the bunker doors were seven local Awakened Lords... men and women whose ornate silks were torn, their mana cores flickering with dangerous instability and their faces hollow with shock.
They looked battered yet they were frantically ushering the citizens downward into the concrete depths.
Nadia stepped closer to the edge of the barrier, squinting up at the glowing breastplate of the floating archon.
There was a crest that she knew all too well.
Nadia gasped, the microphone nearly slipping from her numb fingers.

"That crest..." she stammered, her voice carrying through the syndicate’s international feed, broadcasting to two hundred million terrified viewers across the globe. "You... you’re from Blessed Land?! The domain of Lord Vespera?!"
Up in the air, the cold distant archon expression on the elf’s face subtly cracked.

Aeliana looked down at the disheveled woman holding the microphone with her lips parting into a small remarkably soft breathtakingly radiant smile that completely dispelled the terrifying chill of her presence.
"Indeed," Aeliana replied, her chin lifting with quiet pride. "I am Aeliana, the Astrea Archon of the Stars... I serve as a sworn commander under the banner of Lord Vespera."
She paused, looking across the burning avenues beyond the barrier.

"Make haste into the earth, citizens... I have locked down six shelter access nodes across this quadrant, anchoring spatial stability fields over each opening... As far as my sensory webs can reach, the civilians in this sector will not be touched by the monsters."

"B-But there are too many!" Nadia shouted back, gesturing frantically toward the sky where dozens more black fissures were violently tearing open, disgorging an endless tide of horrors. "The entire northern sky is falling... There are thousands of them, tens of thousands even! You can’t hold this entire sector alone!"
Aeliana’s smile didn’t fade.
If anything, the glow ringing her irises sharpened, brightening with an amused light.
"Alone?" Aeliana chuckled, the sound like silver bells echoing across the ruins. "You misunderstand... I am not alone... My sisters are with me as well. Blessed Land will protect all of you!"
’Did that sound cool...?’ Aeli thought with a bright blush painting her inner thoughts, she was trying as hard as possible to do so.
SCREEEEECH!
Above the honeycombed dome, the sky violently darkened.
A swarm of over fifty Bone-Gryphons, accompanied by hundreds of razor-winged shadow-crows, converged upon Aeliana’s position, drawn by the blinding luminescence of her power.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH! WHOOSH!

They dove in a tight funnel of snapping jaws and barbed bone talons, descending upon the floating elf with enough collective weight to probably level a mountain fortress, however Aeliana didn’t retreat beneath her barrier.
"Hmph."
She simply turned her body to face the incoming swarm of fifty abominations, her golden eyebrows rising in lazy amusement.
’Good,’ she thought, her lips curving into a confident grin. ’Gather close. It makes the challenge so much cleaner.’
CRRRRRRK!
Aeliana raised her left arm with her fingers curling as if gripping an invisible bow!
From the open air, condensation of pure violent purple starlight bled into reality...
In the span of a single second, a magnificent recurved composite greatbow that was forged from translucent cosmic mana materialized in her grip.
Her right hand reached back, drawing an invisible string.
BZZZZZZZZZT-SHRRRRRK!
An arrow formed on the rest and it wasn’t simply a physical projectile... Aeliana needed to show off after all.
’Heh.’

It was a spinning five-foot lance of compressed purple spatial plasma and the energy was spinning so fast that it weaved an inverted gravity well around the arrowhead that caused the atmospheric moisture in the air to instantly freeze into microscopic violet diamonds.
The concussive pressure of the drawn string caused the air around Aeliana to bend, casting rippling distortions across the clouds.
"I hope you’re ready..."
PING!
She released.
KABOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The displacement was so violent that a concussive shockwave exploded outward from Aeliana’s shoulders, ripping through the sky with the roar of a cannon.

Even through the thick, honeycombed purple barrier protecting the plaza below, the blast wave rattled Nadia’s teeth, sending the reporter’s hair thrashing frantically around her face as Samir fought to keep the camera steady.
The purple arrow tore across the sky, leaving a blinding violet trench through the crimson clouds!
SPLAT-CRUNCH!
It slammed directly into the breastbone of the lead Bone-Gryphon!
BOOOOOOM!
The compressed arrow discharged an expansive, blinding shockwave that illuminated three square miles of the city in high-intensity purple radiance.
The lead gryphon, along with eight of the beasts flanking it, was instantly vaporized into drifting white bone-dust.

Beneath her, three of the Bone-Gryphons had survived the outer edge of the blast with their charred wings smoking as they wheeled back for a second pass, shrieking a corrupted wet cry that vibrated the fillings in a mortal jaw from a mile away.
Aeliana didn’t bother drawing again as she simply closed her fist.
CRUNCH-CRUNCH-CRUNCH!

The compressed gravity still lingering from the first detonation folded all three inward at once, crumpling wing, bone, and shrieking beak into a single fist-sized ball of white ash before it had time to fall.
Yet, the remaining forty abominations didn’t halt... Driven by primal frenzy, they surged through the smoke, screeching as their claws reached for Aeliana’s throat.
’The battle was over when I released my attack...’
She stood in mid-air, lowering the bow with her lips curving into an arrogant smirk.
"Collapse," she whispered.
HUMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM!
In the exact point where the first arrow had detonated in the sky... reality violently inverted.
’Huh?’ Nadia thought as a strange spatial phenomenon erupted.
A microscopic pitch-black singularity manifested at the epicenter of the purple smoke.
WHOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!

An irresistible gravitational vacuum roared to life immediately as the forty charging Bone-Gryphons, their shrieking wings beating frantically against the air, found themselves powerless against the spatial pull.
"Come on... die for me!"

Their momentum violently reversed and with sickening unnatural velocity, all forty massive beasts... along with hundreds of falling building fragments and stray shadow-crows were dragged backward through the sky, sucked uncontrollably toward that single microscopic point in space.
’Spatial...’
They collided in mid-air with the horrific wet crunch of snapping bones, twisting into a massive tangled helpless ball of thrashing limbs and shrieking maws.
And then... the singularity reached critical mass.
’Distortion.’
FLASH! KABOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A second spatial detonation tore through the upper atmosphere as the tangled ball of forty apex monsters was completely obliterated in a blinding supernova of purple spatial fire.

The secondary shockwave rolled across the northern sector, smashing through the upper stories of six abandoned corporate high-rises, shearing the concrete towers in two and throwing millions of tons of shattered glass and pulverized masonry into the empty sky...
Beneath the barrier, the hundreds of civilians stood in dead paralyzed silence.
"Wha– what strength..."
Nadia Khoury stared up at the empty sky where forty high-tier monsters had flown bare heartbeats ago.
Not a single feather remained and not a single scrap of bone fell to the earth either.
There was only the quiet gentle drift of purple starlight motes that settled over the city like falling snow.
Aeliana slowly turned her head, looking back down toward the open-mouthed reporter.
"You are safe," Aeliana said calmly. "Get beneath the stone."
Nadia scrambled forward, practically lunging against the outer perimeter of the purple ward, desperately thrusting the microphone toward the sky.

"Lord Archon! Please! Wait!" Nadia shouted, her voice trembling with professional desperation. "Who authorized this intervention?! The World Council has not issued an emergency mandate! Is Lord Vespera deploying her army without any clearance?! What is—"
WHOOSH!
Aeliana didn’t answer.
With a single effortless flick of her armored ankles, Aeliana shot straight up into the air like a rising star with speed that sent a circular ring of white vapor expanding across the clouds.
As she climbed through the freezing skies, sheets of fine crystalline frost began to creep out from the pores of her slender hands, coating her vambraces in sharp translucent rime.
Her eyes scanned the chaotic burning horizon, and beneath the calm dignity of an elf, a sudden deep crimson blush bloomed across the tips of her pointed ears.
’Ten minutes...’ Aeliana thought, her heart hammering against her ribs with an intensity that had nothing to do with the monsters circling in the clouds.

’It has only been ten minutes since our Lord tore open the world and summoned the ten of us into this realm! So this is Earth, huh? Unfortunately the Internet is down... I wanted to see their smut novels.’

paragraphs: Her hands trembled slightly... It was not from fear, but from the boiling excitement coursing through her meridians.
’This whole thing... It’s a game.’
Before Silas had dispatched them across the burning districts of Iunu, a silent unspoken decree had rippled through the ranks of the ten summoned women...

Whoever earned the greatest amount of UP in the Lord’s eyes would receive a single personal reward upon their return, one he’d refused to name aloud, only smiling that casual devastating smile of his when the girls demanded details.
Aeliana’s breath hitched in her throat with her chest heaving as she remembered that smile.

’I don’t even know what it is,’ she thought, her cheeks burning so hot they melted the frost forming on her cheekbones, ’and I already want it more than I have ever wanted anything in my entire existence... Whatever it is, it looked so sweet on his face when he refused to say it out loud... I want it for myself, and I will not share it with anyone.’

’Brida is currently anchoring the southern boulevard with her titan shield! Morwenna is down there, laughing like a drunken cutthroat while she cleaves through monsters! Tasmin is already drowning the western shadows as well! If I spend too much time speaking to people, those shameless vixens will overtake my tally!’
SCREEECH!

Above her, an entire descending formation of two hundred winged chitterers and three massive four-winged rift-beasts broke through a newly formed fissure, diving straight toward her rising silhouette.
Aeliana looked up.
WHOOSH!
"I haven’t gotten to use the extent of my power before... I guess I can test it out on you all."
She simply threw her arms wide, letting her head tilt back into the freezing wind.
’I will not lose to them!’
WOOOOOOO!

The atmospheric pressure around Aeliana’s body violently warped, bending the light, bending the wind, bending the very fabric of space until the clouds began to swirl around her like a celestial whirlpool.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A multi-layered nova of purple spatial energy exploded outward from her chest, with Aeliana standing at the epicenter of the blast.
The heaven-shattering detonation tore through the sky, obliterating all two hundred monsters into subatomic dust, lighting up the sky in a beautiful flash of starlight.
’I need to kill more...’
[Three Miles Away.]
The penthouse floor of the Grand Oasis Palace was a fortress of luxury that had suddenly been transformed into a chamber of suffocating terror.
RUMBLE-SHAKE!
The thirty-story hospitality tower groaned beneath its foundations.
Through the massive, floor-to-ceiling panoramic glass windows that wrapped around the private lounge, the panoramic view of Iunu was a vision of the end of days.
The once-gleaming white limestone avenues were choked with black smoke, burning vehicles, and swarms of dark writhing shapes that poured from the sky like an endless plague of locusts.
Inside the suite, Penelope was pressed against the back of an upholstered sofa, her small hands clutching Lia’s oversized grey cardigan so tightly that her knuckles were bloodless.
Her vibrant purple hair was loose, thrashing against her cheeks as her wide dilated eyes stared out through the glass.
’Big sis...’ Penelope’s thoughts were a frantic bleeding spiral of guilt and terror. ’Silas... where are you...?’
...They were out there.

Somewhere in that burning ocean of falling rifts and screaming monsters, her older sister was either dead or trapped inside the body of a monster and Silas... the man who had looked her in the eyes, smiled, and promised he would bring Harper home had vanished into that exact same abyss.

’It’s my fault,’ Penelope wept silently, her lower lip trembling violently. ’If I hadn’t panicked... if I hadn’t run to their estate and begged Silas to come to this place... they wouldn’t be in this city. None of us would be here.’
Beside her, sitting on the Persian carpet with her knees drawn tightly against her chest, was Lia Graves.
The ten-year-old girl was hyperventilating, her small chest heaving with rapid shallow gasps of air.
Her face was pale as chalk, her large dark eyes reflecting the fire burning across the distant rooftops.
"Martha..." Lia whispered, her voice cracking into a tiny fragile whimper. "Is... is Big Brother going to be okay? The sky... the sky is broken. Why is the sky broken?"
Martha knelt immediately beside the two girls, her starch-stiff maid’s apron rustling as she wrapped her strong steady arms around both of their shoulders, pulling them firmly against her chest.
Despite the blaring sirens and the violent tremors rattling the crystal chandeliers overhead, Martha’s expression was a mask of cold immovable composure.

"Hush now, little miss," Martha murmured softly, her fingers gently smoothing down Lia’s hair. "Your brother is not an ordinary man. Master Silas is a Lord that has walked through the gates of the Sovereign Realm... A few stray rifts and noisy beasts will not claim his life. He gave his word that he would return for dinner, and Master Silas has never once broken a promise to this household."
Standing near the balcony doors, arms crossed over her chest, was Kaede.

The girl’s dark eyes were fixed on the sky with her jaw set and behind her, standing in a tight disciplined diamond formation, were the four elite Awakened bodyguards her older brother Minamoto had assigned to the charter.
Unfortunately they were Adventurers or they would have been able to summon people from their territory.
They were massive men, draped in traditional armor of lacquered black plates and woven spirit-silk with their faces hidden behind dark mempo masks.
The lead guard... a Third Stage veteran named Kenji whose core hummed with steady earth mana stepped forward, his voice carrying the calm confidence of a seasoned military professional.

"Do not distress yourselves, Lady Kaede, Young Miss Graves," Kenji spoke through his mask. "The Grand Oasis Palace was engineered to withstand high-magnitude seismic events and rift incursions... The primary barrier enveloping this tower is an independent Class-Four one, anchored directly to deep bedrock generators. It is designed to deflect bombardment from heavy artillery and aerial beasts so nothing short of a Tier 4 monster could breach this perimeter... We are completely safe within these w—"
Before the shadow ever touched the glass, the sound arrived first.
CREEEEEAK... CREEEEEAK... CREEEEEAK...
A slow groan of shifting obsidian scales against reinforced concrete, each plate the size of a dinner table dragging across the building’s exterior wall like a mountain being slowly skinned alive.
Beneath it, a deep pulse thudded through the floor.
THUD... THUD... THUD... KRA-KRA-KRA-KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The sentence was violently severed by an impact so monstrous that the entire thirty-story tower shrieked like tearing metal...
The Class-Four barrier didn’t deflect the blow as advertised...
CRACK-SHATTER!
The golden hexagonal energy dome enveloping the penthouse shattered into millions of blinding useless sparks in a fraction of a second.
CREEEEEEAK-CRUNCH!
A shadow coiled violently around the exterior of the upper three floors.
It was an abyssal horror of nightmarish proportions... a colossal six-hundred-foot-long Demonic Dune-Serpent.
Its scales weren’t bone or reptile skin... they were thick, overlapping plates of jagged pitch-black obsidian that ground against the concrete with the deafening sound of an industrial rock-crusher.

Hundreds of glowing, crimson compound eyes lined its titanic triangular skull, and its maw, lined with rows of translucent six-foot-long fangs dripping with acidic green bile, spanned forty feet across.
The beast constricted.
CRUNCH! SNAP! GROAN!

The structural steel ribbing of the penthouse crumpled like dry paper... The thirty-story tower violently tilted sixty degrees to the side, throwing furniture, grand pianos, and marble tables sliding across the floor in a chaotic avalanche.
"LOOK OUT!" Kenji roared.
SMASH!
The massive, horned snout of the serpent drove straight through the panoramic floor-to-ceiling glass as ten tons of reinforced, shatter-proof crystal exploded inward in a hurricane of flying shards.

The howling gale-force desert wind flooded the suite, carrying the sickening rotten stench of the serpent’s breath... a smell like boiling copper and decaying organs that instantly made Penelope choke and gag.
"EVACUATE!" Kenji bellowed, his Third Stage earth mana flaring violently around his boots.
"SECURE THE PRINCIPALS! GO! GO!"
The four bodyguards moved with flawless military synchronization.
Kenji lunged forward with his heavy arm scooping Kaede against his chest.
A second guard dove across the tilting floor, grabbing Martha by the waist, while the remaining two guards threw their bodies forward to shield Lia and Penelope.
SCREEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEECH!
The serpent opened its colossal throat, releasing a deafening concussive blast of pure sonic energy.
BOOM!
The shockwave hit the room like a freight train!
The two guards reaching for the girls were violently blasted backward with their heavy armor denting as they slammed through the interior drywall.
Martha screamed, her hand slipping from Lia’s fingers as the force tore them apart.
WHOOOOOOSH!
The floor beneath them completely gave way as the entire outer half of the penthouse suite broke off from the central elevator core, sliding out into the empty three-hundred-foot abyss.
"Ahhhhh!"

Penelope shrieked as she tumbled through the broken window frame, caught in mid-air by the third guard who wrapped his massive, armored arms around her, desperately firing his grapple toward the lower concrete ledges.
Kenji leaped into the void with Kaede, his earth mana coating their skin in a dense crystalline skin, preparing to slam into the lower roofs to absorb the shock.
And Lia...
"LIA!" Martha screamed from mid-air with her hand reaching out into the empty sky as she fell.
Lia Graves was alone.
The ten-year-old girl tumbled through the freezing three-hundred-foot drop while spinning wildly out of control...
The wind tore the breath from her throat, whipping Lia’s hair across her eyes, turning the burning city into a spinning blur of asphalt and smoke.
The ground was rushing toward her at terminal velocity...
Three hundred feet... two hundred feet... one hundred feet...
She looked down at the cold cracked pavement of the avenue below as her small hands clutched the fabric of her dress.
The thought was small.
’...am I going to die?’
WHOOSH!
There was no sound of bones breaking and there was no cold crushing impact against concrete either.
In a fraction of a second, the roaring slipstream simply... vanished.
Lia’s falling momentum decelerated with impossible gentleness, as if she had fallen into a deep warm drift of silk feathers.
TAP!
Lia’s head landed softly.
"Huh?"
She blinked, her breath coming in tiny trembling gasps with her eyes slowly opening.
She wasn’t on the asphalt.
Her head was resting upon a pair of impossibly soft warm delicate thighs draped in diaphanous flowing robes of spun silver-white silk that smelled intoxicatingly of blooming mountain orchids.
Lia slowly tilted her chin upward and her breath completely caught in her throat.
...Looking down at her was a woman.
A woman so breathtakingly beautiful that the concept of mortal beauty seemed like a crude unrefined sketch by comparison.

She possessed a face that looked as though it had been sculpted from living moonlight, framed by long flowing tresses of pale silver-green hair that drifted gently in the breeze like the weeping branches of an ancient willow tree.

Her eyes were deep emerald pools that carried the serene warmth of a forest... eyes that held no fear, no anger, only an infinite maternal gentleness that instantly washed the terror clean from Lia’s shivering soul.
Floating around them in the air, twenty feet above the street, was a gentle undulating sea of radiant emerald-green energy.
Lia looked over the edge of the woman’s lap.

Every single person who had fallen from the thirty-story tower... Kaede, Kenji, the other three bodyguards, Penelope, and Martha was suspended weightlessly in mid-air, cradled safely within soft glowing cocoons of warm green mana that drifted down toward the pavement like dandelion seeds.
A slender cool finger, soft as a flower petal, gently brushed across Lia’s left cheekbone.
Lia blinked.
Bare seconds ago, a stray shard of window glass had carved a bleeding scratch across her skin.
Yet, the moment the woman’s fingertip touched the wound, a soothing tingling warmth flared and the blood vanished.
The torn skin sealed over instantly, leaving behind flawless smooth flesh without so much as a speck of dried crimson.
FLUTTER!
The woman lowered them gently toward the street and the moment the emerald-green energy touched the cracked soot-stained asphalt of the avenue, an extraordinary miraculous phenomenon occurred.
CRACKLE-BLOOM!
From the fissures in the pavement... vibrant, lush green grass exploded outward in a rolling carpet.

Buds of white lilies, radiant blue lotus flowers, and sweet-scented jasmine burst into full fragrant bloom, transforming the burning, war-torn intersection into a breathtaking secluded garden that seemed detached from the burning apocalypse raging above.
’I feel so happy...’
Kaede, Penelope, Martha, and the four guards touched down upon the soft grass, completely unharmed, stumbling slightly as they looked down at their boots in utter disbelieving shock.
"Lia!" Martha gasped, tears of hysterical relief flooding her eyes as she bolted across the grass, dropping to her knees beside the girl. "Lia! Are you hurt?! By the heavens... are you alright?!"
Lia didn’t look at Martha.
She remained sitting on the grass, her wide dark eyes locked entirely onto the silver-green-haired woman who was kneeling gracefully beside her.
"Who... who are you...?" Lia asked, her voice a tiny awe-struck whisper.
SCREEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEECH!
Before the woman could answer, a deafening ear-splitting shriek ripped through the air.
High above the street, coiled around the leaning, shattered frame of the Grand Oasis Palace, the six-hundred-foot Dune-Serpent looked down.
Its hundreds of crimson compound eyes locked onto the glowing garden, its massive obsidian jaws parting as it released a hiss.

Accompanying it, over thirty grotesque, four-legged trench-drakes and a swarm of winged carrion horrors broke away from the surrounding high-rises, diving straight toward the secluded street with hungry snapping jaws.
Kenji’s eyes dilated in terror.
"DEFENSIVE FORMATION! THE SERPENT IS DIVING! SHIELD EVERYONE—"
The silver-green-haired woman’s deep emerald eyes simply... flashed.
HUM! BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
In the sky above the street, dozens of silent concentrated detonations of pure emerald-green nature mana erupted simultaneously.

chapters.title: Chapter 618: Big Brother’s Biggest Glazer [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The moment the green light touched their flesh, their bodies sprouted.

Millions of tiny violent vegetative vines burst from their organs, their bones, and their eyes, instantly consuming their physical mass and dissolving the entire pack of thirty monsters into harmless falling showers of green flower petals that drifted down into the wind.
’I just need to kill them right... It’s not like we can eat these things.’
And the six-hundred-foot Dune-Serpent?
CRACK-CRUNCH!
The green light struck its titanic obsidian skull.
"GRAAAAAA!"
The beast let out a strangled muffled gurgle as its entire body turned to solid petrified wood from the snout to the tail but the petrification didn’t stop at the skull.
CRRRRRRRRRRRRRRK!

It raced backward down six hundred feet of segmented obsidian spine in a single continuous wave with the serpent’s death-scream warping mid-shriek into the dry splintering groan of green wood curing too fast, its hundreds of crimson compound eyes dimming to dull knots in petrified bark one by one, like candles being pinched out down a long hallway.
’Begone.’
SNAP!
The colossal wooden statue cracked down the center, crumbling into harmless sawdust that blew away in the winds.
RUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUMBLE!
The leaning crumpled thirty-story tower of the Grand Oasis Palace, its structural integrity completely destroyed by the serpent’s constriction, finally began to collapse.
Tens of thousands of tons of concrete, steel, and glass began to tilt forward, preparing to slam down directly on top of the street like an avalanche of crushing death.
"THE TOWER!" Penelope screamed, throwing her hands over her head, however the woman sighed softly, it was a gentle and almost bored exhalation.
She lightly tapped her knuckles against the blooming turf.
THUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
The earth beneath the city violently surged.
From the asphalt, six colossal titanic roots of ancient iron-hard divine wood... each root thirty feet thick and glowing with radiant jade runes erupted from the ground.
They wove together like the fingers of a colossal wooden titan, wrapping securely around the base and the leaning spine of the thirty-story tower.
CREEEAK-LIFT!
With terrifying effortless botanical strength, the massive roots caught the falling skyscraper.

They gently pushed the tilted building back into a vertical alignment, righting the shattered tower and lifting it three feet higher into the air, perfectly stabilized and anchored by the living bedrock of the roots.
The four bodyguards stood completely paralyzed as Kenji’s mempo mask fell from his numb fingers, clattering onto the grass.
"W... who...?" Kenji whispered, his knees trembling beneath his plate armor. "She... she just caught a skyscraper with tree roots..."
The woman didn’t pay any attention to the guards as she turned her gaze back down to Lia.
The terrifying reality-bending power vanished in a single second, replaced once more by that soft, gentle, and deeply serene warmth.

Yet, as the woman looked into Lia’s eyes... noticing the distinct hair that had been described to her and the quiet stubborn tilt of the little girl’s chin that looked so remarkably like Silas... a sudden deep crimson blush bloomed across the woman’s porcelain cheeks!
’Hubby said they don’t look similar but they really do... a bit...’
Her emerald eyes darted to the side, her long elegant fingers suddenly fidgeting awkwardly with the silver silk of her sash.
She looked flustered like a young maiden being introduced to her lover’s family for the very first time.

"My... my name is Eluned," she stammered softly, her voice carrying a sweet melodious thoroughly flustered pitch that sounded completely out of place for someone who had just erased a leviathan with a blink.
She swallowed gently, her blush deepening until it reached the tips of her ears with her hands folding neatly over her lap.
"I am the Former Spirit of the World Tree... and the very first Hero that Lord Silas summoned when he stepped onto the soil of the Sovereign Realm."
Eluned paused while taking a tiny trembling breath, her emerald eyes looking down at Lia with earnest sincerity.
"And... and I am... his wife."
Lia sat frozen on the grass as her large dark eyes blinked once... twice and three times...
Lia’s brain completely short-circuited.
’H-HUH?!’

Her fingers, which had been clutching the hem of her skirt, remained locked in place as her dark eyes darted between the serene divine woman kneeling before her and the titanic living wooden roots that held the leaning thirty-story Grand Oasis Palace aloft.
"W-Wife?" Lia finally squeaked, her voice cracking on the single syllable.

Her mind, already strained by the terrifying plummet through the air, violently refused to process the information. "You... you’re married to Silas? My brother? The Silas who used to eat burnt toast so I could have the crusts without charcoal on them?"
Eluned let out a light melodious chuckle that sounded like the rustle of fresh leaves caught in a spring breeze.
FWOOOOOOSH!
She didn’t rise from the grass.
With an effortless imperceptible flick of her pale wrist, a massive translucent ripple of radiant emerald mana expanded outward from her frame.
It swept through the surrounding four-block radius like a rising tide of concentrated life-force.
The dozens of chittering crawlers, barbed drakes, and winged scavengers descending from the broken clouds didn’t even have the chance to screech.
The instant the green wave washed over them, blooming floral vines erupted from their eyes, their ribs, and their joints.

In less than half a heartbeat, twenty high-tier monstrosities were swallowed whole with their flesh dissolving into showers of fragrant white blossom petals that drifted harmlessly down to the street.
The four bodyguards, still standing in a stunned half-circle with their weapons drawn, flinched at the terrifying ease of the slaughter.

Kenji simply swallowed hard, his hands trembling as he slowly lowered his blade, realizing that any defense they could offer was utterly trivial compared to the woman casually tending to the children.
Eluned turned back to Lia, her deep luminous green eyes softening with unmistakable warmth.
"Indeed," Eluned confirmed, nodding with graceful composure. "I am his lawfully bound companion... In every sense recognized by the laws of our realm, I am Lord Silas’s wife."
Lia’s face contorted.
Her eyebrows drew together, her nose wrinkling as she looked the breathtaking ethereal deity up and down.

"Why... why would you settle for him?" Lia blurted out, her genuine bewilderment overriding any sense of decorum. "Look at you! You look like a fairy queen from a storybook! You caught a skyscraper with tree roots! Silas is just... Silas!"
A soft dreamy sigh escaped Eluned’s lips.
She pressed both hands to her cheeks, her porcelain skin flushing with a brilliant radiant pink that seemed to make the surrounding flowers glow brighter.

"Oh, but that is the very heart of his boundless magnificence!" Eluned gushed, her voice pitching upward into breathless worshipful adoration. "Lord Silas possesses the resolve of a primordial titan! In the Sovereign Realm, he walks among terrors with the calm stride of an uncrowned King! He does not bend to the whims of anyone... he commands the earth with a brilliant intellect that outmatches the oldest scholars of our era and yet... despite wielding the authority to overturn empires, his heart remains pure and selfless too! Every coin he hoards, every scrap he claims, is dedicated to shielding his loved ones from the cold! He is so gentle, so fierce, so impossibly handsome when his brow furrows in concentration..."
Lia’s face scrunched up in complete disgust.
She leaned backward, her lips curling into an expression of mortification.
To hear such a beautiful woman wax poetic about her brooding older brother was an assault she was thoroughly unprepared for.
’Gross,’ Lia thought, shivering. ’She’s completely blind... She actually thinks he’s a prince!’
"Wait a second," Lia interrupted, holding up a small hand to halt the torrent of unhinged praise before Eluned could start describing Silas’s jawline. "Where’s your ring?"
Eluned blinked, her dreamy reverie pausing mid-breath. "A... a ring...?"

"Yeah, a ring!" Lia pointed at her own left ring finger. "When people get married in the real world, you exchange rings... A gold or silver band on this finger right here. It proves that you’re married and that nobody else can hit on you. If you’re really his wife, Silas would have given you one."
"Oh!" Eluned’s emerald eyes widened in sudden realization. "The token of binding!"
She lifted her left hand, turning her slender, elegant fingers toward the light.
Resting upon her fourth finger was a delicate band woven from living, petrified celestial vine, cradling a single flawless mana diamond that burned with an inner emerald fire.
With a proud flustered smile, Eluned gently reached up with her other hand, adjusting the delicate leaf-shaped emerald necklace resting against her collarbone.
The gem sat directly over her heart, carved with runes that mirrored the ring perfectly.

"Lord Silas placed this upon my hand not too long ago," Eluned murmured, her voice dipping into a shy tender whisper as she admired the jewel. "He told me that as long as this stone remains intact, his presence would never leave my side..."
Lia stared at the ring then she stared at the necklace.
Her jaw dropped.
’He... he actually bought her a mana diamond?!’ Lia’s thoughts screamed. ’Eh?! Why doesn’t he get me one and a new phone too?!’
Before Lia could voice her mounting existential crisis, a sudden frantic rustle of silk cut through the quiet.
"BIG SIS!"
Penelope had completely ignored the celestial garden, the defeated serpent, and the ongoing conversation.
Her wide purple eyes had landed upon the figure lying slumped against the base of one of the massive wooden roots five paces away.
Penelope sprinted across the turf, practically throwing herself onto the grass.
She wrapped both of her small arms around the unconscious woman, burying her face into Harper’s charcoal suit jacket, weeping with raw violent relief.
"Big sis! Big sis, wake up! Please wake up!" Penelope sobbed, her fingers trembling as she patted Harper’s pale cheeks.
Harper didn’t wake, but her chest rose and fell in a deep peaceful rhythm.
The terrifying green radiance that had plagued her features was entirely gone as her skin was warm and a healthy color was already returning to her lips.
Eluned glided over, her silver-green skirts floating soundlessly above the grass as she knelt beside the weeping eleven-year-old.
Her gentle hand came to rest softly against Penelope’s trembling shoulder.

"Be at ease, little one," Eluned said softly, her voice carrying an innate soothing frequency that slowed Penelope’s heartbeat. "Your sister is completely unharmed. The vile parasite that sought to violate her vessel has been eradicated down to the final thread of its existence... Lord Silas located her in the deep cavern, severed the foreign soul, and pulled her from the dark with his own hands. She is merely exhausted from the strain so sleep is the best medicine for her spirit right now."
Penelope looked up, her face tear-stained with her lower lip quivering. "Silas... Silas really saved her?"
"He did," Eluned nodded, offering a warm reassuring smile. "He promised you he would bring her back, did he not?"
Penelope clutched Harper’s hand to her chest, bowing her head toward Eluned in desperate gratitude.
"Thank you... thank you so much..."
Lia scrambled to her feet, brushing blades of grass from her sweater as she trotted over.
"Wait, where is Silas right now? If he saved Harper, why isn’t he here?"

"Lord Silas remains in the field," Eluned explained, gesturing toward the burning sky where distant flashes of starlight, gold fire, and lightning illuminated the dark clouds. "The destruction of the suppression mechanism has unleashed an unprecedented horde upon this land... My Lord and my sisters are currently locking down the primary containment sectors to ensure the calamity does not swallow the civilian populace whole... He is safe, Little Sister. His power is absolute."
She looked at Martha, who had stepped forward with a hand resting over her apron.
"My orders from Lord Silas are precise," Eluned continued smoothly. "I am to remain here and anchor this sanctuary until Lady Evelyn arrives with the extraction vessel to carry you all to safety..."
Lia blinked, tilting her head.
"Evelyn? How is Evelyn going to get here? The trains and the public skyways are shut down!"
Eluned tilted her head in mild confusion, her finger tapping her chin thoughtfully.
"How...? Well, I am not entirely versed in mortal travel terminology, but... I believe My Lord mentioned something about her arriving in a ’private supersonic jet’?"
The entire street fell into a dead suffocating silence.
