chapters.title: Chapter 619: Thump! [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Martha blinked.
Kenji and the three bodyguards stared at Eluned as if she had spoken in ancient tongues.
"A... a private jet?" Lia echoed, her voice squeaking again. "Big Brother... bought a private jet?!"
’Who is Evelyn... is it that black haired girl that he left with that day?’
"I believe so," Eluned smiled innocently, completely unbothered by the astronomical financial absurdity of the statement. "Lord Silas seemed quite pleased with her efficiency..."
’What kind of ridiculous corrupt billionaire world did my brother fall into?!’ Lia grabbed her own hair with both hands, groaning in disbelief.
Seeing the girl’s flustered state, Eluned’s smile softened into fondness.
She reached into the wide, embroidered folds of her flowing silver-white robes, her fingers searching for a moment before pulling out a sleek handheld camera.
She held the device up with delicate elegant curiosity.
"Before the transport arrives..." Eluned said, a faint charming blush touching her cheeks once more, "would you... would you be willing to take a photograph with me?"
Lia blinked. "A picture?"

"Yes," Eluned murmured, looking at Lia, Martha, and Penelope with earnest sincerity. "You are Lord Silas’s family in this waking world. You are the foundation of everything he fights to protect. I... I have heard him speak of you with such deep reverence in our quiet moments. If it pleases you, I would like to get to know each and every one of you. I wish to know what kind of life my husband cherishes."
Lia looked at the camera, then up into Eluned’s earnest radiant face.

Despite the madness of the situation... Despite the flying monsters and the fact that this beautiful overpowered woman had just claimed to be her sister-in-law, It was impossible to stay defensive against someone looking at her with such pure warmth.

"Well..." Lia muttered, crossing her arms and looking away with an awkward huff. "...I guess one picture won’t hurt but only if you tell me what he’s actually like over there! Does he really act like an emperor, or is he still a giant dork?"
Eluned’s eyes lit up with delight as she knelt beside Lia, angling the lens toward them. "Oh, Lord Silas is..."
Two miles away, in the heart of Sector Two’s commercial transit hub.
SHRIIIIIIIIIIK-SPLAT!
A clean crescent arc of lightless black cleaved through the air with the sharp hiss of a hot wire slicing through silk.
The eight-foot-wide head of an Abyssal Chitin-Crawler slid smoothly from its armored torso, hitting the cracked pavement with a heavy wet thud.
Black acidic ichor sprayed across the concrete, sizzling as it ate into the stone, but not a single drop touched the high-collared shadow-cloak of the woman standing over the corpse.
Tasmin, Shadow Commander of Blessed Land, flicked her wrists.
CLINK!
The twin daggers she held spun effortlessly across her knuckles before snapping into a reverse grip.
Her short jet-black hair, streaked with vivid ribbons of moonlight-silver, barely stirred in the wind as her sharp eyes swept over the burning street with cold detachment.
"Keep moving!" Tasmin’s voice rang out, sharp and commanding as a whip-crack. "Head for the lower maintenance hatch! Form a double line and do not stop to collect baggage!"
A hundred yards down the avenue, dozens of terrified civilians were scrambling toward an open reinforced bunker entrance set into the plaza bedrock.
CRUMBLE-GROAN!
A sudden violent crash echoed from the facade of an alchemical pharmacy three doors down.
A massive slab of reinforced concrete, severed by a falling rift-beast, collapsed outward, pinning an elderly Khemet man beneath two tons of smoking rubble!
"FATHER!" a young woman screamed, desperately clawing at the stone with bleeding fingernails.
SWOOSH!
In a fraction of a second, Tasmin vanished from the center of the street.
Her silhouette simply sank into the dark pavement like a stone dropped into ink with the help of Shadow-Submersion Drift.
POP!
She materialized instantly out of the shadow cast by the falling slab.
"Hold on!"
Tasmin didn’t even draw a breath, the woman drove her bare left hand beneath the two-ton block of reinforced concrete with her muscles flaring.
With an effortless single-armed heave, she hoisted the massive slab off the ground and hurled it twenty yards down the street, where it pulverized three approaching scavenger-hounds into paste.
GRAB!
She scooped the injured old man up by his collar, thrusting him firmly into his daughter’s arms.
"Can he walk?" Tasmin barked, her golden eyes boring into the sobbing girl.
"Y-Yes! Yes, thank you—"
"Save your gratitude for the bunker," Tasmin cut her off cleanly, her hand pointing toward the illuminated shelter hatch thirty yards away. "Move... Now..."
The woman dragged her father toward the doors, scrambling inside just as the heavy blast-rated iron began to slide shut behind them.
Tasmin turned back to the street, letting out a slow irritated breath through her teeth.
SCREEECH! ROOOOAR! HIIIIISS!
The sounds were deafening.
From the alleyways, from the shattered roofs, from the cracks in the skyway overpasses... hundreds of abominations were converging upon the intersection.
Bone-beasts, shadow-stalkers, and multi-jointed trench crawlers flooded the street in a churning ravenous tide, drawn by the scent of human blood and the lingering mana of the shelter.
Within seconds, the intersection was completely surrounded.
A circular perimeter of death closed in on Tasmin from all three hundred and sixty degrees, cutting off every escape route as Tasmin stood alone in the center of the crossroads.
"Heh."

If she was cornered, she could use her badge to call for help which was a new feature that Thora had designed with the help of her sister and the other dwarves... however Tas didn’t call for Aeliana’s artillery or Brida’s shield.
She slowly tilted her head back, rolling her neck with a muted click with her lips curving into a dry condescending smirk.
"Honestly..." Tasmin murmured, her voice laced with razor-thin boredom. "You creatures are so utterly lacking in refinement... All this mindless gnashing and pointless screaming, it’s quite tedious."
She tapped the pommels of her daggers together.
CHIME!
The sunlight filtering through the smoke seemed to dim.
The shadows cast by the buildings, by the abandoned cars, by the piles of rubble... began to crawl.
They didn’t stretch with the angle of the sun at all... the shadows expanded, pooling outward across the asphalt like thick viscous black tar, swallowing the light.
Tasmin’s pupils dilated until her eyes were pools of lightless obsidian.

’Aeliana is turning the sky into a fireworks display,’ Tasmin reflected. ’While Morwenna is down by the canals carving up sea-horrors like a fishmonger... If I rely purely on single-target executions, those loud-mouthed women will take the honors before dinner.’
Her core flared deep within her chest and a cold suffocating pressure dropped over the intersection, pinning the charging monsters mid-stride as the temperature plunged to freezing.
"Might as well test this out once more," Tasmin whispered into the dark.
STEP!
She took a single quiet step forward, directly into the center of the charging horde.
"Domain..."
FSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSH!
The world went pitch-black.
The shadows beneath the charging horde erupted into an ocean of living liquid void that surged fifty feet into the air, and this time the tide didn’t stop at the monsters...
It reached for her too... but Tasmin didn’t step back from it.
She let it take her.
GULP!

The black wave closed over her head at the exact same instant it swallowed the first line of shrieking beasts, and for a single, suspended heartbeat, the entire intersection, predator and prey together, simply ceased to exist on the surface of the world.
There was no falling sensation and there was no cold...
WHOOSH!

There was only a vast starless dark that stretched in every direction at once, and somewhere within it, a hundred voices of frightened furious monsters were already screaming, disoriented and blind in a territory that belonged to someone else entirely.
Tasmin’s eyes opened in the black as the only two points of light in the domain.
"Welcome," she said quietly, to no one who could see her smile, "to my home turf."
CRK! CRK! CRK! WHOOSH!
Inside the inverted hemisphere of her domain, sound felt suffocated.
The sky, the burning high-rises of Sector Two, the choking amber dust of the Khemet desert... all of it had been sheared away by the absolute lightless boundaries of Tasmin’s domain.
To the abominations trapped within the perimeter, the ground had ceased to be cracked asphalt.
It had become a bottomless viscous lake of pitch-black liquid shadow that clung to their hocks, weighed down their leathery wings, and swallowed the sound of their frantic, scraping claws.
The beast turned in blind frantic circles.
Their yellowed compound eyes and burning corpse-fires flickered weakly against the crushing absence of light.
"GRAH! GRA! GRUH!"
They snarled, their jaws snapping at empty air, utterly unable to orient themselves in an artificial expanse where up and down were dictated solely by the will of the woman standing at its center.
Tasmin exhaled with a thin ribbon of pale frosted vapor drifting from her lips and dissolving instantly into the gloom.

’These monsters are varying from Tier 2 to Tier 3,’ she calculated with cold detachment, her pupils sweeping across the pack. ’Not a single Tier 4 is among them... They’re just gutter-dross that tumbled out of the rift’s fissures.’

Even within the notorious Umbral Basin back in the Sovereign Realm... where the darkness bred monsters that were quite strong, Tasmin had rarely seen this specific strain of abyssal vermin gathered in such dense concentrations.
Here, unmoored from the suppression of the world and driven mad by the sudden influx of oxygen, they were quite reckless.
FSSSSSSSS!
A ripple broke across the surface of the black pool beneath her boots but she didn’t drop into a defensive crouch.
"I’ll take you all out..."

Tas merely inclined her head by a fraction of an inch as three Tier 2 razor-fiends... bipedal horrors with exposed calcified ribs and forearms that ended in curved scythe-like bone blades lunged from her blind spot.
SWOOSH!
They didn’t strike flesh...
From the liquid floor, three serrated tendrils of solidified shadow erupted like coiled steel springs.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH! WHOOSH!𝙛𝓻𝒆𝒆𝒘𝙚𝓫𝙣𝙤𝒗𝙚𝓵.𝙘𝙤𝙢
They impaled them from below, driving upward through their lower jaws, spearing their brains, and detonating their cranial cores with a soft wet pop.
SPLAT!

The three fiends dissolved before their bodies could hit the ground, their physical mass breaking down into black thread-like filaments that were instantly reabsorbed into the lake beneath Tasmin’s feet.
’Too slow,’ Tasmin thought, her pulse picking up with a dark electric hum beginning to vibrate behind her collarbones. ’Much too slow.’
She took a slow, leisurely step forward and the lake rippled beneath her soles with the resonance of struck crystal.
SHRIIIIK-CRACK!
A Tier 3 Bone-Raptor... an eight-foot predator whose spine was crowned with iridescent needles that glowed with corrosive acid burst through the gloom from her upper flank.
WHOOSH!
it moved with soundless acceleration with its serrated tail whipping forward in a horizontal arc aimed straight for Tasmin’s neck.
’Ah... fast.’
Tasmin brought her right forearm up to meet the blow, testing the power of the monster.
CHOP!
The raptor’s tail cleaved clean through her right wrist and the severed hand, still clad in its fingerless leather glove, spun into the air.
Yet, there was no spray of crimson blood and there was no white flash of severed bone either.
"Hehehehe~"
There was only a quiet hiss as thick, pressurized ribbons of pure, pitch-black shadow poured from the stump, coiling through the air like hungry blind serpents.
THUMP!
Deep within Tasmin’s chest, the Shadow Heart beat once as an iron vibration echoed through the entire domain.
FWOOOOOOOOOM!
The shadows spilling from her severed wrist turned viscous and boiling hot.
They expanded outward in a jagged, spiraling wave of black spikes that swept through the surrounding twelve meters!
CRUNCH-CRUNCH-CRUNCH-SHATTER!

The black spikes bored through its armored carapace, punched through its chest cavity, and violently ripped its internal organs to shreds.
Six other monsters charging in its wake were instantly impaled, hoisted ten feet into the air, and crushed into fine, necrotic mulch.
SNAP!
The severed right hand reached the apex of its arc, dissolved into black mist, and flowed straight back down into the stump.
The muscle re-braided as the skin sealed over and the leather glove rematerialized without a single stitch out of place.
"This is good..."
Tasmin flexed her newly formed fingers, listening to the small sharp clicks of her knuckles settling into their sockets.
A wide grin cut across her face, exposing white teeth against the darkness of her domain.

"Marvelous," she whispered, her voice husky with rising adrenaline. "The rate of mastery is climbing... The more of these wretched things I drag into the dark, the faster my Heart purges the impurities."

The surviving monsters shrank back with their animalistic instincts finally screaming at them that they weren’t trapped in a feeding pen... they were locked in a slaughterhouse with a butcher who didn’t even bleed as low terrified growls rattled in their throats.
Tasmin’s daggers slid from the hidden magnetic sheaths along her lower back with a dual singing ring.
CLINK!

The twin blades of silver gleamed with a oily purple sheen and wrapped around her forearms were thirty-meter lengths of ultra-fine link-less chain forged from shadow-tempered tungsten, their links crackling with licking embers of dark fire.

"What’s the matter?" Tasmin mocked, her eyes blazing with cruel amusement as she took another stride. "You broke through the heavens to feed on human cattle, didn’t you? Come, then. Fill your bellies."

sentences.text: Martha blinked.
Kenji and the three bodyguards stared at Eluned as if she had spoken in ancient tongues.
"A... a private jet?" Lia echoed, her voice squeaking again.
"Big Brother... bought a private jet?!"
’Who is Evelyn... is it that black haired girl that he left with that day?’
"I believe so," Eluned smiled innocently, completely unbothered by the astronomical financial absurdity of the statement.
"Lord Silas seemed quite pleased with her efficiency..."
’What kind of ridiculous corrupt billionaire world did my brother fall into?!’ Lia grabbed her own hair with both hands, groaning in disbelief.
Seeing the girl’s flustered state, Eluned’s smile softened into fondness.
She reached into the wide, embroidered folds of her flowing silver-white robes, her fingers searching for a moment before pulling out a sleek handheld camera.
She held the device up with delicate elegant curiosity.
"Before the transport arrives..." Eluned said, a faint charming blush touching her cheeks once more, "would you... would you be willing to take a photograph with me?"
Lia blinked.
"A picture?"
"Yes," Eluned murmured, looking at Lia, Martha, and Penelope with earnest sincerity.
"You are Lord Silas’s family in this waking world.
You are the foundation of everything he fights to protect.
I have heard him speak of you with such deep reverence in our quiet moments.
If it pleases you, I would like to get to know each and every one of you.
I wish to know what kind of life my husband cherishes."
Lia looked at the camera, then up into Eluned’s earnest radiant face.
Despite the madness of the situation...

Despite the flying monsters and the fact that this beautiful overpowered woman had just claimed to be her sister-in-law, It was impossible to stay defensive against someone looking at her with such pure warmth.
"Well..." Lia muttered, crossing her arms and looking away with an awkward huff.
"...I guess one picture won’t hurt but only if you tell me what he’s actually like over there!
Does he really act like an emperor, or is he still a giant dork?"
Eluned’s eyes lit up with delight as she knelt beside Lia, angling the lens toward them.
"Oh, Lord Silas is..."
Two miles away, in the heart of Sector Two’s commercial transit hub.
SHRIIIIIIIIIIK-SPLAT!
A clean crescent arc of lightless black cleaved through the air with the sharp hiss of a hot wire slicing through silk.
The eight-foot-wide head of an Abyssal Chitin-Crawler slid smoothly from its armored torso, hitting the cracked pavement with a heavy wet thud.
Black acidic ichor sprayed across the concrete, sizzling as it ate into the stone, but not a single drop touched the high-collared shadow-cloak of the woman standing over the corpse.
Tasmin, Shadow Commander of Blessed Land, flicked her wrists.
CLINK!
The twin daggers she held spun effortlessly across her knuckles before snapping into a reverse grip.
Her short jet-black hair, streaked with vivid ribbons of moonlight-silver, barely stirred in the wind as her sharp eyes swept over the burning street with cold detachment.
"Keep moving!" Tasmin’s voice rang out, sharp and commanding as a whip-crack.
"Head for the lower maintenance hatch!
Form a double line and do not stop to collect baggage!"
A hundred yards down the avenue, dozens of terrified civilians were scrambling toward an open reinforced bunker entrance set into the plaza bedrock.
CRUMBLE-GROAN!
A sudden violent crash echoed from the facade of an alchemical pharmacy three doors down.
A massive slab of reinforced concrete, severed by a falling rift-beast, collapsed outward, pinning an elderly Khemet man beneath two tons of smoking rubble!
"FATHER!" a young woman screamed, desperately clawing at the stone with bleeding fingernails.
SWOOSH!
In a fraction of a second, Tasmin vanished from the center of the street.
Her silhouette simply sank into the dark pavement like a stone dropped into ink with the help of Shadow-Submersion Drift.
POP!
She materialized instantly out of the shadow cast by the falling slab.
"Hold on!"
Tasmin didn’t even draw a breath, the woman drove her bare left hand beneath the two-ton block of reinforced concrete with her muscles flaring.
With an effortless single-armed heave, she hoisted the massive slab off the ground and hurled it twenty yards down the street, where it pulverized three approaching scavenger-hounds into paste.
GRAB!
She scooped the injured old man up by his collar, thrusting him firmly into his daughter’s arms.
"Can he walk?" Tasmin barked, her golden eyes boring into the sobbing girl.
"Y-Yes!
Yes, thank you—"
"Save your gratitude for the bunker," Tasmin cut her off cleanly, her hand pointing toward the illuminated shelter hatch thirty yards away.
"Move...
Now..."
The woman dragged her father toward the doors, scrambling inside just as the heavy blast-rated iron began to slide shut behind them.
Tasmin turned back to the street, letting out a slow irritated breath through her teeth.
SCREEECH!
ROOOOAR!
HIIIIISS!
The sounds were deafening.
From the alleyways, from the shattered roofs, from the cracks in the skyway overpasses... hundreds of abominations were converging upon the intersection.
Bone-beasts, shadow-stalkers, and multi-jointed trench crawlers flooded the street in a churning ravenous tide, drawn by the scent of human blood and the lingering mana of the shelter.
Within seconds, the intersection was completely surrounded.
A circular perimeter of death closed in on Tasmin from all three hundred and sixty degrees, cutting off every escape route as Tasmin stood alone in the center of the crossroads.
"Heh."

If she was cornered, she could use her badge to call for help which was a new feature that Thora had designed with the help of her sister and the other dwarves... however Tas didn’t call for Aeliana’s artillery or Brida’s shield.
She slowly tilted her head back, rolling her neck with a muted click with her lips curving into a dry condescending smirk.
"Honestly..." Tasmin murmured, her voice laced with razor-thin boredom.
"You creatures are so utterly lacking in refinement...
All this mindless gnashing and pointless screaming, it’s quite tedious."
She tapped the pommels of her daggers together.
CHIME!
The sunlight filtering through the smoke seemed to dim.
The shadows cast by the buildings, by the abandoned cars, by the piles of rubble... began to crawl.
They didn’t stretch with the angle of the sun at all... the shadows expanded, pooling outward across the asphalt like thick viscous black tar, swallowing the light.
Tasmin’s pupils dilated until her eyes were pools of lightless obsidian.
’Aeliana is turning the sky into a fireworks display,’ Tasmin reflected. ’While Morwenna is down by the canals carving up sea-horrors like a fishmonger...
If I rely purely on single-target executions, those loud-mouthed women will take the honors before dinner.’
Her core flared deep within her chest and a cold suffocating pressure dropped over the intersection, pinning the charging monsters mid-stride as the temperature plunged to freezing.
"Might as well test this out once more," Tasmin whispered into the dark.
STEP!
She took a single quiet step forward, directly into the center of the charging horde.
"Domain..."
FSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSH!
The world went pitch-black.
The shadows beneath the charging horde erupted into an ocean of living liquid void that surged fifty feet into the air, and this time the tide didn’t stop at the monsters...
It reached for her too... but Tasmin didn’t step back from it.
She let it take her.
GULP!

The black wave closed over her head at the exact same instant it swallowed the first line of shrieking beasts, and for a single, suspended heartbeat, the entire intersection, predator and prey together, simply ceased to exist on the surface of the world.
There was no falling sensation and there was no cold...
WHOOSH!

There was only a vast starless dark that stretched in every direction at once, and somewhere within it, a hundred voices of frightened furious monsters were already screaming, disoriented and blind in a territory that belonged to someone else entirely.
Tasmin’s eyes opened in the black as the only two points of light in the domain.
"Welcome," she said quietly, to no one who could see her smile, "to my home turf."
CRK!
CRK!
CRK!
WHOOSH!
Inside the inverted hemisphere of her domain, sound felt suffocated.
The sky, the burning high-rises of Sector Two, the choking amber dust of the Khemet desert... all of it had been sheared away by the absolute lightless boundaries of Tasmin’s domain.
To the abominations trapped within the perimeter, the ground had ceased to be cracked asphalt.
It had become a bottomless viscous lake of pitch-black liquid shadow that clung to their hocks, weighed down their leathery wings, and swallowed the sound of their frantic, scraping claws.
The beast turned in blind frantic circles.
Their yellowed compound eyes and burning corpse-fires flickered weakly against the crushing absence of light.
"GRAH!
GRA!
GRUH!"
They snarled, their jaws snapping at empty air, utterly unable to orient themselves in an artificial expanse where up and down were dictated solely by the will of the woman standing at its center.
Tasmin exhaled with a thin ribbon of pale frosted vapor drifting from her lips and dissolving instantly into the gloom.
’These monsters are varying from Tier 2 to Tier 3,’ she calculated with cold detachment, her pupils sweeping across the pack. ’Not a single Tier 4 is among them...
They’re just gutter-dross that tumbled out of the rift’s fissures.’

Even within the notorious Umbral Basin back in the Sovereign Realm... where the darkness bred monsters that were quite strong, Tasmin had rarely seen this specific strain of abyssal vermin gathered in such dense concentrations.
Here, unmoored from the suppression of the world and driven mad by the sudden influx of oxygen, they were quite reckless.

chapters.title: Chapter 620: Bickering Women [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: RAHHHHHHHHHHH!
Driven mad by the mockery and the suffocating pressure of the domain, the remaining horde surged forward in a suicidal mass-wave assault.
WHOOOSH! WHOOSH! WHOOSH!
They came from the front, from the sides, leaping across the black water with teeth bared and their claws outstretched, desperate to tear the single woman to pieces by weight of numbers.
"Hm? Good doggies."
...Tasmin didn’t retreat.
She leaned forward with her heels digging into the shadow lake and her arms whipping backward as she prepared to release the chains in a full-perimeter [Voltaic Chain Execution]...
Suddenly... her scalp prickled.
A sharp deafening spike of raw force slammed directly against her sensory field from outside the domain.
’Wait... what the—?!’
Tasmin’s eyes snapped wide.
’FUCK!’
CRACK-SHATTER-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The reinforced shadow-ceiling of her domain was completely obliterated from above.
A massive golden-red projectile... moving at roughly Mach 4 tore through the top of the dark dome like an artillery shell punching through paper.
The atmospheric displacement was so monstrous that the sound wave blew the liquid shadows apart, exposing the burning sun and the soot-choked air of Sector Two in a single concussive flash.
’Fuck you...’
Tasmin reacted on pure hard-wired muscle memory.
SWOOSH!

She severed the domain’s mana flow, launching her body backward in a desperate triple-rotation backflip with her boots skidding across thirty feet of shattered asphalt just as the projectile slammed into the street.
KABOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The intersection cratered.
’I hate you bitch.’
A thirty-foot-deep basin opened in the concrete, throwing hundred-pound chunks of asphalt, sewer pipes, and pulverized rock three hundred feet into the air.

The hundreds of surviving monsters that had been charging Tasmin bare milliseconds ago were instantly flattened beneath forty thousand pounds of pure descending physical mass with their bones and guts vaporized into a crimson grease-stain on the crater floor.
From the center of the dust cloud, rising above the screeching sirens and the roar of the blast, came a booming unapologetic roar of laughter.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHA!"
The dust parted under a sudden violent backhand of wind.

Standing in the center of the shattered crater, resting an eight-foot-long broad-headed cleaver against her right shoulder, was a woman who looked like she had been carved directly from a mountain range.
She was tall... easily six feet four inches of powerful muscle and sun-bronzed skin.
’Ah, she’s using that new skill?’
Brida had gotten a new skill that increased her physical power by a lot and also made her taller as well, it was quite unfair.

Her wild unbraided mane of thick auburn hair whipped in the gale like a war-banner as she wore heavy unpolished plate armor of dark star-iron that clung to her massive shoulders and thighs, completely unadorned by runes or decorative gold, held together by thick leather straps that creaked under the bulk of her frame.
Brida, Grand Titan Bastion of Blessed Land, sniffed the air, spat a glob of dust onto the mangled remnants of an abyssal crawler, and blinked down into the street.
Her round boisterous eyes caught sight of Tasmin crouching on the curb, covered in soot with her twin daggers drawn and her silver-streaked hair standing slightly on end from the shockwave.
"Huh?" Brida boomed, scratching her broad jaw with a thick calloused thumb. "Oh! Hey, Tas! You were down there?"
Tasmin remained frozen in her crouch for two full seconds and her right eye twitched violently.
Beneath her high leather collar, the veins along Tasmin’s neck bulged with dark murderous mana.
Her fingers clamped onto the grips of her silver daggers so hard that the metal let out an agonizing, high-pitched creak.

’I am going to kill her,’ Tasmin’s thoughts snarled, every nerve ending in her brain screaming with homicidal rage. ’I am going to slip into her shadow tonight, drag her into the deepest drainage ditch in the Basin, and cave her thick pig-headed skull in with a cobblestone... I am going to punch her until her face is an unrecognizable lump of bruised meat...’
She drew a long trembling murderous breath through her nose, slowly straightening her spine.

"Brida," Tasmin said, her voice dropping into a tone so quiet and so terrifyingly polite that the nearby asphalt actually began to frost over. "Did you, by any chance, notice the thirty-meter sphere of pitch-black magical energy occupying the center of this thoroughfare before you decided to drop from the heavens like a brainless boulder?"
"Sure did!" Brida grinned broadly, completely oblivious or indifferent to the murderous intent rolling off the smaller woman.

She hoisted her massive titan-cleaver with one hand, resting the flat of the blade against her nape. "Looked like a giant bruised plum sitting in the road! Figured some oversized slug had laid an egg, so I came down to smash it! Didn’t know you were inside playing in the mud! Gwahaha!"

"I was refining my domain," Tasmin hissed through clenched teeth, taking three rigid strides toward the edge of the crater. "I had the targets perfectly contained... I was harvesting their cores to temper my Shadow Heart and you... you oversized farm-animal... you dropped out of the sky and splattered them into fertilizer!"

"Well, your little dome was tiny!" Brida retorted, pouting her lower lip with exaggerated disappointment as she looked around the intersection. "Seriously, Tas, you call that a domain? It was barely bigger than the new shed behind the barracks! A girl can’t even stretch her legs in a closet like that! How was I supposed to see you in all that gloom?"
THUMP!
Brida hopped lightly out of the thirty-foot crater.
The simple casual jump caused the surrounding sidewalk to violently shudder, sending a fresh ripple of cracks tearing through the facade of an adjacent alchemical supply shop.
Tasmin didn’t flinch.
She simply crossed her arms with her daggers hanging loosely from her fingertips and her sharp eyes narrowing into razor-thin slits of pure competitive spite.
"Enough of your excuses, brute," Tasmin snapped. "Let us talk numbers. How many civilians have you evacuated to the underground shelters?"
Brida stopped.
Her broad cheerful brow suddenly furrowed into an intense painful knot of deep intellectual labor.
She blinked once, twice, and then slowly raised her massive, gauntleted left hand to eye level.
She extended her thumb.
She extended her index finger.
"Two..."𝒇𝙧𝙚𝓮𝙬𝙚𝓫𝒏𝓸𝓿𝓮𝒍.𝓬𝙤𝓶
She reached her pinky.
"Five..."
She stared at her empty palm, then looked back at her fingers with her mouth moving silently as she attempted to calculate how many times she had cleared a collapsed tenement block.
Tasmin rolled her eyes so hard she nearly strained an optic nerve.

"By the void, you truly are an illiterate ape," Tasmin sneered, her voice dripping with acidic disdain. "You have five fingers on that hand, Brida... You can’t even count past ten without taking off your iron boots. There is a grand library in Blessed Land containing four thousand volumes of mathematics, basic arithmetic, and business logistics... Master Silas spent thousands of UP stocking those shelves. If your tiny, pea-sized brain requires tutoring, you could always swallow your pride and ask Reina to teach you how to count on an abacus!"
Brida’s face flushed a deep indignant crimson as she lowered her hand, scowling down at Tasmin with genuine wounded pride.

"I can count, you skinny little bat!" Brida barked, crossing her massive plate-armored arms over her chest. "I saved... it was a lot! It was at least... over a hundred and fifty! Maybe two hundred! I hauled an entire school bus out of a sinkhole by its bumper three blocks back! That’s gotta be worth like sixty points right there!"
Tasmin’s lips curved into a smug triumphant sneer that looked like it had been carved from polished marble.
"Two hundred and thirty-seven," Tasmin stated with coldness in her voice.
FSSSS!
Before Brida could open her mouth to argue, Tasmin’s right hand subtly twitched.

Twenty yards down the street, near the smoking ruins of a baker’s pavilion, three panicked civilians... a mother and her two teenage sons were cornered against an iron fence by two leaping shadow-hounds.
Tasmin didn’t even turn her head.
SH-SH-SH!
From the shadows beneath the fence, three thin ribbons of darkness whipped forward.

They caught the three civilians gently around their waists, yanking them fifty feet across the street with weightless momentum, sliding them directly through the blast-rated hatch of the civil bunker.
CLANG!
The hatch slammed shut behind them with the automated locking bolts engaging with a definitive green flash, the Civilians could open it when they needed to enter with a code.
’At least that’s what I heard them say...’
Tasmin slowly turned her golden gaze back to Brida, her smirk widening until her eyes curved into mocking crescents.
"Two hundred and forty," Tasmin corrected herself smoothly. "Keep up, Bastion or our Lord’s reward will be resting in my quarters before the sun touches the dunes."
Brida’s eyes narrowed into fierce competitive embers.
The air between the two women grew thick and crackling with suppressed mana.
This wasn’t merely about the crisis in Iunu...

A week ago, down in the ore veins beneath Blessed Land’s ridge, Silas had turned an ordinary mining shift into a competition between the two of them, laughing that whoever pulled the higher amount of ores could ask him for whatever they wanted in return.
Neither of them had let it go since and today was that day... the day that settled it all.
Brida glared down at Tasmin, her massive jaw setting into a stubborn immovable line.
"Oh, you think you’re so clever with your little shadows, huh?" Brida muttered, her fingers twitching against her thighs.

"I don’t think," Tasmin replied sweetly. "I calculate... Heh... While you waste thirty seconds smashing a single lizard into paste, I have already routed forty citizens to safety. You are a sledgehammer, Brida. In a rescue operation, a sledgehammer merely breaks what is already fragile."
"Is that so?" Brida’s voice dropped into a low deceptively cheerful rumble.
"It is."
SWOOSH!
Brida’s massive armored frame suddenly blurred.
To anyone who didn’t know her, a woman of her size should have moved with the slow ponderous momentum of a glacier but Brida possessed the explosive agility of a high-tier monster.
Before Tasmin’s heightened spatial reflexes could even register the displacement...
GRAB!
Brida’s iron-hard right hand clamped down with vice-like ferocity around Tasmin’s left ankle.
Tasmin’s pupils snapped wide in pure shock.
"What in the—?!"
"Oops!" Brida roared, a wide grin splitting her bronze face. "Oh no! My hand slipped! My grip is just so clumsy today, Tas!"
"BRIDA, YOU WHORE, PUT ME DOW—"
Brida didn’t put her down.
She planted her heavy iron sabatons into the cracked asphalt, twisted her massive hips with the rotational torque of a crane and reared her entire upper body backward.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The asphalt beneath Brida’s boots violently exploded into powder as she hurled Tasmin straight up into the sky.
The shockwave was so monstrous that it blew the windows out of the three adjacent buildings, creating a horizontal cone of displaced air that flattened a lamppost thirty yards away.

"HAVE A NICE FLIGHT, TAS!" Brida bellowed, cupping her hands around her mouth and waving frantically toward the heavens. "DON’T WORRY ABOUT THE GROUND DOWN HERE! THE GRAND TITAN BASTION HAS IT COMPLETELY UNDER CONTROL! GWAHAHAHAHA!"
"BRIIIIIIIIIDAAAAAAAAAAAA!"
Tasmin’s furious high-pitched screech tore through the air as she broke the sound barrier, rocketing straight toward the clouds like an anti-air missile.
The city of Iunu tilted, spinning wildly beneath her vision as the wind whipped her cloak into a frenzied roar.
In less than three seconds, she cleared four thousand feet of elevation with her body hurtling directly toward a swirling cluster of high-altitude rift fissures.
Tasmin gritted her teeth so hard that a tiny bead of crimson leaked from her lower lip.

’That brainless... overgrown... SOW!’ Tasmin raged in the freezing gale, her fingers twitching frantically. ’When we return to the territory, I am going to salt her rations... I am going to pour acid into her bathwater! I will make her life an unceasing waking nightmare!’
She twisted her torso mid-flight, fighting the terminal velocity drag, and looked forward.

Directly in her trajectory, descending from a five-hundred-foot tear in the sky, was an entire flock of sixty Abyss Skystrikers... grotesque four-winged avian horrors with razor-sharp beak-spurs and leathery bodies that crackled with jagged arcs of corrupted green lightning.
Beyond them, the massive wide tear in the sky hung like an open wound with the colossal skeletal hand still gripping the dimensional edge.
’My Lord’s orders were absolute,’
Silas’s voice echoed in her memory.
’Contain the perimeter, protect the civilians and avoid entering the gates at all costs.’
Tasmin’s golden eyes narrowed into deadly focused slits.
"Fine," she hissed into the howling wind. "If you want to throw me into the sky, Brida... then the sky belongs to me."
CLINK!
Tasmin released the silver daggers from her hands but they didn’t fall.

The thirty-meter tungsten chains wrapped around her forearms uncoiled with terrifying fluid speed, the blades spinning around her body in a dual whistling orbit that formed an impenetrable sphere of humming razor-sharp steel.
VUUUUUM!
Her right foot kicked out in mid-air but she didn’t have wings as she didn’t possess Aeliana’s flight.
Instead, a flat, three-foot platform of dense solidified black shadow materialized directly beneath her boot.
CRACK!
She used the shadow platform as a springboard, altering her body by forty-five degrees with an explosive concussive push.
WHOOSH!
Tas shot toward the lead Skystriker like a falling black star.
SHRIIIIIIIIIIK!
The beast screeched, opening its jagged beak to unleash a concentrated bolt of green lightning but Tasmin didn’t even blink.
STEP!
She vanished into the creature’s own shadow with Shadow-Submersion Drift!
POP!
She materialized instantly upon the beast’s scaly back!

sentences.text: RAHHHHHHHHHHH!
Driven mad by the mockery and the suffocating pressure of the domain, the remaining horde surged forward in a suicidal mass-wave assault.
WHOOOSH!
WHOOSH!
WHOOSH!
They came from the front, from the sides, leaping across the black water with teeth bared and their claws outstretched, desperate to tear the single woman to pieces by weight of numbers.
"Hm?
Good doggies."
...Tasmin didn’t retreat.
She leaned forward with her heels digging into the shadow lake and her arms whipping backward as she prepared to release the chains in a full-perimeter [Voltaic Chain Execution]...
Suddenly... her scalp prickled.
A sharp deafening spike of raw force slammed directly against her sensory field from outside the domain.
’Wait... what the—?!’
Tasmin’s eyes snapped wide.
’FUCK!’
CRACK-SHATTER-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The reinforced shadow-ceiling of her domain was completely obliterated from above.
A massive golden-red projectile... moving at roughly Mach 4 tore through the top of the dark dome like an artillery shell punching through paper.
The atmospheric displacement was so monstrous that the sound wave blew the liquid shadows apart, exposing the burning sun and the soot-choked air of Sector Two in a single concussive flash.
’Fuck you...’
Tasmin reacted on pure hard-wired muscle memory.
SWOOSH!

She severed the domain’s mana flow, launching her body backward in a desperate triple-rotation backflip with her boots skidding across thirty feet of shattered asphalt just as the projectile slammed into the street.
KABOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The intersection cratered.
’I hate you bitch.’
A thirty-foot-deep basin opened in the concrete, throwing hundred-pound chunks of asphalt, sewer pipes, and pulverized rock three hundred feet into the air.

The hundreds of surviving monsters that had been charging Tasmin bare milliseconds ago were instantly flattened beneath forty thousand pounds of pure descending physical mass with their bones and guts vaporized into a crimson grease-stain on the crater floor.
From the center of the dust cloud, rising above the screeching sirens and the roar of the blast, came a booming unapologetic roar of laughter.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHA!"
The dust parted under a sudden violent backhand of wind.

Standing in the center of the shattered crater, resting an eight-foot-long broad-headed cleaver against her right shoulder, was a woman who looked like she had been carved directly from a mountain range.
She was tall... easily six feet four inches of powerful muscle and sun-bronzed skin.
’Ah, she’s using that new skill?’
Brida had gotten a new skill that increased her physical power by a lot and also made her taller as well, it was quite unfair.

Her wild unbraided mane of thick auburn hair whipped in the gale like a war-banner as she wore heavy unpolished plate armor of dark star-iron that clung to her massive shoulders and thighs, completely unadorned by runes or decorative gold, held together by thick leather straps that creaked under the bulk of her frame.
Brida, Grand Titan Bastion of Blessed Land, sniffed the air, spat a glob of dust onto the mangled remnants of an abyssal crawler, and blinked down into the street.
Her round boisterous eyes caught sight of Tasmin crouching on the curb, covered in soot with her twin daggers drawn and her silver-streaked hair standing slightly on end from the shockwave.
"Huh?" Brida boomed, scratching her broad jaw with a thick calloused thumb.
"Oh!
Hey, Tas!
You were down there?"
Tasmin remained frozen in her crouch for two full seconds and her right eye twitched violently.
Beneath her high leather collar, the veins along Tasmin’s neck bulged with dark murderous mana.
Her fingers clamped onto the grips of her silver daggers so hard that the metal let out an agonizing, high-pitched creak.

’I am going to kill her,’ Tasmin’s thoughts snarled, every nerve ending in her brain screaming with homicidal rage. ’I am going to slip into her shadow tonight, drag her into the deepest drainage ditch in the Basin, and cave her thick pig-headed skull in with a cobblestone...
I am going to punch her until her face is an unrecognizable lump of bruised meat...’
She drew a long trembling murderous breath through her nose, slowly straightening her spine.
"Brida," Tasmin said, her voice dropping into a tone so quiet and so terrifyingly polite that the nearby asphalt actually began to frost over.
"Did you, by any chance, notice the thirty-meter sphere of pitch-black magical energy occupying the center of this thoroughfare before you decided to drop from the heavens like a brainless boulder?"
"Sure did!" Brida grinned broadly, completely oblivious or indifferent to the murderous intent rolling off the smaller woman.
She hoisted her massive titan-cleaver with one hand, resting the flat of the blade against her nape.
"Looked like a giant bruised plum sitting in the road!
Figured some oversized slug had laid an egg, so I came down to smash it!
Didn’t know you were inside playing in the mud!
Gwahaha!"
"I was refining my domain," Tasmin hissed through clenched teeth, taking three rigid strides toward the edge of the crater.
"I had the targets perfectly contained...
I was harvesting their cores to temper my Shadow Heart and you... you oversized farm-animal... you dropped out of the sky and splattered them into fertilizer!"
"Well, your little dome was tiny!" Brida retorted, pouting her lower lip with exaggerated disappointment as she looked around the intersection.
"Seriously, Tas, you call that a domain?
It was barely bigger than the new shed behind the barracks!
A girl can’t even stretch her legs in a closet like that!
How was I supposed to see you in all that gloom?"
THUMP!
Brida hopped lightly out of the thirty-foot crater.
The simple casual jump caused the surrounding sidewalk to violently shudder, sending a fresh ripple of cracks tearing through the facade of an adjacent alchemical supply shop.
Tasmin didn’t flinch.
She simply crossed her arms with her daggers hanging loosely from her fingertips and her sharp eyes narrowing into razor-thin slits of pure competitive spite.
"Enough of your excuses, brute," Tasmin snapped.
"Let us talk numbers.
How many civilians have you evacuated to the underground shelters?"
Brida stopped.
Her broad cheerful brow suddenly furrowed into an intense painful knot of deep intellectual labor.
She blinked once, twice, and then slowly raised her massive, gauntleted left hand to eye level.
She extended her thumb.
She extended her index finger.
"Two..."𝒇𝙧𝙚𝓮𝙬𝙚𝓫𝒏𝓸𝓿𝓮𝒍.𝓬𝙤𝓶
She reached her pinky.
"Five..."
She stared at her empty palm, then looked back at her fingers with her mouth moving silently as she attempted to calculate how many times she had cleared a collapsed tenement block.
Tasmin rolled her eyes so hard she nearly strained an optic nerve.
"By the void, you truly are an illiterate ape," Tasmin sneered, her voice dripping with acidic disdain.
"You have five fingers on that hand, Brida...
You can’t even count past ten without taking off your iron boots.
There is a grand library in Blessed Land containing four thousand volumes of mathematics, basic arithmetic, and business logistics...
Master Silas spent thousands of UP stocking those shelves.
If your tiny, pea-sized brain requires tutoring, you could always swallow your pride and ask Reina to teach you how to count on an abacus!"
Brida’s face flushed a deep indignant crimson as she lowered her hand, scowling down at Tasmin with genuine wounded pride.
"I can count, you skinny little bat!" Brida barked, crossing her massive plate-armored arms over her chest.
"I saved... it was a lot!
It was at least... over a hundred and fifty!
Maybe two hundred!
I hauled an entire school bus out of a sinkhole by its bumper three blocks back!
That’s gotta be worth like sixty points right there!"
Tasmin’s lips curved into a smug triumphant sneer that looked like it had been carved from polished marble.
"Two hundred and thirty-seven," Tasmin stated with coldness in her voice.
FSSSS!
Before Brida could open her mouth to argue, Tasmin’s right hand subtly twitched.

Twenty yards down the street, near the smoking ruins of a baker’s pavilion, three panicked civilians... a mother and her two teenage sons were cornered against an iron fence by two leaping shadow-hounds.
Tasmin didn’t even turn her head.
SH-SH-SH!
From the shadows beneath the fence, three thin ribbons of darkness whipped forward.

They caught the three civilians gently around their waists, yanking them fifty feet across the street with weightless momentum, sliding them directly through the blast-rated hatch of the civil bunker.
CLANG!
The hatch slammed shut behind them with the automated locking bolts engaging with a definitive green flash, the Civilians could open it when they needed to enter with a code.
’At least that’s what I heard them say...’
Tasmin slowly turned her golden gaze back to Brida, her smirk widening until her eyes curved into mocking crescents.
"Two hundred and forty," Tasmin corrected herself smoothly.
"Keep up, Bastion or our Lord’s reward will be resting in my quarters before the sun touches the dunes."
Brida’s eyes narrowed into fierce competitive embers.
The air between the two women grew thick and crackling with suppressed mana.
This wasn’t merely about the crisis in Iunu...

A week ago, down in the ore veins beneath Blessed Land’s ridge, Silas had turned an ordinary mining shift into a competition between the two of them, laughing that whoever pulled the higher amount of ores could ask him for whatever they wanted in return.
Neither of them had let it go since and today was that day... the day that settled it all.
Brida glared down at Tasmin, her massive jaw setting into a stubborn immovable line.
"Oh, you think you’re so clever with your little shadows, huh?" Brida muttered, her fingers twitching against her thighs.
"I don’t think," Tasmin replied sweetly.
"I calculate...
Heh...
While you waste thirty seconds smashing a single lizard into paste, I have already routed forty citizens to safety.
You are a sledgehammer, Brida.
In a rescue operation, a sledgehammer merely breaks what is already fragile."
"Is that so?" Brida’s voice dropped into a low deceptively cheerful rumble.
"It is."
SWOOSH!
Brida’s massive armored frame suddenly blurred.
To anyone who didn’t know her, a woman of her size should have moved with the slow ponderous momentum of a glacier but Brida possessed the explosive agility of a high-tier monster.
Before Tasmin’s heightened spatial reflexes could even register the displacement...
GRAB!
Brida’s iron-hard right hand clamped down with vice-like ferocity around Tasmin’s left ankle.
Tasmin’s pupils snapped wide in pure shock.
"What in the—?!"
"Oops!" Brida roared, a wide grin splitting her bronze face.
"Oh no!
My hand slipped!
My grip is just so clumsy today, Tas!"
"BRIDA, YOU WHORE, PUT ME DOW—"
Brida didn’t put her down.
She planted her heavy iron sabatons into the cracked asphalt, twisted her massive hips with the rotational torque of a crane and reared her entire upper body backward.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The asphalt beneath Brida’s boots violently exploded into powder as she hurled Tasmin straight up into the sky.
The shockwave was so monstrous that it blew the windows out of the three adjacent buildings, creating a horizontal cone of displaced air that flattened a lamppost thirty yards away.
"HAVE A NICE FLIGHT, TAS!" Brida bellowed, cupping her hands around her mouth and waving frantically toward the heavens.
"DON’T WORRY ABOUT THE GROUND DOWN HERE!
THE GRAND TITAN BASTION HAS IT COMPLETELY UNDER CONTROL!
GWAHAHAHAHA!"
"BRIIIIIIIIIDAAAAAAAAAAAA!"
Tasmin’s furious high-pitched screech tore through the air as she broke the sound barrier, rocketing straight toward the clouds like an anti-air missile.
The city of Iunu tilted, spinning wildly beneath her vision as the wind whipped her cloak into a frenzied roar.
In less than three seconds, she cleared four thousand feet of elevation with her body hurtling directly toward a swirling cluster of high-altitude rift fissures.
Tasmin gritted her teeth so hard that a tiny bead of crimson leaked from her lower lip.
’That brainless... overgrown...
SOW!’ Tasmin raged in the freezing gale, her fingers twitching frantically. ’When we return to the territory, I am going to salt her rations...
I am going to pour acid into her bathwater!
I will make her life an unceasing waking nightmare!’
She twisted her torso mid-flight, fighting the terminal velocity drag, and looked forward.

Directly in her trajectory, descending from a five-hundred-foot tear in the sky, was an entire flock of sixty Abyss Skystrikers... grotesque four-winged avian horrors with razor-sharp beak-spurs and leathery bodies that crackled with jagged arcs of corrupted green lightning.
Beyond them, the massive wide tear in the sky hung like an open wound with the colossal skeletal hand still gripping the dimensional edge.
’My Lord’s orders were absolute,’
Silas’s voice echoed in her memory.
’Contain the perimeter, protect the civilians and avoid entering the gates at all costs.’
Tasmin’s golden eyes narrowed into deadly focused slits.
"Fine," she hissed into the howling wind.
"If you want to throw me into the sky, Brida... then the sky belongs to me."
CLINK!
Tasmin released the silver daggers from her hands but they didn’t fall.

The thirty-meter tungsten chains wrapped around her forearms uncoiled with terrifying fluid speed, the blades spinning around her body in a dual whistling orbit that formed an impenetrable sphere of humming razor-sharp steel.
VUUUUUM!
Her right foot kicked out in mid-air but she didn’t have wings as she didn’t possess Aeliana’s flight.
Instead, a flat, three-foot platform of dense solidified black shadow materialized directly beneath her boot.
CRACK!
She used the shadow platform as a springboard, altering her body by forty-five degrees with an explosive concussive push.
WHOOSH!
Tas shot toward the lead Skystriker like a falling black star.
SHRIIIIIIIIIIK!
The beast screeched, opening its jagged beak to unleash a concentrated bolt of green lightning but Tasmin didn’t even blink.
STEP!
She vanished into the creature’s own shadow with Shadow-Submersion Drift!
POP!
She materialized instantly upon the beast’s scaly back!

chapters.title: Chapter 621: Goals [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Her left hand snapped forward with her fingers coated in a dense diamond-hard shadow.
She drove her bare fingertips straight through the base of the creature’s skull, severing its central nervous conduit in a fraction of a second.
SPLAT!
Before the dying beast could even begin to plummet, Tasmin used its collapsing spine as another launch platform.
BOOM!
She leaped upward, her chains singing through the air and what followed was something that could simply be defined as a... slaughter.
Tasmin danced across the falling flock with terrifying weightless elegance.
She stepped from shadow to shadow, from falling wing to falling horn with her daggers carving clean crescents of destruction through the sky.
SHRIT! CRUNCH! SPLAT!

A Skystriker had its wings sheared from its ribs by a spinning chain... another had its chest cavity blown open by a concentrated blast of dark fire and a third was decapitated before it could turn its head.
Every time she killed, the shadows beneath her boots solidified, creating an ascending staircase of lightless stone that allowed her to climb higher and higher into the storm clouds.
THUMP!
High above the burning towers of Sector Two, at seven thousand feet of elevation, Tasmin reached the apex of her climb.
Her Shadow Heart throbbed violently against her ribs.
’Now,’ she thought, her eyes flashing with pure obsidian fire. ’Let us see the true reach of the blade.’
She crossed her arms over her chest with the thirty-meter tungsten chains pulling taut.
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The shadows radiating from her daggers coalesced into two colossal, sixty-foot-wide scythe-blades of pure concentrated mana that crackled with black and purple lightning.
Tasmin uncrossed her arms, driving both colossal blades downward in a sweeping scissor-like execution arc.
SHRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRK!
The sky tore open as the two massive shadow-blades cleaved through the entire descending formation of forty Skystrikers in a single horizontal stroke.

The beasts weren’t merely cut... their physical mass, their souls, and their corrupted lightning were severed at the molecular level, disintegrating into a colossal drifting cloud of black ash that rained down over the city.
"Hah... Hehehe..." Tasmin exhaled with the black mist flowing smoothly back into the pores of her skin, replenishing her core with refined essence. "I think I got up another stage."
She looked down through the falling ash.
A massive four-winged alpha-beast was plummeting toward a residential terrace four thousand feet below, where several families were trapped on an open balcony.
SWOOSH!
Tasmin dove.
She landed directly upon the alpha-beast’s neck with her knees locking around its armored crest.
Her hands thrust forward with dark ribbons of solidified shadow shooting from her palms, wrapping tightly around the beast’s serrated snout and jaws like a set of impenetrable agonizing reins.
"Come on!"
YANK!

With a brutal merciless wrench of her arms, Tasmin forcibly hauled the monster’s head upward, overriding its flight muscles and steering the shrieking abomination like a winged war-chariot as she banked sharply toward the south.
She looked down at the burning city spreading across the horizon.

’Level up notifications are probably cascading through my Lord’s status,’ Tasmin thought, a cold satisfaction settling into her chest as she felt her physical attributes ticking upward with every beast she purged. ’The power of these creatures... the volume of spiritual essence...’
If she maintained this pace... if she continued carving through the vanguard of the breach, she would advance further in three hours than she could in an entire month of standard territory defense!

She looked down toward the distant streets where Brida was currently smashing through rubble with an auburn speck leaving a trail of collapsed rooftops in her wake sounding loud and clumsy and somehow always exactly where the worst of it was.
A faint grudging smirk touched Tasmin’s lips.
’Thank you, you oversized brute,’ Tasmin thought dryly. ’You actually gave me the high ground.’
Down on the shattered asphalt of the Sector Two intersection.
Brida stood with her feet planted wide with her massive hands resting on the pommel of her titan-cleaver as her head tilted back as she squinted up into the smoky sky.
She watched the distant microscopic flashes of black and purple lightning tearing through the clouds four thousand feet above.
"Hm."
Brida watched the massive shockwaves parting the smoke, followed by the majestic sight of an alpha-beast being wrestled into submission and steered like a common horse.
Brida let out a slow heavy whistle through her teeth.
"Damn," Brida muttered to herself, her voice quiet for once and lacking any of its usual boisterous thunder. "Tas really did get stronger, didn’t she?"
She lowered her gaze, staring down at her own calloused palms.
Despite the constant teasing, despite the endless, petty bickering over rations, library books, and mining rights... Brida wasn’t stupid.
She was simple, yes.

She preferred a straight punch to an intricate mathematical formula, and she would rather carry an entire iron ore cart on her back than spend twenty minutes balancing a ledger with Aeli but she had the sharp instinctual intuition of a born warrior.
She knew Tasmin was driven by something profound.

Brida didn’t know the exact details of the Shadow Commander’s past as she didn’t pry into the quiet dark silences that sometimes settled over Tasmin when she looked out over the northern ridges of Blessed Land but she knew that whatever goal burned inside Tasmin’s chest, it was an all-consuming fire that pushed the woman to train until her muscles tore and her shadow bled.
Brida swallowed hard with a rare dry knot forming in the back of her throat.
"I think..." Brida whispered, her voice barely carrying over the wind, "...if we fought ten times... full-on, to the death, no holding back... Tasmin would probably kill me six times out of ten."
The thought sat heavy in her chest.
It didn’t make her angry and it didn’t breed resentment since Brida wasn’t the jealous type.
She loved her fellow champions with the fierce protective loyalty of a big sister who would take an arrow through the neck to keep them breathing.
’So what about me?’ Brida wondered, her fingers tightening around the cold grip of the Titan’s Cleaver. ’What is my goal?’
Everybody in Blessed Land seemed to have a grand poetic motivation.
Rowenna wanted to unravel the fundamental mystery of runes and become a God of Runes one day...
Aeliana simply wanted to be the best secretary that she could be and write the best smut books that the Sovereign Realm had ever seen.
Tasmin... Now Brida wasn’t so sure about that one however she did know that Vala wanted to master the five elements and prove herself worthy of being Lord Silas’s sword-wife.
’And what about Brida?’ she asked herself, looking down at the massive dark slate armor strapped across her chest.
Her initial goal had been remarkably straightforward... She wanted to be Lord Silas’s most powerful soldier.
She wanted to be the immovable, unbreakable wall that kept the monsters from touching his boots.
That drive had carried her far...
’But is that enough?’ she thought, letting out a deep rumbling sigh that shook her breastplate. ’To just be a soldier? Just a wall of meat that takes hits until the battle ends?’
...She wanted more.

She wanted a fire inside her chest that burned as fiercely as the one driving Tasmin through the clouds and she wanted a reason to become so terrifyingly strong that not even the ancient gods could lay a finger on what she loved.
THWIP!
A familiar whistling sound cut through the air thirty yards above and Brida snapped her head up.
Perched upon the stone parapet of a four-story administration building overlooking the intersection was a slender agile figure draped in a weathered traveler’s cloak of forest green.

Her long honey-blonde hair was tied back in a high ponytail that whipped in the desert wind as she wore fitted leather bracers reinforced with thin strips of brass, and resting in her left hand was an elegant recurved longbow carved from heartwood.
It was Fenna...
The former D-Rank Shieldmaiden-Archer, now standing proudly as an S-Rank sniper whose attacks could pierce a fly’s wing through three stone walls, was crouched on the parapet.
Her sharp eyes were calculating everything like a predator that was hunting its prey.
THUUUUM!
Brida bent her massive knees and leaped.
The street cracked beneath her, and in a single effortless bound, she landed upon the four-story parapet right beside the archer.
"Fenna!" Brida boomed, dusting off her cleaver.
Fenna didn’t jump, hell she didn’t even look up from her sights.
...She had already calculated Brida’s trajectory the moment the titan bent her knees.
"Brida," Fenna replied, unbothered by the giant woman looming over her. "You made quite a mess of the intersection... Boss told us to minimize structural damage where possible."
"Bah! Those buildings were already half-cracked!" Brida waved her hand dismissively.

She planted her weapon against the stone, leaning forward with an uncharacteristically serious expression. "Listen, Fenna. You hold the fort over here for a minute and cover the bunker entrance down below."
Fenna blinked, finally lowering her bow by an inch, tilting her head with mild curiosity. "Hold the fort? Where are you going?"
"I’m going on a walk," Brida grunted, turning her massive back to the parapet. "I need to find a reason to get stronger."
Fenna stared at her, her blonde eyebrows drawing together in complete utter bafflement.
"A... a reason to get stronger? Right now? In the middle of an active breach?!"
"Yeah!" Brida barked over her shoulder, already stepping onto the edge of the roof. "A girl’s gotta have priorities, Fenna! Watch my back!"
WHOOSH!
Before Fenna could utter another word of protest, Brida launched herself forward.
She simply hurled her massive, plate-armored bulk across the rooftops of Sector Two like a two-legged siege engine, jumping from building to building with terrifying earth-shaking velocity.
Fenna stood alone on the parapet, looking at the receding auburn hair of the titan, and let out an exhausted affectionate sigh.
"Idiot," Fenna muttered fondly, shaking her head. "She’s going to drive Boss insane one of these days."
Fenna’s lips twitched.
’I want to claim that reward for myself too.’
She raised her longbow with her fingers smoothly nocking three mana-tipped arrows to the string simultaneously.
TWANG-TWANG-TWANG!
Three blinding streaks of golden light whistled through the smoke, perfectly piercing the eyes of three trench-crawlers attempting to breach the alleyway below.
"Maintain the line!" Fenna yelled down to the fleeing citizens in the street. "Keep your heads down and proceed into the shelter! The archers of Blessed Land have the perimeter!"
CRASH! BOOM! CRUNCH!
Brida bounded across the city like a runaway boulder.
Every time her heavy boots slammed into a rooftop, terracotta tiles shattered, concrete parapets cracked, and the buildings groaned under the output of her travel.
SPLAT!

A Tier 2 gargoyle lunged at her from an ornamental spire but Brida didn’t even break stride, simply smashing her elbow through its stone-armored chest as she passed, turning the creature into gravel before leaping across an eighty-foot boulevard.

’What the hell should my goal be?!’ Brida grumbled internally with her brow knotting tighter with every rooftop she cleared. ’Think, Brida, think! You’ve got a head on your shoulders, use it for once!’
It had to be related to Lord Silas... That was non-negotiable.

Her entire existence, her strength, her evolution, her armor, the cleaver in her hands had been gifted to her by the man who had pulled her card from the ether and treated her like an irreplaceable treasure.
’Should I aim to be his personal warrior? The one who guards his bedroom door?’ she wondered.

’No... Tasmin already hides in his floorboards like a creeping ghost, and Aeliana watches him from the library with that ridiculous telescope of hers she found there... That market is completely saturated.’
’Should I aim to learn runes with Rowenna? Forge weapons for his army like Thora?’
She immediately shook her head, a cold shiver running through her massive shoulders.

’Hell no. The last time I touched one of Rowenna’s delicate runic styluses, I snapped it in half like a dried twig, and the woman burst into tears and hid away from me for three days. I’m built for breaking things, not drawing pretty squiggles...’
STOMP!
She landed upon the roof of a three-story residential apartment complex overlooking an open circular plaza.
SCREEECH!
A sharp terrified scream cut through the rumble of the falling city and Brida froze.
Her round amber eyes snapped downward toward the center of the courtyard.
There, cornered against the iron gate of a dried-up ornamental fountain, was a monster.
