With a brutal merciless wrench of her arms, Tasmin forcibly hauled the monster’s head upward, overriding its flight muscles and steering the shrieking abomination like a winged war-chariot as she banked sharply toward the south.
She looked down at the burning city spreading across the horizon.

’Level up notifications are probably cascading through my Lord’s status,’ Tasmin thought, a cold satisfaction settling into her chest as she felt her physical attributes ticking upward with every beast she purged. ’The power of these creatures... the volume of spiritual essence...’
If she maintained this pace... if she continued carving through the vanguard of the breach, she would advance further in three hours than she could in an entire month of standard territory defense!

She looked down toward the distant streets where Brida was currently smashing through rubble with an auburn speck leaving a trail of collapsed rooftops in her wake sounding loud and clumsy and somehow always exactly where the worst of it was.
A faint grudging smirk touched Tasmin’s lips.
’Thank you, you oversized brute,’ Tasmin thought dryly. ’You actually gave me the high ground.’
Down on the shattered asphalt of the Sector Two intersection.
Brida stood with her feet planted wide with her massive hands resting on the pommel of her titan-cleaver as her head tilted back as she squinted up into the smoky sky.
She watched the distant microscopic flashes of black and purple lightning tearing through the clouds four thousand feet above.
"Hm."
Brida watched the massive shockwaves parting the smoke, followed by the majestic sight of an alpha-beast being wrestled into submission and steered like a common horse.
Brida let out a slow heavy whistle through her teeth.
"Damn," Brida muttered to herself, her voice quiet for once and lacking any of its usual boisterous thunder.
"Tas really did get stronger, didn’t she?"
She lowered her gaze, staring down at her own calloused palms.
Despite the constant teasing, despite the endless, petty bickering over rations, library books, and mining rights...
Brida wasn’t stupid.
She was simple, yes.

She preferred a straight punch to an intricate mathematical formula, and she would rather carry an entire iron ore cart on her back than spend twenty minutes balancing a ledger with Aeli but she had the sharp instinctual intuition of a born warrior.
She knew Tasmin was driven by something profound.

Brida didn’t know the exact details of the Shadow Commander’s past as she didn’t pry into the quiet dark silences that sometimes settled over Tasmin when she looked out over the northern ridges of Blessed Land but she knew that whatever goal burned inside Tasmin’s chest, it was an all-consuming fire that pushed the woman to train until her muscles tore and her shadow bled.
Brida swallowed hard with a rare dry knot forming in the back of her throat.
"I think..." Brida whispered, her voice barely carrying over the wind, "...if we fought ten times... full-on, to the death, no holding back...
Tasmin would probably kill me six times out of ten."
The thought sat heavy in her chest.
It didn’t make her angry and it didn’t breed resentment since Brida wasn’t the jealous type.
She loved her fellow champions with the fierce protective loyalty of a big sister who would take an arrow through the neck to keep them breathing.
’So what about me?’ Brida wondered, her fingers tightening around the cold grip of the Titan’s Cleaver. ’What is my goal?’
Everybody in Blessed Land seemed to have a grand poetic motivation.
Rowenna wanted to unravel the fundamental mystery of runes and become a God of Runes one day...
Aeliana simply wanted to be the best secretary that she could be and write the best smut books that the Sovereign Realm had ever seen.
Tasmin...
Now Brida wasn’t so sure about that one however she did know that Vala wanted to master the five elements and prove herself worthy of being Lord Silas’s sword-wife.
’And what about Brida?’ she asked herself, looking down at the massive dark slate armor strapped across her chest.
Her initial goal had been remarkably straightforward...
She wanted to be Lord Silas’s most powerful soldier.
She wanted to be the immovable, unbreakable wall that kept the monsters from touching his boots.
That drive had carried her far...
’But is that enough?’ she thought, letting out a deep rumbling sigh that shook her breastplate. ’To just be a soldier?
Just a wall of meat that takes hits until the battle ends?’
...She wanted more.

She wanted a fire inside her chest that burned as fiercely as the one driving Tasmin through the clouds and she wanted a reason to become so terrifyingly strong that not even the ancient gods could lay a finger on what she loved.
THWIP!
A familiar whistling sound cut through the air thirty yards above and Brida snapped her head up.
Perched upon the stone parapet of a four-story administration building overlooking the intersection was a slender agile figure draped in a weathered traveler’s cloak of forest green.

Her long honey-blonde hair was tied back in a high ponytail that whipped in the desert wind as she wore fitted leather bracers reinforced with thin strips of brass, and resting in her left hand was an elegant recurved longbow carved from heartwood.
It was Fenna...
The former D-Rank Shieldmaiden-Archer, now standing proudly as an S-Rank sniper whose attacks could pierce a fly’s wing through three stone walls, was crouched on the parapet.
Her sharp eyes were calculating everything like a predator that was hunting its prey.
THUUUUM!
Brida bent her massive knees and leaped.
The street cracked beneath her, and in a single effortless bound, she landed upon the four-story parapet right beside the archer.
"Fenna!" Brida boomed, dusting off her cleaver.
Fenna didn’t jump, hell she didn’t even look up from her sights.
...She had already calculated Brida’s trajectory the moment the titan bent her knees.
"Brida," Fenna replied, unbothered by the giant woman looming over her.
"You made quite a mess of the intersection...
Boss told us to minimize structural damage where possible."
"Bah!
Those buildings were already half-cracked!" Brida waved her hand dismissively.
She planted her weapon against the stone, leaning forward with an uncharacteristically serious expression.
"Listen, Fenna.
You hold the fort over here for a minute and cover the bunker entrance down below."
Fenna blinked, finally lowering her bow by an inch, tilting her head with mild curiosity.
"Hold the fort?
Where are you going?"
"I’m going on a walk," Brida grunted, turning her massive back to the parapet.
"I need to find a reason to get stronger."
Fenna stared at her, her blonde eyebrows drawing together in complete utter bafflement.
"A... a reason to get stronger?
Right now?
In the middle of an active breach?!"
"Yeah!" Brida barked over her shoulder, already stepping onto the edge of the roof.
"A girl’s gotta have priorities, Fenna!
Watch my back!"
WHOOSH!
Before Fenna could utter another word of protest, Brida launched herself forward.
She simply hurled her massive, plate-armored bulk across the rooftops of Sector Two like a two-legged siege engine, jumping from building to building with terrifying earth-shaking velocity.
Fenna stood alone on the parapet, looking at the receding auburn hair of the titan, and let out an exhausted affectionate sigh.
"Idiot," Fenna muttered fondly, shaking her head.
"She’s going to drive Boss insane one of these days."
Fenna’s lips twitched.
’I want to claim that reward for myself too.’
She raised her longbow with her fingers smoothly nocking three mana-tipped arrows to the string simultaneously.
TWANG-TWANG-TWANG!
Three blinding streaks of golden light whistled through the smoke, perfectly piercing the eyes of three trench-crawlers attempting to breach the alleyway below.
"Maintain the line!" Fenna yelled down to the fleeing citizens in the street.
"Keep your heads down and proceed into the shelter!
The archers of Blessed Land have the perimeter!"
CRASH!
BOOM!
CRUNCH!
Brida bounded across the city like a runaway boulder.
Every time her heavy boots slammed into a rooftop, terracotta tiles shattered, concrete parapets cracked, and the buildings groaned under the output of her travel.
SPLAT!

A Tier 2 gargoyle lunged at her from an ornamental spire but Brida didn’t even break stride, simply smashing her elbow through its stone-armored chest as she passed, turning the creature into gravel before leaping across an eighty-foot boulevard.
’What the hell should my goal be?!’ Brida grumbled internally with her brow knotting tighter with every rooftop she cleared. ’Think, Brida, think!
You’ve got a head on your shoulders, use it for once!’
It had to be related to Lord Silas...
That was non-negotiable.

Her entire existence, her strength, her evolution, her armor, the cleaver in her hands had been gifted to her by the man who had pulled her card from the ether and treated her like an irreplaceable treasure.
’Should I aim to be his personal warrior?
The one who guards his bedroom door?’ she wondered.
Tasmin already hides in his floorboards like a creeping ghost, and Aeliana watches him from the library with that ridiculous telescope of hers she found there...
That market is completely saturated.’
’Should I aim to learn runes with Rowenna?
Forge weapons for his army like Thora?’
She immediately shook her head, a cold shiver running through her massive shoulders.
’Hell no.
The last time I touched one of Rowenna’s delicate runic styluses, I snapped it in half like a dried twig, and the woman burst into tears and hid away from me for three days.
I’m built for breaking things, not drawing pretty squiggles...’
STOMP!
She landed upon the roof of a three-story residential apartment complex overlooking an open circular plaza.
SCREEECH!
A sharp terrified scream cut through the rumble of the falling city and Brida froze.
Her round amber eyes snapped downward toward the center of the courtyard.
There, cornered against the iron gate of a dried-up ornamental fountain, was a monster.

chapters.title: Chapter 622: Brida’s Goal [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: It was a Spine-Render... a vile six-legged abomination with skin like wet leather, four snapping mandible-arms, and a long, whip-like tail barbed with bone hooks.
It was dripping dark corrosive saliva onto the cobblestones, circling slowly and savoring the scent of its trapped prey.
And standing between the monster and the fountain wall... was a boy.
He couldn’t have been more than ten years old.
His clothes, a simple dusty tunic of Khemet linen, were torn at the shoulder with his knees scraped and bleeding.
His body was shaking so violently that his heels clicked against the stones.
Yet, he hadn’t curled into a ball and he hadn’t turned his back to flee.
In his small, trembling hands, the boy held a broken wooden broom-handle, holding it out like a spear, pointing the blunt splintered tip straight at the towering eight-foot monster’s face.
Behind him, huddled against the fountain basin, clutching his ragged trousers with both hands, was a little girl.
She was barely four or five, her dark curly hair tangled with dust, her face buried against her brother’s hip as she sobbed in pure breathless terror.
"G-GET AWAY!" the boy screamed with his voice cracking and tears streaming down his soot-stained cheeks. "DON’T YOU TOUCH HER! GET BACK! I’LL KILL YOU, YOU UGLY BASTARD! GET AWAY FROM MY SISTER!"
The Spine-Render let out a low wet clicking hiss that sounded like mocking laughter.
It crouched on its six hocks with its mandible-arms spreading wide, preparing to pounce forward and tear both children into ribbons in a single ravenous snap...
WHOOSH!
From the three-story roof above, a shadow fell like the hammer of a wrathful god.
SPLAT-CRUNCH!
Brida didn’t even draw her axe as she landed directly upon the Spine-Render’s head with both of her plate-armored iron boots.
Forty thousand pounds of descending pressure, reinforced by the unyielding density of her [Unyielding Bedrock Body], met the creature’s skull and the monster didn’t have time to register the impact.
Its armored head, its thorax, its six legs, and its internal organs were instantly pulverized into a flat circular stain of dark ichor and bone fragments that coated the courtyard flags.
THUUUUM!
The impact rattled the fountain, but Brida’s mana swept through the cobblestones, absorbing the shockwave before it could knock the children off their feet.
The boy stood frozen.
His wooden broom-handle remained raised in the air, mere inches from Brida’s massive iron-plated knee.
He stared up with his jaw slacking as he took in the towering silhouette of the woman standing over the flattened corpse.
Brida looked down at the boy, then down at the little girl peeking out from behind his trousers with wide tear-filled eyes.
A massive delighted smile spread across Brida’s bronze face.
"Cute," Brida chuckled softly, the sound deep and resonant, like stones rolling in a riverbed.
She slowly dropped to one knee, bringing her towering frame down to the boy’s eye level.
Her massive calloused hand reached out, gently tapping the tip of his splintered broom-handle with the tip of her index finger.

"You’ve got some serious guts, kid," Brida said, her amber eyes shining with genuine admiration. "Facing down a high-tier abyssal creeper with a stick of wood? That was remarkably brave... You did a good job protecting your sister."
The boy’s lower lip trembled with the adrenaline finally washing out of his small frame, but he stubbornly wiped his nose with his sleeve and refused to look away from her.
GROOOOOOOAN!
Suddenly, the five-story apartment building directly across the courtyard shrieked!

A secondary horror... a massive six-ton Battering Trench-Beast with a skull of solid calcified bone had burrowed straight through the building’s ground-floor support pillars and the foundation buckled.

Tens of thousands of tons of concrete, brick, and iron began to violently tip forward, collapsing toward the courtyard like an avalanche of crushing death, accompanied by the charging roar of the armored beast bursting through the dust.
"LOOK OUT!" the boy shrieked, instinctively throwing his small body over his little sister, closing his eyes tight but Brida didn’t stand up from her knee.
"Calm down..."

She kept her left hand resting gently on the boy’s head, holding the children securely against the stone as she turned her upper body slightly toward the collapsing five-story building and the six-ton charging behemoth and her right arm pulled back.
...Her fingers curled into a massive iron-hard fist.
’Haah,’ Brida thought, her internal mana circulating with a warm feeling. ’Just a normal punch.’
WHOOSH!
She drove her bare right fist straight into the empty air!
KABOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The displacement was so monstrous that the sound wave might have shattered reality...!
From Brida’s single stationary fist, a colossal visible cone of compressed wind mana erupted outward.

The six-ton Battering Trench-Beast was hit by the pressurized air with its bone-armored skull caved inward, its ribs shattered; and its massive six-ton body was horizontally blasted backward through the sky, clearing two city blocks before disintegrating into dust.
And the falling five-story apartment complex?

The blast wave hit the collapsing concrete mid-fall as the force of the punch violently reversed its momentum, blowing thousands of tons of falling brick, steel, and mortar backward into the empty lot behind it, pulverizing the entire structure into fine harmless gravel that settled over the ruins like a gentle cloud.
The courtyard fell dead silent and the boy slowly opened his eyes.
He looked at the empty space where a five-story building had been falling bare seconds ago.
...There was nothing there. It was just an open view of the southern sky, framed by drifting dust motes.
He looked back at the giant woman kneeling before him as Brida grinned with her white teeth flashing.
"Told ya," she winked. "Nothing to worry about."
SWOOP!

With a single effortless motion, Brida reached out with both arms. She scooped the boy up under her left arm like a sack of grain, and lifted the little girl into the crook of her right elbow, cradling the child against her massive warm plate armor.
"Hold on tight, little sprouts," Brida laughed boisterously. "Auntie Brida is giving you a ride!"
BOOM!
She leaped.

Brida didn’t take the rooftops this time, she cleared the entire city block in a single soaring trajectory, sailing three hundred yards through the air before landing lightly upon the manicured turf outside the grand public pavilion of Sector Three.
In the center of the pavilion, glowing with serene starlight, was one of Aeliana’s honeycombed purple barriers.
Inside the protective dome, hundreds of sheltered citizens were watching the skies in terror.
Standing near the front of the barrier with her hair disheveled, her dress torn, weeping frantically as she called out two names over and over, was a middle-aged Khemet woman.
"FAROOQ! AMINA! WHERE ARE MY BABIES?! GODS, PLEASE, SOMEONE FIND MY CHILDREN—"
THUD!
Brida landed softly on the grass right outside the purple barrier as she gently lowered the two children to their feet, nudging the boy forward with the flat of her palm.
"Go on, hero," Brida smiled warmly. "Your mother’s waiting."
The woman inside the barrier froze.
Her tear-filled eyes locked onto the two small figures standing on the grass.
"MOMMY!" the little girl wailed, sprinting straight through the permeable starlight ward!
"AMINA! FAROOQ!"

The mother collapsed to her knees, throwing her arms around both children, sobbing hysterically as she buried her face in their hair, kissing their dusty cheeks over and over, rocking them back and forth in a desperate embrace of pure miraculous salvation.
The mother looked up through her tears, looking at the colossal, auburn-haired titan standing outside the barrier.

"Thank you..." the woman wept, bowing her forehead against the turf. "Thank you! May the heavens bless you! May the sun shine upon your path forever! We were separated when the first gate fell... I thought they were dead... I thought—"
"They’re tough kids," Brida said softly, her voice remarkably gentle. "The boy fought like a lion so you should be proud of him."
The little girl suddenly wriggled free from her mother’s arms.
She turned around, trotting on her tiny feet back toward the edge of the barrier.
She reached into the small dirt-stained pocket of her apron and pulled out a single bright yellow desert-poppy... a wild flower she had picked from the fountain basin before the monster arrived.
She stood on her tiptoes, reaching her small arm up toward Brida’s knees.
Brida blinked, tilting her head. "For me?"
"For the big knight," the little girl lisped shyly, her cheeks turning pink.
Brida’s heart hitched as she slowly knelt down, lowering her massive head until her forehead was level with the little girl’s hands.
With extreme clumsy gentleness, the little girl reached up and tucked the bright yellow poppy carefully behind Brida’s ear, smoothing down a thick strand of auburn hair.

The boy stepped forward, standing tall beside his sister as he looked up into Brida’s eyes, snapped his heels together, and brought his small right hand up to his brow in a crisp, determined, and deeply earnest military salute.
"Thank you, General," The boy said with his voice clear and proud.
’General...’
Brida’s chest tightened with a strange breathtakingly warm sensation as she raised her massive calloused right hand and returned the salute with solemn respect.
"Dismissed, soldier," Brida smiled. "Get underground and keep your family safe."
The boy nodded firmly, took his little sister’s hand, and led her back through the purple barrier, joining their weeping mother as they followed the local Awakened down into the subterranean shelter.
Brida remained kneeling on the grass.
A strong warm desert wind swept through the ruined pavilion, rustling the leaves of the shattered palm trees and gently stirring the yellow poppy tucked into her hair.
HUMMMMMMMMMMMMM!
Deep within Brida’s sternum... deep within the core of her own being... a profound shift occurred.
The chaotic wandering mana that had circulated through her heavy limbs for weeks suddenly began to converge.
It rushed inward, condensing around her physical heart like molten iron pouring into a mold.
Brida looked at the empty gate where the family had vanished into the earth as a slow radiant smile spread across her bronze face.
She reached up with her thick fingers, gently patting the yellow poppy resting behind her ear, her pulse hammering with a steady clear purpose.
’Yeah...’ Brida thought, her breath coming in a soft trembling deeply happy sigh.
’I have a goal.’
The wind grew stronger, howling through the spires of the burning city, but Brida’s massive frame didn’t sway by a single millimeter.
Her thoughts weren’t complex.
...They weren’t woven from prophecies, nor were they burdened by the strength that drove Tasmin through the high clouds.
They were simple.
’I want to have kids,’ Brida thought, her smile softening into something beautifully maternal.
’A shit ton of them. A whole house full of rowdy thick-headed, iron-boned brats who run through the high grass of Blessed Land with wooden swords, screaming their heads off and breaking things...’
Her knuckles curled into fists of unbreakable resolve.

’And I want to be strong enough... I want to be so terrifyingly, god-shatteringly strong... that no rift, no monster, and no deity can ever touch a single hair on their heads... I will protect Lord Silas... I will protect my kids... My grandkids... My great-grandkids... Every single soul born beneath our banner...’
Her chest expanded as the golden-red energy coalescing around her heart locked permanently into place.
’Me... and Lord Silas.’
It was a simple goal.
It was probably an absurd unrefined dream compared to the grand cosmic ambitions of the other nine women walking this sand today.

Yet, as the clarity of that purpose settled into the marrow of her bones, Brida’s massive iron-armored legs began to shake... not from weakness, but from the uncontainable surge of vitality violently erupting through her meridians.
’I feel weird...’
Not only did this power spread from her legs to all of her body, but even her heart began to feel faster.
’I have a purpose... Is this what Tasmin feels?’
The purpose made her... feel a lot stronger for some reason, was it supposed to be like that? Even if she made it her life’s mission to get knocked up like twenty times by Lord Silas?
DING!
[GRAND TITAN BASTION BRIDA HAS DEVELOPED A WARRIOR’S HEART!]

Happy New Month In Advance everyone! Since it’s the last day of the month, I want to thank everyone for all of the castles and golden tickets as you’ve supported the book and it means a lot to me...

And not only that but through your support with Golden Tickets, we’ve managed to hit the Top 10 Ranking in Golden Tickets however it’s not really secured that we’ll get the ranking this month due to an invisible book in the ranking so we’ll need about 200-300+ Golden Tickets to be able to enter Top 8-9 which is secured, from what I know. Thank you! Each and every Golden Ticket matters.
I feel a bit better too so I’m going to start writing for a new month Mass Release so expect that, once again, thank you all for your support! Hope to see you next month!

With extreme clumsy gentleness, the little girl reached up and tucked the bright yellow poppy carefully behind Brida’s ear, smoothing down a thick strand of auburn hair.

The boy stepped forward, standing tall beside his sister as he looked up into Brida’s eyes, snapped his heels together, and brought his small right hand up to his brow in a crisp, determined, and deeply earnest military salute.
"Thank you, General," The boy said with his voice clear and proud.
’General...’
Brida’s chest tightened with a strange breathtakingly warm sensation as she raised her massive calloused right hand and returned the salute with solemn respect.
"Dismissed, soldier," Brida smiled.
"Get underground and keep your family safe."
The boy nodded firmly, took his little sister’s hand, and led her back through the purple barrier, joining their weeping mother as they followed the local Awakened down into the subterranean shelter.
Brida remained kneeling on the grass.
A strong warm desert wind swept through the ruined pavilion, rustling the leaves of the shattered palm trees and gently stirring the yellow poppy tucked into her hair.
HUMMMMMMMMMMMMM!
Deep within Brida’s sternum... deep within the core of her own being... a profound shift occurred.
The chaotic wandering mana that had circulated through her heavy limbs for weeks suddenly began to converge.
It rushed inward, condensing around her physical heart like molten iron pouring into a mold.
Brida looked at the empty gate where the family had vanished into the earth as a slow radiant smile spread across her bronze face.
She reached up with her thick fingers, gently patting the yellow poppy resting behind her ear, her pulse hammering with a steady clear purpose.
’Yeah...’ Brida thought, her breath coming in a soft trembling deeply happy sigh.
’I have a goal.’
The wind grew stronger, howling through the spires of the burning city, but Brida’s massive frame didn’t sway by a single millimeter.
Her thoughts weren’t complex.
...They weren’t woven from prophecies, nor were they burdened by the strength that drove Tasmin through the high clouds.
They were simple.
’I want to have kids,’ Brida thought, her smile softening into something beautifully maternal.
’A shit ton of them.
A whole house full of rowdy thick-headed, iron-boned brats who run through the high grass of Blessed Land with wooden swords, screaming their heads off and breaking things...’
Her knuckles curled into fists of unbreakable resolve.
’And I want to be strong enough...
I want to be so terrifyingly, god-shatteringly strong... that no rift, no monster, and no deity can ever touch a single hair on their heads...
I will protect Lord Silas...
I will protect my kids...
My grandkids...
My great-grandkids...
Every single soul born beneath our banner...’
Her chest expanded as the golden-red energy coalescing around her heart locked permanently into place.
’Me... and Lord Silas.’
It was a simple goal.
It was probably an absurd unrefined dream compared to the grand cosmic ambitions of the other nine women walking this sand today.

Yet, as the clarity of that purpose settled into the marrow of her bones, Brida’s massive iron-armored legs began to shake... not from weakness, but from the uncontainable surge of vitality violently erupting through her meridians.
’I feel weird...’
Not only did this power spread from her legs to all of her body, but even her heart began to feel faster.
’I have a purpose...
Is this what Tasmin feels?’
The purpose made her... feel a lot stronger for some reason, was it supposed to be like that?
Even if she made it her life’s mission to get knocked up like twenty times by Lord Silas?
DING!
[GRAND TITAN BASTION BRIDA HAS DEVELOPED A WARRIOR’S HEART!]

paragraphs: The basalt flagstones of Sector Two were slick with black bile and shredded chitin, hissing faintly where acidic fluids ate through the sealants.
SHRIT-SHRIT!
Two ribbons of link-less tungsten chain whipped through the heavy dust, snapping taut with a hum that set the teeth on edge.
"Ptch!"
Tasmin didn’t look at the three bone-fiends flanking her from the alley... instead she pivoted on her left heel with her weight settling low into the hip as the twin daggers reversed in her palms.
The silver edges caught what little bruised sunlight filtered through the smoke, flashing an oily violet.
CLANG-CRACK!
The nearest beast... a four-legged scavenger whose skull had elongated into a serrated spade lunged forward with its jaw clicking like dry shears and Tasmin’s right elbow flicked.
The chain followed the snap of her shoulder, coiling twice around the monster’s snout before she yanked downward with the full rotational torque of her core.
THUD!
The beast’s face hammered into the curb, fracturing the stone.

Before it could thrash, Tasmin’s left foot drove into the base of its neck, pinning the vertebrae, while her secondary dagger drove smooth and clean through the soft junction beneath the cranial horn.
SPLAT!

There was no wasted motion at all as Tas pulled the blade free with a wet scrape, her thumb immediately nudging a pair of middle-aged shopkeepers toward the glowing starlight ward flickering fifty yards ahead.

"Don’t gawk," Tasmin barked, her voice cutting cleanly through the sirens. "The barrier is twenty paces... Keep your heads below the sill and move your legs. If you drop your parcels, leave them. The stone won’t wait for them at all!"
The two men scrambled over the shattered glass, their breath coming in ragged whistling sobs as they threw themselves through the permeable violet luminescence of Aeliana’s barrier.
The moment their heels cleared the threshold, the honeycombed runes rippled, deflecting a diving swarm of razor-winged carrion crows with a deafening PING-PING-PING.
Tasmin stepped back into the street, letting the chains reel back into the magnetic cuffs along her forearms with smooth, oily clicks.
Her short silver-streaked hair was damp with sweat, clinging to the nape of her neck beneath the high collar of her mantle.

’Fissures are multiplying in the lower levels,’ she assessed, her golden eyes darting across the cracked facades of the district. ’The surface is holding for now, but the crust feels like rotten timber.’
VUUUUUUUM!
A subtle displacement in the upper air caught her ear... it was a sound similar to the hum of a plucked harp string resonating through cold glass.
Tasmin crouched, her soles sinking an inch into the shadow pooled behind an overturned delivery van, and launched herself upward.
She cleared the fourth-story cornice with a single Shadow-Submersion Drift, bursting out from the shade of a decorative limestone gargoyle to land on the broad gravel-strewn roof of another building.
The gravel crunched once.
Before she could rise from her landing crouch, a soft freezing downdraft swept across the roof.
FLUTTER!
Aeliana drifted down through the smoke-choked sky with her slender, star-silver sabatons coming to rest upon the gravel without making so much as a pebble roll.

Her long pale gold hair floated behind her like spun thread, untamed by the wind and the constellation-etched plates of her midnight-blue cuirass gleamed with an immaculate mirror-like polish that defied the soot clinging to the rest of the city.
"You’re working the perimeter close to the ground, Commander," Aeliana said.

Her voice was melodious and carrying that infuriating effortless archon poise that always made Tasmin want to test a dagger against her shoulder plates. "Sector Three’s residential blocks are largely emptied of breathing people... I came across to verify this place."
"They’re moving," Tasmin said, rising and rolling her right shoulder until the joint clicked.

Her gaze swept the burning avenue below. "A bit slow on the uptake, but terrified enough to follow orders when the teeth start clicking behind them... How does the count look on your end, Aeliana? Still hovering above the filth and pretending your boots don’t touch dust?"
Aeliana’s silver-green eyes narrowed by a fraction of a millimeter with a tiny amused smirk touching the corner of her lips.
"My boots remain unsoiled because I understand the utility of elevation, Tasmin," the elf replied smoothly. "Down in the muck, you’ve routed... what? Three hundred? Perhaps three hundred and twenty?"
"Three hundred and forty-two," Tasmin corrected immediately, her tone sharpening with competitive bite. "Well not counting the ones Brida probably flattened by accident while trying to be helpful..."
Aeliana chuckled, it was a light angelic sound that grated against the background hum of the distant explosions.
"A respectable tally for someone crawling through gutters," Aeliana murmured, tilting her head.
’Is she trying to sound cool again...?’ Tamsin thought while rolling her eyes, Aeli always acted like this when she read a new novel.

"I have guided seven hundred and sixteen directly into the deep access hatches... Seven hundred and eighteen, if the two technicians hiding inside the generator room managed to crawl through the intake tube before the ceiling collapsed."
Tasmin turned her head, her golden eyes widening slightly in genuine surprise.

"Seven hundred?" Tasmin repeated, her brow furrowing. "Are you sure the underground bunkers are designed to hold that much people... If you’re stuffing seven hundred into those chambers, they’ll be suffocating on each other’s breath within forty minutes."
"They aren’t remaining in the bunkers," Aeliana said.
The archon’s smile faded, replaced by that deep stillness that usually accompanied her calculations.
She walked to the edge of the parapet, her silver fingers resting lightly upon the weathered coping stone.

"There is an active spatial current operating beneath the city," Aeliana explained. "The moment the citizens descend past the third security bulkhead, they are being caught in a wide-aperture field... It isn’t a simple blink, and it certainly isn’t a crude teleport spell either... The spatial power is terrifyingly refined with folded dimensions, anchored to an external coordinate miles outside this place."
Tasmin stepped up beside her, her hands resting on the pommels of her daggers.
"External? You mean someone is extracting them from Iunu entirely?"

"Yes," Aeliana nodded. "The signature possesses the exact same purity as my own star-weaving... well no, I’m stronger but they do have more mastery than me. It takes real concentration to fold space around ordinary civilians without their organs rupturing from the shear... Whoever is pulling the strings on the other side understands spatial power on a whole new level."
Tasmin’s eyes flickered with suspicion. "Is it an enemy? A second party from the Sovereign Realm taking advantage of the breach to harvest souls...?"
Aeliana shook her head, her pale hair swaying across her pauldrons.

"No," she said softly, a faint reassuring warmth returning to her eyes. "The frequency comes from someone near our Lord’s personal mana signature, woven together with the primordial fire of the Crimson Dragon."
’Do you really have to talk like this, Aeliana?’

"Talira is down there, working around the city alongside him. Between our Lord’s core and Talira’s breath, the refugees are being deposited safely into the southern side of this country beyond the dunes... The citizens are not dying in the dark, Tasmin. That much I can assure you."
Tasmin let out a long slow breath through her teeth, her shoulders easing by a bare half-inch.
"Good," she muttered. "That means we don’t have to worry about the retreat collapsing behind us... We just need to hold the surface until the sky runs out of vermin."
"Indeed," Aeliana said.
Then, she raised her chin slightly, her gaze flicking toward the sky three hundred yards above the library.
A small matte-black metallic cylinder, propelled by four silent micro-rotors, hovered lazily against the grey thermal haze.
A glowing amber lens on its underbelly rotated continuously, tracking the two women on the roof with persistence.
Further along the skyway, two more civilian media drones were circling like vultures, their broadcast diodes blinking rapid green pulses.

"If you haven’t already noticed," Aeliana murmured, her lips barely moving as she spoke without turning her head, "I think it’s the press and they’ve recovered their nerve... Those mechanical eyes have been trailing my starlight for the past twelve minutes. I think like in the novels, they’re broadcasting us across every network there is."
Tasmin’s jaw tightened. "Pests."

"I’ve read about these contraptions in the Blessed Land archives," Aeliana warned, dropping her voice to a strict whisper. "They pick up sound through atmospheric vibration so don’t speak Lord Silas’s name aloud. He walks this earth as Lord Vespera, and until he says otherwise, the public doesn’t get to connect us to his true identity... Use the title."
"I’m not an idiot, Aeli," Tasmin scoffed, crossing her arms. "I’ve been operating in the dark since before your ears grew points. I don’t give my commander’s name away to metal toys."
SCREEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEECH!
The sky above the library violently groaned as the clouds were violently shredded by the sudden descent of a massive, bone-plated horror that dropped from the upper rim of a large fissure in the sky.
It was a Tier 4 Dread-Wyrm... a serpentine nightmare sixty feet from snout to tail, forged from interlocking plates of blackened petrified bone that crackled with sickly corrosive emerald plasma.
’Why are the monsters so big though...?’
It possessed no wings, instead the monster rode the air upon eight pairs of splayed, skeletal ribs that beat against the air like oars, its hollow eye sockets blazing with high-powered fire.
"GRAAAHHHHHHHHHH!"
The concussive shockwave of its roar shattered the remaining glass in the archive’s skylight, raining sharp shards down into the atrium below.
Tasmin’s chains hissed from her cuffs, her silver daggers dropping into her palms with instantaneous readiness.
Beside her, Aeliana’s starlight bow flared into existence, three purple spatial arrows nocking to the string in a single fluid heartbeat.
"What a big thing..." Tasmin commanded, her boots sinking into the roof’s shadow. "I’ll sever the rib-joints, you take the cranial core—"
"Wait," Aeliana whispered, her ears twitching violently. "Above it."
WHOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSSSSH!
A sound like an atmospheric reentry vehicle tearing through the clouds drowned out the roar of the wyrm.
High above the beast, dropping through the smoky haze at high velocity, was a massive hurtling meteor of dark slate and flying auburn hair.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHA!"
The booming ear-splitting laugh echoed off the building walls bare seconds before impact as the woman above wasn’t using a weapon...

She fell through the sky with her massive legs tucked and her right arm cocked back until the thick leather straps of her pauldrons shrieked under the strain of her expanding lats, her calloused iron-hard knuckles glowing with a red-gold hue.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The punch detonated the air around the monster!

Brida’s fist drove straight into the center of the sixty-foot beast’s skull and the ungodly force of the impact completely bypassed the bone armor, sending a visible comical shockwave of pressurized air and golden mana rippling down the monster’s entire spine.
CRACK-CRUNCH-SHATTER!
The Dread-Wyrm didn’t even have time to shriek.

Its skull disintegrated into powdery white meal with its sixty-foot spine shattered into hundreds of flying, jagged shards and the remaining forty tons of its calcified body were violently, horizontally blasted across two hundred yards of open air.

The corpse crashed into the side of an eight-story commercial bank across the boulevard, punching clean through three floors of reinforced concrete before collapsing into a mountain of pulverized brick and shattered bone.
THUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
The roof beneath Tasmin and Aeliana violently lurched!

Brida hit the gravel on both feet with her landing impact driving a six-foot crater into the roof, sending fissures spider-webbing across the concrete deck and raining dust down through the cracked ceiling below.
The dust cloud puffed out in a wide circular ring.
Brida stood in the center of the crater, completely unbothered, dusting off the leather bracer on her right forearm with a broad, cheerful grin that showed off her thick blunt teeth.
The bright yellow poppy the little girl had given her was still tucked neatly behind her left ear, miraculously undamaged by the damage she had just caused.
"Whew!" Brida boomed, rolling her neck with a wet crack. "Now that was a decent head! Had some good crunch to it! Hey, girls! Beautiful day for a stroll, ain’t it?!"
Tasmin and Aeliana stood completely frozen, staring at the giant woman.
The roof was silent save for the distant sirens then, slowly, Tasmin’s pupils contracted.
Beside her, Aeliana’s silver-green eyes narrowed into sharp intense slits of pure, analytical shock.
Something was undeniably wrong.
Or rather... fundamentally different.
To high level Awakened of their caliber, the presence of another warrior was as distinct as a voice in an empty room.
Barely twenty minutes ago, Brida’s mana had been a broad unrefined boulder... It was heavy and immovable, but rough around the edges, leaking pressure like water splashing from an overfilled bucket.
But now...?
The air within ten paces of Brida felt... compressed.
Her sun-bronzed skin didn’t merely look tough, it carried a deep-rooted metallic luster that seemed to absorb the light around her.
Her core, usually roaring with boisterous vitality, had settled into an immovable iron-hard anchor that felt like she was truly Unmovable.
Tasmin stared at her, her eye twitching as she slowly lowered her daggers.

"What the unholy fuck happened to you?" Tasmin hissed, stepping forward and glaring up into Brida’s face. "You were gone for fifteen minutes... You look like you got dipped in melted star-slate and swallowed an iron anvil!"
Brida blinked, scratching the back of her head with a thick hand, her grin widening until her eyes crinkled.

"Oh, that?" Brida laughed, puffing her chest out so hard the dark star-slate armor creaked in protest. "I got a goal! A life goal! A genuine, honest-to-god warrior’s motivation, just like you girls have!"
Aeliana tilted her head, her golden eyebrows furrowing in genuine, bewildered curiosity.
"A goal? You abandoned your defensive sector to go philosophizing in an alleyway?"
"I didn’t abandon nothing!" Brida barked back defensively, planting her fists on her wide hips.
The attack had destroyed the drones nearby which made Aeli allow Brida speak.

"I was thinking! About what Silas said back in the mines and them about me having a fire in my belly that doesn’t go out and I found it! And the moment I figured it out... BAM! This crazy energy slammed into my chest, and my soul gave this giant thump, and suddenly everything felt ten times lighter! I think I’m going to call it Warrior’s Heart!"

The bright yellow poppy the little girl had given her was still tucked neatly behind her left ear, miraculously undamaged by the damage she had just caused.
"Whew!" Brida boomed, rolling her neck with a wet crack.
"Now that was a decent head!
Had some good crunch to it!
Hey, girls!
Beautiful day for a stroll, ain’t it?!"
Tasmin and Aeliana stood completely frozen, staring at the giant woman.
The roof was silent save for the distant sirens then, slowly, Tasmin’s pupils contracted.
Beside her, Aeliana’s silver-green eyes narrowed into sharp intense slits of pure, analytical shock.
Something was undeniably wrong.
Or rather... fundamentally different.
To high level Awakened of their caliber, the presence of another warrior was as distinct as a voice in an empty room.
Barely twenty minutes ago, Brida’s mana had been a broad unrefined boulder...
It was heavy and immovable, but rough around the edges, leaking pressure like water splashing from an overfilled bucket.
But now...?
The air within ten paces of Brida felt... compressed.
Her sun-bronzed skin didn’t merely look tough, it carried a deep-rooted metallic luster that seemed to absorb the light around her.
Her core, usually roaring with boisterous vitality, had settled into an immovable iron-hard anchor that felt like she was truly Unmovable.
Tasmin stared at her, her eye twitching as she slowly lowered her daggers.
"What the unholy fuck happened to you?" Tasmin hissed, stepping forward and glaring up into Brida’s face.
"You were gone for fifteen minutes...
You look like you got dipped in melted star-slate and swallowed an iron anvil!"
Brida blinked, scratching the back of her head with a thick hand, her grin widening until her eyes crinkled.
"Oh, that?" Brida laughed, puffing her chest out so hard the dark star-slate armor creaked in protest.
"I got a goal!
A life goal!
A genuine, honest-to-god warrior’s motivation, just like you girls have!"
Aeliana tilted her head, her golden eyebrows furrowing in genuine, bewildered curiosity.
"A goal?
You abandoned your defensive sector to go philosophizing in an alleyway?"
"I didn’t abandon nothing!" Brida barked back defensively, planting her fists on her wide hips.
The attack had destroyed the drones nearby which made Aeli allow Brida speak.
"I was thinking!
About what Silas said back in the mines and them about me having a fire in my belly that doesn’t go out and I found it!
And the moment I figured it out...
BAM!
This crazy energy slammed into my chest, and my soul gave this giant thump, and suddenly everything felt ten times lighter!
I think I’m going to call it Warrior’s Heart!"

chapters.title: Chapter 624: An Ass That Doesn’t Ripple [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Tasmin’s jaw tightened.
"A Warrior’s Heart... an internal evolution? What ridiculous, high-minded ideal did you conjure up to trigger a breakthrough in the middle of a burning city?"
Tasmin on the other hand was quite jealous, she had to reason a lot of things to dedicate herself to this power that she had now, why had Brida been able to do it instantly.
Brida beamed, her bronze cheeks flushing with a bright proud completely shameless pink.

"I decided I’m gonna have Lord Silas’s babies!" Brida announced at the top of her lungs, her booming voice echoing off the surrounding high-rises with the volume of a brass horn. "A whole damn army of ’em! Ten, maybe twelve or twenty! Strong, thick-headed, iron-boned brats that’ll run around Blessed Land breaking things and making him smile and I’m gonna be so goddamn strong that nothing in the Sovereign Realm can ever touch our family! Me and him, forever!"
...Silence.
Suffocating brain-melting silence descended upon the rooftop.
Tasmin’s daggers slipped from her fingers by half an inch, the chains clinking softly against her leather boots.
Her mouth opened, closed, and opened again with her sharp mind completely unable to formulate a coherent sentence.
’Isn’t... Isn’t that we all want to do?’
She got all this strength from forgetting that she wanted to be bred by Lord Silas and then remembering it...? How bigger of a dummy could she be!
Aeliana stood motionless.
The starlight bow vanished from the elf’s hands in a puff of purple mist.
Her silver-green eyes stared at Brida’s massive beaming face with the expression of a scholar who had just watched a goat solve a four-dimensional differential equation.
"You..." Aeliana stammered, her pale ears suddenly turning bright crimson. "You... your breakthrough... your evolution... was triggered by... breeding instincts?!"

"Damn right!" Brida declared proudly, flexing her massive right bicep until the bronze muscle peaked like a small mountain. "Look at this! Hard as bedrock! Strong as a titan! If a dragon bites my arm right now, the bastard’s teeth are gonna snap in half!"
Aeliana took a slow deliberate step forward with her brow furrowing as she crossed her arms beneath her breastplate.
"Brida," Aeliana said. "Your output has gone up, granted... But there’s a hole in your entire theory big enough to drive a siege engine through."
Brida blinked, lowering her arm. "Flaw? What flaw? More muscle means more strength!"
"In a fight, yes," Aeliana said, raising one slender finger. "In bed? Absolutely not."
Tasmin slowly turned her head toward Aeliana, a look of creeping horror dawning across her face.
"Aeli... please do not do this."

"Quiet, Tasmin, this actually matters," Aeliana said, waving her off and stepping straight into Brida’s space. "I’ve read forty-seven human smut novels out of the Great Library archive, strictly for craft research, since I’m drafting my own, and not one hero wants to climb into bed with something built like a bunker wall... Men want their women soft and warm."
Brida’s smile faltered, her round amber eyes widening slightly. "Soft...?"

"Yes, soft!" Aeliana pressed, deadpan despite her ears glowing like hot coals. "They want to sink their fingers into something that gives! Curves that rebound! How exactly is Lord Silas supposed to enjoy himself with a woman built like a reinforced bunker wall? You’re nothing but dense striation! Look at this!"
Before Brida could react, Aeliana reached out with both hands and aggressively grabbed a massive two-handed handful of Brida’s left buttock.
SQUEEZE!
Aeliana’s slender star-silver fingers strained and her knuckles whitened.
The plate armor didn’t even indent as the petrified muscle beneath the leather refused to budge by a single millimeter.
It was like attempting to knead a solid slab of quarried granite...

"Look!" Aeliana exclaimed, holding her hands in place, turning her head toward Tasmin with vindictive triumph. "Look at this, Tasmin! I cannot even gather a proper palmful! My fingers are slipping off the contour! It is solid slate and there is zero elasticity! How, Brida? How is this supposed to ripple when our Lord takes you from behind?! How will it bounce?! It won’t! It will merely produce a dull concussive clatter, like two shields colliding in an armory!"
Brida’s bronze face turned violently purple.

"H-HEY!" Brida squawked, jumping back half a step, swatting Aeliana’s hands away with a frantic flustered wave of her massive forearms. "WHAT ARE YOU DOING GRABBING MY ASS IN THE MIDDLE OF A WAR ZONE, YOU POINTY-EARED FREAK?!"
Tasmin slapped both hands over her own face, dragging her palms down her cheeks with a long agonizing soul-crushing groan that came from the deepest darkest pit of her stomach.
"I am surrounded by degenerates," Tasmin wept into the empty air, her voice muffled by her gloves. "Lord Silas, please strike me down with lightning... I beg of you."

"I am merely stating a fact!" Aeliana huffed, crossing her arms with her own cheeks burning hot. "If she wants to reach her goal, she needs to understand how human desire actually works! Lord Silas is a gentleman! He’ll break his wrist trying to spank her! Look at me for example... all soft and curvy, if Lord Silas takes me in his office then I’ll bend like a chair and there’ll be loud sounds too~"
"I CAN CONTROL IT!" Brida roared, stamping her foot so hard the parapet gave another groaning shudder.
Aeliana paused, her eyes blinking in surprise. "Control what?"

"The hardness!" Brida yelled, her broad hands gesturing wildly down her own body. "That’s what the [Warrior’s Heart] does! I don’t just stay hard all the time like a dumb rock! I can tighten the mana when I take a hit, and I can loosen the muscle when I’m resting! Watch!"
Brida took a deep shuddering breath.
"Haah..."
Her eyes closed.
She relaxed her shoulders, letting her massive frame settle and releasing the iron tension that usually locked her skeleton in place.
FSSSSSSSS!
A visible soft shimmer of golden-red vitality rippled through her skin, the harsh metallic luster fading into a warm sun-bronzed glow.
The dense muscle beneath her leather tunic subtly softened, expanding slightly into lush, natural fullness.
"There!" Brida snapped, turning her hip toward Aeliana with a defiant scowl. "Touch it now, you little bookworm!"
Aeliana hesitated for a second then, driven by pure shameless curiosity, the elf reached out again.
SQUEEZE!
Aeliana’s hand sank deep into Brida’s hip and buttock.
The flesh yielded smoothly under her fingers, it was impossibly soft this time... possessing a rich velvety bounce that pushed gently back against her palm with astonishing elasticity.
Aeliana’s silver-green eyes went wide as saucers.
"Oh..." Aeliana breathed with her mouth falling open.
She slowly leaned her upper body forward, resting the side of her delicate porcelain cheek directly against Brida’s massive relaxed bicep.
The muscle was like a warm silk-wrapped down pillow, radiating a comforting heat.

"Umm..." Aeliana murmured, her voice dropping into a dazed completely defenseless whisper as her cheek squished against Brida’s arm. "...you’re... you’re really soft. Like... remarkably soft. It feels like fresh bread."
Brida froze for a second, looking down at the elf resting her head on her bicep like a sleepy kitten then, Brida threw her head back.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHA!"
The laugh was so loud that it blew the dust off Aeliana’s hair!

"TOLD YA!" Brida boomed, flexing slightly so Aeliana’s head bounced up and down. "Auntie Brida has got it all! The shield for the war, and the pillows for the master! Gwahaha! You think I’d make a life goal without figuring out the details?! I’m a genius!"
"ENOUGH!"
CLANK!
Tasmin’s daggers slammed together, releasing a shower of violet sparks that separated the two women instantly.
Tasmin stood between them with her dark hair standing on end and her eyes blazing with fury.

"You are both unredeemable perverts," Tasmin hissed, pointing the tip of her left dagger at Brida’s nose, then her right at Aeliana’s forehead. "If either of you speaks another syllable about cushions, buttocks, or our Lord’s bedchamber while the city behind us is falling into the void, I will personally weave shadow-gags into your mouths and hang you from the clock tower by your ankles! Do you understand me?!"
Aeliana quickly cleared her throat, stepping back with a sharp cough, frantically smoothing down the front of her star-silver cuirass while her ears burned an even deeper shade of magenta.

"Ahem... Quite right," Aeliana said, her dignified archon composure slamming back into place with the subtlety of a falling portcullis. "A momentary lapse in discipline as the civilian evacuation remains our primary directive. Sector Five, from what I can see, is beginning to buckle under the strain of a rift formation. I shall take that quadrant immediately."
"Go," Tasmin snapped.
Aeliana nodded once, her silver-green eyes regaining their cold focus.
VUM!
Her slender frame dissolved into a blinding constellation of purple starlight, vanishing in mid-air with a sharp pop as she teleported across miles of urban airspace.
The rooftop fell silent once more, leaving only the dark-haired commander and the bronze titan standing among the cracked gravel.
Brida looked down at Tasmin and Tasmin looked up at Brida.
The wind howled between them, carrying the distant screams of citizens and the thundering roar of collapsing concrete.
Tasmin slowly lowered her daggers, sliding them back into their sheaths.
She extended her right arm, her fingers curling into a small leather-clad fist.
"A Warrior’s Heart," Tasmin said softly, her voice quiet, shorn of its earlier venom. "Congratulations, Brida. Truly..."
Brida blinked, surprised by the sudden genuine sincerity in the smaller woman’s eyes.
A broad, warm smile touched Brida’s lips as she raised her massive calloused fist, meeting Tasmin’s knuckles in the center of the space.
BUMP!
"Thanks, Tas," Brida rumbled softly. "Means a lot, coming from you."
Tasmin nodded once.
"Now then," Tasmin said smoothly.
GRAB!
Before Brida’s slow and newly enlightened brain could even process the shift in momentum—
Tasmin’s left hand shot downward like a striking viper, clamping with terrifying shadow-reinforced leverage around Brida’s right ankle.
Brida’s amber eyes bugged out of her skull. "Wait... WHAT?!"
Tasmin’s core roared with pure mana as her muscles flared and her shadow wrapped around her own boots to anchor herself directly into the roof’s structural steel.
She planted her heels, spun her entire torso in a violent low-slung three-hundred-and-sixty-degree circle, and launched her massive body straight into the sky.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHA!" Tasmin mocked at the top of her lungs, throwing Brida’s own laugh right back into her face! "MY HAND SLIPPED, TITAN! GO EARN YOUR POINTS!"
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

The roof where they stood completely collapsed beneath the launching force as Brida was hurled across the sky like an eight-ton artillery shell, pushing off with a force that shattered the remaining windows of every building within four hundred yards!
"TASMIN, YOU PETTY LITTLE BIIIIIIIIIIIIIIITCH!" Brida’s roar trailed across the sky like rolling thunder as she soared over the rooftops of Sector Three.
The wind whipped violently against her face, but as she looked down through the smoke, her amber eyes sharpened into cold focus.

Directly below her trajectory, in the wide paved concourse of the High Market Plaza, an entire vanguard of ninety Gore-Hounds and three massive armored Trench-Crushers had completely encircled a terrified crowd of two hundred civilians huddled against the steps of a temple.
’Target acquired,’ Brida thought, her lips curling into a feral bloodthirsty grin.
VUUUUUUUUUM!
Mid-flight, Brida willed her [Warrior’s Heart] back into action!

Her muscles hardened into impenetrable star-slate as her skin took on that deep light-devouring metallic sheen and her eight-foot Titan’s Cleaver swung from her shoulder into both hands, igniting with roaring waves of crimson mana.
"OUT OF THE WAY, UGLY!" Brida bellowed!
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
She landed directly in the center of the monster formation and the concussive impact vaporized sixty feet of paved granite into a crater of white-hot dust.
Before the shockwave could even finish expanding, Brida’s eight-foot cleaver tore through the air in a three-hundred-and-sixty-degree horizontal sweep.
SHRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRK!
The crimson blade cleaved through thirty gore-hounds and the three Trench-Crushers in a single devastating stroke.
SPLAT-BOOM-CRASH!
Massive pressurized geysers of black and crimson blood exploded thirty feet into the air, raining down across the plaza like a slaughterhouse monsoon.
From the rear rank, a massive armored drake... moving at three hundred miles per hour dove straight at Brida’s blind spot with its spiked skull aiming directly for the back of her neck.
Brida didn’t even turn around.
CRUNCH!
The drake’s skull slammed directly into the bare unarmored skin of Brida’s upper shoulder but the monster didn’t pierce her... It didn’t push her forward by an inch either.

The moment the beast struck her titan-hardened flesh, its own momentum violently backfired as its skull caved inward like an egg hitting an iron anvil, its neck snapped into four pieces and its entire body pulverized itself against her shoulder, collapsing into a heap of twitching meat at her heels.
Brida lowered her cleaver, resting the bloody edge against the stones, and turned toward the two hundred weeping and trembling civilians huddled on the temple steps.
She reached up, checked that the yellow poppy was still secure behind her ear, and offered them a massive toothy grin.
"Don’t wet yourselves, folks!" Brida shouted cheerfully, waving her bloody gauntlet toward the sky. "Blessed Land has arrived! Nobody dies on Auntie Brida’s watch!"

Brida lowered her cleaver, resting the bloody edge against the stones, and turned toward the two hundred weeping and trembling civilians huddled on the temple steps.
She reached up, checked that the yellow poppy was still secure behind her ear, and offered them a massive toothy grin.
"Don’t wet yourselves, folks!" Brida shouted cheerfully, waving her bloody gauntlet toward the sky.
"Blessed Land has arrived!
Nobody dies on Auntie Brida’s watch!"

chapters.title: Chapter 625: A Wave [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: FLASH!
High above the plaza, a massive circle of purple starlight flared to life.
Aeliana’s voice echoed down from the clouds.
"Teleport."
VUM-VUM-VUM-VUM!
The two hundred civilians vanished from the temple steps in rapid soft bursts of violet light, swept away into the safety of a nearby barrier.
SWOOSH!
From the shadow of a shattered fruit stall at the edge of the plaza, Tasmin materialized, stepping out of the dark with her daggers already wiped clean.
She walked toward the crater, eyeing the mountain of severed monster parts with a sharp suspicious scowl.
"That was my target sector, brute," Tasmin snapped, crossing her arms. "I had this plaza marked with my eyes before you took flight."

"Your sector?!" Brida gasped, leaning against her cleaver with an offended pout. "I was the one who fell out of the clouds and turned thirty of ’em into sausage meat! Those two hundred saves belong on my tally!"

"You didn’t save them," Tasmin retorted smoothly. "Aeliana extracted them and I was the one who provided the trajectory that landed your fat ass in this courtyard in the first place... Technically, every single kill you just logged is a secondary assist derived from my throw!"

"Assists?!" Brida roared, stepping down to Tasmin until their foreheads practically touched. "There ain’t no assists in a warrior’s tally, you skinny little gremlin! I did the smashing, I get the points!"
"You get nothing but a lecture on basic arithmetic—"
RUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUMBLE!
A sound like an entire ocean collapsing down a flight of concrete stairs suddenly drowned out their bickering.
Tasmin and Brida froze as the air in the plaza, previously dry and thick with desert dust, suddenly became damp.
...Violently damp.
A deafening freight-train roar echoed from the wide boulevard leading down from the grand aqueducts of Sector One.
The ground vibrated with the catastrophic weight of millions of tons of churning high-velocity water.
"What in the hell is that...?" Brida blinked, turning her head toward the avenue.
"Brida..." Tasmin’s voice went completely flat. "Move."
KABOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The stone facades of four commercial buildings at the mouth of the boulevard completely disintegrated as a fifty-foot-tall tidal wave of dark saltwater tore into the plaza like a roaring leviathan.
’Fucking hell!’

Contrary to what it looked like, it wasn’t a flood... Instead it was a pressurized aquatic battering ram. The churning wall of water swept through the streets, carrying shattered cars, uprooted palm trees, and dozens of thrashing drowning monsters in its violent belly.
"FUCK!" Tasmin shrieked.
SPLASH-CRASH!
The wave hit them both.

Brida’s body kept her feet anchored to the stone but the monstrous volume of water swallowed her up to her chin while Tasmin was ripped from her footing, cursing violently as she submerged, her hands clawing through the churning foam until she drove a dagger into the base of a lamppost, hauling her dripping head above the surface with a furious gasp.
COUGH-SPIT!
"WHAT MANIAC DROWNED THE DESERT?!" Brida bellowed, spitting a mouthful of salty foam onto the churning surface, her hair plastered across her eyes.
Tasmin wiped the stinging brine from her golden eyes, looking toward the apex of the fifty-foot wave.
Her jaw dropped.

Standing balanced upon the very crest of the colossal churning tsunami... riding the curling lip of the wave with her boots planted wide on a floating slab of polished marble like an surf-rider was a woman.
She wore a long captain’s coat of deep sea-green wool, unbuttoned to reveal a tight leather cuirass and a bare midriff scarred by old blades.

Her wild ink-black hair whipped violently around a face that radiated intoxicating arrogance while her stormy gray eyes burned with pirate glee as she held a sword of glowing blue alloy... Tidebringer above her head!
Morwenna.
"AHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHA!"
Morwenna’s laughter tore across the flooded plaza like a cannonade.
"COME ON, YOU SALTWATER SCUM!" The pirate queen roared. "IS THAT ALL THE TEETH THE SOVEREIGN REALM CAN MUSTER?! MY GRANDMOTHER SWAM THROUGH COLDER SEAS THAN THIS PUDDLE!"
SHRIIIIIIK-CRACK!
A massive Trench-Kraken erupted from a rift directly in her path with its twelve barbed tentacles whipping forward to drag her under but Morwenna didn’t even drop her center of gravity.
SWOOSH!
She stepped off the marble slab in mid-air but she didn’t fall.
The water beneath her boots rose like living steps, catching her feet as she sprinted up the vertical face of the wave.
"Why don’t you die for me...?!"
Tidebringer began to flow!
With an effortless sequence of Tidal-Blade Arts, she redirected the kraken’s massive momentum straight back through its own rubbery flesh.
SHRIT-SHRIT-SHRIT-SPLAT!
Twelve massive tentacles were severed in the span of half a second.

Before the monster could even screech, Morwenna blurred through its central eye cluster, her blade leaving a five-mile-per-hour pressurized water-vacuum in her wake that violently imploded the kraken’s skull from the inside out.
BOOM!

The massive carcass dissolved into fine black chum, swallowed instantly by the roaring wave and down in the churning water below, Tasmin and Brida hauled themselves onto the steps of a temple, coughing up seawater and glaring up at the pirate queen with expressions of murderous disbelief.
"MORWENNA!" Tasmin screamed, her cloak dripping gallons of salt onto the marble. "WHAT THE HELL ARE YOU DOING?! THERE WERE CIVILIANS DOWN HERE!"
Morwenna landed lightly upon the temple roof twenty feet above them, her sword resting casually against her nape as her stormy gray eyes looked down with a teasing grin.
"Keep your breeches on, Shadow-Girl!" Morwenna called down, flicking a glob of seawater from her thumb. "Look at the water! You think I’m a rookie pirate who drowns her own prize?"
Tasmin blinked, looking down at the swirling floodwaters.
It was true as the citizens caught in the wave weren’t drowning.

Enveloping each human was a gentle semi-translucent bubble of pressurized surface-tension that held them upright, carrying them smoothly along the crest of the floodwaters toward the barriers where Aeliana’s starlight teleportation were waiting to pluck them out of the foam.
As for the monsters caught in that same wave...?

The internal currents within the water were spinning at thousands of revolutions per minute creating high-pressure water-blades that shredded the flesh, bone, and organs of the horrors into unrecognizable pulp before they could ever reach the people.
"Haah..."
Morwenna sheathed her cutlass with a crisp oily click, leaning her forearms against the temple balustrade with a triumphant sneer.

"While you two have been bickering in the dust over a few dozen stragglers..." Morwenna bragged, holding up four fingers, "...I breached the aqueduct gates, flooded the northern area, and flushed four thousand citizens out! Four! Thousand! The prize is mine, girls! You can spend tonight polishing my boots!"
Tasmin’s eye twitched so violently that her vision blurred. "You flooded an entire sector of a capital... for contest points?!"
"Hell yes, I did!" Morwenna laughed unapologetically. "That’s pirate logic! Maximum efficiency, minimum paperwork! Captain is gonna be so damn impressed he’ll actually take my virginity!"
She paused, her stormy eyes turning south toward the distant spires of the Grand Oasis Palace and a small smirk crossed the pirate queen’s lips as her thoughts drifted.

’That overgrown weed Eluned is stationed back with the Captain’s family, isn’t she?’ Morwenna mused, her fingers tapping rhythmically against her cutlass hilt. ’She better have used that little glass camera to snap some pictures of his little sister... If I don’t get to see what Silas’s sisters looks like after all this swimming, I’m going to set fire to her favorite flowerbed.’
Two miles away, beneath the towering living wooden roots that held the shattered thirty-story frame of the Grand Oasis Palace aloft.
The air here remained an oasis of miraculous quiet.
The celestial garden that Eluned had called forth from the cracked asphalt had expanded, carpeting three city blocks in lush velvety grass, blooming blue lotuses, and fragrant white jasmine.
The violent earth-shaking rumbles of the collapsing city were muffled by the dense canopy of ancient roots overhead, reduced to a distant harmless hum.

The last of the ordinary hotel guests and staff had already been ushered through the underground and all that remained within the emerald sanctuary was a small, quiet circle seated upon the soft turf.
Martha sat with her spine straight as an iron rod with her hands folded neatly over her apron, though her eyes never left the girls.

Penelope was curled up beside her unconscious older sister, Harper, gently holding Harper’s limp hand against her cheek, listening with quiet tearful relief to the steady rise and fall of Harper’s breathing.
Kaede sat cross-legged near her four Yamato bodyguards with her chin resting on her palm, her dark eyes wide with fascination.
...And sitting right in the center of the grass, her small knees pulled against her chest, was Lia Graves.
Beside Lia knelt Eluned.
The Former Spirit of the World Tree was speaking in a soft melodious voice with her slender hands weaving small, harmless illusions of golden light in the air to illustrate her words.
Lia listened with her eyes wide, occasionally glancing at the massive, thirty-foot-thick tree roots holding a literal skyscraper above their heads.
"So..." Lia said softly, tilting her head. "You all are... really, really strong, right? Like... stronger than the army?"
Eluned smiled, a gentle radiant curve of her lips that made the jasmine blossoms around them lean slightly toward her light.

"We are strong, Little Sister," Eluned replied, her voice carrying certainty. "Each of us has walked through the fires of the Sovereign Realm... We have faced horrors that would shatter the sanity of ordinary mortals."
She paused, her emerald eyes looking down at Lia with deep, unyielding reverence.

"Yet, our strength is not our own. Everything we are... our blades, our evolution, our purpose was granted to us by Lord Silas. When he arrived in our realm, he did not treat us as expendable tools to be bartered away... He poured his blood, his resources, and his very soul into forging us into an unbreakable family. If we are mountains today, it is because he provided the earth upon which we stand."
Lia stared at her with her lower lip trembling slightly as a strange overwhelming lump formed in her throat.

For years, her big brother had been the tired, quiet boy who came home with oil under his fingernails and bruises across his shoulders, counting Spirit Credits on the kitchen counter to make sure they had enough for winter coal.
To hear him spoken of as a savior... as an emperor whose name brought a beautiful woman to her knees in adoration felt like stepping into an impossible dream.
SCREEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEECH!

A high-altitude sonic roar violently shattered the peaceful quiet of the garden and Lia flinched with Martha instantly rising to her feet as her hands dropped over the girls’ shoulders!𝗳𝚛𝗲𝕖𝚠𝚎𝚋𝗻𝗼𝕧𝗲𝐥.𝚌𝚘𝐦
Dropping out of the bruised purple clouds at a blistering angle was a sleek needle-nosed aircraft.
It was a state-of-the-art executive transport... a forty-meter vessel of gleaming white carbon-titanium that moved with the terrifying agility of a fighter craft.
BZZZZZZZZZT-CRACK!
Enveloping the entire fuselage was a multi-layered, interlocking shield of radiant purple mana runes.

Three descending rift-drakes attempted to intercept the descending craft however the moment their claws struck the purple barrier, the runes violently condensed, transforming into dozens of razor-sharp floating violet energy blades that sliced through the beasts, severing their wings and sending their smoking carcasses spinning down into the empty streets.
WHOOOOOOSH!
The jet’s reverse-thrust vector nozzles fired with an ear-splitting hiss of pressurized plasma.

The craft decelerated from Mach 2 to a dead hover in the span of thirty paces with its magnetic landing gear deploying smoothly as it settled onto the flower-strewn asphalt of the intersection with a soft thud.
CH-H-H-H-H-CLICK!
The primary hydraulic passenger ramp hissed open, dropping down to the grass.
Standing in the pressurized airlock, coughing against the sudden rush of desert heat, was Evelyn.
Her tailored blazer was unbuttoned with her silk blouse slightly rumpled, and clamped firmly between her lips was a thin smoldering cigarette.
’Fuck... we made it... a lot earlier than planned.’
Her dark hair was pulled into a hurried messy bun, and her pale face was flushed though there were dark circles under her eyes.
’I hope Silas is okay, well that meanie is a gold core so naturally he will be... I should stop worrying.’
She took a long sharp drag from the cigarette, exhaled a thick plume of grey smoke into the hot air, and glared down the ramp.

"GET YOUR ASSES IN THE CABIN!" Evelyn yelled, her voice sounding hoarse over the whine of the idling turbines. "NOW! MOVE! I had to personally threaten a flight marshal to clear this descent, and the radar is showing seventy more bogeys dropping from the upper thermosphere! MOVE, PEOPLE!"
