chapters.title: Chapter 626: Number 5 [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Martha didn’t hesitate for half a second.
"Up, children," Martha commanded with authority.

Kenji and the Yamato bodyguards moved instantly, two of them carefully lifting the unconscious Harper onto an emergency stretcher, while the other two formed a tight escort around Penelope and Kaede as they bolted up the ramp into the pressurized interior of the jet.
Lia stood up from the grass with her small hand lingering for a moment against the soft fabric of Eluned’s flowing sleeve.
She stopped at the foot of the ramp, looking back over her shoulder.
Eluned remained standing upon the blooming turf, her silver-green hair drifting in the turbine draft as her emerald eyes watched the little girl with infinite patient gentleness.
She raised her slender hand, offering a soft graceful wave.
"Eluned..." Lia called out, her voice trembling slightly over the engine roar. "Will... will I see you again?"
Eluned’s smile widened, bright and radiant as the morning sun breaking over the mountains.

"Of course you will, Little Sister," Eluned replied softly, her voice carrying clearly through the gale. "I am bound to Lord Silas for an eternity... As long as he walks this earth, my place is at his side. We are family now so you will never be rid of me."
A small genuine smile broke across Lia’s face, it was the first real smile she had worn all day.
"Okay," Lia nodded firmly. "Take care of him... He forgets to eat lunch when he’s busy."
"I shall ensure he is thoroughly nourished," Eluned bowed her head gracefully.
Lia turned and sprinted up the ramp with her small boots disappearing into the warm, illuminated cabin of the jet.
Evelyn remained standing by the hatch, taking another sharp puff from her cigarette as her sharp eyes locked onto the ethereal nature deity standing in the middle of a blooming garden.
’Fuck... I can’t stop myself from asking.’
Evelyn’s brow furrowed slightly, her gaze flicking over the miraculous tree roots holding the skyscraper.
"Is he alive?" Evelyn asked, her voice blunt, direct, and stripped of corporate pretense. "Silas. Is he alright down there?"
Eluned slowly rose to her full height with her expression settling into calm confidence.
"My Lord is whole, Lady Evelyn," Eluned answered smoothly. "He has already severed the primary root of this calamity so proceed with the extraction. I shall ensure your departure is unmolested..."
Evelyn exhaled another stream of smoke, nodded once, and tapped the hydraulic door control. "Don’t let him do anything stupid."
CH-H-H-H-H-CLANK!
The heavy airlock door sealed shut, the locking pins driving home with a heavy pressurized thud.
SCREEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEECH!
Above the garden, the sky darkened once more.

Drawn by the massive heat and mana exhaust of the supersonic turbines, an entire swarm of over eighty winged carrion-horrors and three four-winged wyverns dove from the clouds with their talons outstretched, hurtling toward the climbing jet like a falling iron net.
Inside the cockpit, the pilot shoved the throttles forward and the twin turbines roared with deafening fury as the jet leapt off the pavement, rocketing upward toward the open sky.
Eluned stood alone in the center of the empty street.
"I should help..."
She casually raised her right hand with her index finger pointing straight at the descending swarm and her thumb cocked back like the hammer of a pistol.
Her emerald eyes flashed with cold divine authority as her lips parted.
"Bang."
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A concussive invisible blast of razor-sharp wind mana erupted from the tip of her index finger.

The single burst expanded into an shockwave that tore through three thousand feet of open air as all eighty carrion-horrors and the three colossal wyverns were instantly pulverized into a fine drifting red mist.
’Good luck, Evelyn and thank you for keeping them safe...’

The secondary displacement wave slammed directly into the tail-end of Evelyn’s private jet... not with destructive force, but with a perfectly calibrated push that accelerated the aircraft to Mach 4 in less than half a heartbeat, hurling the transport straight through the upper storm clouds and out of sight beyond the horizon.
The sky fell quiet.
Eluned slowly lowered her hand, letting out a soft delicate sigh that rustled the jasmine blossoms at her feet.
"Achoo!"
She paused, blinking with her nose twitching as she sneezed softly into the silk sleeve of her robe.
She rubbed her nose with the back of her wrist, her emerald eyes narrowing as she looked northward toward the flooded streets of Sector Two.
’Someone’s speaking of me,’ Eluned thought, a sharp haughty pout touching her lips.
Her chin tilted upward as her eyes flashed with disdainful mockery.
’Morwenna. It can only be that uncouth, foul-mouthed pirate...’
Eluned smoothed down her silver skirts, turning her gaze back toward the deep crater where Silas’s mana burned bright.
"Tch," Eluned muttered under her breath, her voice dripping with divine pettiness.
"That virgin."
The sky above Kaldmir was rotting.
A hundred and forty miles north of the smoking crater that had once been the White Citadel of Iunu, the horizon had turned the color of bruised plums and curdled milk.
The dry desert wind that usually blew clean and hot off the Great Dune Sea had died completely, replaced by an unnatural wind.
On the roof of the administrative guildhall in the heart of Kaldmir, a woman knelt on one knee upon the sun-cracked terracotta shingles.
Her long sea-green hair whipped across her face in erratic violent snaps with the strands catching against the dark leather of her high collar.
’Is this what our ancestors faced?’
The thought felt heavy in her chest, settling like lead into the pit of her stomach.

She had read the sanitized histories in the libraries and she had studied the woodblock prints of the First Incursion... The legendary catastrophe thousands of years ago when the sky first tore open and the creatures of the Sovereign Realm had poured into the mortal cradle like ants into honey.
But reading about an apocalypse in a leather-bound folio was a different thing from feeling the tectonic foundations beneath your boots shudder under the weight of a dimensional rupture.
And this... this was only the northern part of Khemet.

A single engine in the south had suffered a catastrophic blowout, and already, across five provincial cities, twenty trade towns, and hundreds of miles of paved desert expressway, reality was fraying at the edges.
SHING-CRACK!

Below her, in the wide cobblestone avenue fronting the fountains, a four-legged bone-stalker... its ribs exposed and its snapping jaw dripping acidic black bile lunged at the entrance of an abandoned textile shop.
Before its claws could scrape the limestone, a flash of pure violent violet light cleaved the gloom.
SPLAT!
A woman clad in layered amethyst silk and lacquered star-iron stepped out of the beast’s blind spot.
Her sickle-curved khopesh, humming with an overcharged frequency of purple lightning, flicked upward in a reverse one-handed draw.
The stroke entered the abomination’s pelvic joint, carved cleanly through its petrified vertebrae, and exited through its opposite clavicle.
BOOM!
The severed halves of the monster hit the stones with two distinct wet thuds before dissolving into black oily steam.
"Haah..."
The green-haired woman above... Lady Sarya, an Awakened Baroness sworn to the defense of Khemet let her violet core mana settle back into her meridians.
Her eyes flashed, the royal purple hue receding as her Hero sheathed her blade with an oily snick.
"Kaldmir is empty, My Lady," the Hero called up, her voice steady and shorn of fear. "The sixth and seventh residential rings are devoid of breath as the streets are dead."
Sarya looked out across the rooftops.
It was true.
A city that had housed three hundred thousand merchants, artisans, and foreign travelers barely two hours ago now stood like an ancient necropolis.
Windows banged loose in the rising draft, banners fluttered from abandoned fruit stalls and half-eaten lunches sat cooling on cafe terraces.
Yet, there were no piles of mangled corpses lining the gutters and there were no rivers of arterial red soaking the dust.
’The World Council actually intervened...’ Sarya thought, her fingers tightening around the edge of the clay parapet.
Usually, when a regional crisis occurred, the Council moved with the agonizing pace of an empire bogged down in tripartite committee hearings, diplomatic clearances, and budget allocations.
By the time a strike team cleared customs, entire places were usually reduced to smoking craters but not today.
The moment the high-altitude satellites confirmed the total vaporization of the Royal Carrier in the southern skies, the Council had executed an emergency override.
Every licensed Lord within three hundred nautical miles had received a direct mandate to their emails stamped with the golden seal of the World King.
And more terrifying than the lords... were the two shadows that had descended directly from the Council’s central sanctum.
Number 9 and Number 5.
Sarya slowly tilted her head back, shielding her eyes against the strange purplish glare of the sky.
It was almost impossible to make out with the naked eye, but two miles above the city, suspended motionless at the edge of the troposphere, was a silhouette.
It was a tall, impossibly broad figure draped in heavy ceremonial robes of leaden gray.
His arms were spread wide to his sides, pointing toward the eastern and western horizons like the arms of a colossal sundial.
His face was hidden behind a featureless porcelain mask etched with nine golden circles.

From his outstretched palms, two undulating ribbons of pale crystalline mana... each ribbon thirty paces wide stretched across the sky for hundreds of miles, following the precise curve of the northern desert perimeter.
’Number 9 is anchoring the whole thing,’ Sarya realized, her skin prickling with cold awe.
The strategy was brutal in its simplicity.
The primary Terrestrial Suppression Engine beneath Iunu’s White Citadel had been completely shattered with its internal mechanisms short-circuited and vaporized by a mysterious entity.
But Khemet was an ancient land.
Across the northern and eastern frontiers, other secondary Sub-Suppression Engines still operated deep within the crust.
They had shuddered during the initial detonation with their conduits groaning under the feedback loop, but their cores had held.
Number 9 was currently weaving those secondary engines together with his own Fifth-Stage mana.
He was raising a continental-scale containment barrier across the entire northern territory.
A dome of glass that would seal Iunu, Kaldmir, and the surrounding wastes into a single isolated kill-box.
Nothing would get out so not a single monster would cross into the populated southern valleys or the coastal trade ports...
Humanity was walling off its own arm to stop the poison from reaching the heart!
CLACK!
A sound echoed from the alleyway directly beneath the guildhall as Sarya looked down.

A family of five... a father carrying a toddler on his shoulders, a mother gripping her daughter’s wrist, and an elderly man limping heavily on a wooden cane sprinted out from the shadow of an apothecary.
They threw open the heavy, reinforced iron hatch of a civil protection shelter set into the foundation stone of the avenue and they scrambled down the dark concrete stairs.
CRACKLE!
The moment the grandfather’s trailing foot cleared the third step, the air inside the stairwell violently warped.
There was a brief high-pitched static discharge like silk tearing across ice accompanied by a flash of pale silver runes that flickered across the concrete threshold.
And then... the stairwell was silent as the five life-signatures simply ceased to exist in Kaldmir.
Sarya’s breath hitched.
’Number 5.’
The Fifth Seat of the World Council which was the architect of the invisible corridors.
It was an incomprehensible feat of space.
Across twelve different cities and thousands of regional bunker access points, every single mortal who stepped below the threshold was being caught in a seamless teleportation spell.

The moment their feet touched the concrete, they were instantly displaced across two hundred miles of physical space, deposited into the guarded reception encampments erected outside the containment perimeter in the southern side of Khemet.

’She is holding thousands of spatial anchors open simultaneously,’ Sarya thought with cold sweat beading beneath her bangs. ’To maintain that many microscopic wormholes without a single one collapsing... how much mana does that woman possess?!’
And yet, despite the awe, a cold gnawing terror lingered behind Sarya’s ribs.
What had killed the Pharaoh-President?
The emergency military bulletins had spoken of "an aerial anomaly of black mineral composition."
...A wave of black sand that had wiped nine armored carriers out of the sky in the span of three heartbeats, followed immediately by the total erasure of the White Citadel.
Black sand.
The legends of Khemet spoke of only one entity associated with that specific light-devouring mineral.
An ancient nameless shadow from the First Dominion that was supposed to have been buried in the deepest reaches of the outer abyss ten thousand years ago.
FWOOSH!
A sudden displacement of air broke her concentration.
An Awakened scout, his light courier plate humming with wind-mana, landed on the parapet ten paces away.
His face was gray beneath his visor, his chest heaving with ragged breaths.

"Baroness Sarya!" he gasped, snapping his knuckles against his gorget. "High Command mandate! Number 9’s containment barrier has achieved sixty percent synchronization and this perimeter will lock permanently in twenty minutes... All units are ordered to conduct one final sweep of their assigned grids and fall back to the central extraction points immediately to move to another location"
Sarya stood tall, snapping a flawless salute.
"Affirmative. Kaldmir’s primary sector is clear..."
The scout nodded, launching himself back into the turbulent sky to relay the order to the outer garrisons.
Sarya turned to her Hero waiting in the courtyard below.

"You heard him," Sarya commanded. "Rendezvous with the other nine at the western gate and comb the perimeter alleys one last time. If there is a single child left shivering in an attic, you find them."
"By your command, My Lady," the purple-haired warrior bowed, dissolving into an electric blur as she sprinted toward the thoroughfares.
Sarya remained on the roof for a moment, her gaze drifting south toward the distant bruised horizon where Iunu lay buried under clouds of ash.

’I wonder what Number 5 is doing right now...’ Sarya mused, her heart aching with quiet sympathy. ’To maintain this continental evacuation... she must be locked in a deep meditative trance inside an armored bunker somewhere, burning her core to ash to save our people.’
Forty miles to the south, high above the burning ruins of Iunu.
"Let me down, Kara White."
The voice was irritated and came from roughly three feet above the smoking canopy of a cedar tree.

"I won’t," Kara White replied with an unrepentant smirk. "Tch. You’re remarkably tiny, aren’t you? What are you, five-foot-two? I’m like five-nine or five-ten, and I’m towering over you even when I’m slouching. Hehe~"

sentences.text: Martha didn’t hesitate for half a second.
"Up, children," Martha commanded with authority.

Kenji and the Yamato bodyguards moved instantly, two of them carefully lifting the unconscious Harper onto an emergency stretcher, while the other two formed a tight escort around Penelope and Kaede as they bolted up the ramp into the pressurized interior of the jet.
Lia stood up from the grass with her small hand lingering for a moment against the soft fabric of Eluned’s flowing sleeve.
She stopped at the foot of the ramp, looking back over her shoulder.
Eluned remained standing upon the blooming turf, her silver-green hair drifting in the turbine draft as her emerald eyes watched the little girl with infinite patient gentleness.
She raised her slender hand, offering a soft graceful wave.
"Eluned..." Lia called out, her voice trembling slightly over the engine roar.
"Will... will I see you again?"
Eluned’s smile widened, bright and radiant as the morning sun breaking over the mountains.
"Of course you will, Little Sister," Eluned replied softly, her voice carrying clearly through the gale.
"I am bound to Lord Silas for an eternity...
As long as he walks this earth, my place is at his side.
We are family now so you will never be rid of me."
A small genuine smile broke across Lia’s face, it was the first real smile she had worn all day.
"Okay," Lia nodded firmly.
"Take care of him...
He forgets to eat lunch when he’s busy."
"I shall ensure he is thoroughly nourished," Eluned bowed her head gracefully.
Lia turned and sprinted up the ramp with her small boots disappearing into the warm, illuminated cabin of the jet.
Evelyn remained standing by the hatch, taking another sharp puff from her cigarette as her sharp eyes locked onto the ethereal nature deity standing in the middle of a blooming garden.
’Fuck...
I can’t stop myself from asking.’
Evelyn’s brow furrowed slightly, her gaze flicking over the miraculous tree roots holding the skyscraper.
"Is he alive?" Evelyn asked, her voice blunt, direct, and stripped of corporate pretense.
"Silas.
Is he alright down there?"
Eluned slowly rose to her full height with her expression settling into calm confidence.
"My Lord is whole, Lady Evelyn," Eluned answered smoothly.
"He has already severed the primary root of this calamity so proceed with the extraction.
I shall ensure your departure is unmolested..."
Evelyn exhaled another stream of smoke, nodded once, and tapped the hydraulic door control.
"Don’t let him do anything stupid."

The heavy airlock door sealed shut, the locking pins driving home with a heavy pressurized thud.

Her emerald eyes flashed with cold divine authority as her lips parted.
"Bang."
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A concussive invisible blast of razor-sharp wind mana erupted from the tip of her index finger.

The single burst expanded into an shockwave that tore through three thousand feet of open air as all eighty carrion-horrors and the three colossal wyverns were instantly pulverized into a fine drifting red mist.
’Good luck, Evelyn and thank you for keeping them safe...’

chapters.title: Chapter 627: Tier 6 [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "Haha. Very funny," Number 5 replied with her voice so dry and flat it could have ignited the desert dust.

The Fifth Seat of the World Council was currently dangling through the freezing five-thousand-foot air like an unruly stray cat, suspended by the collar of her oversized ceremonial robes, which were clamped firmly within Kara’s single muscular right hand.
Number 5 wore a voluminous mantle of deep midnight-violet silk, heavily embroidered with spinning platinum compass-roses along the hems.

Her face was completely hidden behind an ornate half-moon porcelain mask of black and silver that revealed only the sharp line of her chin and a pair of dark unblinking eyes that were currently glaring at Kara with venom.
’Ah, she looks so cute.’
RUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUMBLE!
A violent earth-shaking updraft tore through the sky, causing the air around them to violently rock but it wasn’t because of the wind.
It was because they were standing or rather, Kara was standing, and Number 5 was dangling upon the armored crimson back of dragon.
Talira.
The Crimson Dragon had fully shed her humanoid guise.
She spanned eighty paces from horned snout to barbed tail with her scales burning like polished rubies forged in the core of a star.

Every beat of her massive, bat-like wings displaced hundreds of thousands of cubic feet of air, creating howling horizontal vortexes that shredded the low-altitude clouds and sent smaller rift-beasts tumbling out of the sky like crushed insects.

"Keep your wings level, girl!" Kara called down, tapping the dragon’s spine with her leather boot. "Head straight toward that monstrosity climbing out of the sky! Anything with teeth that enters your flight corridor... delete it!"
"GRAHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH!"
Talira let out a heaven-shattering roar that shook the teeth inside Number 5’s skull.
"BY YOUR WILL, MY LORD!" the dragon’s voice echoed directly into their minds, booming with the joy of a beast finally permitted to hunt without restraint.
’Is it just me or did she learn telepathy too? What a cheat!’
From the left, a swarm of forty six-legged bone-gargoyles dove from a rift with their barbed talons clicking as they converged on the dragon’s flank however Talira didn’t even adjust her rudder.
FWOOSH-CRACK!
With a terrifying snap of her wings, two colossal whirlpools of superheated compressed air exploded outward.

The pressure crushed the lead twenty gargoyles instantly with their stone-and-bone frames imploding into powder before they could get within fifty yards and for the twenty surviving beasts that managed to claw through the gale...?
KRAAAAA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Talira raised her serpentine neck, her throat glowing with an incandescent white-hot radiance that illuminated the dark sky!
She opened her jaws, releasing a torrential three-hundred-foot cone of pure draconic flame.
WHOOOOSH!
The fire was so terrifyingly hot that the oxygen in the surrounding air combusted into an instantaneous vacuum!

The gargoyles were erased at the molecular level with their physical mass vaporized into drifting white sparks before the roaring flame-plume tore through three more rift fissures, searing the edges of space until the rifts themselves hissed and closed shut.
"Good girl," Kara murmured, reaching down with her boot to tap the dragon’s armored crest.
The massive crimson lizard’s snout subtly twitched and beneath her thick ruby scales, a ridiculous flush of pink crept across her nostrils.
"E-Ehehe..." Talira rumbled internally, sounding less like a dragon and more like a pampered guard dog whose head had just been scratched. "It was nothing, My Lord... mere pests..."
Kara gave an amused chuckle, finally swinging her arm inward and dropping the Fifth Seat onto the broad flat ridge of scales between Talira’s shoulder blades.
Number 5 hit the warm scales with a soft rustle of silk, immediately smoothing down the crumpled folds of her robes with her posture stiff as a board as she sat cross-legged, refusing to look up.

"You are thoroughly insufferable, Kara White," Number 5 grumbled behind her porcelain mask. "I am an elder of the World Council... I am not a sack of turnips to be hauled around by the scruff of my neck."

"You looked like a turnip," Kara grinned, resting her right hand on her hip, her dark cloak thrashing wildly in the turbine-like slipstream. "And besides, I’m still thoroughly pissed off at you. What happened to our lovely professional relationship? We walked through the World Vault together, you helped me pick out some exquisite toys, and the very moment we concluded our business... you dumped me straight into the Sector Six slums like a bag of wet laundry!"
Number 5 let out an exhausted suffering breath through her mask.

"We were inside a classified room," Number 5 retorted, her voice dripping with dry disdain. "I fulfilled the World King’s mandate by guiding you through the treasury tiers, however I was under zero administrative obligation to provide a luxury limousine ride back to your private estate... When did equipment retrieval constitute a lifelong bond of friendship?"
"Oh, so we’re strangers now?" Kara scoffed, taking two strides across the dragon’s scales, leaning down until her face was three inches from the porcelain mask.
PINCH!
Kara reached out with two fingers and aggressively pinched the soft, fleshy tip of Number 5’s left ear through the edge of her cowl.
"Isn’t that a remarkably rude way to speak to the person who literally saved your life bare minutes ago?" Kara teased, giving the ear a firm, playful tug.
Number 5’s head snapped sideways with her hands flying up to swat Kara’s fingers away and her porcelain mask tilting with murderous indignation.
Now that Kara could see her face... it seemed the woman got pissed off more quickly.
"You did NOT save my life!" Number 5 hissed through clenched teeth.
Kara crossed her single arm, raising an eyebrow with disbelief.

"Really? Because from where I was standing, a four-legged gore-hound had dropped directly out of an alley roof, was mid-leap toward your delicate little spine, and its teeth were approximately four inches from your jugular when I casually incinerated it with a bolt of magic."

"I was aware of the beast!" Number 5 snarled, her voice pitching up with uncharacteristic frustration. "I was in the middle of executing a continuous high-precision spatial inversion across sixty-four shelters! My sensory field is three hundred miles wide! You think a common trench-hound could sneak past my perception?! I had twelve microscopic spatial blades already calibrated around its throat... The moment its momentum carried it three inches closer, it would have been sliced into carpaccio and then you dropped from the sky, blasted it with fire, and began parading around proclaiming you were my heroic savior!"
"Uh-huh," Kara smirked, sounding unimpressed. "And if we asked the satellites, who does the combat log say struck the killing blow?"
Number 5 went silent with her small hands clenched into tight fists against her silk knees.
She couldn’t argue because nobody would ever believe her.
The entire council would assume she had been cornered like a novice and rescued by the new darling of the Exhibition.
Number 5 let out a sharp bitter scoff, turning her head away to stare out at the burning city, refusing to give Kara the satisfaction of another word.
Kara stood above her with the teasing smirk slowly fading from her lips. Her dark eyes narrowed, drifting over the small, cloaked figure sitting on the dragon’s back.
’It’s just like I thought...’ Silas mused in the quiet fortress of his mind.
Ever since the battle in the deep chamber... ever since he had struck Ititius with those six consecutive soul-reversal strikes, something fundamental had permanently shifted behind his eyes.
He didn’t need to channel mana to see it at all.
If he unfocused his gaze by a fraction of a millimeter... if he pushed his intent beyond the physical world of meat, bone, and cloth... the world peeled away.
He could see the Soul.
He had tried experimenting with it on the flight up from the crater, but he had quickly hit an impenetrable wall.
There were no manuals for this.
In the modern world, cultivation was strictly categorized into physical body, elemental affinities, and territorial domains.
There were no scrolls in the libraries that taught "Soul Magic" and no grandmaster walked the academies offering courses on how to shape the spirit.
’Fuck...’

He was essentially stuck since he had been granted the rare ocular perception to gaze directly into the spiritual architecture of living beings, yet possessed zero methods to manipulate it beyond hitting it with raw Gold Core power.
And looking down at Number 5...
Silas felt a genuine cold prickle of unease crawl across his scalp.
Inside the physical chest of the small, masked woman, there wasn’t a single clean soul-core.
There was a swirling turbulent vortex.

A dozen different spiritual essences... flaring in vivid discordant hues of crimson, emerald, pale gold, and deep violet were revolving around a central, lightless axis like planets caught in the gravitational pull of a dying star.
Each soul carried a distinct resonance, whispering against the spiritual ether with voices that didn’t sound like hers.
’What the hell is she?’ Silas wondered, his pulse hitching. ’That’s not a single human... That’s a walking graveyard of bound spirits.’
Number 5 suddenly flinched.
Her spine stiffened, her masked head whipping around to lock her dark eyes straight onto Kara’s face.

"Stop that," Number 5 said, her voice dropping into a quiet, raspy, and genuinely chilling register. "It feels like you’re peeling the skin off my brain and staring directly into my soul... It is exceptionally grotesque."
Kara blinked, forcing her optical focus back to the physical plane with an innocent breezy shrug.
"Just admiring your lovely posture. You sit like an empress."
Number 5 glared at her through the slit visors of the porcelain mask, her tone hardening into a strict deadly warning.

"Listen to me closely, Kara White," Number 5 murmured. "I do not know what peculiar eye spell you unlocked down in that basement, and frankly, I do not care but do not attempt to pry into the spiritual architecture of high-ranking people... Entities who have crossed the threshold of the Fourth and Fifth Stages possess souls that are not merely dense, they are armed... If you stare too deeply into a being whose spiritual sensitivity exceeds your own, the backlash will crack your core before you can blink. You will invite an exceptionally early grave."
Kara held up her single hand, offering a dry placating chuckle.
"Alright, alright. Message received though I wasn’t staring at your soul or whatever... I just like how small you are."
Yet, Silas filed the warning away in the back of his mind.
’A graveyard of souls,’ he thought. ’I’ll deal with whatever that means later... Right now, we have a bigger carcass to butcher.’
Both women turned their faces toward the heavens as the atmosphere around Talira’s climbing silhouette had grown freezing cold.
Directly ahead, at ten thousand feet of elevation, the primary tear in the sky hung like a bleeding wound across the ceiling of the world.
The edges of the rift were weeping dark purple spatial discharge, vibrating with a sound that made the scales on Talira’s spine rattle.𝕗𝕣𝐞𝐞𝘄𝐞𝚋𝚗𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗹.𝚌𝕠𝚖
And reaching out through the center of that void... was the arm, when Kara had seen it from three miles away, it had looked like a terrifying monolith.
But being seen from two hundred yards away, the scale was mind-shattering...
It was an arm forged entirely from petrified yellowed bone... easily the size of an eight-story residential tenement block.
The wrist was a tangled mass of calcified tendons that creaked like ancient ship timbers as the titanic hand flexed its fingers.

The bone was pitted with hundreds of deep, hollow fissures where thousands of screaming weeping humanoid skulls were embedded directly into the marrow, their empty eye sockets dripping with sickly green ethereal fire.
The fingers... each eighty feet long, tipped with jagged obsidian-like talons were clamped firmly over the outer edge of the dimensional rift, hauling a shadowed shoulder through the tear!
Number 5 stared up at the monstrosity with her posture growing rigid and the casual irritation on her face completely vanishing beneath her mask.
"That entity..." Number 5 whispered, her voice tightening with grim assessment, "...is operating at Tier 6. At the very least."
Kara narrowed her eyes, assessing the oppressive mass of the thing. "Tier 6, huh?"

"It is out of our league," Number 5 stated flatly. "In the classifications of the Sovereign Realm, a Tier 6 monster is a regional catastrophe... It possesses enough mass and power to flatten an entire city like Iunu in an afternoon... Our current priority must be containing the breach, not engaging in suicidal heroics."
Kara let out a soft amused scoff, rolling her right shoulder back.

"Come now, Number 5," Kara smirked, her raspy voice dripping with casual, unbothered arrogance. "Don’t be such a pessimist... I’ve taken down a Tier 5 monster before and that was before I grew my second arm back though I’ve cut it off... A Tier 6 is just a Tier 5 that ate too much calcium. We can take it."

Very funny," Number 5 replied with her voice so dry and flat it could have ignited the desert dust.

The Fifth Seat of the World Council was currently dangling through the freezing five-thousand-foot air like an unruly stray cat, suspended by the collar of her oversized ceremonial robes, which were clamped firmly within Kara’s single muscular right hand.
Number 5 wore a voluminous mantle of deep midnight-violet silk, heavily embroidered with spinning platinum compass-roses along the hems.

Her face was completely hidden behind an ornate half-moon porcelain mask of black and silver that revealed only the sharp line of her chin and a pair of dark unblinking eyes that were currently glaring at Kara with venom.
’Ah, she looks so cute.’

FWOOSH-CRACK!

She opened her jaws, releasing a torrential three-hundred-foot cone of pure draconic flame.
WHOOOOSH!
The fire was so terrifyingly hot that the oxygen in the surrounding air combusted into an instantaneous vacuum!

The gargoyles were erased at the molecular level with their physical mass vaporized into drifting white sparks before the roaring flame-plume tore through three more rift fissures, searing the edges of space until the rifts themselves hissed and closed shut.
"Good girl," Kara murmured, reaching down with her boot to tap the dragon’s armored crest.
The massive crimson lizard’s snout subtly twitched and beneath her thick ruby scales, a ridiculous flush of pink crept across her nostrils.
"E-Ehehe..." Talira rumbled internally, sounding less like a dragon and more like a pampered guard dog whose head had just been scratched.
"It was nothing, My Lord... mere pests..."
Kara gave an amused chuckle, finally swinging her arm inward and dropping the Fifth Seat onto the broad flat ridge of scales between Talira’s shoulder blades.
Number 5 hit the warm scales with a soft rustle of silk, immediately smoothing down the crumpled folds of her robes with her posture stiff as a board as she sat cross-legged, refusing to look up.
"You are thoroughly insufferable, Kara White," Number 5 grumbled behind her porcelain mask.
"I am an elder of the World Council...
I am not a sack of turnips to be hauled around by the scruff of my neck."
"You looked like a turnip," Kara grinned, resting her right hand on her hip, her dark cloak thrashing wildly in the turbine-like slipstream.
"And besides, I’m still thoroughly pissed off at you.
What happened to our lovely professional relationship?

We walked through the World Vault together, you helped me pick out some exquisite toys, and the very moment we concluded our business... you dumped me straight into the Sector Six slums like a bag of wet laundry!"
Number 5 let out an exhausted suffering breath through her mask.
"We were inside a classified room," Number 5 retorted, her voice dripping with dry disdain.
"I fulfilled the World King’s mandate by guiding you through the treasury tiers, however I was under zero administrative obligation to provide a luxury limousine ride back to your private estate...
When did equipment retrieval constitute a lifelong bond of friendship?"
"Oh, so we’re strangers now?" Kara scoffed, taking two strides across the dragon’s scales, leaning down until her face was three inches from the porcelain mask.
PINCH!
Kara reached out with two fingers and aggressively pinched the soft, fleshy tip of Number 5’s left ear through the edge of her cowl.
"Isn’t that a remarkably rude way to speak to the person who literally saved your life bare minutes ago?" Kara teased, giving the ear a firm, playful tug.
Number 5’s head snapped sideways with her hands flying up to swat Kara’s fingers away and her porcelain mask tilting with murderous indignation.
Now that Kara could see her face... it seemed the woman got pissed off more quickly.
"You did NOT save my life!" Number 5 hissed through clenched teeth.
Kara crossed her single arm, raising an eyebrow with disbelief.
"Really?

Because from where I was standing, a four-legged gore-hound had dropped directly out of an alley roof, was mid-leap toward your delicate little spine, and its teeth were approximately four inches from your jugular when I casually incinerated it with a bolt of magic."
"I was aware of the beast!" Number 5 snarled, her voice pitching up with uncharacteristic frustration.
"I was in the middle of executing a continuous high-precision spatial inversion across sixty-four shelters!
My sensory field is three hundred miles wide!
You think a common trench-hound could sneak past my perception?!
I had twelve microscopic spatial blades already calibrated around its throat...

The moment its momentum carried it three inches closer, it would have been sliced into carpaccio and then you dropped from the sky, blasted it with fire, and began parading around proclaiming you were my heroic savior!"

chapters.title: Chapter 628: Domain [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Talira let out an ear-splitting vibrating roar of complete agreement with her serpentine neck arching proudly toward the sky.
"HEAR THE TRUTH OF MY LORD!" Talira bellowed mentally. "WITH MY FLAMES AND MY LORD’S WILL, WE SHALL CLEAVE THIS SKELETAL VERMIN INTO ASH AND TREAD UPON ITS BONES!"
Number 5 slowly raised her head, staring at the two of them with an expression of exhausted disbelief.

"Are you two genuinely insane?" Number 5 deadpanned. "I am an elder of the World Council... My personal Core Advancement is significantly higher than yours, Kara White. I have stood upon the battlefields of the Sovereign Realm and I am telling you, with full certainty, that even I could not defeat that monstrosity in direct combat right now."
Kara gave her a sharp side-eyed smirk.
"You mean..." Kara corrected smoothly, "...you’re higher than me in Core Advancement, but still fundamentally weaker in a real fistfight?"
Number 5 choked.
Behind the porcelain mask, she violently coughed into her silk sleeve with her head snapping to the side as her ears flushed a furious indignant pink.

"That is... that is beside the point!" Number 5 spluttered, waving her hands defensively. "I am a specialist! My affinities are dedicated to macro-scale spatial teleportation and defense! I do not engage in crude, vulgar tavern-brawls like a mercenary!"
"Uh-huh," Kara teased. "So you’re weaker... Got it."

"I AM NOT WEAKER!" Number 5 hissed, her fingers twitching with the sudden urge to open a spatial tear beneath Kara’s boots and drop her into a septic tank. "It is not a matter of raw output! It is a matter of the fundamental laws that govern creatures that have reached the peak of Tier 5 and crossed into Tier 6!"
Kara raised an eyebrow, sensing the genuine technical weight behind the woman’s words.
"And what laws would those be?"
Before Number 5 could speak—
CRACK!
The sound wasn’t an explosion or a spell... Instead, it was the dry terrifying sound of a match being struck in an empty pitch-black room.
Suddenly... the world vanished.
The clouds, the desert sun, the distant burning spires of Iunu... all of it was instantly severed from their vision as the sky turned into an infinite suffocating expanse of cold lightless black.
And then... the fire ignited.
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
From the empty void, thousands of ethereal pale-green flames burst to life, floating weightlessly across miles of space like lanterns in an ancient graveyard.
The flames didn’t emit heat, instead tthey radiated a bone-chilling arctic frost that instantly coated Talira’s ruby scales in thick white ice.
High above them, floating at the center of the green fires, the colossal skeletal hand was fully revealed.
Yet, bizarrely... it didn’t seem to be eighty yards away anymore.

Through some terrifying warped perspective of compressed space, the titanic bone arm seemed to hover simultaneously miles away on the horizon and mere inches above their heads, its hollow eye sockets watching them with uncaring malice.

From the dark beneath the floating lanterns, an endless chittering ocean of skeletal horrors... winged bone-drakes, floating ribs crowned with snapping jaws, and serpentine centipedes forged from human spines began to drag themselves out of the shadows, encircling the dragon from every angle.
Number 5’s posture went completely rigid as her voice dropped into a hollow trembling whisper.
"A Domain..." she breathed, the porcelain mask casting long pale shadows across her collar. "A proper... completed Domain."
Kara stood firm on Talira’s back with her single hand dropping to the hilt of the invisible blade resting within her core and her senses flaring at maximum alert.
"Explain. Fast."

"Monsters are different from humans," Number 5 spoke rapidly, her eyes darting across the green lanterns. "In mortal cultivation, lords only begin to touch the concept of a domain at the peak of the Fourth Stage... It is rare, agonizing to manifest, and notoriously unstable. True, fluid mastery of a domain is reserved for the Fifth Stage."
She pointed a trembling finger toward the massive skeletal arm.

"But horrors of the Sovereign Realm do not cultivate like humans! They do not weave spells or balance their meridians... For a monster, their domain is an innate biological organ! At the peak of Tier 5, the seed of the domain awakens within their marrow and the moment they cross the threshold of Tier 6... their domain becomes a reality!"
Kara looked at Number 5, her brow furrowing with sharp impatience.
"And you? You’re a Council elder! Don’t you have a domain of your own?! Can’t you just deploy yours and cancel this out?!"
Number 5 grimaced behind her mask, her hands knotting into her silk sleeves.
"It’s... it is complicated! My domain requires three synchronized anchoring pylons to stabilize its boundary! I cannot deploy it from the back of a flying lizard in the middle of a free-fall..."
SCREEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEECH!
The chittering horde of skeletal monstrosities lunged.
Dozens of winged bone-drakes dove from the green flames with their jaws snapping like bear traps.
"BEGONE, FILTH!" Talira roared.
CRACKLE-BOOM!
The Ancient Crimson Dragon’s body violently discharged a massive spherical web of blinding high-powered White Draconic Lightning...
WHOOSH!
The brilliant white arcs tore through the void, vaporizing twenty bone-drakes into fine powdery ash.
"Hmmmmghh!"
Talira reared her head, channeling the remaining voltage into a massive concentrated lance of white lightning aimed directly at the center of the colossal skeletal hand.
SHRRRRK!
The white bolt struck the petrified bone and yet... The lightning didn’t detonate.
The moment the brilliant white plasma touched the surface of the bone with the green lanterns floating in the air flared with violent, unnatural luminescence.
The very laws of reality within the domain violently bent...
HISSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSS!

The pure cleansing white lightning began to vanish as its elemental composition was violently inverted, within seconds, the brilliant white turned into a thick nauseating torrent of pale-green necrotic fire.
WHOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
The reflected necrotic flames violently rebounded along their original trajectory, rocketing straight back toward Talira’s chest at twice their initial speed.
"WHAT?!" Talira gasped mentally.
SWOOSH!
The dragon rolled her massive bulk in mid-air, banking sharply to the right.
The green flames grazed her underbelly, searing through her thick ruby scales, turning three plates of armor into crumbling brittle green glass with a sickening sizzling hiss.
"RAAHHHHHHHHHHHHHH!"

Talira shrieked in genuine pain, her flight faltering for a terrifying half-second as more green fireballs began condensing around the floating skulls, preparing to unleash a continuous inescapable carpet-bombing.
Kara gritted her teeth with her Gold Core roaring as she caught her balance on the tilting spine.

’Domains...’ Silas thought, his mind racing through the variables like an overcharged supercomputer. ’Inside another entity’s completed domain, the host dictates the physical constants... An attack directed at the master doesn’t just miss, it gets rewritten into the master’s elemental authority!’

More green fireballs erupted from the dark as Talira banked, dove, and spun through the void with her massive wings working frantically as she dodged barrages of inverted plasma, but the safe airspace was shrinking by the millisecond.
Kara snapped her head around, glaring down at the masked woman crouching on the dragon’s back.
"Can we break out?!" Kara barked over the roaring flames. "Can you get us through the wall?!"
Number 5 looked up, her porcelain mask gleaming in the green fire.

"I can," Number 5 replied, her voice remarkably calm. "I am the Fifth Seat of the World Council... A domain can rewrite physics, but it cannot sever the fundamental spatial coordinate network so I can translocate us outside the boundary whenever you wish."
Kara froze.

Her dark eyes narrowed into a lethal murderous glare as she stared at the masked woman for two full seconds while Talira executed a near-vertical barrel roll to avoid being cleaved in half by a flying rib-blade.

"You..." Kara snarled, her voice dropping into a dangerous, terrifying growl. "...you’ve been sitting there watching us get turned into barbecue, knowing full well you could have popped us out of this deathtrap at any second?!"
"You didn’t ask," Number 5 replied with infuriating, bureaucratic precision. "You were busy lecturing me about your superior fist-fighting capabilities..."
"DO IT NOW, YOU DAMN WITCH!" Kara roared!
Above them, forty massive green fireballs converged into a single, colossal sun of necrotic plasma, hurtling straight down toward Talira’s skull!
Number 5 sighed.
She casually raised her right index finger, tapping the air with the tip of her manicured nail.
CHIME! VUM!
The green sun slammed down.
KABOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The massive explosion detonated across empty air with the concussive shockwave rippling through the void without touching a single scale.
POP!
The freezing natural air of the stratosphere rushed back into their lungs as the sky was blue-gray again.
The soot, the wind, and the distant roar of Iunu returned in a sudden, overwhelming crash as Talira, Kara, and Number 5 materialized three hundred yards above the primary rift fissure.
Looking down from their new vantage point, Kara’s jaw tightened.

Suspended in the sky directly below them, anchored to the dimensional tear, was a colossal and perfectly spherical orb... easily two miles in diameter, forged from impenetrable black-and-green spatial glass.

Inside that translucent orb, the green lanterns and the trapped skeletal hordes were visible, swirling like fish in a poisoned bowl and protruding from the bottom of that massive sphere, still gripping the mortal air, was the petrified bone hand of the Tier 6 abomination.𝙛𝒓𝓮𝙚𝔀𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝓵.𝙘𝒐𝒎
Kara didn’t wait.

"Talira!" Kara yelled, stepping to the very edge of the dragon’s snout. "The moment I jump, you hit that sphere from the outside! Pour every single scrap of white lightning you possess directly into the seam and crack the shell!"
Talira roared, her ruby crest flaring with blinding electricity.
"UNDERSTOOD, MY LORD!"
Kara bent her knees.
’I have an idea,’ Silas thought, his blood singing with the cold clarity of an all-or-nothing gamble.

’That thing is too massive to cross the threshold in one go... That’s why only its arm is through! It’s climbing through the dimensional throat like a fat rat stuck in a drainpipe! If I sever the anchor... if I break the limb that’s holding the gate open...’
BOOM!
Kara launched herself off the dragon’s snout but she didn’t fall.
With an explosive roar of wind mana beneath her boots, she accelerated downward like an artillery shell, rocketing toward the colossal two-mile domain orb at four hundred miles per hour.
Above her...
KRA-KRA-KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

Talira unleashed the full unbridled fury of her draconic lineage as a colossal pillar of pure white lightning... forty paces thick crashed down from the heavens, slamming directly into the upper apex of the green domain orb.
CRACK-SHATTER!
The domain was absolute against attacks from within but against a high-tier assault from an Ancient Dragon from the outside...? The glass simply cracked.
TC! TC! TC!
A massive jagged fissure tore across the black-and-green surface, throwing showers of unstable spatial sparks into the slipstream AS Kara plummeted toward that exact fissure.
Her single right hand reached across her chest with her fingers clawing inward toward the center of her sternum.
’Come forth.’
VUUUUUM!
From the spiritual depths of Silas’s soul... a golden radiance erupted.
SHING!
She drew it.
The Dawn Blade... The sacred blade of the Second King...

The moment the three-foot blade cleared Kara’s chest, the gray, bruised sky above Iunu was brilliantly banished as a column of pure dawn sunlight punched through the clouds, bathing the falling woman in a halo of blinding gold.
’What a weird blade...’
The blade hummed with a terrifying vibration that made the air itself bow in reverence.
’You are the blade of the Second King, right?’ Silas thought, pouring every single drop of his Gold Core mana into the blade’s runes.
’The blade that cut through the rift during the First Cleansing, according to Number 5... If you could sever the dark then... you can sever this bone today!’
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
Kara channeled the wind as she wrapped the golden blade in three vortexes of hyper-compressed wind-shears, driving her terminal velocity past Mach 3.
’Thank God I have 30,000 points of mana...’
She could spam this shit for as long as she wanted... The air in front of her compressed into a visible cone-shaped shockwave that glowed cherry-red from atmospheric friction.
Kara locked her eyes onto the jagged crack in the domain orb, aligning her trajectory directly with the eighty-foot bone wrist of the titanic skeletal hand.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Kara struck.
The Dawn Blade, blazing with power of her compressed golden mana, cleaved clean through the outer glass of the two-mile domain orb like an incandescent scalpel slicing through a soap bubble.
SHRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRK!
She tore through the interior void!

sentences.text: Talira let out an ear-splitting vibrating roar of complete agreement with her serpentine neck arching proudly toward the sky.
"HEAR THE TRUTH OF MY LORD!" Talira bellowed mentally.
"WITH MY FLAMES AND MY LORD’S WILL, WE SHALL CLEAVE THIS SKELETAL VERMIN INTO ASH AND TREAD UPON ITS BONES!"
Number 5 slowly raised her head, staring at the two of them with an expression of exhausted disbelief.
"Are you two genuinely insane?" Number 5 deadpanned.
"I am an elder of the World Council...
My personal Core Advancement is significantly higher than yours, Kara White.
I have stood upon the battlefields of the Sovereign Realm and I am telling you, with full certainty, that even I could not defeat that monstrosity in direct combat right now."
Kara gave her a sharp side-eyed smirk.
"You mean..." Kara corrected smoothly, "...you’re higher than me in Core Advancement, but still fundamentally weaker in a real fistfight?"
Number 5 choked.
Behind the porcelain mask, she violently coughed into her silk sleeve with her head snapping to the side as her ears flushed a furious indignant pink.
"That is... that is beside the point!" Number 5 spluttered, waving her hands defensively.
"I am a specialist!
My affinities are dedicated to macro-scale spatial teleportation and defense!
I do not engage in crude, vulgar tavern-brawls like a mercenary!"
"Uh-huh," Kara teased.
"So you’re weaker...
Got it."
"I AM NOT WEAKER!" Number 5 hissed, her fingers twitching with the sudden urge to open a spatial tear beneath Kara’s boots and drop her into a septic tank.
"It is not a matter of raw output!
It is a matter of the fundamental laws that govern creatures that have reached the peak of Tier 5 and crossed into Tier 6!"
Kara raised an eyebrow, sensing the genuine technical weight behind the woman’s words.
"And what laws would those be?"
Before Number 5 could speak—
CRACK!
The sound wasn’t an explosion or a spell...
Instead, it was the dry terrifying sound of a match being struck in an empty pitch-black room.
Suddenly... the world vanished.
The clouds, the desert sun, the distant burning spires of Iunu... all of it was instantly severed from their vision as the sky turned into an infinite suffocating expanse of cold lightless black.
And then... the fire ignited.
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
From the empty void, thousands of ethereal pale-green flames burst to life, floating weightlessly across miles of space like lanterns in an ancient graveyard.
The flames didn’t emit heat, instead tthey radiated a bone-chilling arctic frost that instantly coated Talira’s ruby scales in thick white ice.
High above them, floating at the center of the green fires, the colossal skeletal hand was fully revealed.
Yet, bizarrely... it didn’t seem to be eighty yards away anymore.

Through some terrifying warped perspective of compressed space, the titanic bone arm seemed to hover simultaneously miles away on the horizon and mere inches above their heads, its hollow eye sockets watching them with uncaring malice.

From the dark beneath the floating lanterns, an endless chittering ocean of skeletal horrors... winged bone-drakes, floating ribs crowned with snapping jaws, and serpentine centipedes forged from human spines began to drag themselves out of the shadows, encircling the dragon from every angle.
Number 5’s posture went completely rigid as her voice dropped into a hollow trembling whisper.
"A Domain..." she breathed, the porcelain mask casting long pale shadows across her collar.
"A proper... completed Domain."
Kara stood firm on Talira’s back with her single hand dropping to the hilt of the invisible blade resting within her core and her senses flaring at maximum alert.
"Explain.
Fast."
"Monsters are different from humans," Number 5 spoke rapidly, her eyes darting across the green lanterns.
"In mortal cultivation, lords only begin to touch the concept of a domain at the peak of the Fourth Stage...
It is rare, agonizing to manifest, and notoriously unstable.
True, fluid mastery of a domain is reserved for the Fifth Stage."
She pointed a trembling finger toward the massive skeletal arm.
"But horrors of the Sovereign Realm do not cultivate like humans!
They do not weave spells or balance their meridians...
For a monster, their domain is an innate biological organ!
At the peak of Tier 5, the seed of the domain awakens within their marrow and the moment they cross the threshold of Tier 6... their domain becomes a reality!"
Kara looked at Number 5, her brow furrowing with sharp impatience.
"And you?
You’re a Council elder!
Don’t you have a domain of your own?!
Can’t you just deploy yours and cancel this out?!"
Number 5 grimaced behind her mask, her hands knotting into her silk sleeves.
"It’s... it is complicated!
My domain requires three synchronized anchoring pylons to stabilize its boundary!
I cannot deploy it from the back of a flying lizard in the middle of a free-fall..."
SCREEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEECH!
The chittering horde of skeletal monstrosities lunged.
Dozens of winged bone-drakes dove from the green flames with their jaws snapping like bear traps.
"BEGONE, FILTH!" Talira roared.
CRACKLE-BOOM!
The Ancient Crimson Dragon’s body violently discharged a massive spherical web of blinding high-powered White Draconic Lightning...
WHOOSH!
The brilliant white arcs tore through the void, vaporizing twenty bone-drakes into fine powdery ash.
"Hmmmmghh!"
Talira reared her head, channeling the remaining voltage into a massive concentrated lance of white lightning aimed directly at the center of the colossal skeletal hand.
SHRRRRK!
The white bolt struck the petrified bone and yet...
The lightning didn’t detonate.
The moment the brilliant white plasma touched the surface of the bone with the green lanterns floating in the air flared with violent, unnatural luminescence.
The very laws of reality within the domain violently bent...
HISSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSS!

The pure cleansing white lightning began to vanish as its elemental composition was violently inverted, within seconds, the brilliant white turned into a thick nauseating torrent of pale-green necrotic fire.
WHOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
The reflected necrotic flames violently rebounded along their original trajectory, rocketing straight back toward Talira’s chest at twice their initial speed.
"WHAT?!" Talira gasped mentally.
SWOOSH!
The dragon rolled her massive bulk in mid-air, banking sharply to the right.
The green flames grazed her underbelly, searing through her thick ruby scales, turning three plates of armor into crumbling brittle green glass with a sickening sizzling hiss.
"RAAHHHHHHHHHHHHHH!"

Talira shrieked in genuine pain, her flight faltering for a terrifying half-second as more green fireballs began condensing around the floating skulls, preparing to unleash a continuous inescapable carpet-bombing.
Kara gritted her teeth with her Gold Core roaring as she caught her balance on the tilting spine.
’Domains...’ Silas thought, his mind racing through the variables like an overcharged supercomputer. ’Inside another entity’s completed domain, the host dictates the physical constants...
An attack directed at the master doesn’t just miss, it gets rewritten into the master’s elemental authority!’

More green fireballs erupted from the dark as Talira banked, dove, and spun through the void with her massive wings working frantically as she dodged barrages of inverted plasma, but the safe airspace was shrinking by the millisecond.
Kara snapped her head around, glaring down at the masked woman crouching on the dragon’s back.
"Can we break out?!" Kara barked over the roaring flames.
"Can you get us through the wall?!"
Number 5 looked up, her porcelain mask gleaming in the green fire.
"I can," Number 5 replied, her voice remarkably calm.
"I am the Fifth Seat of the World Council...
A domain can rewrite physics, but it cannot sever the fundamental spatial coordinate network so I can translocate us outside the boundary whenever you wish."
Kara froze.

Her dark eyes narrowed into a lethal murderous glare as she stared at the masked woman for two full seconds while Talira executed a near-vertical barrel roll to avoid being cleaved in half by a flying rib-blade.
"You..." Kara snarled, her voice dropping into a dangerous, terrifying growl.
"...you’ve been sitting there watching us get turned into barbecue, knowing full well you could have popped us out of this deathtrap at any second?!"
"You didn’t ask," Number 5 replied with infuriating, bureaucratic precision.
"You were busy lecturing me about your superior fist-fighting capabilities..."
"DO IT NOW, YOU DAMN WITCH!" Kara roared!
Above them, forty massive green fireballs converged into a single, colossal sun of necrotic plasma, hurtling straight down toward Talira’s skull!
Number 5 sighed.
She casually raised her right index finger, tapping the air with the tip of her manicured nail.
CHIME!
VUM!
The green sun slammed down.
KABOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The massive explosion detonated across empty air with the concussive shockwave rippling through the void without touching a single scale.
POP!
The freezing natural air of the stratosphere rushed back into their lungs as the sky was blue-gray again.
The soot, the wind, and the distant roar of Iunu returned in a sudden, overwhelming crash as Talira, Kara, and Number 5 materialized three hundred yards above the primary rift fissure.
Looking down from their new vantage point, Kara’s jaw tightened.

Suspended in the sky directly below them, anchored to the dimensional tear, was a colossal and perfectly spherical orb... easily two miles in diameter, forged from impenetrable black-and-green spatial glass.

Inside that translucent orb, the green lanterns and the trapped skeletal hordes were visible, swirling like fish in a poisoned bowl and protruding from the bottom of that massive sphere, still gripping the mortal air, was the petrified bone hand of the Tier 6 abomination.𝙛𝒓𝓮𝙚𝔀𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝓵.𝙘𝒐𝒎
Kara didn’t wait.
"Talira!" Kara yelled, stepping to the very edge of the dragon’s snout.
"The moment I jump, you hit that sphere from the outside!
Pour every single scrap of white lightning you possess directly into the seam and crack the shell!"
Talira roared, her ruby crest flaring with blinding electricity.
"UNDERSTOOD, MY LORD!"
Kara bent her knees.
’I have an idea,’ Silas thought, his blood singing with the cold clarity of an all-or-nothing gamble.
’That thing is too massive to cross the threshold in one go...
That’s why only its arm is through!
It’s climbing through the dimensional throat like a fat rat stuck in a drainpipe!
If I sever the anchor... if I break the limb that’s holding the gate open...’
BOOM!
Kara launched herself off the dragon’s snout but she didn’t fall.
With an explosive roar of wind mana beneath her boots, she accelerated downward like an artillery shell, rocketing toward the colossal two-mile domain orb at four hundred miles per hour.
Above her...
KRA-KRA-KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

Talira unleashed the full unbridled fury of her draconic lineage as a colossal pillar of pure white lightning... forty paces thick crashed down from the heavens, slamming directly into the upper apex of the green domain orb.
CRACK-SHATTER!
The domain was absolute against attacks from within but against a high-tier assault from an Ancient Dragon from the outside...?
The glass simply cracked.
TC!
TC!
TC!
A massive jagged fissure tore across the black-and-green surface, throwing showers of unstable spatial sparks into the slipstream AS Kara plummeted toward that exact fissure.
Her single right hand reached across her chest with her fingers clawing inward toward the center of her sternum.
’Come forth.’
VUUUUUM!
From the spiritual depths of Silas’s soul... a golden radiance erupted.
SHING!
She drew it.
The Dawn Blade...
The sacred blade of the Second King...

The moment the three-foot blade cleared Kara’s chest, the gray, bruised sky above Iunu was brilliantly banished as a column of pure dawn sunlight punched through the clouds, bathing the falling woman in a halo of blinding gold.
’What a weird blade...’
The blade hummed with a terrifying vibration that made the air itself bow in reverence.
’You are the blade of the Second King, right?’ Silas thought, pouring every single drop of his Gold Core mana into the blade’s runes.
’The blade that cut through the rift during the First Cleansing, according to Number 5...
If you could sever the dark then... you can sever this bone today!’
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
Kara channeled the wind as she wrapped the golden blade in three vortexes of hyper-compressed wind-shears, driving her terminal velocity past Mach 3.
’Thank God I have 30,000 points of mana...’
She could spam this shit for as long as she wanted...
The air in front of her compressed into a visible cone-shaped shockwave that glowed cherry-red from atmospheric friction.
Kara locked her eyes onto the jagged crack in the domain orb, aligning her trajectory directly with the eighty-foot bone wrist of the titanic skeletal hand.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Kara struck.
The Dawn Blade, blazing with power of her compressed golden mana, cleaved clean through the outer glass of the two-mile domain orb like an incandescent scalpel slicing through a soap bubble.
SHRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRK!
She tore through the interior void!

chapters.title: Chapter 629: The System Wants To Be Rich Too [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She appeared directly at the junction of the eighty-foot skeletal wrist an the titanic bone, dense enough to withstand high grade artillery, met the edge of the Second King’s steel.
...There was no resistance.

The thousands of screaming humanoid skulls embedded in the bone didn’t even have time to shriek as the primordial dawn light bypassed their necrotic enchantments, severing the atomic bonds of the petrified marrow, carving through the eighty-foot wrist in a horizontal flash of golden execution.
FLASH!
Kara burst out through the opposite side of the two-mile sphere, tumbling through the open air three thousand feet below the tear!
Behind her... reality unraveled.
CRACK-CRACK-CRACK-SHATTER!

The colossal two-mile domain orb violently imploded with the black-and-green glass disintegrated into millions of harmless, drifting spatial motes that vanished into the wind and as for the colossal tenement-block-sized skeletal hand...
SNAP!
The severed joint gave way.
The colossal hand which was cut clean at the wrist lost its grip on the edge of the dimensional rift!
CREEEEEEAK-GROAN!
A deafening roar of pure baffled agony echoed from the depths of the Sovereign Realm behind the tear as the titanic armless shoulder was violently sucked backward into the lightless void.
POP!
Without the physical anchor of the hand holding the dimensional fabric open...

The wide rift violently contracted and like an elastic band snapping shut, the colossal tear in the sky sealed itself completely, smoothing over until the upper thermosphere was once again empty and blue.
The severed hand plummeted into the clouds below and the sky fell dead silent.
WHOOSH!
Kara was free-falling.
Her long midnight-blue cloak whipped violently against her back with her wild black hair thrashing in her face as she tumbled through the empty air at two hundred miles per hour.
She held the glowing Dawn Blade loosely in her hand, looking up at the blue sky where a wide rift and an apocalyptic Tier 6 abomination had been threatening the world bare heartbeats ago.
Kara blinked once and then she blinked twice.
A look of bewildered shock spread across her face.
"What the fuck..." Kara muttered into the falling wind, her voice cracking with pure disbelief.
"...that actually worked?"
The freezing draft at seven thousand feet tore through the fabric of Kara White’s unbuttoned midnight-blue traveler’s mantle, snapping the wool like the sail of a dying galleon.
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
The woman was in a dead-weight freefall.

The sky above Iunu, purged of the dimensional tear by the sudden, violent retraction of the severed arm, had collapsed back into an eerie bruised dome of leaden purple and ash-gray clouds though the horizon was still a jagged ring of distant, burning spires and billowing columns of black industrial smoke, but the monstrous cosmic eye that had threatened to swallow the sky was gone.
In Kara’s right palm, the Dawn Blade felt... ordinary.
It had no humming aura now as it radiated none of that heaven-shattering room-clearing solar radiance that had bleached the stratosphere in pure gold bare heartbeats ago.
’It feels normal...’

Resting against her calloused leather glove, it possessed the dull balanced heft of a standard three-foot imperial sidearm forged from unpolished star-iron... neither hot nor cold with its runic grooves sitting dormant and dark like dry irrigation ditches.
’This really is an incomprehensibly bizarre piece of steel,’ Kara mused internally, her dark eyes squinting through the rushing air as her hair whipped wildly across her eyelashes.
When she had channeled her Gold Core into the pommel... forcing every cubic millimeter of her compressed mana down through the hilt, the blade hadn’t resisted at all.
It hadn’t heated up, it hadn’t warped under the strain, and it certainly hadn’t leaked shockwaves into her wrist.

It had simply absorbed thousands of units of output in a single seond, converted the entire load into a razor-thin filament of conceptual severing, and cleaved clean through eighty linear feet of petrified skull-encrusted necrotic bone as though she were pulling a heated copper wire through cold lard.
And speaking of that ungodly limb...
THUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
Two thousand feet below Kara, the severed hand of the titan finally met the earth.
The petrified, eight-story skeletal fist... weighing hundreds of thousands of tons slammed into the northern fringe of the High Market District like an iron asteroid.

The shockwave traveled through the bedrock with the roar of a collapsing mountain range as three multi-tier warehouses, an ancient aqueduct viaduct, and an entire city block of abandoned limestone tenements simply ceased to exist in their vertical configurations, crushed beneath forty million pounds of calcified bone and displaced foundation shale.

A massive circular mushroom plume of pulverized masonry and blinding white bone-dust exploded outward, scouring the surrounding streets and rattling the teeth in Kara’s skull even from her vantage point high in the clouds.

’Well,’ Kara grimaced, her jaw tightening as she watched the dust ring expand across the ruins, ’at the very least, the immediate extinction-level crisis is resolved so nobody is getting crushed by an active fifty-foot claw anymore.’
Yet, as she stared down at the cratered monument of pale bone resting among the ruins, a prickle of cold hair-raising intuition brushed against Kara’s spine.
That arm hadn’t merely been a heavy piece of meat.

The atmospheric pressure around the impact zone had plummeted by twelve millibars and the lingering necrotic chill radiating from the marrow was so intense that the surrounding concrete foundations were actively frosting over with crystalline pale-green frost.
’A limb of that caliber doesn’t just wander out of a common rift,’ Kara thought, her eyes narrowing into cold slits. ’System... wait. Give me more information on what the hell that th—’
Her mental query was clumsy.
With her left arm now fully functional and unpinned, Kara reached instinctively into the empty air before her face, flicking her fingers in a reflexive swipe to clear the visual feed.
BZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZT!
She accidentally clipped the edge of his dormant status icon, violently uncoupling the silent notification damper she had done so for quite a long time.
’Fuck...’
In less than a few seconds, the physical sky vanished behind an avalanche of blinding translucent blue holographic tabs that slammed directly into her eyes with the subtlety of a collapsing bookcase.
PING! PING! PING! PING! PING!
[TASMIN HAS ENGAGED IN CONTINUOUS COMBAT AND IS NEARING ADVANCEMENT.]
[TASMIN HAS REACHED THE SECOND STAGE OF SHADOW HEART!]
TASMIN HAS SEVERED 12X TIER 3 ABYSSAL SKYSTRIKERS. REWARD: +480 UP!]
[HERO: BRIDA HAS EXECUTED TITAN-CRUSH COUNTER. REWARD: +20 UP!]
[HERO: FENNA HAS ELIMINATED 1X MUTATED SCOUT. REWARD: +2 UP!]
[HERO: MORWENNA HAS INITIATED CONTINUOUS AQUATIC MASS-PURGE... 412X KILLS REGISTERED.]
[YOU HAVE GAINED 2,000 UP!]
[YOU HAVE GAINED 1,450 UP!]
[YOU HAVE GAINED 3,800 UP!]
The blue windows stacked three feet deep before her eyes, blinking, vibrating, and scrolling text at roughly four hundred lines per second.

The overload was so much that Kara literally lost her peripheral vision mid-freefall, tumbling blindly through a cloud bank with tabs advertising dead bone-crawlers and displaced water-sprites plastered across her forehead.
"Gah—!" Kara choked out, letting out an involuntary nervous wheeze of hysterical laughter.

’The girls...’ Kara thought, shaking her head until her cheeks wobbled in the freezing slipstream, ’...they haven’t just been holding the perimeter. They’ve been running a high-efficiency abattoir across four different quadrants!’
Silas had expected a solid payout.
When you unleash several S-Rank and SSS-Rank immortals into an unfiltered rift breach choked with hundreds of thousands of low-tier invaders, the return was bound to be significant.
But watching the numbers roll in was like watching an automated stock exchange print currency in real-time.
By the time the dust settled over Khemet, his UP Balance... wouldn’t merely be healthy, they would be disgustingly obscenely swollen.
Her eyes lingered for a fraction of a second on the prominent, gold-bordered notification pinned to the top of the cascade.
[TASMIN HAS REACHED THE SECOND STAGE OF SHADOW HEART.]
A genuine warm smile broke through the cold mask of his female persona.
’Second stage...’ Kara thought with the pride swelling thick behind her ribs. ’Good. She earned every scrap of it.’

Tasmin had spent the last few weeks bleeding into the dark soil of the Umbral Basin, pushing her soul to the verge of collapse, refusing to take an extra hour of sleep even when Rowenna had threatened to dose her evening tea with high-grade sedative tinctures.
The woman ran on pure devotion so she deserved every single stat point, every microscopic advancement in her shadow-conduits, and every ounce of authority her newly evolved core could muster.
’As long as they remain rooted in Blessed Land,’ Kara vowed silently, watching the clouds part below her, ’they will never hit a ceiling... Nobody is going to dictate how far my people can climb.’
GROOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOWL!
A deafening vibration echoed from the misty deck beneath her boots as cutting through the gray moisture like a crimson torpedo, an eighty-pace serpentine silhouette broke through the thermals.
Talira.

The Ancient Crimson Dragon banked sharply on a forty-five-degree horizontal axis with her massive bat-like wings cupping the air with a concussive thwump that displaced several tons of freezing cloud-mist as she positioned her broad flat spinal ridge directly along Kara’s falling vector, matching her velocity with effortless grace.
TAP!
Kara’s boots touched down upon the glowing ruby scales between her shoulder blades with her knees absorbing the landing with a soft practiced dip.
"Nice timing, Talira," Kara murmured, patting the hot iron-hard ridge of her neck.
"ALWAYS, MY LORD!" the dragon’s voice echoed proudly in his consciousness, her scales heating up slightly with delight at the praise.
Sitting six paces behind her, tucked cross-legged against the base of a dorsal spine, was Number 5.
The Fifth Seat of the World Council hadn’t moved an inch.

Her midnight-violet robes were neatly arranged across her shins, her hands tucked deep inside her wide sleeves with her porcelain half-moon mask tilted upward to look at Kara White with an expression of deeply suspicious bewilderment.

"Are you having a stroke, Kara White?" Number 5 asked,. "You were waving your single arm at empty air like an epileptic windmill, and then you started giggling at a cloud... If your Gold Core is leaking cerebrospinal fluid from atmospheric decompression, inform me now so I can calibrate an emergency medical ward."

"I am perfectly balanced, thank you for your deeply touching concern," Silas retorted in Kara’s raspy voice, completely ignoring her as he turned his focus back inward to the interface hovering before his nose.
’System,’ Kara commanded inwardly. ’Query... Identify the origin, classification, and authority of the severed skeletal limb currently embedded in the ground.’
DING!
A single blood-red prompt flashed over his eyes.
[SYSTEM INQUIRY REQUIRES ACCESS TO HIGH-TIER DIVINE CLASSIFICATION RECORD.]
[COMPENSATION REQUIRED TO BYPASS CLASSIFIED VAULT ENCRYPTION: 1,000 UP.]
Kara nearly choked on her own tongue.
"One thousand?!" Kara’s physical vocal cords barked aloud into the open wind, her voice cracking in pure outrage.
Number 5 tilted her head, her porcelain mask gleaming. "One thousand what? Are you hallucinating debts?"
Kara ignored the masked woman completely, glaring at the blinking red cursor hovering six inches from her eyelashes.

’You shameless parasite!" Kara hissed mentally, her eye twitching with a lot of venom. ’You see me out here breaking my back, severing titan limbs, and dragging an entire continent out of an extinction event... you see a few thousand points roll into the account and suddenly you want a thirty percent transaction tax just to read a damn identification tag?! Fuck you! Keep your secrets! I’ll go down there with a chisel and figure it out myself!’
Kara aggressively jerked her head to the right, turning her face away from the prompt with a childish stubborn scowl while crossing his arms over his chest.
’...Fuck you.’
The prompt didn’t vanish.
It hovered and blinked.
...Five seconds passed like that with the wind howled over Talira’s ruby horns.
Kara slowly, painfully turned her eyes back toward the glowing letters.
’...Fine,’ She growled through her teeth with her soul weeping digital tears of blood. ’Whatever. Take the grand, you extortionist bastard. Just give me the damn dossier...’
CHIME!
[1,000 UP DEDUCTED FROM CURRENT BALANCE.]
[DECRYPTING ARCHIVE...]
The blue light shifted, coalescing into a block of text framed by spinning obsidian runic wheels.𝚏𝕣𝕖𝚎𝚠𝚎𝚋𝚗𝐨𝐯𝕖𝕝.𝕔𝐨𝕞
[Target identification: The Right Hand of Thanat-kor, The Seventh Scythe.]
[Classification: Minor Deity Of Entropy And Corporeal Cessation (tier 6 peak / semi-primordial ascendant).]

[In the stratified pantheons of the outer void, death is not a monolithic monarchy, but an armed oligarchy... the sovereign realm recognizes eleven high death gods and forty-four minor death deities. thanat-kor commands the seventh dust-trench, governing the calcification and metabolic severing of skeletal houses.]
[The full manifestation spans approximately 1.4 miles in vertical height and total bone mass exceeds 800,000 tons.]
[Domain radius: 12 miles.]
Kara stared at the text, her brain grinding to a screeching paralyzed halt.
’One... point... four... miles... tall?’
