It had no humming aura now as it radiated none of that heaven-shattering room-clearing solar radiance that had bleached the stratosphere in pure gold bare heartbeats ago.
’It feels normal...’

Resting against her calloused leather glove, it possessed the dull balanced heft of a standard three-foot imperial sidearm forged from unpolished star-iron... neither hot nor cold with its runic grooves sitting dormant and dark like dry irrigation ditches.
’This really is an incomprehensibly bizarre piece of steel,’ Kara mused internally, her dark eyes squinting through the rushing air as her hair whipped wildly across her eyelashes.
When she had channeled her Gold Core into the pommel... forcing every cubic millimeter of her compressed mana down through the hilt, the blade hadn’t resisted at all.
It hadn’t heated up, it hadn’t warped under the strain, and it certainly hadn’t leaked shockwaves into her wrist.

It had simply absorbed thousands of units of output in a single seond, converted the entire load into a razor-thin filament of conceptual severing, and cleaved clean through eighty linear feet of petrified skull-encrusted necrotic bone as though she were pulling a heated copper wire through cold lard.
And speaking of that ungodly limb...
THUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
Two thousand feet below Kara, the severed hand of the titan finally met the earth.
The petrified, eight-story skeletal fist... weighing hundreds of thousands of tons slammed into the northern fringe of the High Market District like an iron asteroid.

The shockwave traveled through the bedrock with the roar of a collapsing mountain range as three multi-tier warehouses, an ancient aqueduct viaduct, and an entire city block of abandoned limestone tenements simply ceased to exist in their vertical configurations, crushed beneath forty million pounds of calcified bone and displaced foundation shale.

A massive circular mushroom plume of pulverized masonry and blinding white bone-dust exploded outward, scouring the surrounding streets and rattling the teeth in Kara’s skull even from her vantage point high in the clouds.

’Well,’ Kara grimaced, her jaw tightening as she watched the dust ring expand across the ruins, ’at the very least, the immediate extinction-level crisis is resolved so nobody is getting crushed by an active fifty-foot claw anymore.’
Yet, as she stared down at the cratered monument of pale bone resting among the ruins, a prickle of cold hair-raising intuition brushed against Kara’s spine.
That arm hadn’t merely been a heavy piece of meat.

The atmospheric pressure around the impact zone had plummeted by twelve millibars and the lingering necrotic chill radiating from the marrow was so intense that the surrounding concrete foundations were actively frosting over with crystalline pale-green frost.
’A limb of that caliber doesn’t just wander out of a common rift,’ Kara thought, her eyes narrowing into cold slits. ’System... wait.
Give me more information on what the hell that th—’
Her mental query was clumsy.
With her left arm now fully functional and unpinned, Kara reached instinctively into the empty air before her face, flicking her fingers in a reflexive swipe to clear the visual feed.
BZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZT!
She accidentally clipped the edge of his dormant status icon, violently uncoupling the silent notification damper she had done so for quite a long time.
’Fuck...’
In less than a few seconds, the physical sky vanished behind an avalanche of blinding translucent blue holographic tabs that slammed directly into her eyes with the subtlety of a collapsing bookcase.
PING!
PING!
PING!
PING!
PING!
[TASMIN HAS ENGAGED IN CONTINUOUS COMBAT AND IS NEARING ADVANCEMENT.]
[TASMIN HAS REACHED THE SECOND STAGE OF SHADOW HEART!]
TASMIN HAS SEVERED 12X TIER 3 ABYSSAL SKYSTRIKERS.
REWARD: +480 UP!]
[HERO: BRIDA HAS EXECUTED TITAN-CRUSH COUNTER.
REWARD: +20 UP!]
[HERO: FENNA HAS ELIMINATED 1X MUTATED SCOUT.
REWARD: +2 UP!]
[HERO: MORWENNA HAS INITIATED CONTINUOUS AQUATIC MASS-PURGE...
412X KILLS REGISTERED.]
[YOU HAVE GAINED 2,000 UP!]
[YOU HAVE GAINED 1,450 UP!]
[YOU HAVE GAINED 3,800 UP!]
The blue windows stacked three feet deep before her eyes, blinking, vibrating, and scrolling text at roughly four hundred lines per second.

The overload was so much that Kara literally lost her peripheral vision mid-freefall, tumbling blindly through a cloud bank with tabs advertising dead bone-crawlers and displaced water-sprites plastered across her forehead.
"Gah—!" Kara choked out, letting out an involuntary nervous wheeze of hysterical laughter.
’The girls...’ Kara thought, shaking her head until her cheeks wobbled in the freezing slipstream, ’...they haven’t just been holding the perimeter.
They’ve been running a high-efficiency abattoir across four different quadrants!’
Silas had expected a solid payout.
When you unleash several S-Rank and SSS-Rank immortals into an unfiltered rift breach choked with hundreds of thousands of low-tier invaders, the return was bound to be significant.
But watching the numbers roll in was like watching an automated stock exchange print currency in real-time.
By the time the dust settled over Khemet, his UP Balance... wouldn’t merely be healthy, they would be disgustingly obscenely swollen.
Her eyes lingered for a fraction of a second on the prominent, gold-bordered notification pinned to the top of the cascade.
[TASMIN HAS REACHED THE SECOND STAGE OF SHADOW HEART.]
A genuine warm smile broke through the cold mask of his female persona.
’Second stage...’ Kara thought with the pride swelling thick behind her ribs. ’Good.
She earned every scrap of it.’

Tasmin had spent the last few weeks bleeding into the dark soil of the Umbral Basin, pushing her soul to the verge of collapse, refusing to take an extra hour of sleep even when Rowenna had threatened to dose her evening tea with high-grade sedative tinctures.
The woman ran on pure devotion so she deserved every single stat point, every microscopic advancement in her shadow-conduits, and every ounce of authority her newly evolved core could muster.
’As long as they remain rooted in Blessed Land,’ Kara vowed silently, watching the clouds part below her, ’they will never hit a ceiling...
Nobody is going to dictate how far my people can climb.’
GROOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOWL!
A deafening vibration echoed from the misty deck beneath her boots as cutting through the gray moisture like a crimson torpedo, an eighty-pace serpentine silhouette broke through the thermals.
Talira.

The Ancient Crimson Dragon banked sharply on a forty-five-degree horizontal axis with her massive bat-like wings cupping the air with a concussive thwump that displaced several tons of freezing cloud-mist as she positioned her broad flat spinal ridge directly along Kara’s falling vector, matching her velocity with effortless grace.
TAP!
Kara’s boots touched down upon the glowing ruby scales between her shoulder blades with her knees absorbing the landing with a soft practiced dip.
"Nice timing, Talira," Kara murmured, patting the hot iron-hard ridge of her neck.
"ALWAYS, MY LORD!" the dragon’s voice echoed proudly in his consciousness, her scales heating up slightly with delight at the praise.
Sitting six paces behind her, tucked cross-legged against the base of a dorsal spine, was Number 5.
The Fifth Seat of the World Council hadn’t moved an inch.

Her midnight-violet robes were neatly arranged across her shins, her hands tucked deep inside her wide sleeves with her porcelain half-moon mask tilted upward to look at Kara White with an expression of deeply suspicious bewilderment.
"Are you having a stroke, Kara White?" Number 5 asked,.
"You were waving your single arm at empty air like an epileptic windmill, and then you started giggling at a cloud...
If your Gold Core is leaking cerebrospinal fluid from atmospheric decompression, inform me now so I can calibrate an emergency medical ward."

"I am perfectly balanced, thank you for your deeply touching concern," Silas retorted in Kara’s raspy voice, completely ignoring her as he turned his focus back inward to the interface hovering before his nose.
’System,’ Kara commanded inwardly. ’Query...
Identify the origin, classification, and authority of the severed skeletal limb currently embedded in the ground.’
DING!
A single blood-red prompt flashed over his eyes.
[SYSTEM INQUIRY REQUIRES ACCESS TO HIGH-TIER DIVINE CLASSIFICATION RECORD.]
[COMPENSATION REQUIRED TO BYPASS CLASSIFIED VAULT ENCRYPTION: 1,000 UP.]
Kara nearly choked on her own tongue.
"One thousand?!" Kara’s physical vocal cords barked aloud into the open wind, her voice cracking in pure outrage.
Number 5 tilted her head, her porcelain mask gleaming.
"One thousand what?
Are you hallucinating debts?"
Kara ignored the masked woman completely, glaring at the blinking red cursor hovering six inches from her eyelashes.

’You shameless parasite!" Kara hissed mentally, her eye twitching with a lot of venom. ’You see me out here breaking my back, severing titan limbs, and dragging an entire continent out of an extinction event... you see a few thousand points roll into the account and suddenly you want a thirty percent transaction tax just to read a damn identification tag?!
Fuck you!
Keep your secrets!
I’ll go down there with a chisel and figure it out myself!’
Kara aggressively jerked her head to the right, turning her face away from the prompt with a childish stubborn scowl while crossing his arms over his chest.
’...Fuck you.’
The prompt didn’t vanish.
It hovered and blinked.
...Five seconds passed like that with the wind howled over Talira’s ruby horns.
Kara slowly, painfully turned her eyes back toward the glowing letters.
’...Fine,’ She growled through her teeth with her soul weeping digital tears of blood. ’Whatever.
Take the grand, you extortionist bastard.
Just give me the damn dossier...’
CHIME!
[1,000 UP DEDUCTED FROM CURRENT BALANCE.]
[DECRYPTING ARCHIVE...]
The blue light shifted, coalescing into a block of text framed by spinning obsidian runic wheels.𝚏𝕣𝕖𝚎𝚠𝚎𝚋𝚗𝐨𝐯𝕖𝕝.𝕔𝐨𝕞
[Target identification: The Right Hand of Thanat-kor, The Seventh Scythe.]
[Classification: Minor Deity Of Entropy And Corporeal Cessation (tier 6 peak / semi-primordial ascendant).]

[In the stratified pantheons of the outer void, death is not a monolithic monarchy, but an armed oligarchy... the sovereign realm recognizes eleven high death gods and forty-four minor death deities. thanat-kor commands the seventh dust-trench, governing the calcification and metabolic severing of skeletal houses.]
[The full manifestation spans approximately 1.4 miles in vertical height and total bone mass exceeds 800,000 tons.]
[Domain radius: 12 miles.]
Kara stared at the text, her brain grinding to a screeching paralyzed halt.
’One... point... four... miles... tall?’

chapters.title: Chapter 630: Thor Arrives [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Kara’s jaw slacked slightly beneath her dark cowl.

’Why in the name of the nine hells was a one-and-a-half-mile-tall Death God trying to climb through that kind of tear?!’ Silas blurted out in mental disbelief. "His shoulders alone must measure six thousand feet across! His hips would have caught on the spatial rim like a fat pig stuck in a fence! What was the plan here?! To stick his hand through, wave at the mortals, and get stuck in the doorway for three centuries?!’
It made zero practical sense.
The gods of death... even the so-called ’minor’ ones who sat in the lower tiers of the pantheons were ancient and disgustingly territorial according to what he could see from the System now.
They spent eons sitting on thrones of petrified marrow in the deep rifts, slowly digesting the souls of collapsed worlds.

They didn’t simply wake up on a Tuesday morning, smell an engine blow out on a terrestrial rock, and decide to cannonball headfirst through a narrow dimensional aperture into a world that still possessed active nuclear deterrence.

’Unless...’ Silas narrowed his eyes, ’...the destruction of the Khemet Suppression Engine didn’t just break the local ceiling. It sent a soul-frequency ringing across everywhere like a dinner bell...?’
Silas scratched the side of his head, looking down past Talira’s trailing tail toward the massive smoking crater where the severed hand lay.
Down in Sector Four, the colossal limb was already beginning to react to regular physics.
Without the active core of Thanat-Kor pumping primordial necrotic mana through the calcified joints, the eighty-foot bone fingers were slowly crumbling.
Massive, powdery sheets of pale-green bone-dust were peeling away from the knuckles, drifting across the ruined streets like an eerie lightless blizzard.
DING!
[Opportunity Detected... Residual Primordial Essence.]
[Being In Direct Proximity To The Unraveling Limb Of A Deity Of Cessation Permits Absorption Of Corporeal Necrotic Particles.]

[Host Possesses An Unblemished Gold Core... Intake Of Thanat-Kor’s Residual Marrow-Mist Will Amplify Innate Death/Entropy Affinity By 340%, Accelerating Soul-Seat Refinement Toward High-Tier Necrotic Resistance!]
Silas’s eyes lit up like twin lanterns.
’Three hundred and forty percent?!’
"Hold the flight, Talira!" Kara shouted aloud, kicking off the dragon’s spine. "Wait right here! I’m going down to harvest some fertilizer!"
WHOOSH!
Kara dove straight off the dragon’s back, tucking her arms and rocketing toward the smoking bone crater at two hundred miles per hour while Number 5 didn’t even flinch.
She simply adjusted her sleeves with a sigh.
"If she splatters on the pavement, I am not scraping the grease off the stones."
Down fell Kara, closing the distance... four thousand feet... three thousand feet... two thousand feet—
BZZZZT-PING!
A bright crimson error window violently materialized three inches from Kara’s nose in mid-air.
[Soul-Vibration Incompatibility Detected!]
[Warning: Host Personally Severed Thanat-Kor’s Right Hand Utilizing The Sacred Artifact [Dawn Blade].]
[Current Divine Status: Thanat-Kor Has Officially Logged Host’s Spiritual Frequency Under [Blood-Cursed Enemy Of The Seventh Scythe].]

[Residual Marrow Particles Carry Active Retribution Will... If Host Ingests Or Enters Direct Absorption Contact With The Ash, The Residual Will Enter The Pulmonary Meridians And Violently Eviscerate Host’s Internal Organs From Within.]
[Recommended Action... Do Not Touch The Ash and Retreat Immediately.]
Kara’s body seized mid-air.
"WHAT?!" Silas shrieked internally.
’Are you fucking kidding me?!’
KABOOM!
Kara slammed her heels together, unleashing an emergency blast of wind-mana straight toward the ground.
The concussive back-blast violently halted her descent at twelve hundred feet, sending her looping upward in an undignified parabolic arc.
SWOOSH!
She flipped backward, kicked off three invisible air-steps, and rocketed straight back up into the stratosphere, landing back on Talira’s ruby spine with a heavy dust-covered thud.
Talira blinked her massive burning crimson eyes, turning her serpentine snout backward to look at her master.
"Back already, My Lord?" Talira rumbled, her voice filled with innocent genuine confusion. "Did you harvest the tribute?"
Kara slowly pushed herself up from her hands and knees, brushing a stray fleck of ash from her cheek with her face taking an expression of twitching exhaustion.
"False alarm," Kara grunted, her raspy voice completely devoid of life. "The dirt is contaminated."

’Type faster next time, you useless piece of junk!’ Silas roared at the system in the silent fortress of his mind. ’You let me free-fall five thousand feet toward an exploding bone pile before mentioning the god wants to turn my liver into soup?!’
He dismissed the screen with a sharp aggressive flick of his wrist.
Yet, despite the irritation, Silas reached inward, his fingers brushing against the spiritual anchor within his chest where the Dawn Blade slept.

’One slash,’ he thought, marveling at the memory. ’A single, clean stroke from that three-foot blade took out the hand of a Death God... What kind of monster was the Second King to forge something like that?’
It was a terrifying realization.
The items he had retrieved from the World Vault weren’t mere high-tier weapons... They were quite some anomalies and tools designed to defy the basic laws of divinity.
’Is it weird that I want more of them for myself?’
After this whole thing, he would definitely go there again.
’I haven’t even had to touch the other items yet,’ Silas thought with a cold confidence settling deep into his marrow.
If this one was like this... what about when he started using the other items as well?
Silas didn’t draw the blade again.
He let it rest within the warm quiet sanctuary of his soul, where his Gold Core mana slowly washed over the steel, cleansing it of the necrotic residue.
Beside him, Number 5 subtly shifted her weight, a tiny involuntary shiver running down the length of her spine beneath her heavy robes.
She slowly turned her porcelain mask toward Kara.

"Why are you smiling like that?" Number 5 asked with a sharp edge of genuine paranoia creeping into her tone. "You have that exact, repulsive expression people get right before they commit a high-order war crime... What are you planning?"
"Nothing at all, Madam Councilwoman," Kara replied sweetly, giving her a slow, terrifyingly unbothered wink. "Just thinking about how much I love public service."
GROOOOOOOOOOOOOOWL!
Talira’s throat vibrated with a deep sound.
"My Lord," the dragon reported, her gaze locking onto the horizon three miles to the east. "The minor vermin are organizing... Another rift has coalesced up above."
Kara rose to her full height, her traveler’s mantle billowing behind her like a raven’s wing.
She looked.
Across the eastern skyway, where the aqueducts crossed into the industrial sector, the air was black with movement.

It wasn’t a chaotic scatter of beasts like one would expect, rather it was a disciplined churning funnel of over four hundred Abyssal Gore-Vultures and eighty Chitinous Trench-Drakes, circling tightly around a central massive anomaly... a hovering four-winged terror whose bloated thorax was crowned with pulsating blue-and-violet lightning sacs.
A Tier 5 Hive-Alpha.

"Looks like the cleanup crew needs a foreman," Kara sighed, rolling her right shoulder until the joint popped cleanly. "Talira... Straight through the center of the formation and don’t waste breath on the scouts, aim directly for the throat of that bloated bird in the middle."
"BY YOUR WILL, LORD!" Talira roared, her ruby wings snapping back, preparing to dive—
Suddenly... the world went blue as a violent azure flash that turned the entire thermosphere into a photographic negative.
CRACK-CRACK-CRACK-KABOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

The sky detonated with the fury of an exploding star as a single colossal bolt of cosmic blue lightning... easily sixty yards in diameter punched straight down through the upper ionosphere like the javelin of an angry titan.
The four hundred Gore-Vultures were vaporized instantly... The eighty Chitinous Trench-Drakes were obliterated as well and as for the Tier 5 Hive-Alpha with the lightning sacs?

Its bloated body was struck with such ungodly voltage that its cells didn’t even have time to burn... its molecular structure simply dissolved into fine, drifting azure ozone before the thunderclap could even reach the ground.
A massive clearing shockwave blew the smoke and clouds away from the eastern sector, leaving three square miles of sky completely clean and empty.
And descending through the center of that smoking ionized vacuum...
"GWAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHA!"
A booming cheerful laugh echoed through the heavens.
"HELL YEAH!"
Floating weightlessly down through the azure static was a woman who looked like she had just kicked open the doors of a celestial tavern.
She was stunning... tall, athletic, with long, wild golden hair braided with strands of crackling blue plasma that arced lazily across her shoulders.

Her skin was lightly tanned, her muscular arms bare, wearing a tight sleeveless tunic of beaten celestial bronze and leather battle-skirts that bore the unmistakable rough-hewn aesthetic of the northern mythological realms.
Resting casually in her right hand, twirling around her fingers by its leather wrist-strap with dizzying velocity, was a short-handled war hammer forged from dark uru-metal.
...Mjolnir.
BURRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRP!

Thor let out a massive belch that rattled the air for thirty yards around her as she blinked, wiping the back of her mouth with her forearm, her bright blue eyes widening in sudden sheepish realization as she looked around.

"Whoops!" Thor laughed, coughing into her fist. "Pardon the thunder! The mead of Blessed Land carries a remarkably sharp fermentation but fear not, fragile mortals! I looked down from the high spires, saw that Midgard was once again choking on its own incompetence, and descended to deliver holy deliverance!"
She floated smoothly across the sky, coming to a hover ten paces from Talira’s snout.
Her bright booming gaze swept over the dragon, then locked onto the single-armed woman standing on its back.

"Greetings, majestic red lizard! Or rather Talira, you’re much stronger since we sparred! Why am I even doing this? We saw each other before you got summoned of course!" Thor beamed, waving her free hand. "And greetings to you, Si—"
Thor abruptly froze.
Her jaw clamped shut mid-syllable with her eyes bulging slightly as she caught the murderous glare Kara was shooting directly into her eyes.
Thor’s eyes darted down toward Number 5 sitting quietly on the scales.
She coughed violently into her fist, clearing her throat with an exaggerated unnatural shift in posture.

"...Ahem! I mean... Greetings, Lord of Blessed Land!" Thor boomed, her voice dropping into a comical and overly formal tone that sounded like a mercenary reading from a royal treaty for the first time. "I, the mighty Champion of the Northern Storms, have officially arrived to provide glorious multilateral assistance to your military operation... Truly, what a completely coincidental and uncoordinated deployment this is!"

Kara stared at her for three long, agonizing seconds then, she slowly stepped forward, walking along the ridge of Talira’s neck until she reached the dragon’s brow, looking down at the floating thunder-goddess with half-lidded amused eyes.
Kara reached out her single right hand, patting the top of Thor’s golden, plasma-streaked head with two firm rhythmic pats.
"Good girl," Kara murmured, her voice dripping with patronizing sweetness. "Such a helpful, obedient little powerhouse."
Silas watched internally with absolute, wicked glee.
’Let’s see how your divine ego handles being treated like a prize hound, you overgrown lightning rod~’
Thor, however, didn’t bristle.
Instead, she simply looked at Kara with an expression of mild unbothered pity, tilting her chin up proudly as she floated three inches higher into the air.

"Obviously I’m a good girl," Thor stated with absolute, unshakeable self-assurance, casually twirling Mjolnir across her knuckles. "I am my father’s favorite daughter, after all! Odin himself remarked many centuries ago that among all his glorious progeny, my hammer strikes with the cleanest trajectory! Praise is merely an acknowledgment of the natural cosmic order!"
Kara’s eyes twitched.

’That wasn’t the point, you arrogant blonde idiot!’ Silas cursed inwardly, dragging his mental hands down his face. ’You’re supposed to get flustered! You’re supposed to huff and cross your arms! You don’t just lean into the dog-patting and quote your dad!’
Beside them, Number 5 slowly rose to her feet upon Talira’s back.
The Fifth Seat brushed a stray speck of soot from her midnight-violet robes, letting out a long remarkably deep sigh of genuine, unvarnished relief that rustled the edges of her porcelain mask.

"This is remarkably good fortune," Number 5 murmured, her dark eyes looking out over the cleared eastern skyway. "With the primary Tier 6 rift-anchor severed, and with high-tier divine artillery of this caliber actively purging the upper airspace, our defensive parameters have stabilized significantly... The casualty projections for the northern sectors just dropped by forty-two percent."
Kara turned her head, looking at the masked woman and a cold knot formed in the pit of Silas’s stomach.
Ever since the blast, hell ever since he had dragged Harper’s unconscious body out of that collapsing shaft... a single terrifying question had been gnawing at the back of his mind.
’Fuck...’
He had gone back down.

Barely twenty minutes after breaking the surface, while the dust was still settling, he had discreetly probed down through the vertical fissure to inspect the place and the Sub-Suppression Engine anchoring the northern sector was gone.
The four-thousand-foot basalt cavern had been violently hollowed out into a smooth glassy sphere of void-melted slag.
There were no gears to replace and there were no runic conduits to repair either.
...The entire machine had simply ceased to exist.

Silas possessed the Absolute Upgrade System as he could take a rusted kitchen knife and turn it into a mythril cleaver, and he could take a cracked stone foundation and reinforce it into titan-slate as well.𝙛𝒓𝓮𝒆𝔀𝒆𝙗𝓷𝒐𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝓶
’...But how the hell am I supposed to upgrade something that isn’t there anymore?!’
He couldn’t point his fingers at empty air and upgrade a concept... You needed a base for that.
And worse... he couldn’t simply pack his bags, take his girls, and board Evelyn’s supersonic jet back to Europa.
’I hate myself...’
Lord Vespera was the face of the World Council’s modern squad.

If Kara White vanished from the frontlines while the northern half of Khemet was still bleeding through hundreds of dimensional tears, the international media would tear her reputation to shreds within forty-eight hours.
The Council would freeze his accounts, the Directorate would launch an inquiry, and the leverage he had carefully cultivated over the past month would evaporate like spit on a hot skillet.
He had to see this through.
He had to keep the World Council firmly on the hook for every single credit, every single drop of blood, and every single resource expended on this damn desert.
Kara gritted her teeth, her jaw setting into a tight miserable line as she looked at Number 5.

"Number 5," Kara spoke, her voice dropping into a low reluctant rasp that practically bled resentment. "The primary engine below the White Citadel... it is thoroughly obliterated. What is the World Council’s actual timeline for manufacturing and installing a replacement anchor?"
Silas held his breath.

He dismissed the screen with a sharp aggressive flick of his wrist.
Yet, despite the irritation, Silas reached inward, his fingers brushing against the spiritual anchor within his chest where the Dawn Blade slept.
’One slash,’ he thought, marveling at the memory. ’A single, clean stroke from that three-foot blade took out the hand of a Death God...
What kind of monster was the Second King to forge something like that?’
It was a terrifying realization.
The items he had retrieved from the World Vault weren’t mere high-tier weapons...
They were quite some anomalies and tools designed to defy the basic laws of divinity.
’Is it weird that I want more of them for myself?’
After this whole thing, he would definitely go there again.
’I haven’t even had to touch the other items yet,’ Silas thought with a cold confidence settling deep into his marrow.
If this one was like this... what about when he started using the other items as well?
Silas didn’t draw the blade again.
He let it rest within the warm quiet sanctuary of his soul, where his Gold Core mana slowly washed over the steel, cleansing it of the necrotic residue.
Beside him, Number 5 subtly shifted her weight, a tiny involuntary shiver running down the length of her spine beneath her heavy robes.
She slowly turned her porcelain mask toward Kara.
"Why are you smiling like that?" Number 5 asked with a sharp edge of genuine paranoia creeping into her tone.
"You have that exact, repulsive expression people get right before they commit a high-order war crime...
What are you planning?"
"Nothing at all, Madam Councilwoman," Kara replied sweetly, giving her a slow, terrifyingly unbothered wink.
"Just thinking about how much I love public service."
GROOOOOOOOOOOOOOWL!
Talira’s throat vibrated with a deep sound.
"My Lord," the dragon reported, her gaze locking onto the horizon three miles to the east.
"The minor vermin are organizing...
Another rift has coalesced up above."
Kara rose to her full height, her traveler’s mantle billowing behind her like a raven’s wing.
She looked.
Across the eastern skyway, where the aqueducts crossed into the industrial sector, the air was black with movement.

It wasn’t a chaotic scatter of beasts like one would expect, rather it was a disciplined churning funnel of over four hundred Abyssal Gore-Vultures and eighty Chitinous Trench-Drakes, circling tightly around a central massive anomaly... a hovering four-winged terror whose bloated thorax was crowned with pulsating blue-and-violet lightning sacs.
A Tier 5 Hive-Alpha.
"Looks like the cleanup crew needs a foreman," Kara sighed, rolling her right shoulder until the joint popped cleanly.
"Talira...
Straight through the center of the formation and don’t waste breath on the scouts, aim directly for the throat of that bloated bird in the middle."
"BY YOUR WILL, LORD!" Talira roared, her ruby wings snapping back, preparing to dive—
Suddenly... the world went blue as a violent azure flash that turned the entire thermosphere into a photographic negative.
CRACK-CRACK-CRACK-KABOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

The sky detonated with the fury of an exploding star as a single colossal bolt of cosmic blue lightning... easily sixty yards in diameter punched straight down through the upper ionosphere like the javelin of an angry titan.
The four hundred Gore-Vultures were vaporized instantly...
The eighty Chitinous Trench-Drakes were obliterated as well and as for the Tier 5 Hive-Alpha with the lightning sacs?

Its bloated body was struck with such ungodly voltage that its cells didn’t even have time to burn... its molecular structure simply dissolved into fine, drifting azure ozone before the thunderclap could even reach the ground.
A massive clearing shockwave blew the smoke and clouds away from the eastern sector, leaving three square miles of sky completely clean and empty.
And descending through the center of that smoking ionized vacuum...
"GWAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHA!"
A booming cheerful laugh echoed through the heavens.
"HELL YEAH!"
Floating weightlessly down through the azure static was a woman who looked like she had just kicked open the doors of a celestial tavern.
She was stunning... tall, athletic, with long, wild golden hair braided with strands of crackling blue plasma that arced lazily across her shoulders.

Her skin was lightly tanned, her muscular arms bare, wearing a tight sleeveless tunic of beaten celestial bronze and leather battle-skirts that bore the unmistakable rough-hewn aesthetic of the northern mythological realms.
Resting casually in her right hand, twirling around her fingers by its leather wrist-strap with dizzying velocity, was a short-handled war hammer forged from dark uru-metal.
...Mjolnir.
BURRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRP!

Thor let out a massive belch that rattled the air for thirty yards around her as she blinked, wiping the back of her mouth with her forearm, her bright blue eyes widening in sudden sheepish realization as she looked around.
"Whoops!" Thor laughed, coughing into her fist.
"Pardon the thunder!
The mead of Blessed Land carries a remarkably sharp fermentation but fear not, fragile mortals!
I looked down from the high spires, saw that Midgard was once again choking on its own incompetence, and descended to deliver holy deliverance!"
She floated smoothly across the sky, coming to a hover ten paces from Talira’s snout.
Her bright booming gaze swept over the dragon, then locked onto the single-armed woman standing on its back.
"Greetings, majestic red lizard!
Or rather Talira, you’re much stronger since we sparred!
Why am I even doing this?
We saw each other before you got summoned of course!" Thor beamed, waving her free hand.
"And greetings to you, Si—"
Thor abruptly froze.
Her jaw clamped shut mid-syllable with her eyes bulging slightly as she caught the murderous glare Kara was shooting directly into her eyes.
Thor’s eyes darted down toward Number 5 sitting quietly on the scales.
She coughed violently into her fist, clearing her throat with an exaggerated unnatural shift in posture.
"...Ahem!
I mean...
Greetings, Lord of Blessed Land!" Thor boomed, her voice dropping into a comical and overly formal tone that sounded like a mercenary reading from a royal treaty for the first time.
"I, the mighty Champion of the Northern Storms, have officially arrived to provide glorious multilateral assistance to your military operation...
Truly, what a completely coincidental and uncoordinated deployment this is!"

Kara stared at her for three long, agonizing seconds then, she slowly stepped forward, walking along the ridge of Talira’s neck until she reached the dragon’s brow, looking down at the floating thunder-goddess with half-lidded amused eyes.
Kara reached out her single right hand, patting the top of Thor’s golden, plasma-streaked head with two firm rhythmic pats.
"Good girl," Kara murmured, her voice dripping with patronizing sweetness.
"Such a helpful, obedient little powerhouse."
Silas watched internally with absolute, wicked glee.
’Let’s see how your divine ego handles being treated like a prize hound, you overgrown lightning rod~’
Thor, however, didn’t bristle.
Instead, she simply looked at Kara with an expression of mild unbothered pity, tilting her chin up proudly as she floated three inches higher into the air.
"Obviously I’m a good girl," Thor stated with absolute, unshakeable self-assurance, casually twirling Mjolnir across her knuckles.
"I am my father’s favorite daughter, after all!
Odin himself remarked many centuries ago that among all his glorious progeny, my hammer strikes with the cleanest trajectory!
Praise is merely an acknowledgment of the natural cosmic order!"
Kara’s eyes twitched.
’That wasn’t the point, you arrogant blonde idiot!’ Silas cursed inwardly, dragging his mental hands down his face. ’You’re supposed to get flustered!
You’re supposed to huff and cross your arms!
You don’t just lean into the dog-patting and quote your dad!’
Beside them, Number 5 slowly rose to her feet upon Talira’s back.
The Fifth Seat brushed a stray speck of soot from her midnight-violet robes, letting out a long remarkably deep sigh of genuine, unvarnished relief that rustled the edges of her porcelain mask.
"This is remarkably good fortune," Number 5 murmured, her dark eyes looking out over the cleared eastern skyway.
"With the primary Tier 6 rift-anchor severed, and with high-tier divine artillery of this caliber actively purging the upper airspace, our defensive parameters have stabilized significantly...
The casualty projections for the northern sectors just dropped by forty-two percent."
Kara turned her head, looking at the masked woman and a cold knot formed in the pit of Silas’s stomach.
Ever since the blast, hell ever since he had dragged Harper’s unconscious body out of that collapsing shaft... a single terrifying question had been gnawing at the back of his mind.
’Fuck...’
He had gone back down.

Barely twenty minutes after breaking the surface, while the dust was still settling, he had discreetly probed down through the vertical fissure to inspect the place and the Sub-Suppression Engine anchoring the northern sector was gone.
The four-thousand-foot basalt cavern had been violently hollowed out into a smooth glassy sphere of void-melted slag.
There were no gears to replace and there were no runic conduits to repair either.
...The entire machine had simply ceased to exist.

Silas possessed the Absolute Upgrade System as he could take a rusted kitchen knife and turn it into a mythril cleaver, and he could take a cracked stone foundation and reinforce it into titan-slate as well.𝙛𝒓𝓮𝒆𝔀𝒆𝙗𝓷𝒐𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝓶
’...But how the hell am I supposed to upgrade something that isn’t there anymore?!’
He couldn’t point his fingers at empty air and upgrade a concept...
You needed a base for that.
And worse... he couldn’t simply pack his bags, take his girls, and board Evelyn’s supersonic jet back to Europa.
’I hate myself...’
Lord Vespera was the face of the World Council’s modern squad.

If Kara White vanished from the frontlines while the northern half of Khemet was still bleeding through hundreds of dimensional tears, the international media would tear her reputation to shreds within forty-eight hours.
The Council would freeze his accounts, the Directorate would launch an inquiry, and the leverage he had carefully cultivated over the past month would evaporate like spit on a hot skillet.
He had to see this through.
He had to keep the World Council firmly on the hook for every single credit, every single drop of blood, and every single resource expended on this damn desert.
Kara gritted her teeth, her jaw setting into a tight miserable line as she looked at Number 5.
"Number 5," Kara spoke, her voice dropping into a low reluctant rasp that practically bled resentment.
"The primary engine below the White Citadel... it is thoroughly obliterated.
What is the World Council’s actual timeline for manufacturing and installing a replacement anchor?"
Silas held his breath.

chapters.title: Chapter 631: Blessed Land Figurines [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: ’Please,’ he prayed silently, ’let it be a week... Let them have a spare engine sitting in a warehouse somewhere and let them say three days.’
Number 5 adjusted her silver cuff.

"Under standard mobilization protocols, assuming all secondary Sub-Engines maintain their structural integrity, and assuming Number 9’s continental containment barrier holds the northern perimeter without collapse..."
She paused, tapping her chin thoughtfully.

"...it will require at least three weeks to align space and create a temporary change however... With our best currently operating within Iunu... meaning you, your summoned champions, and this delightfully noisy storm-woman continue to purge the rift clusters at our current operational tempo... we might be able to compress that timeline down to fourteen days or perhaps twelve. There’s no guarantee we’ll be able to stop it so I say focus on rescuing citizens which is still two to three weeks."
Kara stood completely still as her eyes blinked once and twice.
’Three... weeks?’
’FOURTEEN DAYS OF DIGGING DITCHES IN A FOUR-THOUSAND-DEGREE DESERT CHOKING ON DRIFTING BONE-DUST AND SLEEPING ON CRACKED CONCRETE?!’
Kara’s knees gave out.
Her physical eyes rolled back into her head with her spine turning to overcooked gelatin as she unceremoniously collapsed backward off Talira’s neck.
"Whoa—!"
Number 5 lunged forward, her silk robes fluttering frantically as she caught Kara’s falling upper body by the armpits, staggering under the dead-weight of the single-armed Lord.

"Kara White!" Number 5 shrieked, violently shaking Kara’s limp shoulders as Kara’s head lolled from side to side like a broken doll’s. "Do not faint on me! Wake up! Do not die from exhaustion! Come back to life, you ridiculous woman!"
Thor hovered five feet above them, resting her heavy chin against the flat of Mjolnir, letting out a soft booming chuckle that shook her braids.

’Ah...’ Thor thought, her bright blue eyes twinkling with warm amusement as she watched Silas’s female persona dramatically play dead in the woman’s arms. ’Silas really is so delightfully adorable whenever he overreacts to basic duty.’
[A Week And Five Days Later.]
Twelve hundred miles to the northeast, across the deep azure waters of the inner maritime corridor.
The afternoon sun over Rhyx City was a pale polished gold, glinting off the tiered glass domes and soaring white-granite sky-bridges that connected the spires of the city.
A cool coastal breeze blew off the bay, carrying the clean sharp scent of cedarwood, salt spray, and blooming mountain citrus.
On the high private terrace of the royal residential pavilion, sixty stories above the tranquil streets, a young woman stood with both hands resting lightly upon the carved marble balustrade.
Her long magnificent hair... a vibrant crystalline shade of deep aquatic blue whipped gently in the ocean draft, catching the sunlight like strands of spun lapis lazuli.
She wore a sleeveless, high-collared gown of flowing sea-foam silk that accentuated her slender athletic frame with her pale, porcelain features set in an expression of quiet distant contemplation.
Princess Aki.

Her large brilliant sapphire eyes looked out across the shimmering skyline of the city, but her thoughts were thousands of miles away, wandering through the scorched, lightless ruins of the southern continent.
’I hope Silas is doing well...’
It had been nearly two weeks since the catastrophic blowout in Northern Khemet.
For the past twelve days, the global news networks had spoken of nothing else.

The total vaporization of Pharaoh-President Menes Al-Mansur and the fleet... the mysterious total erasure of the White Citadel; and the unprecedented, terrifying collapse of the Northern Suppression Engine had sent shockwaves through every stock exchange, sovereign court, and military command from Europa to the Yamato Archipelago.

Refugee encampments in the southern territories of Khemet were already swelling with hundreds of thousands of displaced citizens, while neighboring nations were receiving an endless influx of commercial charters and civilian transports.

The World Council had issued three separate emergency communiqués, promising the international community that the northern sector would be completely stabilized and re-anchored "within four to six weeks."
Aki let out a soft wry breath through her teeth with her lips curving into a knowing smile.
’Four to six weeks...’
She knew the council’s bureaucratic double-speak.
As a daughter of the Supreme Royal Family, she understood the brutal realities of high-tier infrastructure better than most.
The World Council didn’t possess a spare Terrestrial Suppression Engine sitting on a warehouse shelf.

Those machines were ancient relics... masterpieces of lost Pre-Apocalypse geometry forged from extinct alloys and to rebuild an anchor of that magnitude from scratch would take months... Perhaps half a year.

In the meantime, the northern half of Khemet remained a brutal, cordoned-off kill-box, sealed beneath Number 9’s continental barrier, where the beasts of the Sovereign Realm were being relentlessly ground to pieces by an isolated garrison of Lords and their people.
’And at the center of that meat-grinder...’ Aki’s heart fluttered with a strange warm ache, ’...is Silas, walking under the name of Kara White.’
CLICK!
The heavy mahogany door leading onto the private terrace swung open with a quiet, oiled whisper.
"Princess?"
Mira, her personal chief maid, stepped onto the sunlit marble.

The older woman was, as always, immaculate in her starched navy dress and crisp white lace apron, but her composed formal posture was slightly compromised by the massive brightly colored cardboard shipping carton balanced carefully in her arms.

"The international courier cleared customs barely twenty minutes ago," Mira reported, stepping across the terrace and setting the parcel down upon the low glass coffee table beside the rattan loungers. "Priority sovereign routing from the Central City commercial logistics hub and stamped with the high-tier wax seal of the Apex Manufactory."
Mira offered a polite knowing curtsy, her lips twitching with faint amusement as she turned and slipped back into the interior suite, pulling the door shut behind her.
Aki stood motionless for a bare half-second.
Then... her royal regal composure completely evaporated.
"It’s here!" Aki squealed, dropping her hands from the balustrade, practically skipping across the marble tiles on her bare feet!

She dropped to her knees upon the plush Persian rug beside the low table with her sapphire eyes sparkling like diamonds as she grabbed the cardboard box, eagerly inspecting the glossy high-definition printing across the packaging.
Across the front of the collector’s box, embossed in shimmering, raised gold foil and high-gloss lacquer, was a title that had completely dominated global commercial markets for the past seven days.
[HEROES OF THE DUST: THE BLESSED LAND CHRONICLES — OFFICIAL COMMEMORATIVE EDITION.]
Aki let out another tiny breathless squeal, pressing her hands against her cheeks with her face flushing with pure unadulterated fangirl delight.
It was madness.
...An unprecedented commercial madness.

In the wake of the initial incursion... after the international syndicate’s live helicopter feed had captured Aeliana vaporizing forty bone-gryphons with starlight arrows, followed by the leaked military telemetry showing the champions of Blessed Land holding four entire sectors without yielding an inch of ground, the world had gone completely insane.
To the eight billion people watching the disaster unfold from their living rooms, Kara White wasn’t merely an Awakened lord... she was like a living breathing myth.

A single-armed dark-haired woman who stood upon the snout of an ancient red dragon, laughed in the face of falling rifts, and commanded an army of terrifyingly beautiful women who saved children with blooming flowers and severed monster limbs with single strokes of gold steel.
The global demand for memorabilia had been instantaneous and ravenous.

The Apex Manufactory... the most prestigious high-end arcane collectible firm on the planet, renowned for its museum-grade hand-sculpted porcelain and enchanted resin figures had moved with terrifying speed.

Securing emergency licensing directly from the World Council with a signed digital authorization rushed through by Kara White herself, who had reportedly demanded a twenty-five percent gross royalty on all international sales, they had launched pre-orders four days ago.
The result had broken the global network.
The commercial servers of seven major continental retailers had crashed within forty-five seconds of the launch.
Secondary market pre-orders were already trading on sovereign dark-nets for three hundred times their retail value...

Every teenager, every Awakened mercenary, and every royal scion from Europa to Yamato had thrown their allowances and corporate credit accounts at the screens, desperate to claim a piece of the legend.
’They’re the single best-selling collectible in the history of the modern world...!’ Aki thought, her fingers trembling slightly as she grabbed the pull-tab on the packaging.

Even Aki who possessed private vaults filled with real star-sapphires, ancient tapestries, and bespoke mythril jewelry had spent forty-five frantic minutes hunched over her private phone with three different priority clearance relays open, hitting the refresh button with white-knuckled desperation to ensure her pre-order cleared the queue.
...RIP!
The tamper-evident golden tape parted with a satisfying clean tear.
Aki gently folded the heavy cardboard flaps back, peering into the velvet-lined interior of the master carton.
"I got it...!" she gasped, her hands flying to her mouth. "I actually got the complete royal tier!"

Inside the box, nestled within custom-molded velvet compartments, were eleven distinct, hand-painted collector’s figures, each sculpted in a dynamic breathtaking action pose... Their surfaces were treated with microscopic mana-reactive lacquers that caused their clothing and weapons to subtly shimmer in the sunlight.
Aki threw her dignity completely out the window.
"KYAAA!"
She squealed aloud on the empty terrace, kicking her bare heels against the carpet like a schoolgirl on holiday with her blue hair thrashing around her shoulders.
...So what if she was twenty-five years old?
...So what if she was a daughter of the World King’s own bloodline, paraded at state banquets as a decorative ornament of the crown?
Was a grown woman not allowed to enjoy perfection?! Especially if it was of her beloved?!
With reverent, trembling care, Aki reached into the box, gently lifting the figures out one by one, letting them settle softly upon the plush white linen of her daybed.

There was Aeliana, sculpted mid-hover upon a translucent pillar of purple resin starlight with her greatbow drawn taut and her spun-gold hair whipping back as well as the micro-inscribed runes along her star-silver cuirass glowing with a small luminescence.

There was Tasmin, crouched upon a shattered basalt cornice, her silver daggers spinning on thirty-millimeter tungsten chains and her half-mask cast in shadow while her eyes painted with such terrifying precision that they seemed to track the viewer across the room.
There was Brida, depicted mid-roar, resting her eight-foot Titan’s Cleaver across her broad shoulder, with an actual microscopic yellow desert-poppy sculpted carefully behind her left ear.

There was Morwenna, balanced upon the crest of a curling, translucent blue resin wave with Tidebringer held high and her wild black hair flying with her face frozen in that unmistakable pirate sneer and many more.
There was also the special multi-pack variants...

Talira in her breathtaking crimson-winged humanoid form, arms crossed, looking arrogant and untouchable and beside her, a massive sixteen-inch scale model of Talira in her full Ancient Crimson Dragon form with her ruby scales individually layered and her jaw agape as a swirling, light-up LED draconic fire-plume coiled from her throat.
"They’re so cute..." Aki whimpered, her hands hovering over the dragon’s tiny horns, her heart melting into a warm gooey puddle. "They’re so ridiculously detailed..."
And then... her gaze dropped to the center compartment.
The master centerpiece.
Aki held her breath.
...Her fingers moved with gentleness as she lifted the primary figure from its velvet cradle.
It was Kara White.
The eight-inch sculpt was a triumph of the artificer’s craft.
The figure depicted the single-armed woman standing upon the edge of a shattered vitrified black-glass precipice.
Her long, midnight-blue traveler’s mantle was frozen mid-billow, its empty left sleeve pinned neatly across her chest, fluttering in an invisible gale.

Beneath the deep shadow of her traveler’s cowl, her sharp features were captured with breathtaking lifelike accuracy... the high cheekbones, the half-lidded, confident dark eyes, and that effortless slightly condescending smile playing at the corner of her lips.

In her right hand, held casually at her side with the point angled toward the earth, was a microscopic perfect replica of the Dawn Blade with its runes catching the afternoon sun and reflecting a soft warm amber gleam across her knuckles.

Aki held the figure up to eye level with her breath turning soft... The coastal wind blew through the terrace, rustling the sea-foam silk of her gown, carrying the distant chime of Rhyx City’s maritime bells.
Aki looked at the tiny smiling face of Kara White.
She looked at the calm immovable confidence in those painted eyes... the same strength she had felt radiating from Silas when he had stood before the lords of the world and refused to bend his knee.
An innocent smile touched the princess’s lips.
"Really cool..." Aki murmured softly into the warm breeze.
"...you really are so incredibly cool, Silas."

Secondary market pre-orders were already trading on sovereign dark-nets for three hundred times their retail value...

Every teenager, every Awakened mercenary, and every royal scion from Europa to Yamato had thrown their allowances and corporate credit accounts at the screens, desperate to claim a piece of the legend.
’They’re the single best-selling collectible in the history of the modern world...!’ Aki thought, her fingers trembling slightly as she grabbed the pull-tab on the packaging.

Even Aki who possessed private vaults filled with real star-sapphires, ancient tapestries, and bespoke mythril jewelry had spent forty-five frantic minutes hunched over her private phone with three different priority clearance relays open, hitting the refresh button with white-knuckled desperation to ensure her pre-order cleared the queue.
...RIP!
The tamper-evident golden tape parted with a satisfying clean tear.
Aki gently folded the heavy cardboard flaps back, peering into the velvet-lined interior of the master carton.
"I got it...!" she gasped, her hands flying to her mouth.
"I actually got the complete royal tier!"
Inside the box, nestled within custom-molded velvet compartments, were eleven distinct, hand-painted collector’s figures, each sculpted in a dynamic breathtaking action pose...
Their surfaces were treated with microscopic mana-reactive lacquers that caused their clothing and weapons to subtly shimmer in the sunlight.
Aki threw her dignity completely out the window.
"KYAAA!"
She squealed aloud on the empty terrace, kicking her bare heels against the carpet like a schoolgirl on holiday with her blue hair thrashing around her shoulders.
...So what if she was twenty-five years old?
...So what if she was a daughter of the World King’s own bloodline, paraded at state banquets as a decorative ornament of the crown?
Was a grown woman not allowed to enjoy perfection?!
Especially if it was of her beloved?!
With reverent, trembling care, Aki reached into the box, gently lifting the figures out one by one, letting them settle softly upon the plush white linen of her daybed.

There was Aeliana, sculpted mid-hover upon a translucent pillar of purple resin starlight with her greatbow drawn taut and her spun-gold hair whipping back as well as the micro-inscribed runes along her star-silver cuirass glowing with a small luminescence.

There was Tasmin, crouched upon a shattered basalt cornice, her silver daggers spinning on thirty-millimeter tungsten chains and her half-mask cast in shadow while her eyes painted with such terrifying precision that they seemed to track the viewer across the room.
There was Brida, depicted mid-roar, resting her eight-foot Titan’s Cleaver across her broad shoulder, with an actual microscopic yellow desert-poppy sculpted carefully behind her left ear.

There was Morwenna, balanced upon the crest of a curling, translucent blue resin wave with Tidebringer held high and her wild black hair flying with her face frozen in that unmistakable pirate sneer and many more.
There was also the special multi-pack variants...

Talira in her breathtaking crimson-winged humanoid form, arms crossed, looking arrogant and untouchable and beside her, a massive sixteen-inch scale model of Talira in her full Ancient Crimson Dragon form with her ruby scales individually layered and her jaw agape as a swirling, light-up LED draconic fire-plume coiled from her throat.
"They’re so cute..." Aki whimpered, her hands hovering over the dragon’s tiny horns, her heart melting into a warm gooey puddle.
"They’re so ridiculously detailed..."
And then... her gaze dropped to the center compartment.
The master centerpiece.
Aki held her breath.
...Her fingers moved with gentleness as she lifted the primary figure from its velvet cradle.
It was Kara White.
The eight-inch sculpt was a triumph of the artificer’s craft.
The figure depicted the single-armed woman standing upon the edge of a shattered vitrified black-glass precipice.
Her long, midnight-blue traveler’s mantle was frozen mid-billow, its empty left sleeve pinned neatly across her chest, fluttering in an invisible gale.

Beneath the deep shadow of her traveler’s cowl, her sharp features were captured with breathtaking lifelike accuracy... the high cheekbones, the half-lidded, confident dark eyes, and that effortless slightly condescending smile playing at the corner of her lips.

In her right hand, held casually at her side with the point angled toward the earth, was a microscopic perfect replica of the Dawn Blade with its runes catching the afternoon sun and reflecting a soft warm amber gleam across her knuckles.
Aki held the figure up to eye level with her breath turning soft...
The coastal wind blew through the terrace, rustling the sea-foam silk of her gown, carrying the distant chime of Rhyx City’s maritime bells.
Aki looked at the tiny smiling face of Kara White.
She looked at the calm immovable confidence in those painted eyes... the same strength she had felt radiating from Silas when he had stood before the lords of the world and refused to bend his knee.
An innocent smile touched the princess’s lips.
"Really cool..." Aki murmured softly into the warm breeze.
"...you really are so incredibly cool, Silas."

chapters.title: Chapter 632: Top And Bottom [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Aki sat cross-legged on the silk counterpane, carefully lifting each sculpt from its foam insert like an archaeologist handling brittle porcelain relics.
She picked up the miniature of Eluned.
"Woah..."
The sculpt was breathtakingly delicate, captured in flowing robes of translucent jade and silver that seemed to whisper with an invisible, gentle breeze.

The Former Spirit of the World Tree was posed with a soft serene tilt of her head with one slender hand resting over her heart while the other reached outward in a gesture of effortless botanical dominion.
Around her delicate ankles, tiny, perfectly cast roots burst through faux cobblestones, cradling microscopic blossoming lotuses.
"She really is so elegant..." Aki murmured to herself, turning the piece under the warm coastal sunlight.
Her fingers brushed against the small joint embedded inside the figurine’s left palm as she turned the box over, checking the miniature pictorial insert, and let out a soft gasp.
"Wait... it has an interlocking peg?"
Aki took the Kara White figure she had set aside, carefully aligning the hands.
With a tiny satisfying click, Eluned’s slender fingers slid perfectly into place, gently clasping onto the single-armed sovereign’s right elbow.
The two sculpts balanced together flawlessly, looking for all the world like an ancient queen resting trustingly against her stalwart champion.
Aki’s heart fluttered in her chest.
"They actually designed them to hold onto each other... That’s so shameless. That’s ridiculously cute."
She set the pair down and continued exploring the carton.
Next was Aeliana, suspended upon an arched rod of violet acrylic that gave the illusion of weightless celestial flight, her longbow pulled taut with an arrow carved from tinted crystal.
Beside her was Tasmin, crouched low, shrouded in sculpted shadow-wisps, her twin daggers gleaming with a mirror-finish coat of chrome paint.

Then came Brida, towering over the others, resting her massive eight-foot cleaver over a plate-armored shoulder with an unapologetic toothy grin that captured her boisterous personality with startling fidelity.
She had seen these ones before, but there were more.
’I’m glad the others got figurines as well, I can’t wait to show them...’
There was Rowenna, posed with a flurry of translucent runes spinning around her fingertips as her expression was a mix of crazy genius and subtle flustered shyness.

Vala’s was mid-spin with her blade wreathed in five distinct swirling bands of elemental power while Fenna was crouched on an angle with a quiver of arrows at her hip and Kadi, grinning like an unhinged little battle maniac, her fists encased in spiked gauntlets of petrified rock.
Then finally, tucked into the very bottom corner in a custom-stamped foil sleeve, was the eleventh piece.
Aki gently peeled the velvet cover back.
"No way..." Aki burst out into a bright musical laugh, holding the figure up to the light. "Thor?! Thor actually got an official figurine in the Blessed Land set?!"
It was unmistakable.

The thunder-goddess was posed with one foot planted boldly atop a shattered abyssal drake skull with her wild golden braids arcing with jagged sparks of blue electric lacquer and her head thrown back in mid-bellowing laugh.

In her right hand, Mjolnir was captured in a blur-sculpt of motion, while tucked under her left arm... sculpted with hilarious irreverent precision was a tiny frothing wooden tankard of northern mead.
"They even gave her the ale mug," Aki chuckled, shaking her head as she arranged the eleven figures in a broad protective semicircle across her duvet.
She tapped Kara’s head with the tip of her pinky finger, speaking in an exaggerated playful whisper.
"Alright, Lord Vespera, your army is assembled. What are your orders for today? Should we go conquer the tea parlor or—"
"A bit ambitious for an afternoon, don’t you think?"
The moment the latch clicked shut behind the doorframe, Aki’s spine went rigid with pure panic.

Her eyes darted wildly between the eleven figures scattered across her duvet and the tall cowled shadow stepping through her balcony doors and in the half-second she had to decide, instinct won over dignity entirely.

She snatched the Kara White figurine off the pillow and clutched it protectively against her chest with both hands, as though hiding the evidence would somehow un-happen the last forty-five minutes of her life.
...It didn’t work as Aki froze.
The air in the bedroom suddenly grew heavy, humming with the unmistakable static of compressed spatial displacement as she whipped her head toward the sunlit balcony doors.
Leaning casually against the open mahogany doorframe, half-shrouded in the sheer white curtains that fluttered in the ocean breeze, was a solitary figure.
She wore a long traveling mantle of midnight-blue wool, its hem dusted with faint streaks of pale-green bone ash.
The left sleeve was pinned neatly across her chest, looking empty while her right hand hung loosely at her hip.
Beneath the deep cowl, a pair of sharp, half-lidded dark eyes observed the princess with a quiet tired amusement.

"K-Kara?!" Aki squeaked, her heart violently hammering against her ribs as she scrambled backward on the bed, her hands instinctively splaying out to guard the army of tiny plastic warriors. "How... how did you get in here?! The royal estate’s warding array is—"
"Shh," Kara murmured softly.
She raised a single finger to her pale lips, stepping soundlessly across the polished cedar threshold into the bedroom.

"Keep your voice down, Aki... I’m running on roughly sixteen minutes of uninterrupted consciousness over the last seventy-two hours, and if your people start firing harpoons at the terrace, I might actually burst into tears."
Kara walked over to the bed, her boots making no sound against the thick wool of the rug.
She looked down at the colorful array of figures scattered across the ivory linen, her dark eyebrows rising in genuine tired bewilderment.
"What do we have here?" Kara asked, crouching down beside the edge of the mattress, resting her chin upon her forearm.

She reached out with a single leather-clad finger, gently tapping the tiny plastic head of the miniature Kara White. "Is that supposed to be me? My jawline looks significantly more villainous than it does in a mirror."
Aki’s face burned a sudden crimson.

She was suddenly acutely aware that she was sitting on her private bed, wearing an informal silk gown, having been caught red-handed playing with toys of the woman currently staring directly at her face...

"They’re... they’re the official commemorative edition!" Aki stammered, pulling her knees against her chest in a desperate attempt to look dignified. "From the Apex Manufactory! They sold out globally in forty seconds! How did you even know about them?!"

"I signed the licensing clearance," Kara sighed, rolling her single shoulder with a muted pop. "Some oily corporate emissary from the High Directorate cornered me in a command tent while I was washing monster bile out of my hair, shoved sixteen pages of contract parchment into my hands, and promised me a twenty-five percent royalty cut on all gross merchandise transactions if I gave them my likeness rights. I signed it just to make him stop talking..."
Kara tilted her head, her gaze drifting over the collection. "How much did you pay for this box?"
"For the full royal collector’s set?" Aki muttered, looking away shyly. "About... twenty thousand Spirit Credits."
Kara’s brow furrowed. "Twenty thousand? For eleven lumps of painted resin and some clear acrylic sticks? That’s it?"
Aki blinked, staring at her in sheer unadulterated disbelief.
"That’s... that is an astronomical sum of money, Kara! Twenty thousand credits could buy a car in Europa!"

"That’s a bit cheap," Kara grunted, shaking her head with the cold cynical calculation of an old merchant. "Considering the Directorate is netting millions of units per production run, twenty thousand is practically a giveaway... Those leeches are underpricing my face. I should have demanded sixty-five percent."
Aki let out a soft exasperated breath.

"Well... the corporate notice said this was merely the early shipment. Because the initial pre-orders shattered every single retail database on the planet, they announced they’re going to release six additional waves over the next half-year with alternate poses and special battle-damaged editions... A deluxe set featuring you riding Talira in her full draconic form with an active plasma-light battery in her throat."
Kara gave a slow enthusiastic nod with her lips curving into a wide bright smile.
"Oh, wonderful," Kara said. "Truly marvelous. I can’t wait to see my face on lunchboxes and novelty keychains."
Aki looked at her closely.
Despite the smiling sarcasm, Aki’s sharp perceptive gaze didn’t miss the faint bruised shadows ringing the dark eyes beneath the hood.

The woman’s skin was pale, lacking its usual vibrant electric luster... her posture, while upright, carried the dragging inertia of an engine that had been burning its fuel injectors on an empty tank for a while.
Kara was exhausted.
"You really worked yourself half to death out there, didn’t you?" Aki said softly, the playful banter draining from her tone, replaced by an earnest warmth.
Kara let out a long ragged groan that rattled the fabric of her cowl as she dropped her forehead flat against the edge of the mattress, burying her face in the soft silk of the duvet.

"You have no idea," Kara muffled into the blanket. "Twelve days, Aki... Twelve days of digging trenches, cutting rifts, listening to Thor belch northern mead into my ear, and watching Number 5 argue with military marshals about evacuating, I haven’t slept on a surface softer than a fractured basalt slab in nearly two weeks... The air in Khemet tastes like copper shavings and burnt hair and I’m pretty sure if I blow my nose right now, a handful of bone-dust will come out."
She slowly pushed herself up, leaning back onto her heels.
CLICK!
Kara reached up with her single hand with her thumb flicking a tiny silver ring embedded into the hand.
FSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSH!
A subtle translucent distortion rippled across her body like heat shimmering off summer asphalt.
The broad shoulders narrowed as the long wild mane of black hair shortened, shifting into a clean slightly messy crop of dark brown locks.
The sharp, feminine jawline squared, the high cheekbones settling into the familiar stubbornly handsome, and quietly exhausted contours of a young man who was taller than Kara.
The pinned left sleeve unraveled, and from the void of the cloak, Silas Graves’s left arm emerged, resting casually against his knee as his regular clothes appeared too.
The disguise ring clicked into his pocket.
Silas let out a deep shuddering breath, rubbing the bridge of his nose where the tension of the transformation always left a dull ache.
"God," he muttered, his true voice filling the quiet bedroom. "I forget how much my ribs hurt after holding that illusion for that long."
Aki’s breath caught in her throat.

Even though she knew his secret... even though she was one of the microscopic few on the entire Earth who understood that the legendary Lord Vespera and the unassuming Europa orphan Silas Graves were the exact same soul, seeing the transition unfold with such casual intimacy in her own bedchamber sent a dizzying warm flutter straight into the base of her stomach.
Silas slowly pushed himself to his feet.
He took two heavy dragging strides toward the edge of the mattress with his boots falling with the leaden weight of a soldier coming home from the front.
"Wait, Silas, the figurines—"
Aki moved with nimble speed.

Her slender hands blurred across the duvet, scooping up Kara, Eluned, Thor, and the rest of the tiny plastic army, quickly transferring them over to the low nightstand beside the headboard, ensuring not a single painted sword or crystal arrow was crushed under his weight.
The moment her hands cleared the linen, Silas collapsed forward.
"Whoa—!"
Aki lunged forward instinctively with her arms reaching out to catch him before his face hit the headboard.
THUD-FLUFF!

Her slender unarmored frame was unprepared for the weight of a high-tier Awakened’s physical mass. Silas, on the other hand, didn’t catch his balance simply fell forward into her arms, taking her down with him.

The two of them tumbled backward onto the massive king-sized down mattress in a chaotic flurry of tangled sea-foam silk and heavy wool with the springs creaking softly beneath their combined momentum.
FLUMP!
Silas landed heavily on top of her.
His broad chest pressed firmly against her ribs with his face buried deep into the crook of her neck and his warm steady breath brushing directly against the sensitive porcelain skin behind her ear.
His arms lay limp at her sides, pinning the hem of her gown against the sheets.
THUMP-THUMP! THUMP-THUMP!
Aki’s heart hammered so violently she was terrified he would feel it through her sternum.
Her sapphire eyes were wide, staring up at the white-painted plaster of the ceiling as her face flushed with such intense heat that she felt dizzy.
The scent of him completely overwhelmed the lavender-scented laundry wash of her pillows.
Silas let out a long heavy infinitely content sigh that deflated his entire frame, sinking deeper into the soft down.

"Even though a Gold Core doesn’t technically require sleep..." Silas murmured, his voice muffled against her skin and vibrating right into her collarbone, "...I swear by the ancient kings, I just needed to feel a bed. A real, soft, clean bed that doesn’t smell like sulfur..."
Aki lay paralyzed beneath him, her hands hovering awkwardly above his back, her fingers trembling in the warm air.
"S-Silas...?" she squeaked, the pitch of her voice barely above a whisper. "You’re... you’re very heavy..."
Silas let out a soft exhausted chuckle.
SHIFT!
