chapters.title: Chapter 633: Aki’s First Kiss [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "So Aki... have you, like ever kissed someone before?"
Aki’s eyes snapped wide.
A bright wave of crimson exploded across her cheeks, rushing up her neck and burning hot enough to singe the silk beneath her head.

"W-What?!" she squeaked, her hands frantically knotting into the sheets at her sides. "N-No! Of course not! I’m the King’s own daughter! My father has had four high-tier maids stationed outside my residential pavilion since I was six years old... I haven’t even held a man’s hand without an armed escort present so why are you asking that right n—"
"Good," Silas said softly.
Before the final syllable could leave her lips, Silas leaned forward.
He didn’t give her time to retreat, and he didn’t give her room to hesitate.

His right hand slid smoothly from her chin with his fingers tangling deep into the silky cool azure tresses behind her neck, gently tilting her head back against the pillow as his lips came down firmly, hungrily upon hers.
Aki’s world violently unraveled...
The impact wasn’t gentle at all.
His mouth captured hers with an effortless certainty with his warm lips parting hers and his tongue sweeping forward to claim the moist trembling sweetness of her mouth with dominance.
"Mmph~"
Aki’s sapphire eyes dilated in dizzying shock and a soft strangled whimper escaped into his throat as the sensation tore through every sensory nerve in her body.
Her mind went blank, bleached clean of thoughts, of treaties, of logic, of her maids too...
Her small hands, which had been clutching the sheets in panic, slowly rose.

Her fingers reached out, trembling against the rough worn fabric of his clothes, before her palms flattened firmly against his chest, feeling the steady rhythm of his heart hammering against her fingertips.

And beneath the dizzying, breathless ecstasy of the kiss, as Silas’s tongue traced the roof of her mouth, a microscopic burning spark of pure gold mana flowed smoothly from his breath, crossing the threshold of her lips, sinking deep into the cold dormant center of her chest.
’Wh...’ Aki’s thoughts fragmented into breathless, spinning starlight as he pulled her closer against his body, drowning her senses in heat. ’...what does he mean... "good"...?’
SMACK! SMACK!
The room was lacking any other sound save for the uneven rhythm of their breath and the soft rustle of silk sheets yielding under their shifted weight.
For Aki, the world had shrunk down to the burning point of contact where their lips met.
It was an uncoordinated clumsy affair on her part.
SMACK!

She had spent twenty five years of her life in the high towers of Rhyx City reading treatises on royal court etiquette, memorizing foreign trade dialects, and studying how the world was before the Apocalypse, but none of those leather-bound folios had ever prepared her for the reality of an actual kiss.
She didn’t know where to tilt her chin, she didn’t know what to do with her teeth, and her tongue felt rigid, trembling in panic every time his lips shifted with effortless certainty.
’Why is he so good at this?!’ The thought spun through her dizzy mind like a top.
Silas was eighteen.

He had grown up an orphan in the concrete gutters of the Europa slums, probably scavenging copper wire and eating stale bread... not that she minded yet the way he tilted her head, the confident pressure with which he parted her lips, the subtle pull that drew a soft embarrassing whimper from the back of her throat... it carried an effortless experience that completely dismantled her defenses.
’So... so good~’
Then, through the hazy fog of her sensory overload, a memory flashed unbidden behind her closed eyes.

When she had been in Blessed Land, she had overheard atwo girls talking... They had been gossiping about Lord Silas with a woman, specifically about the breathtaking Former Spirit of the World Tree, Lady Eluned.

The rumors had spoken of how the two of them were practically inseparable in the Keep, how the divine tree-spirit looked upon him with worshipful adoration, and how they shared private chambers beneath the high arbor.

’Oh.’ A sudden sharp pang of realization struck Aki’s chest, followed immediately by a flush of heat that rushed from her neck to the tips of her ears. ’He must kiss Lady Eluned all the time over there.’
Before she could dwell on the thought, a strange sensation began to spread from her mouth downward.
A pooling warmth settled low in her abdomen making a dizzying moisture gather between her thighs that made her toes curl tightly against the sheets.
"Mmmph~"

That feeling was accompanied by an intense suffocating heat that bloomed directly behind her breastbone, it was scorching hot and a bit painful too, if Aki had to put it into words... it would be like an overwhelming furnace that expanded behind her ribs, dragging the air from her lungs until her vision began to blur with dark spots.
Her trembling hands, which had been clutching the fabric of his clothes, reached up and tapped twice against his shoulder.
’S-sorry...’
She didn’t want the kiss to stop.

A selfish desperate part of her wished she could freeze this exact second for an eternity but her lungs were screaming for oxygen, and the strange radiating fire behind her ribs was threatening to overwhelm her senses entirely.
Silas noticed immediately.
With a soft reluctant sigh that brushed warm against her damp lips, he gently broke the seal of their mouths.
A thin glistening silver thread of saliva connected their parted lips in the warm afternoon light, lingering for a fragile heartbeat before snapping softly against the corners of their mouths.
"Haah... Haah... Haah..."
Aki’s chest heaved with rapid gasps with her lips swollen and bright crimson while her large eyes were glassy, completely out of focus and staring blankly at the ceiling above his shoulder.
Silas propped himself up on one elbow, his dark eyes looking down at her flushed face with soft genuine concern.
"Aki?" he murmured, his voice sounding low and slightly husky. "Are you alright?"
Aki blinked with her gaze slowly traveling down as it landed on his face, before snapping to the right and staring resolutely at the carved mahogany wardrobe across the bedroom.
Her face was burning with enough heat to smelt copper.
"W-We..." she squeaked, her voice trembling like a plucked violin string. "...we kissed."
Silas let out a soft rueful chuckle, his knuckles coming up to rub the back of his neck in mild embarrassment.
"Yeah. We did. Sorry, I probably should have warned you before diving in like a barbarian..."
"N-No!" Aki blurted out, her hands flying up in a small, flustered flutter. "It was fine! Really! It was... fine."
She trailed off, her eyes darting back toward him.
Her nose subtly twitched.
She sniffed the air once, then twice, and the romantic breathless haze in the room suddenly thinned.
Beneath the lingering scent of his clothes, an undeniable potent odor was radiating from the man sprawled across her pristine ivory linen.
It was a ripe suffocating combination of damp sweat and the unmistakable stench of burnt blood that had clung to his body after several days of warfare.
’It seems his smell passes over to his real body.’
Aki slowly turned her head, looking him dead in the eye with an expression of deadpan horror.
"Silas," she said with her voice sounding flat.
"Yeah?"
"You stink."
Silas blinked.
"What?"

"You smell like a burnt armory that sat in a stagnant swamp for three weeks," Aki stated with royal authority, wrinkling her small nose. "You smell terrible... Honestly, it’s a miracle my nose didn’t fall off during that kiss."
A heavy silence settled over the bed and for three seconds, neither of them moved.
Then, slowly, a vibrant unmistakable wave of red crawled up Silas’s neck, burning across his cheeks and settling right into the tips of his ears.
’C-cute...’ Aki thought.
The great Lord Silas looked like an eight-year-old boy who had just been caught tracking mud across his mother’s clean kitchen floor.
"I... uh..." Silas stammered, looking down at his dust-caked tunic with sudden mortification. "...Can I use your bath?"
Aki pressed her lips together, fighting a desperate losing battle against the bright grin threatening to split her face.
She pointed a slender, trembling finger toward a set of arched double doors carved from frosted glass and gold leaf at the far corner of the bedchamber.
"Through there," she giggled softly. "Straight ahead and please, use the lavender salts... All of them..."

"Right. Lavender. Got it," Silas muttered under his breath, scrambling off the bed with a haste that thoroughly lacked dignity, practically sprinting across the Persian rug before ducking through the frosted glass doors.
The heavy latch engaged behind him.
Silas stood in the center of the bathroom, let out a massive shuddering breath, and stared around him.
"...What in the hell is this ridiculous luxury?" he muttered aloud.
Even with his new life outside from the slums, the sight before him looked like the treasury vault of an ancient empire.
The entire chamber was forged from seamless slabs of rose-veined white alabaster that hummed with a dormant heating ward beneath his boots.
The faucets were sculpted from solid, polished orichalcum in the shape of leaping sea-drakes, their eyes set with tiny luminescent aquatic pearls.

The primary tub was not a tub at all but an indoor sunken pool, deep enough to submerge a grown man to his chin, already steaming with crystal-clear mineral water covered in a thick fragrant blanket of frothing white bubbles that smelled faintly of crushed sweet citrus and mountain mint.
"Fucking hell..."
Dominating the western wall was a massive floor-to-ceiling mirror carved from polished celestial silver, framed in intricate gold filigree.
Silas walked over and stopped before the glass, looking at his reflection.
His hair was slightly wild but his dark eyes were clear and the heavy dragging exhaustion that had plagued his temples for a while had begun to settle into a focused quiet.
’It’s about time,’ Silas thought, his gaze turning serious.
He hadn’t made an experimental spatial jump upon arriving in Rhyx City just to play around with royal toys.
Helping Aki awaken her dormant core had been lingering in the back of his mind for a while.
Ever since the summit of the World Council, ever since he had watched her been oppressed by everyone, he had resolved to break the biological cage she had been trapped in since birth.

’I’ve been researching with the System ever since we cleared the second sector in Khemet,’ Silas mused, his brow furrowing deeply. Yet every single time he had submitted a direct inquiry regarding Princess Aki’s specific physical blockage, the interface had behaved erratically... I’m a bit confused though, The System, an omnipresent database capable of decrypting the classified divine lineages of the Sovereign Realm for a handful of Upgrade Points, had consistently refused to yield a clean direct answer regarding her core."
Silas stared into his own reflection with his jaw setting hard.
’What sort of entity does the World King have to be able to solicit this kind of evasive deadlocked reaction from the System of all things?’
Aki was the biological daughter of the current World King.
Her bloodline was directly descended from the highest authority on the terrestrial plane.

If her core had been intentionally locked, if someone had suppressed her spiritual pathways before she had even taken her first breath in the cradle, it wasn’t the work of a petty rival lord or a jealous concubine.
It was the work of something vast, something lurking in the deep shadows behind the World Council’s throne.
"Whatever," Silas grunted, shaking his head. "One problem at a time."
With a lazy, fluid movement, his body seemed to flicker.
His dust-stained clothes, boots, and everything else vanished, dropping into a neat folded pile on the stone bench as he slipped into the steaming water.

The heat hit his skin like an electric shock of pure relief as Silas sank down until the warm mineral bubbles reached his lower lip, letting out a long rumbling groan of transcendent bliss that resonated through the tiled dome.
’At least I’m done with that northern nightmare for now.’
Well, not entirely done.
Technically speaking, he had abandoned his post.

The moment Number 5 had successfully routed the last four thousand refugees through the southern extraction arrays, the masked woman had turned around, cleared her throat, and begun drafting a new military directive ordering Kara and some others to fly north to hunt down six stray Tiers 5s that were currently wandering through the empty salt flats.

chapters.title: Chapter 634: There’s Hope For You [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "Fuck that woman."

Silas had looked at the slate... He had looked at the endless burning horizon too and then, while Number 5 had turned her back to calibrate an orbital communication relay, Silas had simply initiated an emergency spatial blink, vanishing from the place before she could even turn her head after unsummoning his girls of course.

’It’s her own fault,’ Silas scoffed internally, blowing a raft of scented bubbles away from his nose. ’I didn’t sign up to be the World Council’s unpaid exterminator for more than a week while their bloated marshals sit in air-conditioned bunkers drinking iced tea.’
Besides, the trip hadn’t been a waste.
His internal UP balance was resting at an astronomical high, the notifications from the girls’ grinding having pushed his reserves into territory he hadn’t seen before.
As of right now, he had the fuel and he had the foundation too so now he just needed to fix the princess.
Out in the sunlit bedroom, Princess Aki was sitting on the edge of her king-sized bed with her bare feet dangling inches above the plush carpet.
Her slender uncalloused fingers rose, gently touching her lower lip where her skin still tingled.
’We kissed.’ The thought danced through her mind in an endless dizzying loop.
She pressed her knees together, burying her burning face in both hands, letting out a muffled squeaky squeal that was swallowed by the high ceiling.
"Mmph~ That was nice..."
She was completely inexperienced so she desperately hoped she hadn’t embarrassed herself. Did her teeth clack? Was she too stiff? Did she kiss like a dead fish?
’He took my first kiss.’ A soft, dreamy smile spread across her flushed lips as her hands dropped to her lap.
She didn’t mind, not in the slightest.

Even the smell of that awful sulfurous dust hadn’t bothered her nearly as much as she had pretended... beneath the grime, the scent of him was something she had secretly yearned for ever since the day she realized she had fallen for him.
’When he comes out,’ Aki thought, her posture straightening with sudden royal determination, ’I am going to give him his reward. A proper gift for all that brutal work in the desert.’
She had already prepared it days ago, locked inside the small star-iron safe beneath in her closet... It was something that an adventurous reckless lord like Silas would need.
Aki stood up, smoothing the wrinkles from her sea-foam gown, and turned toward the vanity as the frosted glass doors swung open behind her.
Silas stepped out into the bedroom, enveloped in a rolling cloud of sweet citrus-scented steam while Aki stopped mid-step, her breath hitching in her throat.
He wasn’t wearing his armor, and he wasn’t wearing his regular clothes either.

SIlas was wrapped in a plush heavy white terrycloth bathrobe embroidered with a sprawling golden sun-crest along the lapels, a garment that looked suspiciously identical to the luxury amenities provided exclusively in the VIP penthouse suites of the Grand Oasis Palace in Iunu.

"Aha," Silas grinned, running a hand through his damp, towel-dried hair as he strolled casually across the carpet. "I snagged this from one of the linen closets in the hotel before the whole thing started... Knew it would come in handy eventually."
Aki blinked, staring at him.
The steam clinging to his skin made his bare collarbones and neck gleam under the golden afternoon light.

His frame, while lean, carried the perfectly sculpted musculature of a high-tier martial artist, broad shoulders, tight lats, and a posture that radiated effortless balance even in an oversized bathrobe.
"You... you look good," Aki murmured softly with the words slipping past her lips before her brain could stop them.
She tilted her head, her sapphire eyes narrowing slightly as she studied his face.
"Is it just my imagination, or is your hair longer?"
Silas paused, reaching up to tug at the damp strands falling over his forehead.
He gave his head a small shake, letting the dark black locks fall loosely around his cheekbones, reaching nearly down to the nape of his neck.

"Yeah," he admitted, a wry slightly sheepish smile touching his mouth. "It grew out during the trench-clearing... I’m thinking about keeping it a bit longer this time. Sera mentioned the other day that she thought it looked better when it had some length to it."
Aki froze as the soft romantic atmosphere in the room shattered like brittle glass.
’Sera?’ The name echoed through Aki’s brain with the clarity of a church bell. ’Seraphina Bloom.’
The memory hit Aki like a splash of freezing seawater.

Barely two weeks ago, during the preliminary diplomatic sessions at the World Council summit, the legendary Heiress of the Bloom Clan, that gorgeous woman was casually dropping references to how Silas Graves was her ’prospective consort’ as well..

’He kissed me,’ Aki’s internal thoughts hissed, her eyes flaring with a bit of wrath, ’and thirty seconds later, he is standing in my bedroom talking about the aesthetic preferences of another woman?!’
Aki marched across the Persian rug like a miniature storm cloud.
"Hey, Silas?" she said, her voice dripping with deceptively sweet poison.
Silas turned his head with his hand still in his hair. "Hm?"
Aki’s small, unarmored fist jabbed him squarely in the center of his ribs.
"Oof!" Silas grunted, stumbling half a step backward, looking down at her with wide, bewildered eyes. "What was that for?!"

"You insensitive brute!" Aki scowled, crossing her arms beneath her chest, her lower lip pouting so fiercely it was a wonder it didn’t snap. "You kiss me until my knees give out, you steal my luxury bath, and then you come out here waxing poetic about Seraphina Bloom’s grooming advice?! Do you have a single grain of romantic tact inside that thick skull of yours?!"
Silas stared at her, utterly baffled, before the realization finally dawned on him.
A soft, breathless laugh escaped his lips as he reached up, rubbing the sore spot on his ribs, shaking his head with an amused grin.

"Aki, come on," Silas chuckled, his voice gentle and placating. "I’m sorry. I wasn’t thinking but it’s not like Sera and I are engaged or anything. She just talks like that because she enjoys watching everyone around her squirm..."
Aki’s pout did not diminish by a single millimeter. She tilted her chin upward, her eyes narrowing into sharp suspicious slits as she took a half-step into his personal space.
"Did you kiss her?" Aki demanded, her voice dropping into a dangerously quiet tone.
Silas stopped with his eyes darted slightly to the ceiling but he didn’t answer immediately.
He seemed to genuinely ponder the question, his brow furrowing as his brain rapidly sifted through the chaotic memories of their time together.
Aki’s lower lip dropped even further with her eyebrows drawing into a knot of agonizing jealousy.
’He’s thinking about it?! WHY DOES HE HAVE TO THINK ABOUT IT?!’
Finally, Silas looked back down at her, offering an innocent, lopsided shrug.
"None of the times I know of. Unless she slipped something into my tea while I was unconscious, we haven’t locked lips."
Behind Aki’s back, her small right hand discreetly clenched into a tiny, victorious fist, pumping downward once in triumph.
Her composure slammed smoothly back into place, though the bright pink hue on her cheeks refused to fade.
"Hmph," she huffed, turning on her heel with a theatrical swish of her silk gown. "Well... At least you have some standards."
Silas let out an amused sigh, walking past her toward the massive bed.

He sank heavily onto the edge of the mattress with the down pillows indenting beneath his frame as he rested his forearms on his knees, his eyes tracing the intricate floral carvings on the cedar headboard.
Aki followed him, her movements hesitant, before she gently lowered herself onto the mattress beside him, leaving a respectful six-inch gap between their thighs.
She looked at his profile with the damp hair curling slightly at his collar, the sharp stubborn line of his nose, and the quiet stillness that seemed to permanently anchor his presence.
"Silas," she asked softly, her tone shifting, the playful jealousy completely gone. "What was the purpose of that kiss?"
Silas didn’t turn his head immediately. "What do you mean?"

"You’re not a frivolous man," Aki murmured, her fingers resting lightly against the silk of her lap. "You don’t do things without an objective I think. Unless you’ve been secretly harboring intense, scandalous romantic feelings for me, you didn’t kiss me just because the afternoon sun looked pretty..."
She paused, looking at his hands.
"There was a strange sensation during the kiss. A heavy burning heat that settled behind my ribs. It felt foreign, like an electric current entering my marrow..."
Silas turned his head, his dark eyes meeting hers with an expression of quiet approval.
"You really are sharp," he murmured. "You’re right. I was transferring mana into you. My Gold Core essence, calibrated through my breath so your nervous system wouldn’t reject the frequency."
Aki’s eyes widened slightly. "Mana? But why through a kiss?"

"Because your meridians are a bit calcified," Silas explained. "If I tried to force mana into your core through your palms or your spinal acupoints, the feedback would shatter your vascular walls like brittle glass... The oral threshold, the breath, is the only conduit where pure spiritual intent can enter the pulmonary cavities without triggering an automatic immune response."
’I learned that from the System, heh.’
He totally wasn’t reading the tab...
He paused, his expression growing grim.
"Aki, I spent the last three days analyzing your case... The fact that you never awakened, it’s not an accident of nature."
Aki’s breath hitched.

"Someone influenced your vessel," Silas said, the words cold and absolute. "From birth I believe, a microscopic spiritual seal was placed over your soul or something before your infant pathways could even begin to circulate mana. I think it was designed to keep you permanently dormant."
A heavy silence descended over the sunlit bedchamber.
Aki didn’t gasp, and she didn’t cry out in shock. Instead, a slow weary sigh escaped her lips.
She reached across the small distance between them, her slender, trembling fingers sliding gently into Silas’s calloused palm.
Her skin was cool and fragile against his rough knuckles.

"Silas," she whispered, her gaze dropping to their joined hands. "When I was of age, my father summoned the grand alchemists of the High Directorate... They spent three months running diagnostic arrays across my spine... They fed me crushed star-lotus nectar, distilled marrow, and alchemical elixirs that cost more than a merchant fleet. My body burned with fever for six weeks and even then, not a single drop of mana ever circulated."
A sad fragile smile touched her lips as she looked up into his eyes.

"I’ve spent so many years coming to terms with it," she murmured. "I accepted that I would never stand upon the battlefield... I accepted that my place was here so you don’t have to carry this burden for me, Silas. I don’t want you to torture yourself over something that cannot be undone."
Silas looked down at her.
He didn’t look defeated, and he didn’t look pitying. Instead, the corners of his mouth slowly curved into a warm confident smirk.
"Is that so?" Silas asked softly.
"Yes," Aki nodded earnestly.
"Then tell me, Princess," Silas murmured, his free hand slowly rising, "if your core is dead, where did my mana just go?"
Aki blinked. "What?"
Silas’s index finger reached out, gently pressing against the center of her chest, right over her sternum.
Aki looked down and her breath froze in her throat.
Beneath the sea-foam silk of her gown, directly behind the porcelain skin of her thoracic center, a tiny breathtakingly radiant golden glow was pulsing.
It was faint, no larger than a grain of sand, but it beat with a slow heartbeat that vibrated directly against her ribs.
THUMP! THUMP!
It did not fade at all...
It was drinking the air, slowly circulating Silas’s transferred essence through the dormant pathways of her chest, illuminating her collarbones in a soft ethereal halo of light.

sentences.text: "Fuck that woman."
Silas had looked at the slate...

He had looked at the endless burning horizon too and then, while Number 5 had turned her back to calibrate an orbital communication relay, Silas had simply initiated an emergency spatial blink, vanishing from the place before she could even turn her head after unsummoning his girls of course.

’It’s her own fault,’ Silas scoffed internally, blowing a raft of scented bubbles away from his nose. ’I didn’t sign up to be the World Council’s unpaid exterminator for more than a week while their bloated marshals sit in air-conditioned bunkers drinking iced tea.’
Besides, the trip hadn’t been a waste.
His internal UP balance was resting at an astronomical high, the notifications from the girls’ grinding having pushed his reserves into territory he hadn’t seen before.
As of right now, he had the fuel and he had the foundation too so now he just needed to fix the princess.
Out in the sunlit bedroom, Princess Aki was sitting on the edge of her king-sized bed with her bare feet dangling inches above the plush carpet.
Her slender uncalloused fingers rose, gently touching her lower lip where her skin still tingled.
’We kissed.’ The thought danced through her mind in an endless dizzying loop.
She pressed her knees together, burying her burning face in both hands, letting out a muffled squeaky squeal that was swallowed by the high ceiling.
"Mmph~ That was nice..."
She was completely inexperienced so she desperately hoped she hadn’t embarrassed herself.
Did her teeth clack?
Was she too stiff?
Did she kiss like a dead fish?
’He took my first kiss.’ A soft, dreamy smile spread across her flushed lips as her hands dropped to her lap.
She didn’t mind, not in the slightest.

Even the smell of that awful sulfurous dust hadn’t bothered her nearly as much as she had pretended... beneath the grime, the scent of him was something she had secretly yearned for ever since the day she realized she had fallen for him.
’When he comes out,’ Aki thought, her posture straightening with sudden royal determination, ’I am going to give him his reward.
A proper gift for all that brutal work in the desert.’
She had already prepared it days ago, locked inside the small star-iron safe beneath in her closet...
It was something that an adventurous reckless lord like Silas would need.
Aki stood up, smoothing the wrinkles from her sea-foam gown, and turned toward the vanity as the frosted glass doors swung open behind her.
Silas stepped out into the bedroom, enveloped in a rolling cloud of sweet citrus-scented steam while Aki stopped mid-step, her breath hitching in her throat.
He wasn’t wearing his armor, and he wasn’t wearing his regular clothes either.

SIlas was wrapped in a plush heavy white terrycloth bathrobe embroidered with a sprawling golden sun-crest along the lapels, a garment that looked suspiciously identical to the luxury amenities provided exclusively in the VIP penthouse suites of the Grand Oasis Palace in Iunu.
"Aha," Silas grinned, running a hand through his damp, towel-dried hair as he strolled casually across the carpet.
"I snagged this from one of the linen closets in the hotel before the whole thing started...
Knew it would come in handy eventually."
Aki blinked, staring at him.
The steam clinging to his skin made his bare collarbones and neck gleam under the golden afternoon light.

His frame, while lean, carried the perfectly sculpted musculature of a high-tier martial artist, broad shoulders, tight lats, and a posture that radiated effortless balance even in an oversized bathrobe.
"You... you look good," Aki murmured softly with the words slipping past her lips before her brain could stop them.
She tilted her head, her sapphire eyes narrowing slightly as she studied his face.
"Is it just my imagination, or is your hair longer?"
Silas paused, reaching up to tug at the damp strands falling over his forehead.
He gave his head a small shake, letting the dark black locks fall loosely around his cheekbones, reaching nearly down to the nape of his neck.
"Yeah," he admitted, a wry slightly sheepish smile touching his mouth.
"It grew out during the trench-clearing...
I’m thinking about keeping it a bit longer this time.
Sera mentioned the other day that she thought it looked better when it had some length to it."
Aki froze as the soft romantic atmosphere in the room shattered like brittle glass.
’Sera?’ The name echoed through Aki’s brain with the clarity of a church bell. ’Seraphina Bloom.’
The memory hit Aki like a splash of freezing seawater.

Barely two weeks ago, during the preliminary diplomatic sessions at the World Council summit, the legendary Heiress of the Bloom Clan, that gorgeous woman was casually dropping references to how Silas Graves was her ’prospective consort’ as well..

’He kissed me,’ Aki’s internal thoughts hissed, her eyes flaring with a bit of wrath, ’and thirty seconds later, he is standing in my bedroom talking about the aesthetic preferences of another woman?!’
Aki marched across the Persian rug like a miniature storm cloud.
"Hey, Silas?" she said, her voice dripping with deceptively sweet poison.
Silas turned his head with his hand still in his hair.
"Hm?"
Aki’s small, unarmored fist jabbed him squarely in the center of his ribs.
"Oof!" Silas grunted, stumbling half a step backward, looking down at her with wide, bewildered eyes.
"What was that for?!"
"You insensitive brute!" Aki scowled, crossing her arms beneath her chest, her lower lip pouting so fiercely it was a wonder it didn’t snap.
"You kiss me until my knees give out, you steal my luxury bath, and then you come out here waxing poetic about Seraphina Bloom’s grooming advice?!
Do you have a single grain of romantic tact inside that thick skull of yours?!"
Silas stared at her, utterly baffled, before the realization finally dawned on him.
A soft, breathless laugh escaped his lips as he reached up, rubbing the sore spot on his ribs, shaking his head with an amused grin.
"Aki, come on," Silas chuckled, his voice gentle and placating.
"I’m sorry.
I wasn’t thinking but it’s not like Sera and I are engaged or anything.
She just talks like that because she enjoys watching everyone around her squirm..."
Aki’s pout did not diminish by a single millimeter.
She tilted her chin upward, her eyes narrowing into sharp suspicious slits as she took a half-step into his personal space.
"Did you kiss her?" Aki demanded, her voice dropping into a dangerously quiet tone.
Silas stopped with his eyes darted slightly to the ceiling but he didn’t answer immediately.
He seemed to genuinely ponder the question, his brow furrowing as his brain rapidly sifted through the chaotic memories of their time together.
Aki’s lower lip dropped even further with her eyebrows drawing into a knot of agonizing jealousy.

WHY DOES HE HAVE TO THINK ABOUT IT?!’

Behind Aki’s back, her small right hand discreetly clenched into a tiny, victorious fist, pumping downward once in triumph.
Her composure slammed smoothly back into place, though the bright pink hue on her cheeks refused to fade.

chapters.title: Chapter 635: A Memory [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Aki stared at the golden light and her vision blurred as hot heavy tears welled in her large sapphire eyes, spilling over her lashes and tracing silent burning tracks down her cheeks.
"It’s glowing," she choked out, a strangled sob tearing from her throat as she pressed her own trembling hand over his finger. "Silas, it’s actually glowing."

"You awakened a core, Aki," Silas said softly, his voice washing over her like a warm summer wave. "You always had one... The seal prevented the seed from recognizing it which is another reason why your blood is special and needed for the gloves... You couldn’t become a Lord because the lock severed your connection to the Sovereign Realm."
He leaned closer, his dark eyes locking onto hers.
"I can break the lock and I can forge the pathways but you have to trust me, Aki. Completely... Without hesitation..."
Aki clutched his hand against her chest, her fingers knotting into his skin as she wept openly, her head shaking in desperate affirmation.

"I trust you," she sobbed, her voice breaking with years of buried grief and newfound miraculous hope. "I trust you with my life, Silas. Even if you told me to jump into hell, I would jump, because I know you would catch me."
’Ah... isn’t that a bit too much?!’
She took a ragged trembling breath, looking up through her tears into his face.
"Why?" she whispered with her voice barely audible. "Why are you doing this for me? Why would you expend so much of your own core for someone who can offer you nothing in return?"
Silas smiled.
His hand shifted with his fingers gently wiping away the hot tears pooling beneath her eyes while his touch felt feather-soft and tender.

"Because I care about you, Aki," Silas said softly, the words were simple and honest, though they meant the world to him. "I gave you a name... and I stood behind you in front of everyone because I take responsibility for the people who stand with me but beyond that..."
He leaned in slightly, his lips mere inches from her ear. "I like you. A lot."
Aki’s mind stopped. The weeping hitched in her throat as her large blue eyes widened to their limits and her heart gave a violent acrobatic leap that sent the blood roaring through her ears.
’Is this a confession?!’ Aki’s brain lit up into a glorious, spinning supernova of pure ecstasy.
He liked her!
Silas Graves had just looked her in the eye and told her he liked her!
Her lips parted.
A radiant breathless smile broke across her tear-stained face, her hands reaching up to cup his jaw, the words rising from the depths of her soul.
"Silas... I... I like you too—"
"And besides," Silas interrupted smoothly, pulling back half an inch with a straight face, "you’re already twenty five years old."
Aki blinked, the confession freezing on the tip of her tongue.
"...What?"

"At this rate," Silas continued, speaking with the grave, solemn concern of a physician addressing a terminal illness, "if you stay unawakened, you’re going to grow into a frail wrinkly old woman by the time you’re eighty... Meanwhile, my Gold Core will keep me looking like a strapping twenty-year-old for the next three centuries. You’ll be sitting in a rocking chair with a shawl, seething with jealousy over my immaculate jawline!"
Silence descended upon the bedroom.
Aki sat frozen on the silk mattress with her hands remaining hovering in the air and her mouth remaining slightly parted.
Her brain took three full seconds to process the transition from a transcendent soul-stirring declaration of romantic devotion to an unprompted offensive lecture about skin-aging.
A tick formed beneath Aki’s left eye.
"You..." she hissed, her voice vibrating with enough fury to crack the windows. "...you... you... Id—"
Before she could finish the word, Silas’s open right palm flattened firmly against the glowing golden center of her chest.
His eyes snapped shut, his Gold Core roaring to life within his chest with the concussive intensity of an ignited star.
’System,’ Silas commanded. ’Target Aki’s Dormant Core and initiate an upgrade to Purple.’
He deliberately did not push for a Gold Core.
...Not yet.
A Gold core like him was an anomaly that drew the immediate, paranoid gaze of the world council and the World King.
If a second Gold Core suddenly detonated within the private residence of a daughter of the Royal Family, the fallout would bring an entire fleet of inquisitors to Rhyx City within forty minutes.
Once he dismounted those bloated old bastards from their thrones in the future, once Blessed Land possessed the authority to dictate terms to the entire planet, he would forge her into gold.
For now, an unblemished peerless Purple Core would grant her the staggering magical output of a noble.
A brilliant notification slate materialized before Silas’s mental vision.
[UPGRADE INITIATING...]
[CONSUMING 34,000 UP.]
[COMMENCING PURPLE CORE REFINEMENT...]
A massive torrential cascade of violent, royal-purple mana erupted from Silas’s palm, pouring directly into the golden seed behind Aki’s ribs.
Aki’s eyes dilated with her back arching off the mattress as a breathless silent gasp tore from her throat.

The spiritual seal locking her meridians unraveled completely at the molecular level, dissolved by the authority of the upgrade as new incandescent purple pathways branched outward from her chest like delicate crystalline lightning, weaving through her vascular system, revitalizing her dormant organs with a flood of pure vitality.
And then, right beneath the completion bar, a secondary pitch-black notification tab violently tore through Silas’s optic nerves, dripping with crimson-bordered glyph.
[SOUL-RESIDUE ACCESSED.]
[SEAL HAS UNLOCKED A MEMORY FRAGMENT.]
[YOU HAVE UNLOCKED ???’s MEMORY.]
Silas’s mental voice hitched in shock.
’Huh?’
Before he could pull his hand back, before he could even draw a breath, the sunlit bedroom of Rhyx City, the silk sheets, the lavender scent of the bath, and Princess Aki’s arching frame vanished.
The world turned pitch-black.
"I want to die."
The voice carried the thin dry scrape of linen dragging across sand and Silas blinked.
The suffocating dark did not roll back like a curtain or shatter like glass.
It simply frayed, the blackness thinning into pale morning haze that smelled a bit of salt air as the world gathered its weight around him.
He was standing on the flagstones of a wide private terrace that jutted out over an empty blue bay.
Below, the sea was glass-still, undisturbed by tides or wind, framed by chalk-white cliffs that rose toward an unblemished, empty sky.
There were no maritime bells ringing in the distance either, it was just stillness.
In the center of the terrace, framed by trailing vines of pale star-jasmine, an old wooden rocking chair moved with a slow monotonous rhythm.
Sitting in it was a woman.
At first glance, Silas felt his breath catch behind his ribs.
Her silhouette was so startlingly familiar that for half a second he thought he was looking at Aki if she was older but as the haze settled, the differences sharpened.

Her long hair was not the bright aquatic lapis lazuli of the princess... it was thick, ink-black, falling over her shoulders in loose waves that caught the flat morning light and when she turned her profile toward the bay, her eyes were not sapphire.
They were deep violet, the color of twilight over a cold mountain pass.

"It really doesn’t matter," she murmured softly, leaning her cheek against her palm with her knuckles resting on the arm of the rocker. "All this dying, and dying again... What will it matter at the end of the day if I just come back?"
She swallowed, her throat working with a dry click, her violet gaze drifting down toward her own lap.
Her hands moved slowly, settling over the broad heavy swell of her belly.
She was heavily pregnant, the linen of her loose white gown stretched taut over the curve, rising and falling with her slow shallow breaths.

"I don’t want this for you," she whispered to the swelling child, her voice trembling, stripped of self-pity and carrying only the quiet exhausted weight of fatigue. "Not the throne... Not the bloodline... Not the endless, stupid butcher’s work... I just want you to be normal."
Silas remained motionless at the perimeter of the terrace, his boots making no impression on the flagstones.
’A memory,’ he thought, his jaw setting hard. ’Her mother.’
It was obvious.
The bone structure, the stubborn tilt of the chin, the quiet melancholy that Aki carried beneath her royal manners, it was all rooted right here in this woman’s frame.
Yet, as Silas looked down at his own hands, he realized he had no physical weight.
He cast no shadow against the white stone so he was a foreign observer dropped into an old echo etched into a broken seal.
’Why would my core breaking her lock pull me into this?’ he wondered, his mind turning over the pieces. ’A dormant seal placed before birth. Was it an enemy of the World King, or was it—’
"But you don’t want her to be normal, do you?"
Silas froze.
The woman didn’t tilt her head to the empty air, and she didn’t murmur it to the sky.
She turned her neck slowly, her deep violet eyes locking squarely onto Silas’s face...
She was looking right at him.
A cold prickle crept up the back of Silas’s neck.
From what he was aware, memories were fixed things that happened before... so... How? How was this woman was looking directly into his pupils.
’She sees me? How the hell can a recording see me?!’
The woman didn’t scream or reach for a weapon, instead a tired smile curved her pale lips, though her violet eyes remained sharp, piercing through the illusion of time with eerie clarity.

"This is an imprint I carved into my daughter’s spiritual foundation," she said, her voice steady and melodious despite her weariness. "A lock forged from my own soul to keep her dormant and since you are standing here inside the inner sanctum of that seal, I can only assume you are the one who took a chisel to my work..."
Silas parted his lips to speak.
"I didn’t mean to pry, I was only—"

"Save your breath," she interrupted gently, waving a limp hand through the air. "You really don’t need to explain yourself to an echo. What’s done is done... Every soul born under the sun has a right to choose its own path, I suppose."
Her hand returned to her belly with her thumb tracing small soothing circles over the linen.
A sudden sharp bitterness flashed across her features, hardening the soft lines of her face.

"Just so you know, I locked her core out of spite, you know," she admitted with dry honesty. "To spite that good-for-nothing man since he wanted another weapon... Another sovereign to march across the dust of the Sovereign Realm under his banner... what a man he is, I want to give him nothing... An empty vessel, maybe a daughter who would live a quiet mortal life, useless to his grand ambitions since he’s so weak to do so himself since he’s such a bitch."
She paused, her rocking chair slowing to a halt.

"If you’ve spent the blood and mana to dismantle a seal of that power that went from her soul to her core," she said, looking Silas up and down with her gaze lingering on his broad shoulders and the dark immovable stillness in his eyes, "that must mean you love her very much."
The woman placed her palms flat on the wooden armrests and pushed herself up from the chair.
Silas instinctively flinched, shifting his weight into a defensive half-step before he remembered he was an incorporeal phantom.
She walked toward him.
Her bare feet made soft damp scuffs against the flagstones with her loose white gown swaying around her ankles as she stopped barely two paces away, tilting her head back to look up at him.

"That’s very good," she murmured softly, her violet eyes softening until they shone with a maternal warmth. "I’m glad. If she must walk the bloody path after all, at least she won’t be walking it alone."
Silas stared down at her, his brow knitting into a bewildered knot.
"How is this even possible? You’re a memory right... A memory can’t adapt to an external intruder, let alone hold a conversation."
The woman’s lips parted into a small playful smirk, a look so identical to Aki’s mischievous grins that Silas nearly blinked.

A tick formed beneath Aki’s left eye.
"You..." she hissed, her voice vibrating with enough fury to crack the windows.
Id—"
Before she could finish the word, Silas’s open right palm flattened firmly against the glowing golden center of her chest.
His eyes snapped shut, his Gold Core roaring to life within his chest with the concussive intensity of an ignited star.
’System,’ Silas commanded. ’Target Aki’s Dormant Core and initiate an upgrade to Purple.’
He deliberately did not push for a Gold Core.
...Not yet.
A Gold core like him was an anomaly that drew the immediate, paranoid gaze of the world council and the World King.
If a second Gold Core suddenly detonated within the private residence of a daughter of the Royal Family, the fallout would bring an entire fleet of inquisitors to Rhyx City within forty minutes.
Once he dismounted those bloated old bastards from their thrones in the future, once Blessed Land possessed the authority to dictate terms to the entire planet, he would forge her into gold.
For now, an unblemished peerless Purple Core would grant her the staggering magical output of a noble.
A brilliant notification slate materialized before Silas’s mental vision.
[UPGRADE INITIATING...]
[CONSUMING 34,000 UP.]
[COMMENCING PURPLE CORE REFINEMENT...]
A massive torrential cascade of violent, royal-purple mana erupted from Silas’s palm, pouring directly into the golden seed behind Aki’s ribs.
Aki’s eyes dilated with her back arching off the mattress as a breathless silent gasp tore from her throat.

The spiritual seal locking her meridians unraveled completely at the molecular level, dissolved by the authority of the upgrade as new incandescent purple pathways branched outward from her chest like delicate crystalline lightning, weaving through her vascular system, revitalizing her dormant organs with a flood of pure vitality.
And then, right beneath the completion bar, a secondary pitch-black notification tab violently tore through Silas’s optic nerves, dripping with crimson-bordered glyph.
[SOUL-RESIDUE ACCESSED.]
[SEAL HAS UNLOCKED A MEMORY FRAGMENT.]
[YOU HAVE UNLOCKED ???’s MEMORY.]
Silas’s mental voice hitched in shock.
’Huh?’
Before he could pull his hand back, before he could even draw a breath, the sunlit bedroom of Rhyx City, the silk sheets, the lavender scent of the bath, and Princess Aki’s arching frame vanished.
The world turned pitch-black.
"I want to die."
The voice carried the thin dry scrape of linen dragging across sand and Silas blinked.
The suffocating dark did not roll back like a curtain or shatter like glass.
It simply frayed, the blackness thinning into pale morning haze that smelled a bit of salt air as the world gathered its weight around him.
He was standing on the flagstones of a wide private terrace that jutted out over an empty blue bay.
Below, the sea was glass-still, undisturbed by tides or wind, framed by chalk-white cliffs that rose toward an unblemished, empty sky.
There were no maritime bells ringing in the distance either, it was just stillness.
In the center of the terrace, framed by trailing vines of pale star-jasmine, an old wooden rocking chair moved with a slow monotonous rhythm.
Sitting in it was a woman.
At first glance, Silas felt his breath catch behind his ribs.
Her silhouette was so startlingly familiar that for half a second he thought he was looking at Aki if she was older but as the haze settled, the differences sharpened.

Her long hair was not the bright aquatic lapis lazuli of the princess... it was thick, ink-black, falling over her shoulders in loose waves that caught the flat morning light and when she turned her profile toward the bay, her eyes were not sapphire.
They were deep violet, the color of twilight over a cold mountain pass.
"It really doesn’t matter," she murmured softly, leaning her cheek against her palm with her knuckles resting on the arm of the rocker.
"All this dying, and dying again...
What will it matter at the end of the day if I just come back?"
She swallowed, her throat working with a dry click, her violet gaze drifting down toward her own lap.
Her hands moved slowly, settling over the broad heavy swell of her belly.
She was heavily pregnant, the linen of her loose white gown stretched taut over the curve, rising and falling with her slow shallow breaths.
"I don’t want this for you," she whispered to the swelling child, her voice trembling, stripped of self-pity and carrying only the quiet exhausted weight of fatigue.
"Not the throne...
Not the bloodline...
Not the endless, stupid butcher’s work...
I just want you to be normal."
Silas remained motionless at the perimeter of the terrace, his boots making no impression on the flagstones.
’A memory,’ he thought, his jaw setting hard. ’Her mother.’
It was obvious.
The bone structure, the stubborn tilt of the chin, the quiet melancholy that Aki carried beneath her royal manners, it was all rooted right here in this woman’s frame.
Yet, as Silas looked down at his own hands, he realized he had no physical weight.
He cast no shadow against the white stone so he was a foreign observer dropped into an old echo etched into a broken seal.
’Why would my core breaking her lock pull me into this?’ he wondered, his mind turning over the pieces. ’A dormant seal placed before birth.
Was it an enemy of the World King, or was it—’
"But you don’t want her to be normal, do you?"
Silas froze.
The woman didn’t tilt her head to the empty air, and she didn’t murmur it to the sky.
She turned her neck slowly, her deep violet eyes locking squarely onto Silas’s face...
She was looking right at him.
A cold prickle crept up the back of Silas’s neck.
From what he was aware, memories were fixed things that happened before... so...
How?
How was this woman was looking directly into his pupils.
’She sees me?
How the hell can a recording see me?!’
The woman didn’t scream or reach for a weapon, instead a tired smile curved her pale lips, though her violet eyes remained sharp, piercing through the illusion of time with eerie clarity.
"This is an imprint I carved into my daughter’s spiritual foundation," she said, her voice steady and melodious despite her weariness.
"A lock forged from my own soul to keep her dormant and since you are standing here inside the inner sanctum of that seal, I can only assume you are the one who took a chisel to my work..."
Silas parted his lips to speak.
"I didn’t mean to pry, I was only—"
"Save your breath," she interrupted gently, waving a limp hand through the air.
"You really don’t need to explain yourself to an echo.
What’s done is done...
Every soul born under the sun has a right to choose its own path, I suppose."
Her hand returned to her belly with her thumb tracing small soothing circles over the linen.
A sudden sharp bitterness flashed across her features, hardening the soft lines of her face.
"Just so you know, I locked her core out of spite, you know," she admitted with dry honesty.
"To spite that good-for-nothing man since he wanted another weapon...
Another sovereign to march across the dust of the Sovereign Realm under his banner... what a man he is, I want to give him nothing...
An empty vessel, maybe a daughter who would live a quiet mortal life, useless to his grand ambitions since he’s so weak to do so himself since he’s such a bitch."
She paused, her rocking chair slowing to a halt.

"If you’ve spent the blood and mana to dismantle a seal of that power that went from her soul to her core," she said, looking Silas up and down with her gaze lingering on his broad shoulders and the dark immovable stillness in his eyes, "that must mean you love her very much."
The woman placed her palms flat on the wooden armrests and pushed herself up from the chair.
Silas instinctively flinched, shifting his weight into a defensive half-step before he remembered he was an incorporeal phantom.
She walked toward him.
Her bare feet made soft damp scuffs against the flagstones with her loose white gown swaying around her ankles as she stopped barely two paces away, tilting her head back to look up at him.
"That’s very good," she murmured softly, her violet eyes softening until they shone with a maternal warmth.
"I’m glad.
If she must walk the bloody path after all, at least she won’t be walking it alone."
Silas stared down at her, his brow knitting into a bewildered knot.
"How is this even possible?
You’re a memory right...
A memory can’t adapt to an external intruder, let alone hold a conversation."
The woman’s lips parted into a small playful smirk, a look so identical to Aki’s mischievous grins that Silas nearly blinked.

chapters.title: Chapter 636: Vassal Lord Of Blessed Land [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "Well," she said, tapping her temple with a pale fingertip, "it is my soul and my memory to influence... Let a dying woman have her secrets."
She took one more step, closing the distance until she was standing directly in front of him.
Her violet eyes narrowed slightly, sweeping across his face with sharp scrutiny.
"You made my daughter fall for you, didn’t you?" she asked, her voice dropping into a quiet murmur.
Silas opened his mouth, but before he could form an answer, an unmistakable bright pink blush suddenly bloomed across the woman’s porcelain cheeks.
Her cool regal composure completely evaporated, replaced by an adorably flustered pout that looked utterly ridiculous on a woman who had just been musing about death.
She raised her right hand, curling her fingers into a fist, and aggressively jabbed her index finger straight into the center of Silas’s chest.
"Take responsibility!" she huffed with her face red as she was glaring at him with fierce wide eyes.
The moment the tip of her pale finger touched Silas’s sternum, the white limestone terrace beneath their feet violently shuddered.
A thin jagged fracture tore through the flagstones, running from her bare heels straight out into the bay.
The sea itself cracked like brittle green ice with long fissures spider-webbing across the sky.
The woman lowered her hand, her expression softening once more as the world around them began to dissolve into drifting white dust.
"Tell me," she whispered, her voice fading beneath the rising sound of breaking glass. "What did you name her? What is her name?"
Silas looked at the fractures spreading across her shoulders and he didn’t hesitate.
A small, warm smile touched his lips.
"Aki," Silas said softly. "Her name is Aki."
The woman blinked as her eyebrows drew together in a sudden offended scowl.

"Aki?" she complained loudly, her voice echoing over the rumbling collapse of the terrace. "Just Aki?! That’s it?! Gods above, so little effort was put into it! What kind of lazy single-syllable nonsense is—"
Another massive fissure ripped clean through the center of the terrace, severing the space between them.
The woman’s complaint was cut off.
She looked down at the dissolving stone, then looked back at Silas through the drifting light with her lips curving into a gentle tender smile.
"Actually," she murmured, her voice barely a whisper carried on the dissolving wind, "it’s a very nice name."
The white terrace, the glass bay, the rocking chair, and the black-haired woman shattered into millions of blinding silent white motes.
"Silas! Silas, wake up! Silas?!"
The sounds of the waking world rushed back into his ears in a sudden burst as Silas gasped with his eyelids flying open.
The soft lavender-scented down mattress of the Rhyx City bedchamber yielded beneath his palms.
The golden afternoon light was still slanting through the high glass terrace doors, catching the sea-foam curtains fluttering in the ocean draft.
He sat upright, shaking his head to clear the static behind his eyes.
"Oh," Silas murmured with his voice rough. "Aki."
Standing in the center of the Persian rug, three paces from the edge of the mattress, was Princess Aki.
She was not lying down, and she was not weeping in pain either. The older woman was standing tall on her bare feet with her back straight and her hands trembling at her sides.
"Look, Silas!" Aki gasped, her voice cracking with breathless hysteria with tears of overwhelming joy spilling freely over her lashes. "Look! LOOK!"
Silas turned his head, his dark eyes focusing on her frame and his jaw slowly dropped.
Swirling around Aki’s slender body was a brilliant, radiant tempest of pure royal-purple mana.

It didn’t leak like smoke... it danced along her skin in tight crackling ribbons of crystalline violet light, weaving around her wrists, surging through the hem of her silk gown, and crowning her sapphire hair with a soft iridescent violet halo.
Her meridians were singing.

"I can use mana," Aki choked out, pressing both hands over her mouth, laughing through her tears. "Silas, I can actually feel it! It’s right here! It’s flowing through my arms! It’s warm, it’s so warm!"
She dropped her hands, her sapphire eyes blazing with sudden fierce focus.
"And look at this!" she cried, spinning on her heel toward the carved cedar side-table.
Sitting atop the wood was a heavy ornamental porcelain vase painted with traditional Khemet lotus patterns.
Aki raised her right hand, pointing her slender index finger toward the ceramic and her brow furrowed in intense concentration as her purple mana funneling down her arm toward her fingertip.
It was slow...
For two full seconds, nothing happened then a tiny, dark purple spark flickered against the glazed porcelain.
The vase did not shatter from impact, and it did not melt from heat.
Beginning at the rim, the porcelain simply began to unbind.
The molecular structure unraveled, shedding fine dark-purple ash that drifted silently downward onto the cedar surface.
Millimeter by millimeter, the vase was systematically disassembled, dissolving into nothingness until only a small pile of purple-tinged dust remained upon the tabletop.
Aki whirled back toward him, her face flushed with triumph.

"I can use Father’s Destruction!" she gasped, clenching her small fist. "It’s slow, it’s so much slower than his, and it took almost half my focus just to unbind a flowerpot, but it’s Destruction... The element of the Royal Bloodline! With enough time, with enough training in the Sovereign Realm, I’ll be able to wield it properly, Silas! I’ll actually be able to fight!"
Silas looked at the pile of dust on the table, then looked back at her radiant tear-streaked face as a wide genuine smile broke across his exhausted features.
"Congratulations, Princess," Silas said softly, his voice full of quiet pride. "You’re an Awakened now... A real one."
Aki practically launched herself across the bed, throwing her arms tightly around Silas’s neck, burying her face into the curve of his collarbone with a breathless joyful sob.
"Thank you," she wept, her small body shaking against his chest. "Thank you, thank you, thank you. Silas...."
Silas’s arms wrapped naturally around her waist, pulling her onto his lap as she nestled against him.
He held her securely, letting his chin rest against the top of her blue head, breathing in the clean scent of her hair while her tears soaked into the terrycloth of his stolen bathrobe.
A pale translucent notification slate flickered to life directly before Silas’s eyes.
He blinked, his gaze traveling across the text:
[Target: Princess Aki Has Transitioned To Awakened Status.]

[Because Target’s Core Was Awakened Directly Via Host’s Sacred Mana Transfer, Target’s Future Territory Shall Be Formally Registered As A [Vassal Territory] Beneath The Primary Dominion Of [Blessed Land].]

[Authority Clause: Host Retains Command Over Target’s Borders... All Heroes And Troop Formations Summoned Beneath Target’s Banner Shall Simultaneously Operate As Secondary Units Of Blessed Land’s Core Armed Forces.]
Silas’s hands tightened slightly around Aki’s waist. His dark eyes narrowed, his brow furrowing as he read the clauses over twice.
’A Vassal Territory?’ A cold pang of hesitation struck his chest.
Silas could understand... It was with the help of the System of course but he had somehow managed to make Aki a Vassal Lord to Blessed Land.
In the brutal hierarchy of the Sovereign Realm, a ’Vassal Lord’ was essentially a subordinate governor.
You answered to the Supreme Lord, your borders paid tithes to the central treasury, and your troops could be mobilized at your master’s whim.

If someone had stepped into Blessed Land and informed Silas that his hard-earned territory was being placed beneath another sovereign’s boot, he would have drawn the Dawn Blade and severed their head before the ink on the treaty was dry...

’Would she hate this?’ Silas worried silently, his stomach knotting. ’She’s a royal princess and she’s the daughter of the World King... To awaken her core only to bind her territory to mine, she might think I tricked her.’
He gently patted her back, leaning back slightly so he could look down into her face.
"Aki," Silas said, keeping his tone careful, measured, and transparent. "There’s something you need to know about how the awakening."
Aki sniffled, wiping her eyes with the sleeve of her gown, looking up at him with innocent trusting curiosity. "What is it?"

"Because your core was jump-started directly using my Gold Core mana," Silas explained, watching her expression closely, "Your future domain as a Vassal Territory... It means your land will operate officially beneath the banner of Blessed Land. You’ll still be the ruling Lord of your own borders, but legally and militarily, your territory is subordinate to mine."
Silas braced himself for the shift.
He waited for the pride to flare, for the furrowed brow, for the indignation of a Princess learning she was legally a vassal.
’Hopefully she doesn’t get too mad...’
Instead, Aki’s sapphire eyes went wide as dinner plates.
"Wait," she gasped, her hands clutching his lapels with sudden excitement. "Does that mean our territories are going to be connected?!"
Silas blinked, caught completely off-guard. "Well, yes... Troops and resources can cross borders from what I think at least."
"Yes!" Aki squeaked aloud, bouncing up and down on his lap with enough force to make the bedsprings squeak. "That’s amazing! That’s literally the best possible outcome!"
Silas stared at her, completely dumbfounded. "You’re happy about being a vassal?"

"Of course I am, you giant idiot!" Aki beamed, twirling a loose strand of blue hair around her index finger with her cheeks turning a charming shade of pink. "Why on earth would I want an isolated lonely territory out in the middle of nowhere where Lords raiders can harass my borders?! If I’m a vassal of Blessed Land, our forces are combined! I can visit your orchards whenever I want! Lady Eluned and Lady Aeliana can come over for tea, we can share defensive garrisons, and if any slimy Lord tries to do me anything, I can just tell them to take it up with Lord Vespera!"
She puffed her small chest out with immense satisfaction.
"I am officially an executive commander of Blessed Land..."
Silas sat frozen for two seconds, staring at her beaming face then a quiet, helpless laugh tumbled from his throat.
’I really overreacted,’ Silas thought, shaking his head with an amused sigh. ’I forgot who I was talking to.’
Still, a stray specific thought flickered through Silas’s mind as he looked down at her.
’I do wonder... will the passive domain aura of Blessed Land carry over to her vassal borders?’
Blessed Land operated under the blessing of the Divine Sanctum.

Due to the specific traits of his initial territory roll, the territory possessed an overwhelming passive harmonic affinity that attracted female champions, boosted female unit stats, and discouraged male recruitment.
Silas didn’t have a personal hatred for men as he wasn’t on some ideological crusade against testosterone.

’But still,’ Silas reasoned, ’does Blessed Land really need men around? I’m already doing the work of a hundred men... Maybe a thousand. The girls are disciplined too and an all-female territory is remarkably tidy.’
He cleared his throat, pulling his wandering thoughts back to reality.

"Alright, Princess," Silas smiled, resting his hands on her hips. "Now that you’ve got an active core, you have to prepare for the Novice Trial which is for a week. Do you have supplies ready? Descending for the first time is brutal... You need troop tickets and building materials or the wild beasts will overrun your perimeter before your hall even renders."
’Oh right, the Sovereign Realm does give you ten daily tickets...’
Aki’s eyes lit up with sudden remembrance.
"Oh! The gifts!"
She scrambled off his lap, her bare feet hitting the carpet with light rapid slaps as she scurried across the room toward the ornate cedar vanity.
She dropped to her knees, reaching deep into the dark space beneath the central drawer.
"Mm mm..."
Aki’s fingers found a hidden latch, and with a soft click, she dragged out a heavy rectangular chest forged from solid enchanted star-iron.
"Here it is."
Aki hoisted the heavy chest onto the edge of the bed with a breathless grunt, flipping the twin brass latches open.

Silas didn’t have a personal hatred for men as he wasn’t on some ideological crusade against testosterone.
’But still,’ Silas reasoned, ’does Blessed Land really need men around?
I’m already doing the work of a hundred men...
Maybe a thousand.
The girls are disciplined too and an all-female territory is remarkably tidy.’
He cleared his throat, pulling his wandering thoughts back to reality.
"Alright, Princess," Silas smiled, resting his hands on her hips.
"Now that you’ve got an active core, you have to prepare for the Novice Trial which is for a week.
Do you have supplies ready?
Descending for the first time is brutal...
You need troop tickets and building materials or the wild beasts will overrun your perimeter before your hall even renders."
’Oh right, the Sovereign Realm does give you ten daily tickets...’
Aki’s eyes lit up with sudden remembrance.
"Oh!
The gifts!"
She scrambled off his lap, her bare feet hitting the carpet with light rapid slaps as she scurried across the room toward the ornate cedar vanity.
She dropped to her knees, reaching deep into the dark space beneath the central drawer.
"Mm mm..."
Aki’s fingers found a hidden latch, and with a soft click, she dragged out a heavy rectangular chest forged from solid enchanted star-iron.
"Here it is."
Aki hoisted the heavy chest onto the edge of the bed with a breathless grunt, flipping the twin brass latches open.

chapters.title: Chapter 637: Princess Aki’s Boyfriend? [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "These were originally the gifts I had prepared for you," Aki explained, her voice bright and proud as she opened the heavy lid. "I had my maids scour the private auctions across Europa and the maritime ports for the past few weeks... Even with the shortage caused by the Khemet incursion, I managed to secure quite a haul."
Silas leaned forward, looking into the velvet-lined interior as his eyes nearly popped out of his skull.
Sitting inside, tied neatly in thick bundles of gold ribbon, were stacks upon stacks of thick summoning tickets embossed with the iridescent silver runes of the Sovereign Realm.
"One hundred and fifty Hero Summoning tickets," Aki said casually, lifting a heavy stack in her small hand, "and about a thousand Troop Summoning tickets."
She reached deeper into the chest, pulling out three compact miniature space capsules that hummed with mana.

"These are compressed capsules," she continued, setting them on the duvet. "Enough quarried titan-stone, reinforced timber, and refined copper to construct twelve Tier 3 structures... I was going to hand all of this to you as a reward for saving Khemet, but well, since I’m descending today, I might have to borrow all of them for my own territory!"
She giggled, playfully dumping several thick bundles of tickets across the white sheets like poker chips.

"Though, obviously," Aki added with wisdom, "a territory’s summoning capacity depends heavily on its initial radius... It doesn’t make sense to crack hundreds of Troop summoning tickets on day one if your central hall can’t feed them. You’d just cause a famine before the first wave hits."
Silas stared at the glowing mountain of summoning tickets covering the mattress as a dry whistling breath escaped his teeth.

"What a ridiculous collection you have," Silas muttered, picking up a pristine gold-edged Hero summoning tickets with his fingers tingling from the pure, dormant potential locked inside the tickets. "Princess, if the World Council saw this pile... Well what do you think they’d say? Including your father."
Aki puffed her cheeks out, looking thoroughly pleased with herself.
"My father doesn’t know about half of these! I purchased them using the independent revenue from my personal pearl fisheries! Every single ticket here was bought with a clean unmonitored allowance!"
She scooped up a massive armful of tickets, at least a hundred Hero tickets and eight hundred Troop tickets, and pushed them firmly into Silas’s lap.

"Take them," Aki smiled, her sapphire eyes shining with earnest generosity. "You did amazing impossible work in Northern Khemet, Silas... You saved hundreds of thousands of people so you deserve this, and so much more."
Silas looked down at the fortune in his lap.
He didn’t take them all.
Without a word, he split the massive pile in two so he took seventy-five Hero tickets and five hundred Troop tickets, sliding them gently back across the linen into her hands.

"Fifty-fifty," Silas said firmly, meeting her gaze with an immovable smirk. "You’re entering an active territory, Aki and the novice trial doesn’t care that you’re a royal princess... You need elite guards, and you need laborers to dig your trenches."

"Silas, no!" Aki protested, pushing the tickets back toward his chest. "I already told you, my initial territory radius won’t be able to sustain that many units! Ten Hero summoning tickets and two hundred troops is more than enough for my novice perimeter... You’re the one managing Blessed Land! You have a lot of acres to defend!"
"And I have more than ten people who can cleave mountains in two," Silas retorted, pushing them back. "Take the tickets, Aki. Don’t be stubborn."
"I am a royal princess... Being stubborn is my birthright—"
The heavy mahogany bedroom door swung open.
"Princess Aki, the port authority sent the revised—"
Mira stopped dead in her tracks.
The head maid, holding a leather folio in her hands, stood frozen in the open doorway as her sharp middle-aged eyes swept across the room in a single second.

She saw the bed. She saw the tangled, rumpled silk sheets. She saw Princess Aki, flushed bright red, kneeling on the mattress in a disheveled gown and sitting right beside her, sprawled in a VIP hotel bathrobe with his collar hanging wide open, his dark hair damp and messy, was a young stunningly handsome man with sharp dark eyes and a casual dangerous presence.
The bedroom fell into a silence so absolute that the rustle of the curtains sounded like thunder.
Mira’s hands tightened around her leather folio until the seams creaked.
’This is the man the Princess has been stalking? Her boyfriend, Silas Graves?!’
He was dangerously good-looking.
Even draped in cheap terrycloth with damp hair, the man carried an immovable gravity that made the hair on Mira’s forearms stand on end.
For half a second, an absurd inappropriate flutter of feminine jealousy brushed against the veteran maid’s chest.
Then her gaze dropped back to the bathrobe... the damp hair... the rumpled sheets and the flushed cheeks too.
’Did they just?! IN THE MIDDLE OF THE AFTERNOON?! BEFORE THE OFFICIAL BETROTHAL TREATIES WERE EVEN DRAFTED?!’
"MIRA, SHUT UP!" Aki shrieked, her face exploding into crimson.
Mira snapped her mouth shut instantly, though her eyes remained wide as saucers, darting frantically between Silas’s bare collarbones and Aki’s swollen lips.
"It is NOT what it looks like!" Aki yelled, scrambling off the bed so fast she nearly tripped over the hem of her gown. "We weren’t, he was just, I AWAKENED!"
Mira blinked once. "You... what?"
"Look!"
Aki raised her trembling hand, pointing her finger at an ornamental brass paperweight resting on the vanity table.

Her royal-purple mana surged once more, the air crackling as well and the brass paperweight groaned as a tiny dark-purple spark ignited against the metal, and slowly, the solid brass began to unbind, crumbling into a neat fine pile of metallic purple dust that drifted onto the polished wood.
Mira’s jaw dropped.
The leather folio slipped from her numb fingers, hitting the Persian rug with a heavy thud.
"Destruction," Mira whispered, her voice trembling with unvarnished shock. "The royal lineage mana... Princess, you awakened?"
"Yes!" Aki cried, her eyes shining with triumphant tears once more. "I have a Purple Core, Mira! A real, unblemished core!"
’Isn’t she crying a bit too much...?’

"By the heavens," Mira gasped, pressing both hands over her heart, tears of genuine joy welling in her eyes as she took three hurried steps forward. "Praise the ancestors... Praise the high tides! Oh, Princess, your mother would have wept... We must inform the King immediately! The royal fleet must be summoned! A grand celebration across the entire province—"
"NO!" Aki cut her off sharply as Mira paused, looking confused.

"You will not report a single word to my father," Aki commanded firmly, stepping between Mira and the bed, her small frame radiating unyielding resolve. "Not yet... You will draft the formal dispatch, but you will hold the transmission until after I have entered the Sovereign Realm and initiated my novice trial."
Mira’s eyes widened.
"Princess! The novice trial is perilous! If you enter without something—"
"I am entering under the sovereign protection of Blessed Land," Aki stated, her chin lifting with quiet pride. "My territory is an official vassal domain so I’ll be safe."

’I guess it’s alright for her to say that.’ Silas thought, It wasn’t like the World Council knew much about it to question anything... If they asked him how he did it, he would tell them he had a Gold core so they could go figure. ’That’s a sufficient answer...’
She stepped closer to her maid, her sapphire eyes narrowing with deadly seriousness.

"And most importantly, Mira, you did not see Silas Graves in this room... If a single whisper of his presence reaches the city guards, I will strip you of your pension and banish you to the salt docks. Do you understand me?"
Mira looked at the fierce, glowing young woman standing before her then she swallowed hard, slowly dropping into a deep flawless court curtsy.
"By your command, My Princess," Mira murmured with obedience. "My lips are sealed."

She retrieved her folio from the carpet, offered one last suspicious glance toward Silas lounging on the bed, and backed out of the bedchamber, pulling the heavy mahogany doors shut behind her with a soft click.
The room fell quiet once more.
Silas let out a low, amused whistle.
"Fierce... Remind me never to get on your bad side, Princess."
Aki turned around, her fierce expression instantly melting back into a soft flustered pout.
"Oh, hush. We have a schedule to keep."
After five more minutes of quiet negotiation, they finally reached a compromise.
Silas adamantly refused to let her leave with bare pockets and Aki reluctantly accepted two hundred Troop Summoning Tickets and ten Hero Summoning Tickets, alongside four of the material containers.
Silas swept the remaining seventy-five Hero tickets and eight hundred Troop tickets into his own spatial ring with a broad satisfied grin.
’This should be enough... not too much... not too less.’
He would keep them on hand in case.
Aki tapped the air before her chest and the air unfolded making her breath hitch, it was a shimmering blue interface that only she could see.

With a few delicate taps of her manicured fingers, the stacks of parchment tickets and the heavy iron material boxes vanished into thin air, absorbed smoothly into her newly initialized Lord Inventory.
She stared at her empty palms, her sapphire eyes wide with childlike wonder.
"It really works," she whispered softly. "I have an inventory..."
She turned toward Silas, her breath catching slightly as she looked into his dark eyes.
"I guess," Aki murmured, her voice dropping into a quiet tender melody, "I’ll see you back in Blessed Land, My Lord."
Silas smiled warmly, nodding his head.
"I’ll have the welcoming banquet ready. Good luck, Aki."
Aki took a deep steadying breath.
Her finger rose, hovering over the pulsing rune at the center of her interface.
[DESCEND]
Her heart hammered against her ribs like a trapped bird.

This was the moment every person of the mortal realm dreamed of, the terrifying, magnificent leap into the unknown, crossing the veil into a world of infinite monsters, ancient treasures, and thrones.
She tapped the rune.
A blinding vertical pillar of royal-purple spatial light erupted from the bedroom floor, enveloping Aki’s body in a swirling weightless cyclone of dimensional ether.
The system’s descending confirmation began to chime in the air with the spatial displacement pulling at her hair, whipping her blue locks into a wild luminous tempest.
And then, right before the veil closed, Aki didn’t close her eyes in fear. She lunged forward.

Her soft trembling lips pressed firmly, warmly against Silas’s right cheek, leaving behind a lingering sweet spark of purple mana that tingled against his skin as she pulled back with a brilliant breathless laugh, her sapphire eyes shining through the light.
The pillar of purple light collapsed inward and the wind died as the Persian rug was now empty.
Silas sat alone on the edge of the massive down bed with his hand slowly rising to touch his cheek where her lips had landed.
He let out a long quiet breath through his nose with his dark eyes looking at the empty space where she had stood.

’Well, fuck,’ Silas thought, a wry, slightly anxious smirk touching his lips. ’I hope she rolls a good starting sector... An Unknown Zone with high-tier resources would be ideal, somewhere quiet where she can build her walls without getting ambushed by a roaming behemoth on day one.’
He shook his head, running a hand through his damp brown hair.
’Either way, it’s time to go home.’
Silas rose to his feet. He reached into his pocket, slipping the disguise ring back onto his finger.

The optical illusion blurred across his frame, the bathrobe vanishing, replaced once more by the high-collared traveler’s mantle of Kara White, with the empty left sleeve pinned neatly across his chest.
He stepped toward the open balcony doors with his boots making no sound against the carpet.
Behind him, the heavy mahogany bedroom door swung open once more.
"Princess Aki?" Mira’s voice called out hesitantly from the threshold. "Forgive the intrusion, but the port marshal requires your personal wax seal to clear the—"
Mira froze.
She stepped into the bedroom and the bed was neatly rumpled.
The tall, handsome young man in the bathrobe was gone and Princess Aki, the Royal Family’s first daughter, was nowhere to be found as well.
Mira stood alone in the empty sunlit suite with her mouth falling open as her eyes darted between the open balcony doors and the vacant bed.
"Princess...?" Mira stuttered into the quiet breeze, her voice rising in panic.
"...Princess Aki?!"
